paragraphs: In the beginning, God creates the heavens and the earth.
The earth is formless and empty. Darkness is over the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God is hovering over the face of the waters.
The First Day
And God says, “Let there be light.” And there is light.
And God sees that the light is good. And God separates the light from the darkness.
God calls the light Day, and the darkness he calls Night.
And there is evening and there is morning — the first day.
The Second Day
And God says, “Let there be an expanse in the midst of the waters, and let it separate waters from waters.”
And God makes the expanse and separates the waters below the expanse from the waters above the expanse. And it is so.
And God calls the expanse Sky.
And there is evening and there is morning — the second day.
The Third Day
And God says, “Let the waters below the sky be gathered to one place, and let the dry ground appear.” And it is so.
And God calls the dry ground Earth, and the gathered waters he calls Seas. And God sees that it is good.
And God says, “Let the earth sprout vegetation — plants bearing seed, and fruit trees bearing fruit according to their kinds, with their seed in them, on the earth.” And it is so.
And the earth brings forth vegetation — plants bearing seed according to their kinds, and trees bearing fruit with their seed in them according to their kinds. And God sees that it is good.
And there is evening and there is morning — the third day.
The Fourth Day
And God says, “Let there be lights in the expanse of the sky to separate the day from the night. And let them be for signs and for appointed times, and for days and years.
And let them be lights in the expanse of the sky to give light on the earth.” And it is so.
And God makes the two great lights — the greater light to rule the day and the lesser light to rule the night — and the stars.
And God sets them in the expanse of the sky to give light on the earth,
to rule over the day and over the night, and to separate the light from the darkness. And God sees that it is good.
And there is evening and there is morning — the fourth day.
The Fifth Day
And God says, “Let the waters swarm with swarms of living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth across the face of the expanse of the sky.”

And God creates the great sea creatures and every living creature that moves, with which the waters swarm, according to their kinds, and every winged bird according to its kind. And God sees that it is good.
And God blesses them, saying, “Be fruitful and multiply and fill the waters in the seas, and let birds multiply on the earth.”
And there is evening and there is morning — the fifth day.
The Sixth Day
And God says, “Let the earth bring forth living creatures according to their kinds — livestock and creeping things and wild animals according to their kinds.” And it is so.
And God makes the wild animals according to their kinds and the livestock according to their kinds and everything that creeps on the ground according to its kind. And God sees that it is good.

And God says, “Let us make the human in our image, after our likeness. And let them have dominion over the fish of the sea and over the birds of the sky and over the livestock and over all the earth and over every creeping thing that creeps on the earth.”
And God creates the human in his own image —
in the image of God he creates him —
male and female he creates them.

And God blesses them. And God says to them, “Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth and subdue it. Rule over the fish of the sea and over the birds of the sky and over every living thing that moves on the earth.”
And God says, “Look — I give you every plant bearing seed that is on the face of all the earth, and every tree that has fruit bearing seed. They shall be food for you.
And to every wild animal and to every bird of the sky and to everything that creeps on the earth — everything that has the breath of life — I give every green plant for food.” And it is so.
And God sees everything he has made — and look, it is very good.
And there is evening and there is morning — the sixth day.
The Seventh Day
And the heavens and the earth and all their host are completed.
And on the seventh day God finishes his work that he has done. And he rests on the seventh day from all his work that he has done.
And God blesses the seventh day and makes it holy — because on it he rests from all his work that God has created by making.
This is the account of the heavens and the earth when they were created.
In the day YHWH God makes earth and heaven —
before any plant of the field is in the earth and before any herb of the field has sprung up (for YHWH God has not yet sent rain on the earth, and there is no human to work the ground),
and a mist is rising from the earth and watering the whole face of the ground —
then YHWH God forms the man from the dust of the ground and breathes into his nostrils the breath of life. And the man becomes a living creature.
And YHWH God plants a garden in Eden, toward the east. And there he puts the man he has formed.

And out of the ground YHWH God causes to grow every tree that is pleasant to the sight and good for food — and the tree of life in the midst of the garden, and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
A river flows out of Eden to water the garden. And from there it divides and becomes four rivers.
The name of the first is Pishon — it is the one that flows around the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold.
And the gold of that land is good. Bdellium and onyx stone are there.
The name of the second river is Gihon — it is the one that flows around the whole land of Cush.
And the name of the third river is Tigris, which flows east of Assyria. And the fourth river is the Euphrates.
And YHWH God takes the man and settles him in the garden of Eden to work it and to keep it.
And YHWH God commands the man: “You may freely eat from every tree of the garden.
But from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil — you shall not eat from it. For in the day you eat from it, you will surely die.”
And YHWH God says, “It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make him a helper as his counterpart.”

And YHWH God forms from the ground every wild animal and every bird of the sky and brings them to the man to see what he would call them. And whatever the man calls every living creature, that is its name.
And the man gives names to all the livestock and to the birds of the sky and to every wild animal. But for the man there is not found a helper as his counterpart.
So YHWH God causes a deep sleep to fall on the man. And while he sleeps, he takes one of his sides and closes up the flesh in its place.
And YHWH God builds the side he has taken from the man into a woman and brings her to the man.
And the man says:
“This at last — bone of my bones
and flesh of my flesh.
She shall be called Woman,
for from Man she was taken.”
Therefore a man shall leave his father and his mother and hold fast to his wife, and they shall be one flesh.
And the man and his wife are both naked and feel no shame.
Now the serpent is more crafty than any other wild animal that YHWH God has made. And he says to the woman, “Did God really say, ‘You shall not eat from any tree in the garden’?”
“We may eat from the fruit of the trees of the garden,” the woman says to the serpent.
“But from the fruit of the tree that is in the midst of the garden, God said, ‘You shall not eat from it and you shall not touch it, lest you die.’”
“You will not surely die,” the serpent says to the woman.
“For God knows that in the day you eat from it, your eyes will be opened — and you will be like God, knowing good and evil.”

And the woman sees that the tree is good for food, and that it is a delight to the eyes, and that the tree is desirable for gaining wisdom. And she takes from its fruit and eats. And she also gives some to her husband who is with her — and he eats.
And the eyes of both of them are opened. And they know that they are naked. And they sew fig leaves together and make themselves coverings.
And they hear the sound of YHWH God walking in the garden in the cool of the day. And the man and his wife hide themselves from the presence of YHWH God among the trees of the garden.
And YHWH God calls to the man: “Where are you?”
“I heard the sound of you in the garden,” he says, “and I was afraid, because I was naked. And I hid.”
“Who told you that you were naked?” he says. “Have you eaten from the tree I commanded you not to eat from?”
“The woman you gave to be with me — she gave me fruit from the tree. And I ate.”
“What is this you have done?” YHWH God says to the woman.
“The serpent deceived me,” the woman says. “And I ate.”
And YHWH God says to the serpent:
“Because you have done this —
cursed are you above all livestock
and above all wild animals.
On your belly you shall go,
and dust you shall eat
all the days of your life.
I will put enmity between you and the woman,
and between your offspring and her offspring.
He will crush your head,
and you will strike his heel.”
To the woman he says:
“I will greatly multiply your pain in childbearing —
in pain you shall bring forth children.
Your desire will be toward your husband,
and he will rule over you.”
And to the man he says:
“Because you listened to the voice of your wife
and ate from the tree I commanded you —
‘You shall not eat from it’ —
cursed is the ground because of you.
In toil you shall eat from it
all the days of your life.
Thorns and thistles it shall bring forth for you,
and you shall eat the plants of the field.
By the sweat of your face you shall eat bread,
until you return to the ground —
for out of it you were taken.
For you are dust,
and to dust you shall return.”
The man calls his wife’s name Havvah — because she is the mother of all living.
And YHWH God makes garments of skins for the man and for his wife and clothes them.
And YHWH God says, “Look — the man has become like one of us, knowing good and evil. And now, lest he reach out his hand and take also from the tree of life and eat, and live forever —”
So YHWH God sends him out from the garden of Eden to work the ground from which he was taken.
He drives the man out. And at the east of the garden of Eden he places the cherubim and the whirling flaming sword — to guard the way to the tree of life.
Now the man knows Havvah his wife. And she conceives and bears Cain. And she says, “I have gotten a man with the help of YHWH.”
And she goes on to bear his brother Abel. Now Abel is a keeper of sheep, and Cain is a worker of the ground.
In the course of time Cain brings an offering to YHWH from the fruit of the ground.
And Abel also brings an offering — from the firstborn of his flock, from their fat portions. And YHWH looks with favor on Abel and his offering,
but on Cain and his offering he does not look with favor. And Cain is very angry, and his face falls.
“Why are you angry?” YHWH says to Cain. “And why has your face fallen?
If you do well, will you not be accepted? And if you do not do well, sin is crouching at the door. Its desire is for you — but you must rule over it.”
And Cain says to Abel his brother, “Let us go out to the field.” And when they are in the field, Cain rises against Abel his brother and kills him.
“Where is Abel your brother?” YHWH says to Cain.
“I don’t know,” he says. “Am I my brother’s keeper?”
“What have you done?” he says. “The voice of your brother’s blood is crying to me from the ground.
And now — cursed are you from the ground, which has opened its mouth to receive your brother’s blood from your hand.
When you work the ground, it shall no longer yield to you its strength. You shall be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth.”
“My punishment is greater than I can bear,” Cain says to YHWH.
“Look — you have driven me today from the face of the ground. And from your face I shall be hidden. I shall be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth, and whoever finds me will kill me.”
“Therefore,” YHWH says to him, “whoever kills Cain will suffer vengeance sevenfold.”
And YHWH puts a mark on Cain so that no one who finds him will strike him down.
And Cain goes out from the presence of YHWH and settles in the land of Nod, east of Eden.
And Cain knows his wife. And she conceives and bears Enoch. And Cain builds a city, and calls the name of the city after the name of his son, Enoch.
To Enoch is born Irad. And Irad fathers Mehujael. And Mehujael fathers Methushael. And Methushael fathers Lamech.
And Lamech takes two wives. The name of the one is Adah, and the name of the other is Zillah.
Adah bears Jabal — he is the father of those who dwell in tents and have livestock.
And his brother’s name is Jubal — he is the father of those who play the lyre and the pipe.
Zillah also bears Tubal-cain, the forger of every cutting instrument of bronze and iron. And the sister of Tubal-cain is Naamah.
And Lamech says to his wives:
“Adah and Zillah — hear my voice,
wives of Lamech — listen to what I say.
I kill a man for wounding me,
a young man for striking me.
If Cain is avenged sevenfold,
then Lamech seventy-sevenfold.”
And Adam knows his wife again. And she bears a son and calls his name Seth, saying, “God has appointed for me another offspring in place of Abel, for Cain killed him.”
And to Seth also a son is born. He calls his name Enosh. At that time people begin to call on the name of YHWH.
This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day that God creates the human, in the likeness of God he makes him.
Male and female he creates them. And he blesses them and calls their name ‘Human’ in the day they are created.

Adam is 130 years old when he fathers a son in his own likeness, after his image, and names him Seth. After Seth’s birth, Adam lives 800 years and has other sons and daughters. Adam lives 930 years in all. Then he dies.
Seth is 105 years old when he fathers Enosh. After Enosh’s birth, Seth lives 807 years and has other sons and daughters. Seth lives 912 years in all. Then he dies.
Enosh is 90 years old when he fathers Kenan. After Kenan’s birth, Enosh lives 815 years and has other sons and daughters. Enosh lives 905 years in all. Then he dies.
Kenan is 70 years old when he fathers Mahalaleel. After Mahalaleel’s birth, Kenan lives 840 years and has other sons and daughters. Kenan lives 910 years in all. Then he dies.
Mahalaleel is 65 years old when he fathers Jared. After Jared’s birth, Mahalaleel lives 830 years and has other sons and daughters. Mahalaleel lives 895 years in all. Then he dies.
Jared is 162 years old when he fathers Enoch. After Enoch’s birth, Jared lives 800 years and has other sons and daughters. Jared lives 962 years in all. Then he dies.

Enoch is 65 years old when he fathers Methuselah. After Methuselah’s birth, Enoch walks with God 300 years and has other sons and daughters. Enoch lives 365 years in all. Enoch walks with God — and then he is gone, for God takes him.
Methuselah is 187 years old when he fathers Lamech. After Lamech’s birth, Methuselah lives 782 years and has other sons and daughters. Methuselah lives 969 years in all. Then he dies.

Lamech is 182 years old when he fathers a son and calls his name Noah, saying, “This one will bring us relief from our work and from the painful toil of our hands, from the ground that YHWH has cursed.” After Noah’s birth, Lamech lives 595 years and has other sons and daughters. Lamech lives 777 years in all. Then he dies.
After Noah is 500 years old, Noah fathers Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
And it happens, when humanity begins to multiply on the face of the ground and daughters are born to them,
that the sons of God see that the daughters of humanity are beautiful. And they take as wives any they choose.
And YHWH says, “My Spirit shall not contend with humanity forever, since he is flesh. His days shall be 120 years.”

The Nephilim are on the earth in those days — and also afterward — when the sons of God come in to the daughters of humanity and they bear children to them. These are the mighty ones who were of old, the men of renown.
And YHWH sees that the wickedness of humanity is great on the earth, and that every inclination of the thoughts of his heart is only evil all the day.
And YHWH regrets that he has made humanity on the earth, and it grieves him to his heart.
“I will blot out the human that I have created from the face of the ground — human and animal and creeping thing and bird of the sky — for I regret that I have made them.”
But Noah finds favor in the eyes of YHWH.
These are the generations of Noah. Noah is a righteous man, blameless in his generation. Noah walks with God.
And Noah fathers three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
Now the earth is corrupt before God, and the earth is filled with violence.
And God looks on the earth, and look — it is corrupt. For all flesh has corrupted their way on the earth.
And God says to Noah, “The end of all flesh has come before me — for the earth is filled with violence because of them. Look — I am about to destroy them with the earth.
Make yourself an ark of gopher wood. Make rooms in the ark and cover it inside and out with pitch.
This is how you shall make it: the length of the ark 300 cubits, its breadth 50 cubits, and its height 30 cubits.
Make a window for the ark and finish it to a cubit above. Set the door of the ark in its side. Make it with lower, second, and third decks.
For look — I am bringing a flood of waters upon the earth to destroy all flesh under the sky in which there is the breath of life. Everything that is on the earth shall die.
But I will establish my covenant with you. And you shall come into the ark — you and your sons and your wife and your sons’ wives with you.
And of every living thing of all flesh, you shall bring two of every kind into the ark to keep them alive with you. They shall be male and female.
Of the birds according to their kinds, and of the animals according to their kinds, of every creeping thing of the ground according to its kind — two of every kind shall come to you to be kept alive.
Also take with you every sort of food that is eaten and store it up. It shall serve as food for you and for them.”
And Noah does this. According to everything God commands him — so he does.
And YHWH says to Noah, “Go into the ark — you and all your household. For I have seen that you are righteous before me in this generation.
Take with you seven pairs — a male and its mate — of every clean animal, and a pair — a male and its mate — of every animal that is not clean,
and seven pairs of the birds of the sky also, male and female, to keep their offspring alive on the face of all the earth.
For in seven days I will send rain on the earth, forty days and forty nights. And every living thing I have made I will blot out from the face of the ground.”
And Noah does everything YHWH commands him.
Noah is six hundred years old when the flood of waters comes on the earth.
And Noah and his sons and his wife and his sons’ wives go into the ark ahead of the waters of the flood.
Of clean animals, and of animals that are not clean, and of birds, and of everything that creeps on the ground,
two by two they go into the ark with Noah — male and female, as God has commanded Noah.
And after seven days the waters of the flood come on the earth.

In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life, in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month — on that very day all the fountains of the great deep burst open, and the windows of the sky are opened.
And the rain falls on the earth forty days and forty nights.
On that very same day Noah and Shem and Ham and Japheth, the sons of Noah, and Noah’s wife and the three wives of his sons with them go into the ark —

they and every beast according to its kind, and all the livestock according to their kind, and every creeping thing that creeps on the earth according to its kind, and every bird according to its kind, every winged thing of every sort.
They come to Noah into the ark, two by two of all flesh in which there is the breath of life.
And those that come, male and female of all flesh, come as God commanded him. And YHWH shuts him in.
The flood is forty days on the earth. The waters increase and lift up the ark, and it rises above the earth.
The waters surge and increase greatly on the earth, and the ark floats on the face of the waters.
And the waters rise more and more over the earth, covering all the high mountains under the whole sky.
The waters rise fifteen cubits above the mountains, covering them.
And all flesh that moves on the earth perishes — birds, livestock, wild animals, all swarming creatures that swarm on the earth, and all humanity.
Everything on dry land in whose nostrils was the breath of life — it dies.

And every living thing on the face of the ground is blotted out — human and animal and creeping thing and bird of the sky. They are blotted out from the earth. Only Noah is left, and those with him in the ark.
And the waters have power over the earth for a hundred and fifty days.
And God remembers Noah and all the wild animals and all the livestock that are with him in the ark. And God makes a wind pass over the earth — and the waters subside.
The fountains of the deep and the windows of the sky are closed. The rain from the sky is restrained.
And the waters recede from the earth steadily. By the end of a hundred and fifty days the waters had diminished.
And in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, the ark comes to rest on the mountains of Ararat.
And the waters continue to decrease until the tenth month. In the tenth month, on the first day of the month, the tops of the mountains become visible.
And it happens at the end of forty days that Noah opens the window of the ark that he has made
and sends out a raven. It goes out, going back and forth, until the waters dry up from the earth.
Then he sends out a dove from him, to see whether the waters have receded from the face of the ground.

But the dove finds no resting place for the sole of her foot, and she returns to him into the ark — for the waters are still on the face of all the earth. And he reaches out his hand and takes her and brings her in to himself into the ark.
He waits another seven days and again sends the dove out from the ark.
And the dove comes back to him in the evening, and look — a freshly plucked olive leaf is in her mouth. And Noah knows that the waters have receded from the earth.
Then he waits another seven days and sends out the dove, and she does not return to him anymore.

In the six hundred and first year, in the first month, on the first day of the month, the waters are dried up from the earth. And Noah removes the covering of the ark and looks — and look, the face of the ground is dry.
In the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, the earth is dry.
And God speaks to Noah:
“Go out from the ark — you and your wife and your sons and your sons’ wives with you.

Bring out with you every living thing that is with you of all flesh — birds and animals and every creeping thing that creeps on the earth — so they can swarm on the earth and be fruitful and multiply on the earth.”
So Noah goes out, and his sons and his wife and his sons’ wives with him.
And every beast, every creeping thing, and every bird — everything that moves on the earth — goes out from the ark by families.
And Noah builds an altar to YHWH and takes some of every clean animal and some of every clean bird and offers burnt offerings on the altar.

And YHWH smells the pleasing aroma. And YHWH says in his heart, “I will never again curse the ground because of the human, for the inclination of the human heart is evil from youth. And I will never again strike down every living creature as I have done.
While the earth remains, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night — they shall not cease.”
And God blesses Noah and his sons and says to them, “Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth.

The fear and dread of you will fall on every animal of the earth and every bird of the sky, on every creature that moves along the ground, and on all the fish of the sea. Into your hand they are given.
Every moving thing that lives shall be food for you. Just as I gave you the green plants, I now give you everything.
But you must not eat flesh with its life — that is, its blood — still in it.
And for your lifeblood I will require a reckoning: from every animal I will require it, and from each human being I will require a reckoning for the life of another human being.
“Whoever sheds the blood of a human,
by a human shall his blood be shed —
for in the image of God he made the human.
And you — be fruitful and multiply, swarm on the earth and multiply in it.”
And God says to Noah and to his sons with him:
“Look — I am establishing my covenant with you and with your offspring after you,
and with every living creature that is with you — birds, livestock, and every wild animal with you — every living creature that came out of the ark.
I establish my covenant with you: never again shall all flesh be cut off by the waters of a flood, and never again shall there be a flood to destroy the earth.”
“This is the sign of the covenant I am making between me and you and every living creature that is with you, for all future generations.
I have set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be a sign of the covenant between me and the earth.
When I bring clouds over the earth and the bow is seen in the cloud,
I will remember my covenant that is between me and you and every living creature of all flesh. And the waters shall never again become a flood to destroy all flesh.
When the bow is in the cloud, I will see it and remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh that is on the earth.”
And God says to Noah, “This is the sign of the covenant that I have established between me and all flesh that is on the earth.”
The sons of Noah who went out from the ark are Shem, Ham, and Japheth. (Ham is the father of Canaan.)
These three are the sons of Noah. And from them the whole earth is populated.
Noah, a man of the soil, begins and plants a vineyard.
And he drinks of the wine and becomes drunk and lies uncovered in his tent.
And Ham, the father of Canaan, sees the nakedness of his father and tells his two brothers outside.

Then Shem and Japheth take a garment, lay it over both their shoulders, and walk backward and cover the nakedness of their father. Their faces are turned away, and they do not see their father’s nakedness.
When Noah wakes from his wine and finds out what his youngest son has done to him,
he says:
“Cursed be Canaan —
the lowest of slaves shall he be
to his brothers.”
He also says:
“Blessed be YHWH, the God of Shem —
and let Canaan be his slave.
May God enlarge Japheth,
and let him dwell in the tents of Shem —
and let Canaan be his slave.”
After the flood, Noah lives 350 years.
And all the days of Noah are 950 years. Then he dies.
These are the generations of the sons of Noah — Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Sons are born to them after the flood.
The sons of Japheth: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
The sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
The sons of Javan: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
From these the coastland peoples spread in their lands, each with his own language, by their clans, in their nations.
The sons of Ham: Cush, Egypt, Put, and Canaan.
The sons of Cush: Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. The sons of Raamah: Sheba and Dedan.
And Cush fathers Nimrod. He is the first on earth to become a mighty warrior.
He is a mighty hunter before YHWH — that is why it is said, ‘Like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before YHWH.’
The beginning of his kingdom is Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.
From that land he goes out into Assyria and builds Nineveh, Rehoboth-Ir, Calah,
and Resen between Nineveh and Calah — that is the great city.
Egypt fathers Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim,
Pathrusim, Casluhim (from whom the Philistines come), and Caphtorim.
Canaan fathers Sidon his firstborn, and Heth,
and the Jebusites, the Amorites, the Girgashites,
the Hivites, the Arkites, the Sinites,
the Arvadites, the Zemarites, and the Hamathites. Afterward the clans of the Canaanites spread abroad.
And the territory of the Canaanites extends from Sidon in the direction of Gerar as far as Gaza, and in the direction of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, as far as Lasha.
These are the sons of Ham, by their clans, their languages, their lands, and their nations.
To Shem also, the father of all the children of Eber, the elder brother of Japheth, children are born.
The sons of Shem: Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, and Aram.
The sons of Aram: Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash.
Arpachshad fathers Shelah, and Shelah fathers Eber.
To Eber are born two sons: the name of the one is Peleg, for in his days the earth is divided. And his brother’s name is Joktan.
Joktan fathers Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,
Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,
Obal, Abimael, Sheba,
Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these are the sons of Joktan.
The territory they live in extends from Mesha in the direction of Sephar, the hill country of the east.
These are the sons of Shem, by their clans, their languages, their lands, and their nations.
These are the clans of the sons of Noah, according to their genealogies, in their nations. And from these the nations spread abroad on the earth after the flood.
Now the whole earth has one language and the same words.
And as people migrate from the east, they find a plain in the land of Shinar and settle there.
And they say to one another, “Come — let us make bricks and fire them thoroughly.” And they use brick for stone and bitumen for mortar.
And they say, “Come — let us build ourselves a city and a tower with its top in the heavens, and let us make a name for ourselves, lest we be scattered over the face of the whole earth.”
And YHWH comes down to see the city and the tower that the children of humanity had built.
And YHWH says, “Look — they are one people with one language, and this is only the beginning of what they will do. And now nothing they plan to do will be impossible for them.
Come — let us go down and confuse their language there, so that they will not understand one another’s speech.”
And YHWH scatters them from there over the face of all the earth. And they stop building the city.
Therefore its name is called Babel — because there YHWH confused the language of all the earth. And from there YHWH scatters them over the face of all the earth.
These are the generations of Shem. When Shem is 100 years old, two years after the flood, he fathers Arpachshad.
After Arpachshad’s birth, Shem lives 500 years and has other sons and daughters.
Arpachshad is 35 years old when he fathers Shelah. After Shelah’s birth, Arpachshad lives 403 years and has other sons and daughters.
Shelah is 30 years old when he fathers Eber. After Eber’s birth, Shelah lives 403 years and has other sons and daughters.
Eber is 34 years old when he fathers Peleg. After Peleg’s birth, Eber lives 430 years and has other sons and daughters.
Peleg is 30 years old when he fathers Reu. After Reu’s birth, Peleg lives 209 years and has other sons and daughters.
Reu is 32 years old when he fathers Serug. After Serug’s birth, Reu lives 207 years and has other sons and daughters.
Serug is 30 years old when he fathers Nahor. After Nahor’s birth, Serug lives 200 years and has other sons and daughters.
Nahor is 29 years old when he fathers Terah. After Terah’s birth, Nahor lives 119 years and has other sons and daughters.
Terah is 70 years old when he fathers Abram, Nahor, and Haran.
Now these are the generations of Terah. Terah fathers Abram, Nahor, and Haran. And Haran fathers Lot.
Haran dies in the presence of his father Terah in the land of his birth, in Ur of the Chaldeans.
And Abram and Nahor take wives. The name of Abram’s wife is Sarai, and the name of Nahor’s wife is Milcah, the daughter of Haran the father of Milcah and the father of Iscah.
Now Sarai is barren — she has no child.

And Terah takes Abram his son and Lot the son of Haran, his grandson, and Sarai his daughter-in-law, the wife of his son Abram. And they go out together from Ur of the Chaldeans to go to the land of Canaan. But when they come to Haran, they settle there.
The days of Terah are 205 years, and Terah dies in Haran.
And YHWH says to Abram:
“Go from your land
and from your kindred
and from your father’s house
to the land that I will show you.
And I will make you into a great nation.
And I will bless you
and make your name great.
And you shall be a blessing.
I will bless those who bless you,
and the one who curses you I will curse.
And in you all the families of the earth
shall be blessed.”
So Abram goes, as YHWH has told him. And Lot goes with him. Abram is seventy-five years old when he departs from Haran.

And Abram takes Sarai his wife, and Lot his brother’s son, and all their possessions that they have gathered, and the people they have acquired in Haran. And they set out to go to the land of Canaan. And they come to the land of Canaan.
And Abram passes through the land to the place at Shechem, to the oak of Moreh. At that time the Canaanites are in the land.
And YHWH appears to Abram and says, “To your offspring I will give this land.” And he builds there an altar to YHWH, who had appeared to him.
And from there he moves to the hill country on the east of Bethel and pitches his tent — Bethel on the west and Ai on the east. And he builds there an altar to YHWH and calls on the name of YHWH.
And Abram journeys on, going on toward the Negeb.
And there is a famine in the land. So Abram goes down to Egypt to sojourn there, for the famine is severe in the land.
And when he is about to enter Egypt, he says to Sarai his wife, “Look — I know that you are a woman beautiful in appearance.
And when the Egyptians see you, they will say, ‘This is his wife.’ Then they will kill me, but they will let you live.
Say you are my sister, so that it may go well with me because of you, and that my life may be spared for your sake.”
And when Abram enters Egypt, the Egyptians see that the woman is very beautiful.
And the princes of Pharaoh see her and praise her to Pharaoh. And the woman is taken into Pharaoh’s house.
And it goes well with Abram because of her. He acquires sheep, oxen, male donkeys, male servants, female servants, female donkeys, and camels.
But YHWH strikes Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai, Abram’s wife.
So Pharaoh calls Abram and says, “What is this you have done to me? Why did you not tell me she was your wife?
Why did you say, ‘She is my sister,’ so that I took her for my wife? Now then — here is your wife. Take her and go.”
And Pharaoh gives men orders concerning him, and they escort him away — along with his wife and everything he has.
So Abram goes up from Egypt — he and his wife and everything he has, and Lot with him — into the Negeb.
And Abram is very rich in livestock, in silver, and in gold.
And he journeys on from the Negeb, going stage by stage, to Bethel — to the place where his tent had been at the beginning, between Bethel and Ai,
to the place where he had made the altar at first. And there Abram calls on the name of YHWH.
And Lot, who was traveling with Abram, also has flocks and herds and tents.
And the land cannot support them both dwelling together — their possessions are so great that they cannot dwell together.
And there is strife between the herdsmen of Abram’s livestock and the herdsmen of Lot’s livestock. At that time the Canaanites and the Perizzites are dwelling in the land.
Then Abram says to Lot, “Let there be no strife between me and you, and between my herdsmen and your herdsmen — for we are brothers.
Is not the whole land before you? Separate yourself from me. If you go to the left, I will go to the right. If you go to the right, I will go to the left.”

And Lot lifts up his eyes and sees that the whole plain of the Jordan is well watered everywhere — like the garden of YHWH, like the land of Egypt — in the direction of Zoar. This is before YHWH had destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.
So Lot chooses for himself the whole plain of the Jordan and journeys east. And they separate from each other.
Abram settles in the land of Canaan, and Lot settles among the cities of the plain and moves his tent as far as Sodom.
Now the men of Sodom are wicked — great sinners against YHWH.
And YHWH says to Abram, after Lot has separated from him:
“Lift up your eyes and look from the place where you are —
northward and southward and eastward and westward.
For all the land that you see I will give to you
and to your offspring forever.
I will make your offspring as the dust of the earth —
so that if one can count the dust of the earth,
your offspring also can be counted.
Arise, walk through the length and breadth of the land —
for I will give it to you.”
So Abram moves his tent and comes and dwells by the oaks of Mamre, which are at Hebron. And he builds there an altar to YHWH.
In the days of Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goiim,
these kings make war with Bera king of Sodom, Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela (that is, Zoar).
All these join forces in the Valley of Siddim — that is, the Salt Sea.
For twelve years they have served Chedorlaomer, and in the thirteenth year they rebel.
In the fourteenth year Chedorlaomer and the kings who are with him come and strike the Rephaim in Ashteroth-karnaim, the Zuzim in Ham, the Emim in Shaveh-kiriathaim,
and the Horites in their hill country of Seir as far as El-paran on the edge of the wilderness.
Then they turn back and come to En-mishpat (that is, Kadesh) and strike all the country of the Amalekites and also the Amorites who were living in Hazazon-tamar.
Then the king of Sodom, the king of Gomorrah, the king of Admah, the king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela (that is, Zoar) go out. And they join battle in the Valley of Siddim
with Chedorlaomer king of Elam, Tidal king of Goiim, Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar — four kings against five.
Now the Valley of Siddim is full of bitumen pits, and as the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah flee, some fall into them, and the rest flee to the hill country.
So the enemy takes all the possessions of Sodom and Gomorrah and all their food, and they go.
They also take Lot, the son of Abram’s brother, who was dwelling in Sodom, and his possessions, and go.
Then a fugitive comes and tells Abram the Hebrew — who is living by the oaks of Mamre the Amorite, brother of Eshcol and of Aner. These are allies of Abram.
When Abram hears that his kinsman has been taken captive, he leads out his trained men, born in his house — three hundred and eighteen of them — and goes in pursuit as far as Dan.
And he divides against them by night — he and his servants — and strikes them and pursues them as far as Hobah, which is north of Damascus.
Then he brings back all the possessions and also brings back his kinsman Lot with his possessions — as well as the women and the rest of the people.
After his return from the defeat of Chedorlaomer and the kings who were with him, the king of Sodom goes out to meet him at the Valley of Shaveh — that is, the Valley of the King.
And Melchizedek king of Salem brings out bread and wine. He is a priest of God Most High.
And he blesses him and says:
“Blessed be Abram by God Most High,
creator of heaven and earth.
And blessed be God Most High,
who has delivered your enemies into your hand.”
And Abram gives him a tenth of everything.
And the king of Sodom says to Abram, “Give me the people, and take the possessions for yourself.”
But Abram says to the king of Sodom, “I have lifted my hand to YHWH, God Most High, creator of heaven and earth,
that I would not take a thread or a sandal strap or anything that is yours, lest you should say, ‘I have made Abram rich.’
I will take nothing but what the young men have eaten, and the share of the men who went with me — Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre. Let them take their share.”
After these things the word of YHWH comes to Abram in a vision:
“Don’t be afraid, Abram.
I am your shield.
Your reward shall be very great.”
“Lord YHWH,” Abram says, “what will you give me? For I am going childless, and the heir of my house is this Eliezer of Damascus.”
And Abram says, “Look — you have given me no offspring. And a member of my household will be my heir.”
And look — the word of YHWH comes to him: “This man shall not be your heir. Your very own son shall be your heir.”
And he brings him outside and says, “Look toward the sky and count the stars, if you are able to count them.”
And he says to him, “So shall your offspring be.”
And he believes YHWH, and he counts it to him as righteousness.
And he says to him, “I am YHWH who brought you out from Ur of the Chaldeans to give you this land to possess it.”
“Lord YHWH,” he says, “how am I to know that I shall possess it?”
“Bring me a heifer three years old, a female goat three years old, a ram three years old, a turtledove, and a young pigeon,” he says to him.
And he brings him all these, cuts them in half, and lays each half over against the other. But he does not cut the birds in half.
And when birds of prey come down on the carcasses, Abram drives them away.
As the sun is going down, a deep sleep falls on Abram. And look — a dread and a great darkness falls upon him.
And YHWH says to Abram, “Know for certain that your offspring will be sojourners in a land that is not theirs, and will be servants there, and they will be afflicted for four hundred years.
But I will bring judgment on the nation they serve, and afterward they shall come out with great possessions.
As for you — you shall go to your fathers in peace. You shall be buried in a good old age.
And they shall come back here in the fourth generation — for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet complete.”
When the sun has gone down and it is dark, look — a smoking fire pot and a flaming torch pass between the pieces.
On that day YHWH cuts a covenant with Abram, saying,
“To your offspring I give this land —
from the river of Egypt
to the great river, the river Euphrates:
the land of the Kenites, the Kenizzites, the Kadmonites,
the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Rephaim,
the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Girgashites, and the Jebusites.”
Now Sarai, Abram’s wife, has borne him no children. She has an Egyptian servant whose name is Hagar.
And Sarai says to Abram, “Look — YHWH has kept me from bearing children. Go in to my servant — perhaps I shall be built up through her.”
And Abram listens to the voice of Sarai.
So Sarai, Abram’s wife, takes Hagar the Egyptian, her servant, and gives her to Abram her husband as a wife — after Abram had lived ten years in the land of Canaan.
And he goes in to Hagar, and she conceives. And when she sees that she has conceived, her mistress becomes contemptible in her eyes.

And Sarai says to Abram, “May the wrong done to me be on you! I gave my servant to your arms, and when she saw that she had conceived, I became contemptible in her eyes. May YHWH judge between me and you.”
“Look — your servant is in your hands,” Abram says to Sarai. “Do to her as you please.”
And Sarai treats her harshly, and she flees from her face.
And the angel of YHWH finds her by a spring of water in the wilderness — by the spring on the road to Shur.
“Hagar, servant of Sarai — where have you come from and where are you going?” he says.
“I am fleeing from the face of my mistress Sarai,” she says.
“Return to your mistress,” the angel of YHWH says to her, “and submit yourself under her hands.”
And the angel of YHWH says to her:
“I will surely multiply your offspring
so that they cannot be numbered for multitude.”
And the angel of YHWH says to her:
“Look — you are pregnant and shall bear a son.
You shall call his name Ishmael —
for YHWH has heard your affliction.
He shall be a wild donkey of a man,
his hand against everyone
and everyone’s hand against him.
And he shall dwell over against all his brothers.”
So she calls the name of YHWH who spoke to her: “You are El-roi” — for she says, “Have I truly seen here the one who sees me?”
Therefore the well is called Beer-lahai-roi. It is between Kadesh and Bered.
And Hagar bears Abram a son, and Abram calls the name of his son, whom Hagar bore, Ishmael.
Abram is eighty-six years old when Hagar bears Ishmael to Abram.
And when Abram is ninety-nine years old, YHWH appears to Abram and says to him, “I am El Shaddai. Walk before me and be blameless,
and I will make my covenant between me and you, and will multiply you greatly.”
Then Abram falls on his face, and God speaks with him:
“As for me — look, my covenant is with you, and you shall be the father of a multitude of nations.
No longer shall your name be called Abram, but your name shall be Abraham. For I have made you the father of a multitude of nations.
I will make you exceedingly fruitful, and I will make you into nations, and kings shall come from you.
And I will establish my covenant between me and you and your offspring after you throughout their generations, as an everlasting covenant — to be God to you and to your offspring after you.
And I will give to you and to your offspring after you the land of your sojournings, all the land of Canaan, for an everlasting possession. And I will be their God.”
And God says to Abraham, “As for you — you shall keep my covenant, you and your offspring after you throughout their generations.
This is my covenant which you shall keep, between me and you and your offspring after you: every male among you shall be circumcised.
You shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin, and it shall be a sign of the covenant between me and you.
He who is eight days old among you shall be circumcised — every male throughout your generations, whether born in your house or bought with your money from any foreigner who is not of your offspring.
Both he who is born in your house and he who is bought with your money shall surely be circumcised. So shall my covenant be in your flesh an everlasting covenant.
Any uncircumcised male who is not circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin shall be cut off from his people — he has broken my covenant.”
And God says to Abraham, “As for Sarai your wife — you shall not call her name Sarai, for Sarah shall be her name.
I will bless her, and moreover I will give you a son by her. I will bless her, and she shall become nations — kings of peoples shall come from her.”
Then Abraham falls on his face and laughs, and says in his heart, “Shall a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old? Shall Sarah, who is ninety years old, bear a child?”
And Abraham says to God, “Oh that Ishmael might live before you!”
“No — Sarah your wife shall bear you a son, and you shall call his name Isaac,” God says. “AndI will establish my covenant with him as an everlasting covenant for his offspring after him.
As for Ishmael — I have heard you. Look, I will bless him and make him fruitful and multiply him greatly. He shall father twelve princes, and I will make him into a great nation.
But my covenant I will establish with Isaac, whom Sarah shall bear to you at this time next year.”
When he finishes talking with him, God goes up from Abraham.

Then Abraham takes Ishmael his son and all those born in his house or bought with his money — every male among the men of Abraham’s house — and circumcises the flesh of their foreskins that very day, as God has said to him.
Abraham is ninety-nine years old when he is circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.
And Ishmael his son is thirteen years old when he is circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.
That very day Abraham and his son Ishmael are circumcised.
And all the men of his house — those born in the house and those bought with money from a foreigner — are circumcised with him.
And YHWH appears to him by the oaks of Mamre, while he is sitting at the entrance of his tent in the heat of the day.
He lifts up his eyes and looks — and look, three men are standing in front of him. When he sees them, he runs from the entrance of his tent to meet them and bows himself to the earth
and says, “My lord — if I have found favour in your sight, do not pass by your servant.
Let a little water be brought, and wash your feet, and rest yourselves under the tree.
And let me bring a piece of bread, that you may refresh yourselves — and after that you may pass on, since you have come to your servant.”
“Do as you have said,” they say.
And Abraham hurries into the tent to Sarah and says, “Quick — three measures of fine flour! Knead it and make cakes.”
And Abraham runs to the herd and takes a calf — tender and good — and gives it to a young man, who hurries to prepare it.
Then he takes curds and milk and the calf that he has prepared and sets it before them. And he stands beside them under the tree while they eat.
“Where is Sarah your wife?” they say to him.
“She is there — in the tent,” he says.
“I will surely return to you about this time next year,” he says, “and Sarah your wife shall have a son.”
Now Sarah is listening at the entrance of the tent, which is behind him.
And Abraham and Sarah are old, well advanced in years. Sarah has passed the way of women.
So Sarah laughs to herself, saying, “After I am worn out and my lord is old — shall I have pleasure?”
“Why did Sarah laugh?” YHWH says to Abraham. “Saying, ‘Shall I indeed bear a child, now that I am old?’
Is anything too hard for YHWH? At the appointed time I will return to you, about this time next year, and Sarah shall have a son.”
But Sarah denies it: “I did not laugh.”
For she is afraid.
“No — you did laugh,” he says.
Then the men set out from there and look down toward Sodom. And Abraham walks with them to see them off.
And YHWH says, “Shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do,
seeing that Abraham shall surely become a great and mighty nation, and all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in him?

For I have chosen him, so that he may command his children and his household after him to keep the way of YHWH by doing righteousness and justice, so that YHWH may bring to Abraham what he has promised him.”
Then YHWH says, “The outcry of Sodom and Gomorrah is very great, and their sin is very grave.
I will go down and see whether they have done altogether according to the outcry that has come to me. And if not, I will know.”
So the men turn from there and go toward Sodom. But Abraham still stands before YHWH.
Then Abraham draws near and says, “Will you really sweep away the righteous with the wicked?
What if there are fifty righteous within the city? Will you really sweep it away and not spare the place for the fifty righteous who are in it?

Far be it from you to do such a thing — to put the righteous to death with the wicked, so that the righteous fare as the wicked! Far be it from you! Shall not the Judge of all the earth do what is just?”
“If I find at Sodom fifty righteous in the city,” YHWH says, “I will spare the whole place for their sake.”
Abraham answers: “Look — I have undertaken to speak to the Lord, I who am but dust and ashes.
What if five are lacking from the fifty righteous? Will you destroy the whole city for lack of five?”
“I will not destroy it if I find forty-five there,” he says.
Again he speaks to him: “What if forty are found there?”
“I will not do it for the sake of forty,” he says.
“Oh let not the Lord be angry, and I will speak. What if thirty are found there?”
“I will not do it if I find thirty there,” he says.
He says, “Look — I have undertaken to speak to the Lord. What if twenty are found there?”
“I will not destroy it for the sake of twenty,” he says.
Then he says, “Oh let not the Lord be angry, and I will speak just this once. What if ten are found there?”
“I will not destroy it for the sake of ten,” he says.
And YHWH goes his way, when he has finished speaking to Abraham. And Abraham returns to his place.
The two angels come to Sodom in the evening, and Lot is sitting in the gate of Sodom. When Lot sees them, he rises to meet them and bows himself with his face to the earth
and says, “My lords, please turn aside to your servant’s house and spend the night and wash your feet. Then you may rise early and go on your way.”
“No,” they say, “we will spend the night in the town square.”
But he presses them strongly. And they turn aside to him and enter his house. And he makes them a feast and bakes unleavened bread, and they eat.
Before they lie down, the men of the city — the men of Sodom, both young and old, all the people to the last man — surround the house.
And they call to Lot, “Where are the men who came to you tonight? Bring them out to us, that we may know them.”
Lot goes out to them at the entrance, shuts the door behind him,
and says, “I beg you, my brothers, do not act so wickedly.
Look — I have two daughters who have not known any man. Let me bring them out to you, and do to them as you please. Only do nothing to these men, for they have come under the shelter of my roof.”

“Stand back!” they say. And they say, “This fellow came to sojourn, and now he would play the judge! We will deal worse with you than with them.” And they press hard against Lot and draw near to break down the door.
But the men reach out their hands and bring Lot into the house with them and shut the door.
And they strike the men at the entrance of the house with blindness, both small and great, so that they wear themselves out trying to find the door.
Then the men say to Lot, “Have you anyone else here? A son-in-law, your sons, your daughters, or anyone you have in the city — bring them out of the place.
For we are about to destroy this place, because the outcry against its people has become great before YHWH, and YHWH has sent us to destroy it.”

So Lot goes out and says to his sons-in-law, who were pledged to marry his daughters, “Get up, get out of this place! For YHWH is about to destroy the city.” But he seems to his sons-in-law to be jesting.
When morning dawns, the angels urge Lot, saying, “Get up, take your wife and your two daughters who are here, lest you be swept away in the punishment of the city.”
But he lingers. So the men take hold of his hand and the hand of his wife and the hands of his two daughters — YHWH being merciful to him — and they bring him out and set him outside the city.
And as they bring them out, one says, “Flee for your life. Do not look behind you or stop anywhere in the valley. Flee to the hills, lest you be swept away.”
“Oh no, my lords,” Lot says to them.
“Your servant has found favour in your sight, and you have shown me great kindness in saving my life. But I cannot flee to the hills, lest the disaster overtake me and I die.
Look — this city is near enough to flee to, and it is a little one. Let me escape there — is it not a little one? — and my life will be saved.”
“Be assured,” he says to him, “I grant you this favour too, and I will not overthrow the city of which you have spoken.
Escape there quickly, for I can do nothing until you arrive there.” Therefore the name of the city is called Zoar.
The sun has risen over the earth when Lot arrives at Zoar.
Then YHWH rains on Sodom and Gomorrah sulfur and fire from YHWH out of heaven.
And he overthrows those cities and all the valley, and all the inhabitants of the cities and what grows on the ground.
But Lot’s wife looks back behind him — and she becomes a pillar of salt.
And Abraham goes early in the morning to the place where he had stood before YHWH.
And he looks down toward Sodom and Gomorrah and toward all the land of the valley — and look, the smoke of the land goes up like the smoke of a furnace.
So it is that when God destroys the cities of the valley, God remembers Abraham and sends Lot out of the midst of the overthrow when he overthrows the cities in which Lot had lived.
Now Lot goes up from Zoar and settles in the hills with his two daughters, for he is afraid to live in Zoar. So he lives in a cave with his two daughters.
And the firstborn says to the younger, “Our father is old, and there is not a man on earth to come in to us after the manner of all the earth.
Come, let us make our father drink wine, and we will lie with him, that we may preserve offspring from our father.”
So they make their father drink wine that night. And the firstborn goes in and lies with her father. He does not know when she lies down or when she rises.

The next day, the firstborn says to the younger, “Look, I lay with my father last night. Let us make him drink wine tonight also. Then you go in and lie with him, that we may preserve offspring from our father.”
So they make their father drink wine that night also. And the younger rises and lies with him, and he does not know when she lies down or when she rises.
Thus both the daughters of Lot become pregnant by their father.
The firstborn bears a son and calls his name Moab. He is the father of the Moabites to this day.
The younger also bears a son and calls his name Ben-ammi. He is the father of the Ammonites to this day.
From there Abraham journeys toward the territory of the Negeb and settles between Kadesh and Shur. And he sojourns in Gerar.
And Abraham says of Sarah his wife, “She is my sister.” And Abimelech king of Gerar sends and takes Sarah.
But God comes to Abimelech in a dream at night and says to him, “Look — you are a dead man because of the woman you have taken, for she is a man’s wife.”
Now Abimelech has not come near her. So he says, “Lord, will you kill an innocent people?
Did he not himself say to me, ‘She is my sister’? And she herself said, ‘He is my brother.’ In the integrity of my heart and the innocence of my hands I have done this.”
“Yes, I know that in the integrity of your heart you have done this,” God says to him in the dream, “and it was I who kept you from sinning against me. Therefore I did not let you touch her.
Now then — return the man’s wife, for he is a prophet and he will pray for you, and you shall live. But if you do not return her — know that you shall surely die, you and all who are yours.”
So Abimelech rises early in the morning and calls all his servants and tells them all these things. And the men are very much afraid.

Then Abimelech calls Abraham and says to him, “What have you done to us? And how have I sinned against you, that you have brought on me and my kingdom a great sin? You have done to me things that ought not to be done.”
And Abimelech says to Abraham, “What did you see, that you did this thing?”
“Abraham says, “I did it because I thought, ‘There is no fear of God at all in this place, and they will kill me because of my wife.’
Besides, she really is my sister — the daughter of my father though not the daughter of my mother — and she became my wife.
And when God caused me to wander from my father’s house, I said to her, ‘This is the kindness you must do me: at every place we come to, say of me, “He is my brother.”’”
And Abimelech takes sheep and oxen and male servants and female servants and gives them to Abraham, and returns Sarah his wife to him.
And Abimelech says, “Look — my land is before you. Settle wherever is good in your sight.”
To Sarah he says, “Look — I have given your brother a thousand pieces of silver. It is a covering of the eyes for you before all who are with you. Before everyone you are fully vindicated.”
Then Abraham prays to God, and God heals Abimelech and also heals his wife and his female servants so that they bear children.
For YHWH had completely closed all the wombs of the house of Abimelech because of Sarah, Abraham’s wife.
And YHWH visits Sarah as he had said, and YHWH does to Sarah as he had promised.
And Sarah conceives and bears Abraham a son in his old age — at the appointed time of which God had spoken to him.
And Abraham calls the name of his son who is born to him, whom Sarah bears him, Isaac.
And Abraham circumcises his son Isaac when he is eight days old, as God has commanded him.
Abraham is a hundred years old when his son Isaac is born to him.
And Sarah says, “God has made laughter for me. Everyone who hears will laugh with me.”
And she says, “Who would have said to Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? Yet I have borne him a son in his old age.”
And the child grows and is weaned. And Abraham makes a great feast on the day that Isaac is weaned.
But Sarah sees the son of Hagar the Egyptian, whom she had borne to Abraham, laughing.
So she says to Abraham, “Cast out this slave woman with her son! For the son of this slave woman shall not be heir with my son Isaac.”
And the thing is very displeasing to Abraham on account of his son.
But God says to Abraham, “Do not be distressed over the boy or over your slave woman. Whatever Sarah says to you, listen to her voice, for through Isaac shall your offspring be named.
And I will also make a nation of the son of the slave woman, because he is your offspring.”

So Abraham rises early in the morning and takes bread and a skin of water and gives it to Hagar, putting it on her shoulder, along with the child, and sends her away. And she departs and wanders in the wilderness of Beersheba.
When the water in the skin is gone, she puts the child under one of the bushes.
Then she goes and sits down opposite him, about a bowshot away — for she says, “Let me not look on the death of the child.” And she sits opposite him and lifts up her voice and weeps.
And God hears the voice of the boy. And the angel of God calls to Hagar from heaven and says to her, “What troubles you, Hagar? Do not be afraid, for God has heard the voice of the boy where he is.
Get up, lift up the boy and hold him with your hand — for I will make him into a great nation.”
Then God opens her eyes, and she sees a well of water. And she goes and fills the skin with water and gives the boy a drink.
And God is with the boy, and he grows up. He lives in the wilderness and becomes an archer.
He lives in the wilderness of Paran, and his mother takes a wife for him from the land of Egypt.
At that time Abimelech and Phicol the commander of his army say to Abraham, “God is with you in everything you do.

So now swear to me here by God that you will not deal falsely with me or with my descendants or with my posterity. As I have dealt kindly with you, so you will deal with me and with the land where you have sojourned.”
“I will swear,” Abraham says.
But Abraham reproves Abimelech about a well of water that Abimelech’s servants had seized.
“I do not know who has done this thing,” Abimelech says. “You did not tell me, and I have not heard of it until today.”
So Abraham takes sheep and oxen and gives them to Abimelech, and the two men make a covenant.
And Abraham sets apart seven ewe lambs of the flock.
“What is the meaning of these seven ewe lambs that you have set apart?” Abimelech says to Abraham.
“These seven ewe lambs you will accept from my hand, so that it may be a witness for me that I dug this well,” he says.
Therefore that place is called Beersheba — because both of them swore an oath there.
So they make a covenant at Beersheba. Then Abimelech and Phicol the commander of his army rise up and return to the land of the Philistines.
And Abraham plants a tamarisk tree in Beersheba and calls there on the name of YHWH, the Everlasting God.
And Abraham sojourns in the land of the Philistines many days.
After these things God tests Abraham and says to him, “Abraham.”
“Here I am,” he says.
“Take your son,” he says, “your only son Isaac, whom you love, and go to the land of Moriah, and offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains of which I shall tell you.”

So Abraham rises early in the morning and saddles his donkey and takes two of his young men with him, and his son Isaac. And he cuts the wood for the burnt offering and arises and goes to the place of which God had told him.
On the third day Abraham lifts up his eyes and sees the place from afar.
Then Abraham says to his young men, “Stay here with the donkey. The boy and I will go over there and worship and come back to you.”
And Abraham takes the wood of the burnt offering and lays it on Isaac his son. And he takes in his hand the fire and the knife. And they go, both of them together.
And Isaac says to Abraham his father, “My father.”
“Here I am, my son,” he says.
“Look — the fire and the wood. But where is the lamb for a burnt offering?”
“God will provide himself the lamb for a burnt offering, my son,” Abraham says.
And they go, both of them together.
When they come to the place of which God had told him, Abraham builds the altar there and lays the wood in order and binds Isaac his son and lays him on the altar, on top of the wood.
Then Abraham reaches out his hand and takes the knife to slaughter his son.
But the angel of YHWH calls to him from heaven and says, “Abraham! Abraham!”
“Here I am,” he says.
“Do not lay your hand on the boy or do anything to him — for now I know that you fear God, seeing you have not withheld your son, your only son, from me.”
And Abraham lifts up his eyes and looks, and look — behind him is a ram, caught in a thicket by its horns. And Abraham goes and takes the ram and offers it up as a burnt offering instead of his son.
So Abraham calls the name of that place “YHWH will provide” — as it is said to this day: “On the mountain of YHWH it will be provided.”
And the angel of YHWH calls to Abraham a second time from heaven
and says, “By myself I have sworn, declares YHWH, because you have done this and have not withheld your son, your only son —
I will surely bless you, and I will surely multiply your offspring as the stars of heaven and as the sand on the seashore. And your offspring shall possess the gate of his enemies,
and in your offspring all the nations of the earth shall be blessed — because you have listened to my voice.”
So Abraham returns to his young men, and they arise and go together to Beersheba. And Abraham lives at Beersheba.
Now after these things it is told to Abraham, “Look — Milcah also has borne children to your brother Nahor:
Uz his firstborn, Buz his brother, Kemuel the father of Aram,
Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel.”
Bethuel fathers Rebekah. These eight Milcah bears to Nahor, Abraham’s brother.
Moreover, his concubine, whose name is Reumah, bears Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.
Sarah lives 127 years — these are the years of the life of Sarah.
And Sarah dies at Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron) in the land of Canaan. And Abraham comes to mourn for Sarah and to weep for her.
And Abraham rises from before his dead and speaks to the Hittites:
“I am a sojourner and foreigner among you. Give me property among you for a burial place, that I may bury my dead out of my sight.”
The Hittites answer Abraham:
“Hear us, my lord. You are a mighty prince among us. Bury your dead in the choicest of our tombs. None of us will withhold his tomb from you for burying your dead.”
Abraham rises and bows to the Hittites, the people of the land.
And he speaks with them, saying, “If you are willing that I should bury my dead out of my sight, hear me and entreat for me Ephron the son of Zohar,
that he may give me the cave of Machpelah, which he owns, which is at the end of his field. For the full price let him give it to me in your presence as property for a burial place.”
Now Ephron was sitting among the Hittites. And Ephron the Hittite answers Abraham in the hearing of the Hittites, of all who had entered the gate of his city:
“No, my lord — hear me: I give you the field and I give you the cave that is in it. In the sight of the sons of my people I give it to you. Bury your dead.”
Then Abraham bows down before the people of the land.
And he speaks to Ephron in the hearing of the people of the land: “But if you will, please hear me. I will give the price of the field. Accept it from me, that I may bury my dead there.”
Ephron answers Abraham:
“My lord, listen to me. A piece of land worth four hundred shekels of silver — what is that between you and me? Bury your dead.”

Abraham listens to Ephron. And Abraham weighs out for Ephron the silver that he had named in the hearing of the Hittites — four hundred shekels of silver, according to the weights current among the merchants.
So the field of Ephron in Machpelah, which was to the east of Mamre — the field with the cave that was in it and all the trees that were in the field, throughout its whole area — is made over
to Abraham as a possession in the sight of the Hittites, before all who entered the gate of his city.
After this, Abraham buries Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah east of Mamre (that is, Hebron) in the land of Canaan.
The field and the cave that is in it are made over to Abraham as property for a burial place by the Hittites.
Now Abraham is old, well advanced in years. And YHWH has blessed Abraham in all things.
And Abraham says to his servant, the oldest of his household, who had charge over everything he had, “Put your hand under my thigh,
that I may make you swear by YHWH, the God of heaven and God of the earth, that you will not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I dwell,
but will go to my country and to my kindred and take a wife for my son Isaac.”
“Perhaps the woman may not be willing to follow me to this land,” the servant says to him. “Should I then take your son back to the land from which you came?”
“See to it that you do not take my son back there,” Abraham says to him.

“YHWH, the God of heaven, who took me from my father’s house and from the land of my birth, and who spoke to me and swore to me, ‘To your offspring I will give this land’ — he will send his angel before you, and you shall take a wife for my son from there.
And if the woman is not willing to follow you, then you will be free from this oath of mine. Only you must not take my son back there.”
So the servant puts his hand under the thigh of Abraham his master and swears to him concerning this matter.
Then the servant takes ten of his master’s camels and departs, taking all sorts of choice gifts from his master. And he arises and goes to Mesopotamia, to the city of Nahor.
And he makes the camels kneel down outside the city by the well of water at evening time — the time when women go out to draw water.
And he says, “YHWH, God of my master Abraham, please grant me success today and show steadfast love to my master Abraham.
Look — I am standing by the spring of water, and the daughters of the men of the city are coming out to draw water.

Let the young woman to whom I shall say, ‘Please let down your jar that I may drink,’ and who shall say, ‘Drink — and I will water your camels too’ — let her be the one you have appointed for your servant Isaac. By this I shall know that you have shown steadfast love to my master.”
Before he has finished speaking, look — Rebekah, who is born to Bethuel the son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham’s brother, comes out with her jar on her shoulder.
The young woman is very beautiful in appearance — a virgin, whom no man had known. She goes down to the spring and fills her jar and comes up.
Then the servant runs to meet her and says, “Please give me a little water to drink from your jar.”
“Drink, my lord,” she says. And she quickly lets down her jar onto her hand and gives him a drink.
When she has finished giving him a drink, she says, “I will draw water for your camels too, until they have finished drinking.”
So she quickly empties her jar into the trough and runs again to the well to draw water. And she draws for all his camels.
The man gazes at her in silence, wondering whether YHWH has made his journey successful or not.
When the camels have finished drinking, the man takes a gold ring weighing half a shekel, and two bracelets for her wrists weighing ten gold shekels,
and says, “Whose daughter are you? Tell me, is there room in your father’s house for us to spend the night?”
“I am the daughter of Bethuel the son of Milcah, whom she bore to Nahor,” she says to him.
She adds, “We have plenty of straw and fodder, and room to spend the night.”
The man bows his head and worships YHWH

and says, “Blessed be YHWH, the God of my master Abraham, who has not forsaken his steadfast love and his faithfulness toward my master. As for me, YHWH has led me in the way to the house of my master’s kinsmen.”
And the young woman runs and tells her mother’s household about these things.
Rebekah has a brother whose name is Laban. Laban runs out to the man at the spring.

As soon as he sees the ring and the bracelets on his sister’s arms and hears the words of Rebekah his sister, “Thus the man spoke to me,” he goes to the man — who is still standing by the camels at the spring.
“Come in, blessed of YHWH,” Laban says. “Why do you stand outside? For I have prepared the house and a place for the camels.”
So the man comes to the house. And Laban unloads the camels and gives straw and fodder to the camels and water to wash his feet and the feet of the men who are with him.
Then food is set before him to eat. But he says, “I will not eat until I have said what I have to say.”
“Speak on,” Laban says.
So he says: “I am Abraham’s servant.
YHWH has greatly blessed my master, and he has become great. He has given him flocks and herds, silver and gold, male servants and female servants, camels and donkeys.
And Sarah my master’s wife bore a son to my master when she was old, and to him he has given everything he has.
My master made me swear, saying, ‘You shall not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I dwell,
but you shall go to my father’s house and to my clan and take a wife for my son.’
I said to my master, ‘Perhaps the woman will not follow me.’
But he said to me, ‘YHWH, before whom I have walked, will send his angel with you and make your way successful. You shall take a wife for my son from my clan and from my father’s house.
Then you will be free from my oath, when you come to my clan. And if they will not give her to you, you will be free from my oath.’
“So I came today to the spring and said, ‘YHWH, God of my master Abraham — if now you will make my way successful on which I go —
look, I am standing by the spring of water. Let the young woman who comes out to draw, to whom I shall say, ‘Please give me a little water to drink from your jar,’
and who will say to me, ‘Drink, and I will draw for your camels too’ — let her be the woman whom YHWH has appointed for my master’s son.’
“Before I had finished speaking in my heart, look — Rebekah came out with her jar on her shoulder, and she went down to the spring and drew water. I said to her, ‘Please give me a drink.’
She quickly let down her jar from her shoulder and said, ‘Drink, and I will give your camels a drink too.’ So I drank, and she also gave the camels a drink.
Then I asked her, ‘Whose daughter are you?’ She said, ‘The daughter of Bethuel, Nahor’s son, whom Milcah bore to him.’ So I put the ring on her nose and the bracelets on her arms.
Then I bowed my head and worshipped YHWH and blessed YHWH, the God of my master Abraham, who had led me by the right way to take the daughter of my master’s kinsman for his son.
Now then, if you are going to show steadfast love and faithfulness to my master, tell me. And if not, tell me, that I may turn to the right hand or to the left.”
Then Laban and Bethuel answer: “The thing has come from YHWH. We cannot speak to you bad or good.
Look — Rebekah is before you. Take her and go, and let her be the wife of your master’s son, as YHWH has spoken.”
When Abraham’s servant hears their words, he bows himself to the earth before YHWH.
And the servant brings out jewels of silver and of gold and garments and gives them to Rebekah. He also gives to her brother and to her mother costly gifts.
And he and the men who are with him eat and drink. And they spend the night. When they arise in the morning, he says, “Send me away to my master.”
“Let the young woman remain with us a while — at least ten days,” her brother and her mother say. “After that she may go.”
“Do not delay me,” he says to them, “since YHWH has made my journey successful. Send me away so that I may go to my master.”
“Let us call the young woman and ask her,” they say.
And they call Rebekah and say to her, “Will you go with this man?”
“I will go,” she says.
So they send away Rebekah their sister and her nurse, and Abraham’s servant and his men.
And they bless Rebekah and say to her:
“Our sister — may you become
thousands of ten thousands.
And may your offspring possess
the gate of those who hate them.”
Then Rebekah and her young women arise and ride on the camels and follow the man. So the servant takes Rebekah and goes.
Now Isaac has returned from Beer-lahai-roi and is dwelling in the Negeb.
And Isaac goes out to meditate in the field toward evening. And he lifts up his eyes and sees — and look, camels are coming.
And Rebekah lifts up her eyes and sees Isaac. And she gets down from the camel
and says to the servant, “Who is that man walking in the field to meet us?”
“He is my master,” the servant says. So she takes her veil and covers herself.
And the servant tells Isaac all the things he has done.
Then Isaac brings her into the tent of Sarah his mother. He takes Rebekah, and she becomes his wife, and he loves her. So Isaac is comforted after his mother’s death.
Abraham takes another wife. Her name is Keturah.
She bears him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.
Jokshan fathers Sheba and Dedan. The sons of Dedan are Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim.
The sons of Midian: Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these are the children of Keturah.
Abraham gives all he has to Isaac.
But to the sons of his concubines Abraham gives gifts. And while he is still living he sends them away from his son Isaac, eastward to the east country.
These are the days of the years of Abraham’s life: 175 years.
And Abraham breathes his last and dies in a good old age — old and full of years — and is gathered to his people.
Isaac and Ishmael his sons bury him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron the son of Zohar the Hittite, east of Mamre,
the field that Abraham purchased from the Hittites. There Abraham is buried, with Sarah his wife.
After the death of Abraham, God blesses his son Isaac. And Isaac settles at Beer-lahai-roi.
These are the generations of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah’s servant, bore to Abraham.
These are the names of the sons of Ishmael, named in the order of their birth: Nebaioth, the firstborn of Ishmael; and Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
Mishma, Dumah, Massa,
Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
These are the sons of Ishmael and these are their names, by their villages and by their encampments — twelve princes according to their tribes.
These are the years of the life of Ishmael: 137 years. He breathes his last and dies and is gathered to his people.
They settle from Havilah to Shur, which is opposite Egypt in the direction of Assyria. He settled over against all his kinsmen.
These are the generations of Isaac, Abraham’s son. Abraham fathers Isaac.
And Isaac is forty years old when he takes Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel the Aramean of Paddan-aram, the sister of Laban the Aramean, to be his wife.
And Isaac prays to YHWH for his wife, because she is barren. And YHWH grants his prayer, and Rebekah his wife conceives.
The children struggle within her, and she says, “If it is to be this way, why is this happening to me?” So she goes to inquire of YHWH.
And YHWH says to her:
“Two nations are in your womb,
and two peoples from within you shall be divided.
The one shall be stronger than the other,
and the elder shall serve the younger.”
