Six branches extend from its sides — three from one side, three from the other.
Three cups shaped like almond blossoms, each with calyx and flower, on one branch — and three on the other — so for all six branches.
On the shaft itself, four cups shaped like almond blossoms, with calyxes and flowers,
and a calyx of one piece with it under each pair of the six branches.
Their calyxes and branches are of one piece with it — the whole a single piece of hammered work, pure gold.
He makes its seven lamps, its snuffers, and its trays of pure gold.
He makes it and all its utensils from a talent of pure gold.
The Incense Altar, the Oil, and the Incense · 37:25–29
He makes the incense altar of acacia wood — a cubit long, a cubit wide, square, two cubits high. Its horns are of one piece with it.
He overlays its top, its sides all around, and its horns with pure gold, and makes a moulding of gold around it.
He makes two gold rings under its moulding on opposite sides, as holders for the poles.
He makes the poles of acacia wood and overlays them with gold.
He also makes the holy anointing oil and the pure fragrant incense — blended by a skilled perfumer.
The Altar of Burnt Offering Made · 38:1–7
He makes the altar of burnt offering of acacia wood — five cubits long, five cubits wide, square, three cubits high.
He makes horns at its four corners — of one piece with it — and overlays it with bronze.
He makes all the altar's utensils — the pots, shovels, basins, forks, and firepans — all of bronze.
He makes a grating of bronze mesh for the altar, set under its ledge, extending halfway down.
He casts four rings at the four corners of the bronze grating as holders for the poles.
He makes the poles of acacia wood and overlays them with bronze.
He puts the poles through the rings on the sides of the altar for carrying it. He makes it hollow, with planks.
The Basin Made · 38:8
He makes the basin of bronze and its stand of bronze — from the mirrors of the women who served at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
The Court Made · 38:9–20
He makes the court. On the south side, the court hangings are of fine twisted linen — one hundred cubits long,
with twenty pillars and twenty bronze bases, the hooks and bands of the pillars in silver.
On the north side, one hundred cubits — twenty pillars, twenty bronze bases, hooks and bands in silver.
On the west side, fifty cubits — ten pillars, ten bases, hooks and bands in silver.
The east side — fifty cubits.
Fifteen cubits of hangings for one side of the gate, with three pillars and three bases.
The same for the other side — fifteen cubits, three pillars, three bases.
All the hangings around the court are of fine twisted linen.
The bases for the pillars are bronze; the hooks and bands of silver. The capitals are overlaid with silver and all the court pillars are banded with silver.
The screen for the court gate is embroidered work in blue and purple and crimson yarn and fine twisted linen — twenty cubits long, five cubits high, matching the court hangings.
Its four pillars and four bronze bases, with silver hooks, and capitals and bands overlaid with silver.
All the pegs of the Tabernacle and all the pegs of the court all around are of bronze.
The Record of Materials · 38:21–31
These are the records of the Tabernacle — the Tabernacle of the testimony — recorded at Moses' command by the Levites under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, made everything YHWH commanded Moses.
With him was Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan — engraver, designer, and embroiderer in blue and purple and crimson yarn and fine linen.
All the gold used for the work — the gold of the wave offering for all the construction of the sanctuary — was twenty-nine talents and seven hundred and thirty shekels, by the sanctuary standard.
The silver from the registered members of the congregation was one hundred talents and one thousand seven hundred and seventy-five shekels, by the sanctuary standard —
a half-shekel per head — for everyone listed in the census from twenty years old and upward: six hundred and three thousand, five hundred and fifty men.
The hundred talents of silver were used for casting the bases of the sanctuary and the bases of the veil — one talent per base.
From the remaining one thousand seven hundred and seventy-five shekels he made hooks for the pillars, overlaid their capitals, and made their bands.
The bronze wave offering was seventy talents and two thousand four hundred shekels.
With it he made the bases for the entrance of the tent of meeting, the bronze altar and its bronze grating, all the altar's utensils,
the bases of the court all around, the bases for the court gate, all the pegs of the Tabernacle, and all the pegs of the court.
The Ephod Made · 39:1–7
From the blue and purple and crimson yarns they make the woven vestments for serving in the Holy Place, and the sacred garments for Aaron — just as YHWH commanded Moses.
He makes the ephod of gold, blue and purple and crimson yarns, and fine twisted linen.
They hammer out sheets of gold and cut them into threads to weave into the blue and purple and crimson yarn and the fine linen — skilled work.
They make shoulder pieces for the ephod, joined to it at its two edges.
The woven band on it is of the same materials and workmanship — gold, blue and purple and crimson yarn, and fine twisted linen — just as YHWH commanded Moses.
They set the onyx stones in gold filigree settings, engraved with the names of the sons of Israel like seal engravings.
He fastens them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as stones of remembrance for the sons of Israel — just as YHWH commanded Moses.
The Breastpiece Made · 39:8–21
He makes the breastpiece in skilled work, in the manner of the ephod — of gold, blue and purple and crimson yarn, and fine twisted linen.
It is square and doubled — a span in length, a span in width.
They set in it four rows of stones: a ruby, a topaz, and an emerald in the first row;
a turquoise, a sapphire, and a diamond in the second;
a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst in the third;
a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper in the fourth — all set in gold filigree.
The twelve stones bear the names of the sons of Israel — one name for each stone, engraved like a seal, for the twelve tribes.
They make twisted chains of pure gold, like cords, for the breastpiece.
They make two gold settings and two gold rings and fasten the rings to the two upper corners of the breastpiece.
They attach the two gold cords to the two rings at the corners,
and fasten the other ends of the cords to the two settings, attaching them to the front of the ephod's shoulder pieces.
They make two gold rings and attach them to the two lower corners of the breastpiece, on the inner edge next to the ephod.
They make two more gold rings and attach them to the lower part of the shoulder pieces, at the front, at the seam above the ephod's woven band.
They bind the breastpiece by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a blue cord, so it lies against the woven band and cannot come loose — just as YHWH commanded Moses.
The Robe, the Plate, and the Other Garments · 39:22–31
He makes the robe of the ephod — all of woven blue —
with an opening in the middle, a woven collar around it so it cannot tear.
On the hem they make pomegranates of blue and purple and crimson yarn and fine twisted linen.
They make bells of pure gold and put them between the pomegranates around the hem —
a bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, all the way around the hem of the robe for ministering — just as YHWH commanded Moses.
They make the tunics of fine linen — woven work — for Aaron and his sons,
the turban of fine linen, the headbands of fine linen, the linen undergarments of fine twisted linen,
and the sash of fine twisted linen, blue and purple and crimson yarn — embroidered work — just as YHWH commanded Moses.
They make the plate of the holy crown of pure gold and engrave on it, like a seal inscription: Holy to YHWH.
They tie a cord of blue to it to fasten it to the top of the turban — just as YHWH commanded Moses.
The Work Finished and Presented · 39:32–43
All the work of the Tabernacle — the tent of meeting — is finished. The people of Israel have done everything just as YHWH commanded Moses. So they do.
They bring the Tabernacle to Moses — the tent and all its furnishings: its clasps, frames, bars, pillars, and bases;
the covering of tanned rams' skins and fine leather, and the curtain veil;
the ark of the testimony with its poles and the mercy seat;
the table with all its utensils and the bread of the Presence;
the pure gold lampstand with its lamps set in place, all its utensils, and the oil for the light;
the gold altar, the anointing oil and the fragrant incense, and the entrance screen for the tent;
the bronze altar with its bronze grating, poles, and all utensils; the basin and its stand;
the hangings of the court, its pillars and bases, the screen for the court gate, its cords and pegs; all the furnishings for the service of the Tabernacle, the tent of meeting;
the woven vestments for ministering in the Holy Place, the sacred garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons for their priestly service.
The people of Israel have done all the work exactly as YHWH commanded Moses.
Moses inspects all the work — and they have done it. They have done it exactly as YHWH commanded. And Moses blesses them.
YHWH Commands the Assembly · 40:1–15
YHWH speaks to Moses:
"On the first day of the first month you shall erect the Tabernacle — the tent of meeting.
Place the ark of the testimony inside it and screen it off with the veil.
Bring in the table and set it in order. Bring in the lampstand and set up its lamps.
Place the gold altar of incense before the ark of the testimony and hang the entrance screen for the Tabernacle.
Set the altar of burnt offering in front of the entrance of the Tabernacle.
Place the basin between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water in it.
Set up the court all around and hang the screen at the court gate.
Take the anointing oil and anoint the Tabernacle and everything in it. Consecrate it and all its furnishings — it will be holy.
Anoint the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils. Consecrate it — it will be most holy.
Anoint the basin and its stand, and consecrate it.
Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tent of meeting and wash them with water.
Dress Aaron in the sacred garments, anoint him, and consecrate him — that he may serve me as priest.
Bring his sons forward, put the tunics on them,
and anoint them as you anointed their father, that they may serve me as priests. Their anointing will mark them for a priesthood that is theirs for ever throughout their generations."
Moses Assembles the Tabernacle · 40:16–33
Moses does everything just as YHWH commanded him — so he does.
The Tabernacle is erected on the first day of the first month of the second year.
Moses erects it: he lays the bases, sets up the frames, puts in the bars, and raises the pillars.
He spreads the tent over the Tabernacle and puts the outer covering on top — just as YHWH commanded him.
He takes the testimony and places it in the ark, puts the poles on the ark, and sets the mercy seat above it.
He brings the ark into the Tabernacle and hangs the curtain veil, screening off the ark of the testimony — just as YHWH commanded him.
He puts the table in the tent of meeting on the north side, outside the veil,
and arranges the bread on it before YHWH — just as YHWH commanded him.
He places the lampstand in the tent of meeting, opposite the table on the south side,
and sets up the lamps before YHWH — just as YHWH commanded him.
He places the gold altar in the tent of meeting, before the veil,
and burns fragrant incense on it — just as YHWH commanded him.
He puts up the entrance screen for the Tabernacle.
He sets the altar of burnt offering at the entrance — and offers on it a burnt offering and a grain offering — just as YHWH commanded him.
He places the basin between the tent of meeting and the altar and puts water in it for washing.
Moses and Aaron and his sons wash their hands and feet from it
whenever they enter the tent of meeting and whenever they approach the altar — just as YHWH commanded Moses.
He erects the court around the Tabernacle and the altar and puts up the screen for the court gate.
And Moses finishes the work.
The Glory of YHWH Fills the Tabernacle · 40:34–38
Then the cloud covers the tent of meeting,
and the glory of YHWH fills the Tabernacle.
Moses cannot enter the tent of meeting — because the cloud has settled on it, and the glory of YHWH fills the Tabernacle.
Throughout all their journeys,
whenever the cloud lifts from the Tabernacle,
the people of Israel set out.
But if the cloud does not lift,
they do not set out —
until the day it lifts.
For the cloud of YHWH is over the Tabernacle by day,
and fire is in it by night —
in the sight of all the house of Israel,
throughout all their journeys.
YHWH calls to Moses from the Tent of Meeting and speaks to him:
“Speak to the people of Israel and say to them: When any of you brings an offering to the LORD, bring it from the livestock — from the herd or from the flock.
If the offering is a burnt offering from the herd, it must be a male without blemish. He is to bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, so that it may be accepted before the LORD.
He shall lay his hand on the head of the burnt offering, and it will be accepted for him — to make atonement on his behalf.

He is to slaughter the bull before the LORD. Then Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall bring the blood and throw it against all sides of the altar — the altar that stands at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
He shall skin the burnt offering and cut it into pieces.
The sons of Aaron the priest shall put fire on the altar and lay wood on the fire.
Then Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall arrange the pieces — the head and the fat — on the wood burning over the fire on the altar.
The inner parts and the legs he shall wash with water. Then the priest burns it all on the altar — a burnt offering, a gift given by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
If the offering is a burnt offering from the flock — whether from the sheep or the goats — he must bring a male without blemish.
He shall slaughter it on the north side of the altar before the LORD. Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall throw its blood against all sides of the altar.
He shall cut it into pieces, along with its head and its fat. The priest arranges them on the wood burning over the fire on the altar.
The inner parts and the legs he shall wash with water. The priest offers it all and burns it on the altar — a burnt offering, a gift given by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
If the offering to the LORD is a burnt offering from birds, he shall bring his offering from the turtledoves or from the young pigeons.
The priest shall bring it to the altar, wring off its head, and burn it on the altar. Its blood is drained along the side of the altar.
He shall remove the crop and its contents and cast it beside the altar on the east side — in the place where the ashes are kept.
He shall tear it open by its wings but not sever it completely. The priest burns it on the altar, on the wood over the fire — a burnt offering, a gift given by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.”
When any person brings a grain offering to the LORD, it shall be of fine flour. He shall pour oil over it and lay frankincense on it,

and bring it to Aaron’s sons the priests. The priest shall take a full handful of the fine flour and oil — together with all the frankincense — and burn this token portion on the altar: a gift given by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
What remains of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons. It is most holy — taken from the LORD’s gifts given by fire.
When you bring a grain offering baked in the oven, it shall be fine flour — either unleavened loaves mixed with oil, or thin unleavened wafers spread with oil.
If your offering is a grain offering prepared on a griddle, it shall be fine flour mixed with oil, unleavened.
Break it into pieces and pour oil over it — it is a grain offering.
If your offering is a grain offering from a deep pan, it shall be made of fine flour with oil.
You shall bring to the LORD the grain offering prepared in any of these ways. Present it to the priest, who brings it to the altar.
The priest shall take the token portion from the grain offering and burn it on the altar — a gift given by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
What remains of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons — most holy, from the LORD’s gifts given by fire.
No grain offering you bring to the LORD shall be made with leaven — burn nothing leavened and no honey as a gift given by fire to the LORD.
You may present them to the LORD as a firstfruits offering — but they shall not go up on the altar as a pleasing aroma.
You shall season every grain offering with salt. Never let the salt of the covenant of your God be absent from your grain offering — with every offering you bring, offer salt.
If you bring a grain offering of firstfruits to the LORD, bring roasted grain — fresh kernels crushed from the ear — as your firstfruits offering.
Pour oil over it and lay frankincense on it — it is a grain offering.
The priest shall burn the token portion: some of the crushed grain and its oil, along with all the frankincense — a gift given by fire to the LORD.
If the offering is a peace offering from the herd — whether male or female — he shall bring it without blemish before the LORD.
He shall lay his hand on the head of the offering and slaughter it at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. Aaron’s sons the priests shall throw the blood against all sides of the altar.
From the peace offering he shall present to the LORD as a gift given by fire: the fat covering the inner parts and all the fat on them,
the two kidneys with the fat on them at the loins, and the lobe of the liver — which he shall remove with the kidneys.
Aaron’s sons shall burn it on the altar, on top of the burnt offering on the wood over the fire — a gift given by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
If the offering for a peace offering is from the flock — male or female — it shall be brought without blemish.
If he brings a lamb as his offering, he shall present it before the LORD,
lay his hand on the head of the offering, and slaughter it before the Tent of Meeting. Aaron’s sons shall throw its blood against all sides of the altar.

From the peace offering he shall present to the LORD as a gift given by fire: the fat — including the broad tail removed close to the backbone — the fat covering the inner parts and all the fat on them,
the two kidneys with the fat on them at the loins, and the lobe of the liver — which he shall remove with the kidneys.
The priest shall burn it on the altar — food, a gift given by fire to the LORD.
If his offering is a goat, he shall present it before the LORD,
lay his hand on its head, and slaughter it before the Tent of Meeting. Aaron’s sons shall throw its blood against all sides of the altar.
From it he shall present to the LORD as his gift given by fire: the fat covering the inner parts and all the fat on them,
the two kidneys with the fat on them at the loins, and the lobe of the liver — which he shall remove with the kidneys.
The priest shall burn them on the altar — food, a gift given by fire, a pleasing aroma. All the fat belongs to the LORD.
This is a lasting ordinance for all your generations, wherever you live: you shall eat neither fat nor blood.
YHWH spoke to Moses:
“Speak to the people of Israel and say: When anyone sins unintentionally against any of the LORD’s commands — doing what is forbidden — the following shall apply.
If it is the anointed priest who sins, bringing guilt upon the people, he shall offer a young bull without blemish to the LORD as a sin offering for his sin.
He shall bring the bull to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting before the LORD, lay his hand on its head, and slaughter it before the LORD.
The anointed priest shall take some of the bull’s blood and carry it into the Tent of Meeting.
Dipping his finger in the blood, he shall sprinkle it seven times before the LORD — in front of the curtain of the sanctuary.

He shall put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of fragrant incense before the LORD — the altar that stands inside the Tent of Meeting. The remaining blood he shall pour out at the base of the altar of burnt offering at the entrance of the Tent.
He shall remove all the fat from the sin-offering bull: the fat covering the inner parts and all the fat on them,
the two kidneys with the fat on them at the loins, and the lobe of the liver — removed with the kidneys —
just as the fat is removed from the ox of the peace offering. The priest shall burn it all on the altar of burnt offering.
But the bull’s hide and all its flesh — head, legs, inner parts, and dung —
the whole bull he shall carry outside the camp to a clean place, to the ash heap, and burn it there on a wood fire.
If the whole congregation of Israel sins unintentionally and the matter is hidden from the assembly — they have done what the LORD’s commands forbid and are guilty —
when the sin becomes known, the assembly shall offer a young bull as a sin offering and bring it before the Tent of Meeting.
The elders of the congregation shall lay their hands on the head of the bull before the LORD, and it shall be slaughtered before the LORD.
The anointed priest shall bring some of the bull’s blood into the Tent of Meeting,
dip his finger in the blood, and sprinkle it seven times before the LORD in front of the curtain.
He shall put some of the blood on the horns of the altar inside the Tent before the LORD, and pour the rest of the blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering at the entrance of the Tent.
He shall remove all the fat and burn it on the altar.
He shall do with this bull exactly as he did with the bull of the priest’s sin offering. The priest makes atonement for them, and it shall be forgiven them.
He shall carry the bull outside the camp and burn it as he burned the first — it is the sin offering for the assembly.
When a leader sins unintentionally — doing what the LORD his God has commanded must not be done — and becomes aware of his guilt,
he shall bring as his offering a male goat without blemish.
He shall lay his hand on the goat’s head and slaughter it in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered before the LORD — it is a sin offering.
The priest shall take some of the blood with his finger, put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour the rest at the base of the altar.
He shall burn all the fat on the altar as in the peace offering. The priest makes atonement for him from his sin, and it shall be forgiven him.
If any of the common people sins unintentionally — doing what the LORD’s commands forbid — and becomes aware of guilt,
he shall bring a female goat without blemish as his offering for the sin he has committed.
He shall lay his hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter it where the burnt offering is slaughtered.
The priest shall take some of its blood with his finger, put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour the rest at the base of the altar.
He shall remove all the fat as from the peace offering. The priest burns it on the altar as a pleasing aroma to the LORD, makes atonement for him, and it shall be forgiven him.
If he brings a lamb as his sin offering instead, he shall bring a female without blemish,
lay his hand on its head, and slaughter it where the burnt offering is slaughtered.
The priest shall take some of its blood with his finger, put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour the rest at the base of the altar.

He shall remove all its fat as the lamb’s fat is removed from the peace offering, and the priest shall burn it on the altar, on the LORD’s gifts given by fire. The priest makes atonement for his sin, and it shall be forgiven him.”
If anyone sins by failing to speak up when they hear a public call for testimony — when they have witnessed something or know about it — they bear their guilt.

If anyone touches any unclean thing — the carcass of an unclean wild animal, an unclean livestock carcass, or an unclean swarming creature — and it was hidden from them, they have become unclean and are guilty.
If anyone touches human uncleanness — any form of uncleanness that makes a person unclean — and it was hidden from them, then when they learn of it, they are guilty.
If anyone makes a rash oath with their lips — swearing to do evil or to do good, in any matter, without thinking — then when they learn of it, they are guilty in any of these things.
When anyone is guilty in one of these ways, they shall confess the sin they have committed.
As their penalty for the sin, they shall bring to the LORD a female from the flock — a lamb or a female goat — as a sin offering. The priest shall make atonement for them for their sin.
If they cannot afford a sheep, they shall bring to the LORD, as their penalty, two turtledoves or two young pigeons — one for a sin offering and one for a burnt offering.
They shall bring them to the priest, who shall first offer the one for the sin offering. He shall wring its head from the back of its neck without severing it completely.
He shall sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering on the side of the altar, and the rest of the blood shall be drained at the base of the altar — it is a sin offering.
The second bird he shall offer as a burnt offering according to the rule. The priest shall make atonement for them for the sin they have committed, and it shall be forgiven them.

If they cannot afford two birds, they shall bring as their offering one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a sin offering. They shall put no oil on it and lay no frankincense on it — it is a sin offering.
They shall bring it to the priest, who shall take a handful of it as the token portion and burn it on the altar, on top of the LORD’s gifts given by fire — it is a sin offering.
The priest shall make atonement for them for whichever of these sins they have committed, and it shall be forgiven them. The remainder belongs to the priest, as with the grain offering.
YHWH spoke to Moses:

“When anyone commits a trespass and sins unintentionally against the LORD’s holy things, they shall bring to the LORD as their penalty a ram without blemish from the flock — at the proper value in silver shekels, by the sanctuary weight — as a guilt offering.

They shall make restitution for what they misappropriated from the holy things, adding a fifth of its value, and give it to the priest. The priest shall make atonement for them with the ram of the guilt offering, and they will be forgiven.”
YHWH spoke to Moses:
“If anyone sins and does any one of the things the LORD has commanded must not be done — though they were not aware of it — they are still guilty and shall bear the consequences.

They shall bring to the priest a ram without blemish from the flock, at the proper value, as a guilt offering. The priest shall make atonement for the error they committed without knowing it, and it will be forgiven them. It is a guilt offering — they were indeed guilty before the LORD.”
YHWH spoke to Moses:
“When anyone sins and is unfaithful to the LORD by deceiving a neighbor in a matter of deposit or security, by robbery, or by extorting them,
or by finding something lost and lying about it, or by swearing falsely in any of these things — such are the ways a person becomes guilty.
When anyone is guilty in this way, they shall return what they took by robbery or extortion, or the deposit entrusted to them, or the lost thing they found,
or whatever they swore falsely about. They shall make full restitution, adding a fifth of its value, and return it to its owner on the very day they present their guilt offering.
They shall bring to the LORD as their penalty a ram without blemish from the flock, at the proper value, as a guilt offering to the priest.
The priest shall make atonement for them before the LORD, and they shall be forgiven for any of the things that bring guilt.”
YHWH spoke to Moses:

“Give Aaron and his sons this command: This is the law of the burnt offering. The burnt offering shall remain on the hearth of the altar all night until morning, and the altar fire shall be kept burning.
The priest shall put on his linen robe and linen undergarments next to his body. He shall remove the ashes of what the fire has consumed on the altar and place them beside the altar.
Then he shall take off those garments, put on other clothes, and carry the ashes outside the camp to a clean place.
The fire on the altar shall be kept burning — it must not go out. Each morning the priest shall add wood to it, arrange the burnt offering on it, and burn the fat of the peace offerings on top.
The fire shall be kept burning on the altar continually — it must never go out.
This is the law of the grain offering. Aaron’s sons shall bring it before the LORD, in front of the altar.
The priest shall take a handful of the fine flour and oil from the grain offering, along with all the frankincense on it, and burn the token portion on the altar as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
What remains Aaron and his sons shall eat. It shall be eaten without leaven in the court of the Tent of Meeting.
It shall not be baked with leaven. I have given it as their portion from my gifts given by fire — it is most holy, like the sin offering and the guilt offering.
Every male among Aaron’s sons may eat it. This is a lasting ordinance throughout your generations from the LORD’s gifts given by fire. Whoever touches them shall be consecrated.”
YHWH spoke to Moses:

“This is the offering Aaron and his sons shall bring to the LORD on the day he is anointed: one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a regular grain offering — half in the morning and half in the evening.
It shall be prepared on a griddle with oil. Bring it well mixed and offer it in baked pieces as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
The anointed priest who succeeds his father shall bring it. It is the LORD’s — a lasting ordinance. It shall be wholly burned.
Every grain offering of a priest shall be wholly burned — it shall not be eaten.”
YHWH spoke to Moses:
“Speak to Aaron and his sons: This is the law of the sin offering. The sin offering shall be slaughtered before the LORD in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered — it is most holy.
The priest who offers it for sin shall eat it. It shall be eaten in the court of the Tent of Meeting.
Whatever touches its flesh shall be consecrated. If any of its blood is spattered on a garment, the stained part shall be washed in a holy place.
The clay vessel in which the offering was boiled shall be broken. If it was boiled in a bronze vessel, that vessel shall be scoured and rinsed with water.
Every male among the priests may eat it — it is most holy.
But no sin offering may be eaten if its blood has been brought into the Tent of Meeting to make atonement in the sanctuary. It shall be burned in the fire.”
This is the law of the guilt offering. It is most holy.
The guilt offering shall be slaughtered in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered, and its blood shall be thrown against all sides of the altar.
All its fat shall be offered: the fat tail and the fat covering the inner parts,
the two kidneys with the fat on them at the loins, and the lobe of the liver — removed with the kidneys.
The priest shall burn them on the altar as a gift given by fire to the LORD — it is a guilt offering.
Every male among the priests may eat it. It shall be eaten in a holy place — it is most holy.
The guilt offering is like the sin offering: one law governs them both. The priest who makes atonement with it shall have it.
The priest who presents someone’s burnt offering shall keep its hide for himself.
Every grain offering baked in the oven and every offering made on a griddle or pan shall belong to the priest who presents it.
Every grain offering mixed with oil or dry shall belong equally to all the sons of Aaron.
This is the law of the peace offering that may be brought to the LORD.

If it is offered as a thanksgiving, together with the sacrifice of thanksgiving he shall offer unleavened loaves mixed with oil, unleavened wafers spread with oil, and loaves of fine flour mixed with oil and well kneaded.
Along with his thanksgiving peace offering he shall bring loaves of leavened bread.
From each offering he shall present one piece as a contribution to the LORD — it belongs to the priest who throws the blood of the peace offering.
The flesh of his thanksgiving peace offering shall be eaten on the day it is offered — none of it shall be kept until morning.
But if the sacrifice is a vow or a freewill offering, it shall be eaten on the day it is presented, and what remains may be eaten the next day.
Whatever flesh of the sacrifice remains on the third day shall be burned in fire.

If any flesh of the peace offering is eaten on the third day, the one who offered it will not be accepted — it counts as nothing for him. The one who eats it shall bear the guilt, for it has become defiled.
Flesh that has touched anything unclean shall not be eaten — it shall be burned in fire. As for clean flesh, every clean person may eat it.
But whoever is unclean and eats flesh from the LORD’s peace offering shall be cut off from their people.

If anyone touches anything unclean — human uncleanness, an unclean animal, or any unclean detestable thing — and then eats flesh from the LORD’s peace offering, that person shall be cut off from their people.
YHWH spoke to Moses:
“Say to the people of Israel: You shall eat no fat of ox, sheep, or goat.
The fat of an animal that has died on its own or been torn by wild animals may be used for other purposes, but you must never eat it.
Anyone who eats the fat of an animal from which a gift given by fire is made to the LORD shall be cut off from their people.
And you shall eat no blood — of bird or animal — in any of your dwellings.
Anyone who eats any blood shall be cut off from their people.”
YHWH spoke to Moses:
“Speak to the people of Israel: Whoever brings a peace offering to the LORD shall bring their contribution from it with their own hands.
They shall bring the gift given by fire to the LORD with their own hands — they shall bring the fat on the breast and wave the breast as a wave offering before the LORD.
The priest shall burn the fat on the altar, but the breast shall belong to Aaron and his sons.
The right thigh you shall give to the priest as a contribution from your peace offerings.
The son of Aaron who offers the blood and fat of the peace offering shall have the right thigh as his portion.

For I have taken the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution from the people of Israel out of their peace offerings and given them to Aaron the priest and his sons — a lasting ordinance from among the people of Israel.”
This is the allotted share of Aaron and his sons from the LORD’s gifts given by fire, set apart from the day they were brought forward to serve the LORD as priests.
The LORD commanded this to be given to them on the day he anointed them — a lasting ordinance throughout their generations.
This is the law of the burnt offering, the grain offering, the sin offering, the guilt offering, the ordination offering, and the peace offering —
the law the LORD gave to Moses on Mount Sinai, on the day he commanded the people of Israel to bring their offerings to the LORD in the wilderness of Sinai.
YHWH speaks to Moses:
“Take Aaron and his sons with him, and bring the garments, the anointing oil, the bull for the sin offering, the two rams, and the basket of unleavened bread.
Assemble the whole congregation at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.”
Moses does as the LORD commands him, and the congregation assembles at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
Moses says to the congregation: “This is what the LORD has commanded to be done.”
Moses brings Aaron and his sons forward and washes them with water.
He puts the tunic on Aaron, ties the sash around him, clothes him in the robe, and puts the ephod on him. He ties the skillfully woven waistband of the ephod around him, fastening it securely.
He places the breastpiece on him and puts the Urim and Thummim in the breastpiece.
He sets the turban on Aaron’s head, and on the front of the turban he places the gold plate — the holy crown — just as the LORD commanded Moses.
Moses takes the anointing oil and anoints the tabernacle and everything in it, consecrating them all.
He sprinkles some of it on the altar seven times and anoints the altar and all its utensils, and the basin with its stand, consecrating them.
He pours some of the anointing oil on Aaron’s head and anoints him, consecrating him.
Moses then brings Aaron’s sons forward, clothes them in tunics, ties sashes around them, and binds caps on their heads — just as the LORD commanded Moses.
He brings forward the bull for the sin offering. Aaron and his sons lay their hands on its head,

and Moses slaughters it. He takes the blood and puts it on the horns of the altar all around with his finger, purifying the altar. The rest of the blood he pours out at the base of the altar. He consecrates it and makes atonement for it.
He takes all the fat on the inner parts, the lobe of the liver, and the two kidneys with their fat, and burns them on the altar.
The bull — its hide, its flesh, and its dung — he burns outside the camp, just as the LORD commanded Moses.
He brings the ram for the burnt offering. Aaron and his sons lay their hands on its head,
and Moses slaughters it. He throws the blood against all sides of the altar.
He cuts the ram into pieces and burns the head, the pieces, and the fat.
He washes the inner parts and the legs with water, then burns the whole ram on the altar — a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma, a gift given by fire to the LORD, just as the LORD commanded Moses.
He brings the second ram — the ordination ram. Aaron and his sons lay their hands on its head,
and Moses slaughters it. He takes some of its blood and puts it on the lobe of Aaron’s right ear, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.

He brings Aaron’s sons forward and puts blood on the lobes of their right ears, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. The rest of the blood Moses throws against all sides of the altar.
He takes the fat — the broad tail and all the fat on the inner parts, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys with their fat — and the right thigh.
From the basket of unleavened bread before the LORD he takes one unleavened loaf, one loaf made with oil, and one wafer, and places them on the fat and on the right thigh.
He puts all of it in the hands of Aaron and his sons and waves it as a wave offering before the LORD.
Then Moses takes it back from their hands and burns it on the altar, on top of the burnt offering — it is the ordination offering, a pleasing aroma, a gift given by fire to the LORD.
Moses takes the breast and waves it as a wave offering before the LORD — from the ordination ram, this is Moses’ own portion, just as the LORD commanded Moses.

Moses takes some of the anointing oil and some of the blood from the altar and sprinkles it on Aaron and his garments, and on his sons and their garments. He consecrates Aaron and his garments, and his sons and their garments, together.

Moses says to Aaron and his sons: “Boil the flesh at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting and eat it there with the bread in the ordination basket, just as I was commanded: Aaron and his sons shall eat it.
What remains of the flesh and the bread you shall burn in fire.
You shall not leave the entrance of the Tent of Meeting for seven days — until the days of your ordination are complete, for it takes seven days to ordain you.
What has been done today, the LORD has commanded to be done, to make atonement for you.
You shall remain at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting day and night for seven days, keeping the LORD’s charge, so that you do not die — for so I have been commanded.”
And Aaron and his sons do everything the LORD has commanded through Moses.
On the eighth day Moses calls Aaron and his sons and the elders of Israel.
He says to Aaron: “Take a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering, both without blemish, and bring them before the LORD.
Then say to the people of Israel: Take a male goat for a sin offering, and a calf and a lamb — both a year old and without blemish — for a burnt offering,
and a bull and a ram for peace offerings to sacrifice before the LORD, and a grain offering mixed with oil. For today the LORD will appear to you.”
They bring what Moses commanded before the Tent of Meeting, and the whole congregation comes forward and stands before the LORD.
Moses says: “This is what the LORD has commanded you to do, so that the glory of the LORD may appear to you.”

Moses says to Aaron: “Come to the altar and offer your sin offering and your burnt offering, and make atonement for yourself and for the people. Then present the people’s offering and make atonement for them, just as the LORD has commanded.”
Aaron comes to the altar and slaughters the young bull for his own sin offering.
His sons bring the blood to him. He dips his finger in it and puts it on the horns of the altar, then pours the rest out at the base of the altar.
The fat, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver from the sin offering he burns on the altar, just as the LORD commanded Moses.
The flesh and the hide he burns outside the camp.
He then slaughters the burnt offering. His sons hand him the blood, and he throws it against all sides of the altar.
They hand him the burnt offering piece by piece, including the head, and he burns them on the altar.
He washes the inner parts and the legs and burns them on top of the burnt offering on the altar.
He then presents the people’s offering. He takes the sin offering goat, slaughters it, and presents it for sin, just as he did with the first.
He presents the burnt offering and offers it according to the rule.
He brings the grain offering, takes a handful from it, and burns it on the altar — in addition to the morning’s burnt offering.
He slaughters the bull and the ram as the peace offerings for the people. His sons hand him the blood, and he throws it against all sides of the altar.
The fat portions from the bull and the ram — the broad tail, the fat covering the inner parts, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver —
they lay on the breasts, and Aaron burns the fat portions on the altar.
Aaron waves the breasts and the right thigh as a wave offering before the LORD — just as Moses commanded.
Aaron lifts his hands toward the people and blesses them. Then he comes down, having completed the sin offering, the burnt offering, and the peace offerings.
Moses and Aaron go into the Tent of Meeting. When they come out, they bless the people — and the glory of the LORD appears to all the people.
Fire comes out from before the LORD and consumes the burnt offering and the fat portions on the altar. All the people see it. They shout aloud and fall on their faces.
Aaron’s sons Nadab and Abihu each take their censers, put fire in them, and lay incense on it. They offer unauthorized fire before the LORD — fire he had not commanded them to offer.
Fire comes out from before the LORD and consumes them. They die before the LORD.
Moses says to Aaron: “This is what the LORD meant when he said: Among those who come near me I will be treated as holy, and before all the people I will be honored.” And Aaron is silent.
Moses calls Mishael and Elzaphan, sons of Aaron’s uncle Uzziel, and says to them: “Come forward and carry your brothers away from the front of the sanctuary, outside the camp.”
They come forward and carry them in their tunics outside the camp, just as Moses said.

Moses says to Aaron and to his sons Eleazar and Ithamar: “Do not uncover your heads and do not tear your garments, or you will die and wrath will come on the whole congregation. Let all the house of Israel mourn for those the LORD has burned.
But you shall not leave the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, or you will die — for the LORD’s anointing oil is on you.” They do as Moses says.
YHWH speaks to Aaron:
“You and your sons are not to drink wine or strong drink when you enter the Tent of Meeting, or you will die. This is a lasting ordinance throughout your generations.
You must distinguish between the holy and the common, and between the unclean and the clean,
and you must teach the people of Israel all the statutes that the LORD has spoken to them through Moses.”

Moses speaks to Aaron and to his surviving sons Eleazar and Ithamar: “Take the grain offering that remains from the LORD’s gifts given by fire and eat it without leaven beside the altar, for it is most holy.
Eat it in a holy place, for it is your portion and your sons’ portion from the LORD’s gifts given by fire — so I have been commanded.

The breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution you shall eat in a clean place — you, your sons, and your daughters with you — for they are given as your portion and your children’s portion from the peace offerings of the people of Israel.

The thigh of the contribution and the breast of the wave offering they shall bring with the gifts given by fire from the fat portions, to wave as a wave offering before the LORD. They will be a lasting portion for you and your children, just as the LORD commanded.”
Moses then asks closely about the sin offering goat and finds it has been burned. He is angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron’s surviving sons, and says:
“Why did you not eat the sin offering in the holy place? It is most holy, and the LORD gave it to you to carry the guilt of the congregation and make atonement for them before the LORD.
Its blood was not brought into the inner sanctuary — you should certainly have eaten it in the sanctuary, just as I commanded.”

Aaron says to Moses: “Today they offered their sin offering and their burnt offering before the LORD, and yet these things happened to me. If I had eaten the sin offering today, would it have been acceptable in the LORD’s sight?”
Moses hears this and is satisfied.
YHWH speaks to Moses and Aaron together:
“Say to the people of Israel: Among all the land animals, these are the creatures you may eat.
Any animal that has split hooves — a hoof completely divided in two — and that chews the cud, that one you may eat.
But among those that chew the cud or have split hooves, these you shall not eat: the camel — it chews the cud but does not have split hooves; it is unclean for you.
The rock hyrax — it chews the cud but does not have split hooves; it is unclean for you.
The hare — it chews the cud but does not have split hooves; it is unclean for you.
The pig — it has split hooves, a hoof completely divided, but does not chew the cud; it is unclean for you.
You shall not eat their flesh, and you shall not touch their carcasses — they are unclean for you.
Among all creatures in the waters — in the seas or in the rivers — any creature that has fins and scales you may eat.
But anything in the seas or rivers that does not have fins and scales — all the swarming creatures in the water, all the living things that are in the water — they are detestable to you.
They shall remain detestable to you; you shall not eat their flesh, and you shall regard their carcasses as detestable.
Everything in the water without fins and scales is detestable to you.
The following birds you shall regard as detestable — they shall not be eaten, for they are detestable: the eagle, the bearded vulture, the black vulture,
the red kite and every kind of black kite,
every kind of raven,
the ostrich, the nighthawk, the seagull, and every kind of hawk,
the little owl, the cormorant, the great owl,
the barn owl, the desert owl, the carrion vulture,
the stork, every kind of heron, the hoopoe, and the bat.
All winged insects that go on all fours are detestable to you.
But among all winged insects that go on all fours, you may eat those that have jointed legs above their feet — legs with which to leap on the ground.
Of these you may eat: every kind of locust, every kind of cricket, every kind of katydid, and every kind of grasshopper.
But all other winged insects that have four legs are detestable to you.
By these you shall make yourselves unclean: whoever touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening,
and whoever carries any part of their carcass shall wash their clothes and be unclean until evening.
Any animal that has hooves but no split, and does not chew the cud — it is unclean for you; whoever touches it shall be unclean.
All creatures that walk on their paws among the animals that go on all fours are unclean for you; whoever touches their carcass shall be unclean until evening.
Whoever carries their carcass shall wash their clothes and be unclean until evening — they are unclean for you.
Among the creatures that swarm on the ground, these are unclean for you: the mole rat, the mouse, every kind of great lizard,
the gecko, the monitor lizard, the common lizard, the sand lizard, and the chameleon.
These are unclean for you among all the swarming things. Whoever touches them when they are dead shall be unclean until evening.

Anything on which any of them falls when dead — any wooden article, clothing, leather, or sacking — any such article used for any purpose shall be put in water and be unclean until evening; then it shall be clean.
Any clay vessel into which any of them falls shall be unclean, and you shall break it.
Any food that could be eaten — food on which water has come — shall be unclean; and any drinkable liquid in any such vessel shall be unclean.
Anything on which any of their carcasses falls shall be unclean: an oven or a cooking range shall be torn down — they are unclean and shall remain unclean for you.
But a spring or a cistern that holds water shall remain clean; whoever touches their carcass in it shall be unclean.
If any part of their carcass falls on seed grain that is to be sown, it remains clean.
But if water has been put on the seed and any part of their carcass falls on it, it is unclean for you.
If an animal you are permitted to eat dies on its own, whoever touches its carcass shall be unclean until evening.
Whoever eats from its carcass shall wash their clothes and be unclean until evening. Whoever carries its carcass shall wash their clothes and be unclean until evening.
Every creature that swarms on the ground is detestable — it shall not be eaten.
Whatever moves on its belly, whatever goes on all fours, or whatever has many legs — any creature that swarms on the ground — you shall not eat them, for they are detestable.
Do not make yourselves detestable by any creature that swarms. Do not defile yourselves by them so as to become unclean.
For I am the LORD your God. Consecrate yourselves, therefore, and be holy — for I am holy. You shall not defile yourselves by any creature that swarms on the ground.
For I am the LORD who brought you up from the land of Egypt to be your God. You shall be holy, for I am holy.
This is the law about animals and birds and every living creature that moves through the water and every creature that swarms on the ground,
to distinguish between the unclean and the clean, and between the living creature that may be eaten and the one that may not be eaten.”
YHWH speaks to Moses:
“Say to the people of Israel: When a woman conceives and gives birth to a son, she shall be unclean for seven days — unclean as in the days of her menstrual impurity.
On the eighth day the flesh of the child’s foreskin shall be circumcised.
She shall then remain for thirty-three days in the blood of her purification. She shall not touch anything sacred or enter the sanctuary until the days of her purification are complete.
If she gives birth to a daughter, she shall be unclean for two weeks — as in her menstruation — and she shall remain for sixty-six days in the blood of her purification.

When the days of her purification are complete — whether for a son or a daughter — she shall bring to the priest at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting a lamb in its first year as a burnt offering and a young pigeon or a turtledove as a sin offering.

The priest shall present these before the LORD and make atonement for her, and she shall be clean from the flow of her blood. This is the law for the woman who gives birth — whether to a son or a daughter.

If she cannot afford a lamb, she shall bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons — one for a burnt offering and one for a sin offering. The priest shall make atonement for her, and she shall be clean.”
YHWH speaks to Moses and Aaron:
“When a person has on their skin a swelling, a scab, or a bright spot that becomes a diseased affliction, they shall be brought to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons the priests.

The priest shall examine the diseased spot. If the hair in the spot has turned white and the spot appears deeper than the surrounding skin, it is a diseased affliction. The priest shall examine it and declare the person unclean.
If the bright spot on the skin is white but does not appear deeper than the skin, and no hair has turned white, the priest shall isolate the affected person for seven days.
On the seventh day the priest shall examine them again. If in his assessment the spot has not spread and no white hair has appeared in it, the priest shall isolate them for another seven days.

On the seventh day the priest shall examine them once more. If the spot has faded and has not spread on the skin, the priest shall declare them clean — it is only a scab. They shall wash their clothes and be clean.
But if the scab spreads further on the skin after they have appeared before the priest for their cleansing, they shall come before the priest again.
The priest shall examine them. If the scab has spread on the skin, he shall declare them unclean — it is a diseased affliction.
When a diseased affliction is on a person, they shall be brought to the priest.
The priest shall examine them. If there is a white swelling on the skin that has turned the hair white and there is raw flesh in the swelling,
it is a chronic skin disease. The priest shall declare them unclean. He need not isolate them, for they are already unclean.
If the disease breaks out widely on the skin and covers the entire body of the affected person from head to foot — everywhere the priest looks —
and the priest sees that the disease has covered all the body, he shall declare the person clean. Since it has entirely turned white, they are clean.
But whenever raw flesh appears, they shall be unclean.
When the priest sees the raw flesh, he shall declare them unclean — raw flesh is unclean; it is a diseased affliction.
But if the raw flesh turns white again, they shall come to the priest,
who shall examine them. If the spot has turned white, the priest shall declare the person clean — they are clean.
When a person has a boil on their skin and it heals,
and in the place of the boil there appears a white swelling or a reddish-white bright spot, they shall present themselves to the priest.
The priest shall examine it. If it appears deeper than the skin and the hair has turned white, the priest shall declare them unclean — it is a diseased affliction that has broken out in the boil.
But if the priest examines it and there is no white hair in it, it is not deeper than the skin and has faded, the priest shall isolate them for seven days.
If it spreads on the skin, the priest shall declare them unclean — it is an affliction.
But if the bright spot stays in place and has not spread, it is the scar from the boil. The priest shall declare them clean.
When skin has a burn injury from fire, and the raw flesh of the burn becomes a bright spot — reddish-white or white —

the priest shall examine it. If the hair in the bright spot has turned white and it appears deeper than the skin, it is a diseased affliction that has broken out in the burn. The priest shall declare them unclean — it is a diseased affliction.
But if the priest examines it and there is no white hair in the spot, it is not deeper than the skin and has faded, the priest shall isolate them for seven days.
On the seventh day the priest shall examine them. If it has spread on the skin, the priest shall declare them unclean — it is a diseased affliction.
But if the bright spot has not spread and is no brighter than before, it is the scar of the burn. The priest shall declare them clean — it is only the mark of the burn.
When a man or woman has a diseased spot on the head or chin,

the priest shall examine the spot. If it appears deeper than the skin and there is thin yellow hair in it, the priest shall declare them unclean — it is a scaly condition, a skin disease of the head or chin.
If the priest examines the scaly spot and it does not appear deeper than the skin and there is no black hair in it, the priest shall isolate the person for seven days.
On the seventh day the priest shall examine the condition. If it has not spread and there is no yellow hair and it does not appear deeper than the skin,
the person shall shave themselves — but not the scaly spot. The priest shall isolate them for another seven days.

On the seventh day the priest shall examine the scaling condition. If it has not spread on the skin and does not appear deeper than the skin, the priest shall declare them clean. They shall wash their clothes and be clean.
But if the scaly condition spreads on the skin after they have been declared clean,
the priest shall examine them. If the condition has spread on the skin, the priest need not look for yellow hair — the person is unclean.
But if the condition appears to have stopped spreading and black hair has grown in it, it has healed. The person is clean, and the priest shall declare them clean.
When a man or woman has bright spots on the skin — white bright spots —
the priest shall examine them. If the bright spots on the skin are dull white, it is only a harmless rash that has broken out on the skin — the person is clean.
A man whose hair has fallen from his head is bald; he is clean.
If his hair has fallen from his forehead, he has a receding hairline; he is clean.
But if there is a reddish-white diseased spot on the bald head or bald forehead, it is a skin disease breaking out there.
The priest shall examine him. If the swelling of the diseased spot is reddish-white on the bald head or forehead, appearing as a skin disease of the body,
he is diseased and unclean. The priest shall declare him unclean — the disease is on his head.
The person who bears the diseased affliction shall wear torn clothes and let their hair hang loose, and shall cover their upper lip and call out: Unclean! Unclean!
They shall remain unclean as long as they carry the disease. They are unclean — they shall live alone. Their dwelling shall be outside the camp.
When a diseased spot appears in a garment — in a woolen or a linen garment,
in the warp or the woof of linen or wool, in a leather article or in anything made of leather —
if the spot in the garment, the leather, the warp or the woof, or any leather article is greenish or reddish, it is a diseased spot. It shall be shown to the priest.
The priest shall examine the diseased spot and shut away the affected article for seven days.
On the seventh day he shall examine the spot. If it has spread in the garment, in the warp or the woof, or in the leather — whatever its use — the spot is a persistent mildew. It is unclean.
He shall burn the garment — or the warp or woof of wool or linen, or any leather article in which the spot appears. Since it is a persistent mildew, it shall be burned in fire.
But if the priest examines it and the spot has not spread in the garment, in the warp or woof, or in any leather article,
the priest shall command that the article with the spot be washed and set aside for another seven days.

After washing, the priest shall examine the spot again. If the spot has not changed its appearance and has not spread, it is unclean. You shall burn it in fire — whether the rot is on the inner face or the outer, it is a persistent mildew.
But if the priest sees that the spot has faded after washing, he shall tear it out of the garment, the leather, or the warp or woof.
If the spot appears again in the garment, in the warp or the woof, or in the leather article, it is breaking out afresh — you shall burn in fire whatever has the spot.
The garment, warp, woof, or any leather article from which the spot disappears after washing shall be washed again, and it shall be clean.
This is the law about a diseased spot in a woolen or linen garment, in the warp or the woof, or in any leather article — for declaring it clean or unclean.”
YHWH speaks to Moses:
“This is the law for the person with a diseased affliction on the day of their cleansing. They shall be brought to the priest.
The priest shall go outside the camp and examine them. If the diseased affliction has been healed in the person,
the priest shall command that two living clean birds, cedar wood, crimson yarn, and hyssop be brought for the person being cleansed.
The priest shall command that one of the birds be slaughtered over a clay vessel containing fresh water.
He shall take the living bird with the cedar wood, the crimson yarn, and the hyssop and dip them in the blood of the bird slaughtered over the fresh water.
He shall sprinkle it seven times on the one being cleansed of the diseased affliction, declare them clean, and release the living bird over the open field.

The person being cleansed shall wash their clothes, shave off all their hair, and bathe in water — and they will be clean. After this they may enter the camp, but they shall remain outside their tent for seven days.
On the seventh day they shall shave off all their hair — head, beard, and eyebrows, every hair — wash their clothes, and bathe in water. They will be clean.

On the eighth day they shall bring two male lambs without blemish, one ewe lamb in its first year without blemish, three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering, and one log of oil.
The priest who declares them clean shall present both the person being cleansed and these offerings before the LORD at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
The priest shall take one of the male lambs and offer it as a guilt offering, along with the log of oil, and wave them as a wave offering before the LORD.
He shall slaughter the lamb in the holy place where the sin offering and the burnt offering are slaughtered — for the guilt offering, like the sin offering, belongs to the priest; it is most holy.

The priest shall take some of the blood of the guilt offering and put it on the lobe of the right ear of the one being cleansed, on the thumb of their right hand, and on the big toe of their right foot.
The priest shall take some of the log of oil and pour it into the palm of his own left hand,
dip his right finger in the oil in his left palm, and sprinkle some of the oil with his finger seven times before the LORD.

Some of the remaining oil in his palm the priest shall put on the lobe of the right ear of the one being cleansed, on the thumb of their right hand, and on the big toe of their right foot — over the blood of the guilt offering.
The rest of the oil in the priest’s palm he shall put on the head of the one being cleansed. The priest shall make atonement for them before the LORD.
The priest shall then offer the sin offering and make atonement for the one being cleansed from their uncleanness. After that he shall slaughter the burnt offering.
The priest shall offer the burnt offering and the grain offering on the altar. The priest shall make atonement for them, and they shall be clean.

But if they are poor and cannot afford these things, they shall bring one male lamb as a guilt offering to be waved — to make atonement for them — together with one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering, and a log of oil,
and two turtledoves or two young pigeons, whichever they can afford — one as a sin offering and one as a burnt offering.
On the eighth day they shall bring them for their cleansing to the priest, at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting before the LORD.
The priest shall take the guilt-offering lamb and the log of oil and wave them as a wave offering before the LORD.

He shall slaughter the guilt-offering lamb and take some of its blood and put it on the lobe of the right ear of the one being cleansed, on the thumb of their right hand, and on the big toe of their right foot.
The priest shall pour some of the oil into the palm of his own left hand
and with his right finger sprinkle some of the oil from his left palm seven times before the LORD.

Some of the oil in his palm the priest shall put on the lobe of the right ear of the one being cleansed, on the thumb of their right hand, and on the big toe of their right foot — in the place where the blood of the guilt offering was put.
The rest of the oil in the priest’s palm he shall put on the head of the one being cleansed, to make atonement for them before the LORD.
Then they shall offer one of the turtledoves or young pigeons, whichever they can afford —
one as a sin offering and one as a burnt offering, together with the grain offering. The priest shall make atonement before the LORD for the one being cleansed.
This is the law for the person who has a diseased affliction and cannot afford the full offerings for their cleansing.”
YHWH speaks again to Moses and Aaron:
“When you come into the land of Canaan, which I am giving you as a possession, and I put a diseased spot in a house in the land of your possession,
the owner of the house shall come and tell the priest: There appears to be some kind of disease in my house.

The priest shall command that the house be cleared before he goes in to examine the disease, so that everything in the house will not become unclean. After this the priest shall go in to inspect the house.
He shall examine the diseased spot. If the spot on the walls consists of greenish or reddish depressions that appear to go deeper than the surface,
the priest shall go out of the house to its entrance and shut the house up for seven days.
On the seventh day the priest shall return to inspect. If the disease has spread on the walls of the house,
the priest shall command that the diseased stones be torn out and thrown outside the city into an unclean place.
He shall have the inside of the house scraped all around, and the plaster that has been scraped off shall be dumped outside the city in an unclean place.
Then they shall take other stones and put them in the place of the old ones, and take fresh plaster and replaster the house.
If the diseased spot breaks out again in the house after the stones have been torn out and the house has been scraped and replastered,
the priest shall come and examine it. If the disease has spread in the house, it is a persistent mildew — the house is unclean.
He shall tear down the house — its stones, its timber, and all the plaster — and carry them outside the city to an unclean place.
Anyone who enters the house during the time it is shut up shall be unclean until evening.
Anyone who lies down or eats in the house shall wash their clothes.
But if the priest comes and examines it and the disease has not spread after the house was replastered, he shall declare the house clean — the disease is healed.
To cleanse the house he shall take two birds, cedar wood, crimson yarn, and hyssop,
and slaughter one of the birds over a clay vessel containing fresh water.
He shall take the cedar wood, the hyssop, the crimson yarn, and the living bird, and dip them in the blood of the slaughtered bird and in the fresh water, and sprinkle the house seven times.
He shall cleanse the house with the blood of the bird, the fresh water, the living bird, the cedar wood, the hyssop, and the crimson yarn.
He shall release the living bird outside the city over the open field. He shall make atonement for the house, and it will be clean.
This is the law for any diseased affliction — for scaly conditions,
for mildew in garments or in houses,
for swellings, scabs, and bright spots —
to determine when something is unclean and when it is clean. This is the law concerning diseased afflictions.”
YHWH speaks to Moses and Aaron:
“Say to the people of Israel: When any man has a discharge from his body, his discharge is unclean.
This is how his uncleanness applies: whether his body runs with the discharge or holds it back, it is unclean.
Every bed on which the man with the discharge lies shall be unclean, and everything on which he sits shall be unclean.
Anyone who touches his bed shall wash their clothes and bathe in water and be unclean until evening.
Whoever sits on anything the man with the discharge has sat on shall wash their clothes and bathe in water and be unclean until evening.
Whoever touches the body of the man with the discharge shall wash their clothes and bathe in water and be unclean until evening.
If the man with the discharge spits on someone who is clean, they shall wash their clothes and bathe in water and be unclean until evening.
Any saddle on which the man with the discharge rides shall be unclean.
Whoever touches anything that was under him shall be unclean until evening, and whoever carries such things shall wash their clothes and bathe in water and be unclean until evening.
Anyone the man with the discharge touches — without first rinsing his hands in water — shall wash their clothes and bathe in water and be unclean until evening.
A clay vessel he touches shall be broken; every wooden article shall be rinsed with water.
When a man with a discharge is healed of it, he shall count seven days for his cleansing, wash his clothes, and bathe his body in fresh water — and he will be clean.
On the eighth day he shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and come before the LORD at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting and give them to the priest.
The priest shall offer them — one as a sin offering and one as a burnt offering. The priest shall make atonement for him before the LORD for his discharge.
When a man has an emission of semen, he shall bathe his whole body in water and be unclean until evening.
Every garment and every leather article on which the semen comes shall be washed in water and be unclean until evening.
If a man lies with a woman and there is an emission of semen, both of them shall bathe in water and be unclean until evening.
When a woman has a discharge of blood from her body, she shall be in her menstrual separation for seven days. Whoever touches her shall be unclean until evening.
Everything on which she lies during her menstrual separation shall be unclean, and everything on which she sits shall be unclean.
Whoever touches her bed shall wash their clothes and bathe in water and be unclean until evening.
Whoever touches anything on which she has sat shall wash their clothes and bathe in water and be unclean until evening.
Whether it is the bed or anything else on which she has sat — when anyone touches it, they shall be unclean until evening.
If a man lies with her and her menstrual blood touches him, he shall be unclean for seven days, and every bed on which he lies shall be unclean.

If a woman has a discharge of blood for many days — not at the time of her monthly period — or if her discharge continues beyond her usual time, she shall be unclean as long as her discharge lasts, just as during her menstruation.
Every bed on which she lies during all the days of her discharge shall be as her menstrual bed, and everything on which she sits shall be unclean, as in the uncleanness of her menstruation.
Whoever touches these things shall be unclean and shall wash their clothes and bathe in water and be unclean until evening.
But if she is healed of her discharge, she shall count seven days, and after that she shall be clean.
On the eighth day she shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them to the priest at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
The priest shall offer one as a sin offering and one as a burnt offering. The priest shall make atonement for her before the LORD for her unclean discharge.
You shall keep the people of Israel separate from their uncleanness, so that they do not die in their uncleanness by defiling my dwelling that is in their midst.
This is the law for the man with a discharge, and for the man who has an emission of semen making him unclean,
and for the woman in her menstrual impurity — for anyone, male or female, who has a
discharge — and for the man who lies with a woman who is unclean.”
YHWH speaks to Moses after the death of Aaron’s two sons — after they drew near before the LORD and died.

The LORD says to Moses: “Tell your brother Aaron that he must not come at any time into the holy place inside the curtain, before the atonement cover on the ark — or he will die. For I appear in the cloud over the atonement cover.
This is how Aaron shall enter the holy place: with a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.

He shall put on the holy linen tunic, with linen undergarments next to his body, and tie the linen sash around him, and put on the linen turban. These are the holy garments. He shall bathe his body in water and then put them on.
From the congregation of the people of Israel he shall take two male goats for a sin offering and one ram for a burnt offering.
Aaron shall offer the bull as a sin offering for himself and make atonement for himself and for his household.
He shall take the two goats and present them before the LORD at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
Aaron shall cast lots over the two goats — one lot for the LORD and one lot for Azazel.
Aaron shall bring the goat on which the lot fell for the LORD and offer it as a sin offering.
But the goat on which the lot fell for Azazel shall be presented alive before the LORD to make atonement over it, that it may be sent away to Azazel into the wilderness.
Aaron shall present the bull as a sin offering for himself and shall make atonement for himself and for his household. He shall slaughter the bull.
He shall take a censer full of burning coals from the altar before the LORD, and two handfuls of finely ground fragrant incense, and bring them inside the curtain.
He shall put the incense on the fire before the LORD, so that the cloud of incense covers the atonement cover over the covenant. Then he will not die.

He shall take some of the bull’s blood and sprinkle it with his finger on the front of the atonement cover, and before the atonement cover he shall sprinkle some of the blood seven times with his finger.

He shall then slaughter the goat of the sin offering for the people and bring its blood inside the curtain. He shall do with its blood as he did with the bull’s blood — sprinkling it on the atonement cover and before it.

Thus he shall make atonement for the holy place, because of the uncleannesses of the people of Israel and because of their transgressions — all their sins. He shall do the same for the Tent of Meeting, which dwells among them in the midst of their uncleanness.

No one shall be in the Tent of Meeting from the time Aaron enters to make atonement in the holy place until he comes out and has made atonement for himself, for his household, and for all the assembly of Israel.

Then he shall go out to the altar that is before the LORD and make atonement for it. He shall take some of the bull’s blood and some of the goat’s blood and put it on the horns of the altar all around.
He shall sprinkle some of the blood on it with his finger seven times, and cleanse it and consecrate it from the uncleannesses of the people of Israel.
When he has finished making atonement for the holy place, the Tent of Meeting, and the altar, he shall present the live goat.

Aaron shall lay both his hands on the head of the live goat and confess over it all the iniquities of the people of Israel and all their transgressions — all their sins. He shall put them on the head of the goat and send it away into the wilderness by the hand of a man appointed for the task.
The goat shall carry on itself all their iniquities to a remote and desolate place, and the man shall release it in the wilderness.
Aaron shall enter the Tent of Meeting and remove the linen garments he wore when he entered the sanctuary, and leave them there.

He shall bathe his body in water in a holy place, put on his regular garments, then come out and offer his own burnt offering and the burnt offering of the people, making atonement for himself and for the people.
He shall burn the fat of the sin offering on the altar.
The man who released the goat for Azazel shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and after that he may enter the camp.
The bull and the goat of the sin offering — whose blood was brought in to make atonement in the holy place — shall be carried outside the camp. Their hide, flesh, and dung shall be burned in fire.
The man who burns them shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and after that he may enter the camp.
This shall be a lasting ordinance for you: on the tenth day of the seventh month you shall afflict yourselves and do no work — whether native-born or a foreigner living among you.
For on this day atonement shall be made for you, to cleanse you. From all your sins you shall be clean before the LORD.
It is a sabbath of complete rest for you, and you shall afflict yourselves — it is a lasting ordinance.
The priest who is anointed and ordained to serve in his father’s place shall perform the atonement rite. He shall put on the holy linen garments
and make atonement for the holy sanctuary, for the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and for the priests and for all the people of the assembly.
This shall be a lasting ordinance for you: once a year atonement shall be made for all the sins of the people of Israel.”
And it was done just as the LORD commanded Moses.
YHWH speaks to Moses:
“Speak to Aaron and his sons and to all the people of Israel and say to them: This is what the LORD has commanded.
Any man from the house of Israel who slaughters an ox, a lamb, or a goat — in the camp or outside the camp —

and does not bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting to offer it as a gift to the LORD before the LORD’s dwelling: that man shall be held guilty of bloodshed. He has shed blood and shall be cut off from among his people.

This is so that the people of Israel will bring their slaughter — whatever they have been slaughtering out in the open field — to the LORD at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, to the priest, and sacrifice it there as a peace offering to the LORD.
The priest shall sprinkle the blood on the LORD’s altar at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting and burn the fat as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
They shall no longer sacrifice their offerings to the goat-demons, after whom they have gone prostituting. This is a lasting ordinance for them throughout their generations.
Say to them also: Any man from the house of Israel, or any foreigner living among them, who offers a burnt offering or a sacrifice
and does not bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting to offer it to the LORD — that man shall be cut off from his people.
