If any man from the house of Israel or any foreigner living among them eats any blood, I will set my face against that person and cut them off from among their people.
For the life of the flesh is in the blood, and I have given it to you on the altar to make atonement for your lives. It is the blood that makes atonement, by the life it carries.
Therefore I say to the people of Israel: No person among you shall eat blood. No foreigner living among you shall eat blood.
Any man from the house of Israel or any foreigner living among them who hunts and catches a wild animal or a bird that may be eaten shall pour out its blood and cover it with earth.

For the life of every creature is its blood — it is its life. I say to the people of Israel: You shall not eat the blood of any creature, for the life of every creature is its blood. Whoever eats it shall be cut off.
Every person — native-born or foreigner — who eats what died of itself or was torn by wild animals shall wash their clothes and bathe in water and be unclean until evening. Then they will be clean.
But if they do not wash their clothes and bathe their body, they shall bear their guilt.”
YHWH speaks to Moses:
“Say to the people of Israel: I am the LORD your God.
You shall not do as they do in the land of Egypt, where you lived, and you shall not do as they do in the land of Canaan, where I am bringing you. You shall not follow their statutes.
You shall follow my ordinances and keep my statutes and walk by them. I am the LORD your God.
Keep my statutes and my ordinances. By doing them a person shall live. I am the LORD.
None of you shall approach any close relative to uncover their nakedness. I am the LORD.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father, which is the nakedness of your mother — she is your mother; you shall not uncover her nakedness.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s wife; it is your father’s nakedness.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your sister — your father’s daughter or your mother’s daughter, whether born in the household or outside it.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your son’s daughter or your daughter’s daughter — their nakedness is your own nakedness.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s wife’s daughter, born to your father; she is your sister.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s sister — she is your father’s own flesh.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your mother’s sister — she is your mother’s own flesh.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s brother — do not approach his wife; she is your aunt.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your daughter-in-law; she is your son’s wife. You shall not uncover her nakedness.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your brother’s wife; it is your brother’s nakedness.

You shall not uncover the nakedness of a woman and her daughter, and you shall not take her son’s daughter or her daughter’s daughter to uncover her nakedness. They are her own flesh — it is depravity.
You shall not take a woman as a rival wife to her sister, uncovering her nakedness alongside the other during her lifetime.
You shall not approach a woman to uncover her nakedness while she is in her menstrual impurity.
You shall not lie with your neighbor’s wife and so defile yourself with her.
You shall not give any of your children to be offered to Molech, and so profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.
You shall not lie with a male as with a woman; it is an abomination.
You shall not lie with any animal and defile yourself with it, nor shall a woman offer herself to an animal to mate with it — it is a perversion.
Do not defile yourselves by any of these things, for by all of them the nations I am driving out before you have defiled themselves.
The land itself became defiled, so I punished it for its sin — and the land vomited out its inhabitants.
But you shall keep my statutes and my ordinances and do none of these abominations — neither the native-born nor the foreigner living among you —
for all these abominations were done by the people of the land before you, and the land was defiled.
So the land does not vomit you out when you defile it, as it vomited out the nation that was before you.
For everyone who does any of these abominations shall be cut off from among their people.
Keep my charge: never practice any of these abominable customs that were practiced before you, and never defile yourselves by them. I am the LORD your God.”
YHWH speaks to Moses:
“Speak to all the congregation of the people of Israel and say to them: Be holy, for I the LORD your God am holy.
Each of you shall respect your mother and your father, and you shall keep my Sabbaths. I am the LORD your God.
Do not turn to idols or make for yourselves gods of cast metal. I am the LORD your God.
When you sacrifice a peace offering to the LORD, sacrifice it so that you may be accepted.
It shall be eaten on the day you sacrifice it, or on the next day. Whatever remains on the third day shall be burned in fire.
If it is eaten at all on the third day, it is defiled and will not be accepted.
Whoever eats it shall bear their guilt, for they have profaned what is holy to the LORD. That person shall be cut off from their people.
When you harvest the grain of your land, do not harvest all the way to the edges of your field, and do not gather the gleanings of your harvest.
Do not go over your vineyard a second time, and do not pick up the fallen grapes of your vineyard. Leave them for the poor and the foreigner. I am the LORD your God.
You shall not steal. You shall not deal falsely. You shall not lie to one another.
You shall not swear falsely by my name, and so profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.
You shall not defraud your neighbor or rob them. The wages of a hired worker shall not remain with you overnight until morning.
You shall not curse the deaf or put a stumbling block before the blind. You shall fear your God. I am the LORD.
You shall do no injustice in court. You shall not be partial to the poor or show deference to the great, but you shall judge your neighbor with justice.
You shall not go around spreading slander among your people. You shall not stand by while your neighbor’s life is in danger. I am the LORD.
You shall not hate your brother in your heart. You shall reprove your neighbor frankly, lest you incur guilt because of them.
You shall not take vengeance or bear a grudge against any of your people. You shall love your neighbor as yourself. I am the LORD.
Keep my statutes. Do not let your animals breed with a different kind. Do not sow your field with two kinds of seed. Do not wear a garment made of two kinds of material mixed together.

If a man lies with a woman sexually, and she is a slave betrothed to another man but has not yet been ransomed or given her freedom, an inquiry shall be held. They shall not be put to death, because she was not free.
But the man shall bring to the LORD at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting a ram as a guilt offering.
The priest shall make atonement for him with the guilt-offering ram before the LORD for the sin he has committed. He shall be forgiven for the sin.
When you come into the land and plant any tree for food, you shall treat its fruit as forbidden. For three years it shall be forbidden — it may not be eaten.
In the fourth year all its fruit shall be set apart as holy — an offering of praise to the LORD.
In the fifth year you may eat its fruit, that its yield may increase for you. I am the LORD your God.
You shall not eat anything with blood in it. You shall not practice divination or seek omens.
You shall not cut the hair at the sides of your head or clip the edges of your beard.
You shall not make any cuts in your body for the dead or tattoo yourselves. I am the LORD.
Do not profane your daughter by making her a prostitute, lest the land fall into prostitution and be filled with wickedness.
You shall keep my Sabbaths and revere my sanctuary. I am the LORD.
Do not turn to mediums or seek out spiritists, for you will be defiled by them. I am the LORD your God.
You shall stand up in the presence of the aged and show honor to the elderly. Fear your God. I am the LORD.
When a foreigner lives with you in your land, you shall not oppress them.
The foreigner living among you shall be treated like one native-born among you. You shall love them as yourself, for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
You shall do no wrong in judgment — in measures of length, weight, or quantity.
You shall have honest scales, honest weights, an honest ephah, and an honest hin. I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.
You shall keep all my statutes and all my ordinances and do them. I am the LORD.”
YHWH speaks to Moses:

“Say to the people of Israel: Any person from the people of Israel, or any foreigner living in Israel, who gives any of their children to Molech shall surely be put to death. The people of the land shall stone them.
I myself will set my face against that person and cut them off from among their people, because they gave their children to Molech and defiled my sanctuary and profaned my holy name.
If the people of the land turn a blind eye to that person when they give their children to Molech, and do not put them to death,
then I will set my face against that person and against their family, and I will cut them off from among their people — them and all who follow them in prostituting themselves after Molech.
If any person turns to mediums and spiritists, prostituting themselves after them, I will set my face against that person and cut them off from among their people.
Consecrate yourselves therefore and be holy, for I am the LORD your God.
Keep my statutes and do them. I am the LORD who makes you holy.
If anyone curses their father or mother, they shall surely be put to death. They have cursed their father or mother — their blood is on their own head.
If a man commits adultery with the wife of his neighbor, both the adulterer and the adulteress shall surely be put to death.
If a man lies with his father’s wife, he has uncovered his father’s nakedness. Both of them shall be put to death — their blood is on their own heads.
If a man lies with his daughter-in-law, both of them shall be put to death. They have committed a perversion — their blood is on their own heads.
If a man lies with a male as with a woman, both of them have committed an abomination. They shall be put to death — their blood is on their own heads.
If a man takes a woman and her mother also, it is depravity. He and they shall be burned in fire, that there may be no depravity among you.
If a man lies with an animal, he shall surely be put to death, and you shall kill the animal.
If a woman approaches any animal and mates with it, you shall kill the woman and the animal. They shall be put to death — their blood is on their own heads.

If a man takes his sister — his father’s daughter or his mother’s daughter — and sees her nakedness and she sees his, it is a disgrace. They shall be cut off in the sight of their people. He has uncovered his sister’s nakedness — he shall bear his guilt.
If a man lies with a woman during her menstrual period and uncovers her nakedness, he has exposed her flow and she has exposed her flow — both of them shall be cut off from among their people.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your mother’s sister or your father’s sister, for that is to lay bare one’s own flesh. They shall bear their guilt.
If a man lies with his uncle’s wife, he has uncovered his uncle’s nakedness. They shall bear their sin — they shall die childless.
If a man takes his brother’s wife, it is impurity. He has uncovered his brother’s nakedness — they shall be childless.
Keep all my statutes and all my ordinances and do them, so that the land where I am bringing you to live may not vomit you out.
You shall not walk in the customs of the nation I am driving out before you, for they did all these things — and I detested them.
But I have said to you: You shall inherit their land — I will give it to you to possess, a land flowing with milk and honey. I am the LORD your God, who has separated you from the peoples.

You shall therefore distinguish between the clean animal and the unclean, and between the clean bird and the unclean. Do not make yourselves detestable through animal or bird or anything that swarms on the ground, which I have set apart for you as unclean.
You shall be holy to me, for I the LORD am holy and have separated you from the peoples to be mine.
A man or a woman who is a medium or a spiritist shall surely be put to death — they shall be stoned. Their blood is on their own heads.”
YHWH says to Moses: “Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron, and say to them:
A priest shall not defile himself by contact with the dead among his people, except for his closest relatives — his mother, his father, his son, his daughter, his brother,
and his virgin sister who is near to him and has no husband — for her he may defile himself.
He shall not defile himself as a husband among his people and so profane himself.
They shall not shave their heads, nor shave off the edges of their beards, nor make any cuts in their flesh.
They shall be holy to their God and not profane the name of their God, for they offer the LORD’s gifts given by fire — the food of their God. They shall be holy.
They shall not marry a woman who has been defiled by prostitution, nor shall they marry a woman divorced from her husband — for the priest is holy to his God.
You shall consecrate him, for he offers the food of your God. He shall be holy to you, for I the LORD who makes you holy am holy.
If a priest’s daughter profanes herself through prostitution, she profanes her father. She shall be burned in fire.
The priest who is greatest among his brothers — on whose head the anointing oil has been poured and who has been consecrated to wear the garments — shall not dishevel his hair or tear his garments.
He shall not go near any dead body. He shall not defile himself even for his father or his mother.
He shall not leave the sanctuary or profane the sanctuary of his God, for the consecration of the anointing oil of his God is on him. I am the LORD.
He shall marry a woman who is a virgin.
A widow, a divorced woman, a woman who has been defiled, or a prostitute — these he shall not marry. He shall marry only a virgin from his own people,
so that he does not profane his offspring among his people — for I am the LORD who makes him holy.
YHWH speaks to Moses:
“Say to Aaron: No man among your descendants throughout their generations who has a blemish may come near to offer the food of his God.
No man with a blemish may approach — whether a man who is blind or lame, or one with a disfigured face or a limb that is too long,
or a man with a broken foot or a broken hand,
or a hunchback or a dwarf, or a man with a defect in his sight, or a man with a skin rash or scabs, or a man with crushed testicles.
No descendant of Aaron the priest who has a blemish shall come near to offer the LORD’s gifts given by fire. Since he has a blemish, he shall not come near to offer the food of his God.
He may eat the food of his God — both the most holy and the holy —
but he shall not go before the curtain or approach the altar, because he has a blemish. He shall not profane my sanctuaries, for I am the LORD who makes them holy.”
So Moses speaks to Aaron and his sons and to all the people of Israel.
YHWH speaks to Moses:
“Tell Aaron and his sons to treat with care the holy things that the people of Israel dedicate to me, so they do not profane my holy name. I am the LORD.

Say to them: If any man from all your descendants approaches the holy things that the people of Israel dedicate to the LORD while he is unclean, that person shall be cut off from before me. I am the LORD.

Any man from the descendants of Aaron who has a skin disease or a discharge shall not eat of the holy things until he is clean. Whoever touches anything made unclean by contact with a corpse, or a man who has had an emission of semen,
or whoever touches any swarming creature by which he is made unclean, or a person who makes him unclean — whatever the uncleanness —
the person who touches any such thing shall be unclean until evening and shall not eat of the holy things unless he has bathed his body in water.
When the sun goes down he shall be clean, and afterward he may eat of the holy things, for they are his food.
He shall not eat what has died of itself or what has been torn by wild animals, making himself unclean by it. I am the LORD.
They shall keep my charge, lest they bear sin for it and die because of it when they profane it. I am the LORD who makes them holy.
No unauthorized person shall eat a holy thing. A guest of the priest or a hired worker shall not eat of the holy things.
But if a priest purchases a slave as his property, that person may eat of it, and anyone born in his house may eat his food.
If a priest’s daughter marries a man outside the priestly family, she shall not eat of the contribution of the holy things.

But if a priest’s daughter becomes a widow or is divorced — and has no children and returns to her father’s house as in her youth — she may eat of her father’s food. No unauthorized person shall eat of it.
If a man eats a holy thing unintentionally, he shall add a fifth of its value to it and give the holy thing to the priest.
The priests shall not allow the holy things of the people of Israel to be profaned,
which they offer to the LORD — lest they cause the people to bear the guilt of a trespass by eating their holy things. For I am the LORD who makes them holy.
YHWH speaks to Moses:

“Speak to Aaron and his sons and all the people of Israel and say to them: When any person from the house of Israel or a foreigner living in Israel presents a burnt offering as a vow or a freewill offering to the LORD,
to be accepted it must be a male without blemish from the cattle, sheep, or goats.
You shall not offer anything that has a blemish, for it will not be accepted for you.
When anyone offers a peace offering to the LORD from the herd or flock — whether as a vow or as a freewill offering — it must be without blemish to be accepted. There shall be no defect in it.
Animals that are blind or injured or maimed, or that have a discharge, itch, or scabs — you shall not offer these to the LORD or give them as a gift given by fire on the altar.
A bull or a lamb with a limb too long or too short you may offer as a freewill offering, but it will not be accepted for a vow.
Any animal with bruised, crushed, torn, or cut testicles you shall not offer to the LORD. You shall not do this in your land,
and you shall not accept such animals from a foreigner as the food of your God. Since they are damaged, with a blemish in them, they will not be accepted for you.
YHWH speaks to Moses:
“When an ox or sheep or goat is born, it shall remain seven days with its mother, and from the eighth day on it may be accepted as a gift given by fire to the LORD.
But you shall not slaughter an ox or a sheep together with its young on the same day.
When you sacrifice a thanksgiving offering to the LORD, sacrifice it so that you may be accepted.
It shall be eaten on the same day. You shall leave none of it until morning. I am the LORD.
Keep my commandments and do them. I am the LORD.
You shall not profane my holy name, that I may be sanctified among the people of Israel. I am the LORD who makes you holy,
who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD.”
YHWH speaks to Moses:
“Speak to the people of Israel and say to them: These are the appointed times of the LORD that you shall proclaim as holy convocations — they are my appointed times.
Six days shall work be done, but on the seventh day there shall be a Sabbath of complete rest, a holy convocation. You shall not do any work. It is a Sabbath to the LORD in all your dwellings.
These are the appointed times of the LORD, the holy convocations, which you shall proclaim at their appointed times.
In the first month, on the fourteenth day at twilight, is the LORD’s Passover.
And on the fifteenth day of the same month is the Feast of Unleavened Bread to the LORD. For seven days you shall eat unleavened bread.
On the first day you shall hold a holy convocation. You shall not do any ordinary work.
But you shall present a gift given by fire to the LORD for seven days. On the seventh day is a holy convocation — you shall not do any ordinary work.”
YHWH speaks to Moses:
“Speak to the people of Israel and say to them: When you come into the land that I give you and harvest its grain, you shall bring the firstfruits sheaf of your harvest to the priest.
He shall wave the sheaf before the LORD, so that you may be accepted. On the day after the Sabbath the priest shall wave it.
On the day you wave the sheaf, you shall offer as a burnt offering to the LORD a male lamb without blemish in its first year.
Its grain offering shall be two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil — a gift given by fire to the LORD as a pleasing aroma — and its drink offering shall be a quarter of a hin of wine.

You shall eat no bread or roasted grain or fresh grain until this very day, until you have brought the offering of your God. This is a lasting ordinance throughout your generations in all your dwellings.”
YHWH speaks to Moses:

“You shall count seven full weeks from the day after the Sabbath — from the day you brought the wave-sheaf offering. Count fifty days to the day after the seventh Sabbath. Then you shall present a new grain offering to the LORD.
From wherever you live, bring two loaves of bread to be waved, made from two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour, baked with leaven, as firstfruits to the LORD.

You shall present with the bread seven lambs without blemish in their first year, one bull from the herd, and two rams as a burnt offering to the LORD, with their grain offering and drink offerings — a gift given by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
You shall also offer one male goat as a sin offering and two male lambs in their first year as peace offerings.
The priest shall wave them — the two lambs — with the bread of the firstfruits as a wave offering before the LORD. They shall be holy to the LORD for the priest.
On that same day you shall make a proclamation and hold a holy convocation. You shall not do any ordinary work. This is a lasting ordinance in all your dwellings throughout your generations.

When you reap the harvest of your land, do not reap to the very edges of your field, and do not gather the gleanings of your harvest. Leave them for the poor and the foreigner. I am the LORD your God.”
YHWH speaks to Moses:
“Speak to the people of Israel: In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, you shall observe a day of complete rest, a memorial proclaimed with a trumpet blast — a holy convocation.
You shall not do any ordinary work, and you shall present a gift given by fire to the LORD.”
YHWH speaks to Moses:
“The tenth day of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement. Hold a holy convocation, afflict yourselves, and present a gift given by fire to the LORD.
You shall not do any work on that very day, for it is the Day of Atonement, to make atonement for you before the LORD your God.
Whoever does not afflict themselves on that very day shall be cut off from their people.
And whoever does any work on that very day — I will destroy that person from among their people.
You shall not do any work. This is a lasting ordinance throughout your generations in all your dwellings.

It shall be a Sabbath of complete rest for you, and you shall afflict yourselves. From the evening of the ninth day of the month until the following evening — evening to evening — you shall keep your Sabbath.”
YHWH speaks to Moses:
“Say to the people of Israel: On the fifteenth day of this seventh month is the Feast of Booths to the LORD, lasting seven days.
On the first day shall be a holy convocation. You shall not do any ordinary work.

For seven days you shall present a gift given by fire to the LORD. On the eighth day you shall hold a holy convocation and present a gift given by fire to the LORD. It is a solemn assembly — you shall not do any ordinary work.

These are the appointed times of the LORD that you shall proclaim as holy convocations — for presenting to the LORD gifts given by fire: burnt offerings, grain offerings, sacrifices, and drink offerings, each on its proper day —
besides the LORD’s Sabbaths, besides your gifts, besides all your vow offerings, and besides all your freewill offerings that you give to the LORD.

But on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when you have gathered in the produce of the land, you shall celebrate the feast of the LORD for seven days. On the first day there shall be complete rest, and on the eighth day complete rest.
On the first day you shall take the fruit of the finest trees, branches of palms, boughs of leafy trees, and willows of the brook. You shall rejoice before the LORD your God for seven days.
You shall celebrate it as a feast to the LORD for seven days in the year. This is a lasting ordinance throughout your generations. You shall celebrate it in the seventh month.
You shall dwell in booths for seven days. Every native-born Israelite shall dwell in booths,
so that your generations may know that I made the people of Israel live in booths when I brought them out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.”
So Moses declares to the people of Israel the appointed times of the LORD.
YHWH speaks to Moses:
“Command the people of Israel to bring you pure beaten olive oil for the lamp, so that a light may burn continually.
Outside the curtain of the covenant, in the Tent of Meeting, Aaron shall tend it from evening to morning before the LORD continually. It is a lasting ordinance throughout your generations.
He shall tend the lamps on the pure gold lampstand before the LORD continually.
You shall take fine flour and bake twelve loaves from it, two-tenths of an ephah in each loaf.
Set them in two rows of six on the table of pure gold before the LORD.
Put pure frankincense on each row, to serve as a memorial portion — a gift given by fire to the LORD.
Every Sabbath Aaron shall arrange them before the LORD continually on behalf of the people of Israel as a lasting covenant.
They shall belong to Aaron and his sons, who shall eat them in a holy place — for they are most holy to him from the LORD’s gifts given by fire, a lasting portion.”
A man goes out among the people of Israel — the son of an Israelite woman and an Egyptian man. He gets into a fight in the camp with an Israelite man.
The son of the Israelite woman blasphemes the Name with a curse. They bring him to Moses. His mother’s name is Shelomith daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.
They put him in custody until the LORD’s will becomes clear to them.
YHWH speaks to Moses:
“Bring the one who has cursed outside the camp. Let all who heard him lay their hands on his head, and let the whole congregation stone him.
Say to the people of Israel: Anyone who curses their God shall bear their sin.

Whoever blasphemes the name of the LORD shall surely be put to death. The whole congregation shall stone them. Foreigner and native-born alike — when they blaspheme the Name, they shall be put to death.
Whoever takes a human life shall surely be put to death.
Whoever takes an animal’s life shall make it good — life for life.
If anyone injures their neighbor, what they have done shall be done to them —
fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth. Whatever injury they gave another person shall be given to them.
Whoever kills an animal shall make it good. Whoever kills a person shall be put to death.
You shall have the same rule for the foreigner as for the native-born — for I am the LORD your God.”
So Moses speaks to the people of Israel. They take the one who has cursed outside the camp and stone him. The people of Israel do as the LORD commanded Moses.
YHWH speaks to Moses on Mount Sinai:
“Speak to the people of Israel and say to them: When you come into the land that I give you, the land shall keep a Sabbath to the LORD.
For six years you shall sow your field, and for six years prune your vineyard and gather in its fruit,
but in the seventh year there shall be a Sabbath of complete rest for the land — a Sabbath to the LORD. You shall not sow your field or prune your vineyard.
You shall not reap what grows of itself from your harvest, and you shall not gather the grapes of your unpruned vines. It is a year of complete rest for the land.
The Sabbath of the land shall provide food for you — for yourself, your male and female servants, your hired worker, and the sojourner who lives with you.
For your livestock and the wild animals in your land, all its yield shall be for food.
Count seven weeks of years — seven times seven — so that the seven weeks of years give you forty-nine years.
Then on the tenth day of the seventh month you shall sound the loud trumpet. On the Day of Atonement you shall sound the trumpet throughout all your land.

Consecrate the fiftieth year and proclaim liberty throughout the land to all its inhabitants. It shall be a Jubilee for you — each of you shall return to your ancestral property and each to your family.
That fiftieth year shall be a Jubilee for you. You shall not sow or reap what grows on its own or gather from the unpruned vines.
For it is a Jubilee — it shall be holy to you. You shall eat what the land produces out of the field.
In this year of Jubilee each of you shall return to your property.
If you make a sale to your neighbor or buy from your neighbor, you shall not wrong one another.
You shall buy from your neighbor according to the number of years since the Jubilee, and your neighbor shall sell to you according to the number of harvests remaining.
If the years are many, increase the price; if the years are few, reduce it — for what is being sold is the number of harvests.
You shall not wrong one another, but shall fear your God. For I am the LORD your God.
Keep my statutes and do my ordinances. If you do, you will live in the land securely.
The land will yield its fruit, and you will eat your fill and live there in safety.
And if you ask: What shall we eat in the seventh year, if we neither sow nor gather in our harvest?
I will command my blessing on you in the sixth year, and it will produce a crop sufficient for three years.
When you sow in the eighth year, you will still be eating from the old crop. Until the ninth year, when the new crop arrives, you shall eat the old.
The land shall not be sold in perpetuity, for the land is mine. You are but strangers and sojourners with me.
Throughout all the land you possess, you shall allow redemption of the land.
If your brother becomes poor and sells part of his property, his nearest kinsman-redeemer shall come and redeem what his brother has sold.
If a man has no one to redeem it for him, but he himself becomes prosperous and finds sufficient means to redeem it,
he shall calculate the years since its sale and repay the difference to the man he sold it to, then return to his property.
But if he does not have sufficient means to recover it, what he sold shall remain with the buyer until the year of Jubilee. In the Jubilee it shall be released, and he shall return to his property.
If a man sells a dwelling house in a walled city, he may redeem it within a full year of its sale — his right of redemption shall last one year.
If it is not redeemed within a full year, the house in the walled city shall pass in perpetuity to the buyer and his descendants. It shall not be released in the Jubilee.
But houses in villages without surrounding walls shall be treated as open land — they may be redeemed, and they shall be released in the Jubilee.
As for the cities of the Levites — the houses in the cities they possess — the Levites have a permanent right of redemption.

If one of the Levites does not exercise that right, the house sold in any of their cities shall still be released in the Jubilee, for the houses in Levitical cities are their possession among the people of Israel.
But the fields of common land belonging to their cities may not be sold, for that is their permanent possession.
If your brother becomes poor and cannot maintain himself beside you, you shall support him as you would a stranger or sojourner, so that he may live beside you.
Take no interest or increase from him, but fear your God, that your brother may live beside you.
You shall not lend him your money at interest or sell him your food for profit.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan, and to be your God.
If your brother becomes poor beside you and sells himself to you, you shall not make him serve as a slave.
He shall be with you as a hired worker and as a sojourner. He shall serve with you until the year of Jubilee.
Then he shall leave you — he and his children with him — and return to his family and to the property of his ancestors.
For they are my servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. They shall not be sold as slaves.
You shall not rule over them ruthlessly, but shall fear your God.
As for male and female slaves: you may acquire them from the nations around you.
You may also acquire from among the children of sojourners living among you and from their clans who are in your land. These may become your property.
You may pass them on as inherited property to your children after you and hold them permanently. But over your brothers, the people of Israel, you shall not rule one another ruthlessly.
If a stranger or sojourner with you becomes wealthy, and your brother beside him becomes poor and sells himself to that stranger or to a member of his clan,
after he has sold himself he retains the right of redemption. One of his brothers may redeem him,
or his uncle or his cousin may redeem him, or any close relative from his clan may redeem him. If he himself becomes prosperous, he may redeem himself.

He shall calculate with his buyer from the year he sold himself until the year of Jubilee. The price of his sale shall be proportional to the number of years — the time with his owner treated as the time of a hired worker.
If many years remain, he shall pay back a proportional share of his purchase price as the redemption payment.
If only a few years remain until the Jubilee, he shall calculate accordingly and pay for his redemption in proportion to his remaining years of service.
His owner shall treat him as a worker hired year by year. He shall not rule over him ruthlessly in your sight.
And if he is not redeemed by any of these means, he and his children shall go free in the year of Jubilee.
For the people of Israel are my servants — they are my servants whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.”
“You shall not make idols for yourselves or set up a carved image or a pillar, and you shall not place figured stone in your land to bow down to it. I am the LORD your God.
Keep my Sabbaths and revere my sanctuary. I am the LORD.
If you walk in my statutes and keep my commandments and do them,
I will give you your rains in their season, and the land shall yield its produce, and the trees of the field shall yield their fruit.
Your threshing shall last until the grape harvest, and the grape harvest shall last until the time for sowing. You shall eat your bread to the full and live in your land securely.
I will give peace in the land, and you shall lie down with no one to make you afraid. I will remove harmful creatures from the land, and the sword shall not pass through your land.
You shall chase your enemies, and they shall fall before you by the sword.
Five of you shall chase a hundred, and a hundred of you shall chase ten thousand — your enemies shall fall before you by the sword.
I will turn to you and make you fruitful and multiply you, and I will confirm my covenant with you.
You shall eat old grain long kept, and you shall clear out the old to make room for the new.
I will make my dwelling among you, and my soul shall not abhor you.
I will walk among you and will be your God, and you shall be my people.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, that you should not be their slaves. I have broken the bars of your yoke and made you walk with your heads held high.
But if you will not listen to me and will not do all these commandments,
if you spurn my statutes and your soul abhors my ordinances — refusing to do all my commandments — and you break my covenant,
then I will do this to you: I will visit you with panic, with wasting disease and fever that consume the eyes and make the heart ache. You shall sow your seed in vain, for your enemies shall eat it.
I will set my face against you, and you shall be struck down before your enemies. Those who hate you shall rule over you, and you shall flee when no one pursues you.
And if in spite of this you will not listen to me, I will discipline you again sevenfold for your sins.
I will break your proud power, and I will make your sky like iron and your earth like bronze.
Your strength shall be spent in vain, for your land shall not yield its produce, and the trees of the land shall not yield their fruit.
Then if you walk contrary to me and will not listen to me, I will multiply your strokes sevenfold according to your sins.
I will let loose wild animals against you, and they shall bereave you of your children and destroy your livestock and make you few in number, so that your roads shall be deserted.
And if by this discipline you are not turned to me but continue to walk contrary to me,
then I too will walk contrary to you, and I myself will strike you sevenfold for your sins.
I will bring a sword against you that executes vengeance for the covenant. If you gather within your cities, I will send pestilence among you, and you shall be delivered into the hand of the enemy.
When I cut off your supply of bread, ten women shall bake your bread in a single oven and dole it out by weight — you shall eat and not be satisfied.
But if in spite of this you will not listen to me, but walk contrary to me,
then I will walk contrary to you in fury, and I myself will discipline you sevenfold for your sins.
You shall eat the flesh of your sons, and you shall eat the flesh of your daughters.
I will destroy your high places and cut down your incense altars, and I will cast your dead bodies on the dead bodies of your idols. My soul shall abhor you.
I will lay your cities waste and make your sanctuaries desolate, and I will refuse to smell your pleasing aromas.
I will devastate the land myself, so that your enemies who settle in it shall be appalled.
And I will scatter you among the nations, and I will draw the sword after you. Your land shall be a desolation, and your cities shall be a waste.
Then the land shall enjoy its Sabbaths as long as it lies desolate, while you are in your enemies’ land. Then the land shall rest and enjoy its Sabbaths.
All the days it lies desolate it shall have rest — the rest it did not have on your Sabbaths when you were living in it.

And as for those of you who survive, I will send faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies. The sound of a driven leaf shall put them to flight, and they shall flee as one flees from the sword — and fall when no one pursues.
They shall stumble over one another as if fleeing a sword, though no one pursues. You shall have no power to stand before your enemies.
You shall perish among the nations, and the land of your enemies shall consume you.
And those who survive shall waste away in the lands of their enemies because of their iniquity, and also because of the iniquities of their ancestors they shall rot away with them.
But if they confess their iniquity and the iniquity of their ancestors in the treachery they committed against me, and in walking contrary to me —
so that I walked contrary to them and brought them into the land of their enemies — if then their uncircumcised heart is humbled and they make amends for their iniquity,
then I will remember my covenant with Jacob, and my covenant with Isaac, and my covenant with Abraham, and I will remember the land.

But the land shall be abandoned by them and shall enjoy its Sabbaths while it lies desolate without them, and they shall make amends for their iniquity, because they spurned my ordinances and their soul abhorred my statutes.
Yet for all that, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not spurn them or abhor them so as to destroy them utterly and break my covenant with them — for I am the LORD their God.
But I will remember for their sake the covenant with their ancestors, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt in the sight of the nations, that I might be their God. I am the LORD.”
These are the statutes and ordinances and laws that the LORD established between himself and the people of Israel through Moses on Mount Sinai.
YHWH speaks to Moses:
“Speak to the people of Israel and say to them: When a person makes a special vow to the LORD involving the valuation of a person,
the valuation for a male between twenty and sixty years old shall be fifty shekels of silver by the sanctuary weight.
For a female, the valuation shall be thirty shekels.
For a person between five and twenty years old, the valuation for a male shall be twenty shekels, and for a female ten shekels.
For a person between one month and five years old, the valuation for a male shall be five shekels of silver, and for a female three shekels of silver.
For a person sixty years old or over: for a male, fifteen shekels, and for a female ten shekels.
If the person is too poor to pay the valuation, they shall be presented before the priest, and the priest shall assess them at what the one who vowed can afford.
If the vow is an animal fit to be offered to the LORD, any such animal given to the LORD shall be holy.
One shall not replace or exchange it — good for bad or bad for good. And if one does exchange animal for animal, both it and the substitute shall be holy.
If the vow concerns an unclean animal that is not fit to be offered to the LORD, the animal shall be presented before the priest,
and the priest shall value it as either good or bad. As the priest values it, so it shall be.
But if the one who vowed wishes to redeem it, he shall add a fifth of its value to the priest’s assessment.
When a man dedicates his house as holy to the LORD, the priest shall assess it as good or bad. As the priest assesses it, so it shall stand.
If the one who dedicated it wishes to redeem his house, he shall add a fifth of its assessed value, and it shall be his.
If a man dedicates to the LORD part of his ancestral field, its valuation shall be set according to its seed — a homer of barley at fifty shekels of silver.
If he dedicates his field from the year of Jubilee, it shall stand at the full valuation.
But if he dedicates it after the Jubilee, the priest shall calculate the price in proportion to the years remaining until the next Jubilee, and the valuation shall be reduced.
If the one who dedicated the field wishes to redeem it, he shall add a fifth to the assessed value, and it shall revert to him.
But if he does not redeem the field, or if he has already sold it to another man, it may no longer be redeemed.
When the field is released at Jubilee, it shall be holy to the LORD as a field that has been devoted — it shall become the priest’s possession.
If a man dedicates to the LORD a field he has purchased — which is not part of his ancestral field —
the priest shall calculate the proportional valuation up to the year of Jubilee, and the man shall pay that amount on that day as a holy gift to the LORD.
In the year of Jubilee the field shall revert to the one from whom it was bought, to the one whose ancestral land it was.
Every valuation shall be reckoned by the sanctuary shekel: twenty gerahs to the shekel.
A firstborn animal already belongs to the LORD by right; no one may dedicate it — whether ox or sheep, it is the LORD’s.
If it is an unclean animal, it may be redeemed at its assessed value with a fifth added. If it is not redeemed, it shall be sold at its assessed value.
But nothing that a person has devoted to the LORD — whether a person, an animal, or ancestral land — may be sold or redeemed. Every devoted thing is most holy to the LORD.
No person who has been devoted may be ransomed — he shall surely be put to death.
Every tithe of the land — whether of the seed of the land or of the fruit of the trees — belongs to the LORD. It is holy to the LORD.
If a man wishes to redeem any of his tithe, he shall add a fifth of its value to it.
And every tithe of herds and flocks — every tenth animal that passes under the shepherd’s staff — shall be holy to the LORD.
One shall not look for the good and pass over the bad, nor make a substitute. If a substitute is made, both it and the substitute shall be holy — it shall not be redeemed.”
These are the commandments that the LORD commanded Moses for the people of Israel on Mount Sinai.
YHWH speaks to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai — in the tent of meeting — on the first day of the second month, in the second year after the Israelites came out of Egypt. He says:
“Take a census of the whole congregation of Israel by their clans and their ancestral houses, registering every male by name, head by head —
everyone in Israel from twenty years old and upward who is able to go out to war. You and Aaron are to muster them, company by company.
One man from each tribe is to stand with you — each one the head of his ancestral house.”
These are the names of the men who will stand with you. From Reuben: Elizur son of Shedeur.
From Simeon: Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
From Judah: Nahshon son of Amminadab.
From Issachar: Nethanel son of Zuar.
From Zebulun: Eliab son of Helon.
From Ephraim, from the sons of Joseph: Elishama son of Ammihud. From Manasseh: Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
From Benjamin: Abidan son of Gideoni.
From Dan: Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
From Asher: Pagiel son of Ochran.
From Gad: Eliasaph son of Deuel.
From Naphtali: Ahira son of Enan.
These are the men summoned from the congregation — the leaders of their ancestral tribes, the heads of the thousands of Israel.
Moses and Aaron take these men who are named and on the first day of the second month they assemble the whole congregation.
They register everyone by their clans and ancestral houses, and every male from twenty years old and upward is counted by name, head by head —
just as YHWH commands Moses. So he musters them in the wilderness of Sinai.

The descendants of Reuben — Israel’s firstborn — by their lineages, their clans, and their ancestral houses: every male from twenty years old and upward, everyone able to go out to war, counted one by one.
The muster of the tribe of Reuben: forty-six thousand five hundred.
The descendants of Simeon, by their lineages, their clans, and their ancestral houses: every male from twenty years old and upward, everyone able to go out to war, counted one by one.
The muster of the tribe of Simeon: fifty-nine thousand three hundred.
The descendants of Gad, by their lineages, their clans, and their ancestral houses: every male from twenty years old and upward, everyone able to go out to war —
the muster of the tribe of Gad: forty-five thousand six hundred and fifty.
The descendants of Judah, by their lineages, their clans, and their ancestral houses: every male from twenty years old and upward, everyone able to go out to war —
the muster of the tribe of Judah: seventy-four thousand six hundred.
The descendants of Issachar, by their lineages, their clans, and their ancestral houses: every male from twenty years old and upward, everyone able to go out to war —
the muster of the tribe of Issachar: fifty-four thousand four hundred.
The descendants of Zebulun, by their lineages, their clans, and their ancestral houses: every male from twenty years old and upward, everyone able to go out to war —
the muster of the tribe of Zebulun: fifty-seven thousand four hundred.
The descendants of Ephraim, sons of Joseph, by their lineages, their clans, and their ancestral houses: every male from twenty years old and upward, everyone able to go out to war —
the muster of the tribe of Ephraim: forty thousand five hundred.
The descendants of Manasseh, sons of Joseph, by their lineages, their clans, and their ancestral houses: every male from twenty years old and upward, everyone able to go out to war —
the muster of the tribe of Manasseh: thirty-two thousand two hundred.
The descendants of Benjamin, by their lineages, their clans, and their ancestral houses: every male from twenty years old and upward, everyone able to go out to war —
the muster of the tribe of Benjamin: thirty-five thousand four hundred.
The descendants of Dan, by their lineages, their clans, and their ancestral houses: every male from twenty years old and upward, everyone able to go out to war —
the muster of the tribe of Dan: sixty-two thousand seven hundred.
The descendants of Asher, by their lineages, their clans, and their ancestral houses: every male from twenty years old and upward, everyone able to go out to war —
the muster of the tribe of Asher: forty-one thousand five hundred.
The descendants of Naphtali, by their lineages, their clans, and their ancestral houses: every male from twenty years old and upward, everyone able to go out to war —
the muster of the tribe of Naphtali: fifty-three thousand four hundred.
These are the men Moses and Aaron muster, along with the twelve leaders of Israel, each representing his ancestral house.
All the Israelites from twenty years old and upward who are able to go out to war are counted by their ancestral houses —
the total: six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty.
But the Levites are not counted among them by their ancestral tribe.
YHWH has spoken to Moses:
“Only the tribe of Levi you are not to count. Do not include them in the census of the Israelites.

Instead, appoint the Levites over the tabernacle of the testimony — over all its furnishings and everything belonging to it. They are to carry the tabernacle and all its furnishings, minister to it, and camp around it.
Whenever the tabernacle sets out, the Levites take it down; and when it is to be set up, the Levites do so. Any outsider who comes near is to be put to death.
The Israelites are to pitch their tents in their own companies — each man under his own standard, by his own banner.
But the Levites are to camp around the tabernacle of the testimony so that wrath does not fall on the congregation of Israel. The Levites are to keep watch over the tabernacle of the testimony.”
The Israelites do everything YHWH commands Moses — that is exactly what they do.
YHWH speaks to Moses and Aaron:
“The Israelites are to camp, each man by his own standard, under the banners of their ancestral house. They camp around the tent of meeting at a distance.”
Those on the east side — toward the sunrise — camp under the standard of the division of Judah, arranged in companies. The leader of the people of Judah is Nahshon son of Amminadab.
His company as counted: seventy-four thousand six hundred.
Camping next to him is the tribe of Issachar. The leader of the people of Issachar is Nethanel son of Zuar.
His company as counted: fifty-four thousand four hundred.
Then the tribe of Zebulun. The leader of the people of Zebulun is Eliab son of Helon.
His company as counted: fifty-seven thousand four hundred.
The total of all those counted for the division of Judah, company by company: one hundred and eighty-six thousand four hundred. These set out first.
The standard of the division of Reuben is to the south, arranged in companies. The leader of the people of Reuben is Elizur son of Shedeur.
His company as counted: forty-six thousand five hundred.
Camping next to him is the tribe of Simeon. The leader of the people of Simeon is Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
His company as counted: fifty-nine thousand three hundred.
Then the tribe of Gad. The leader of the people of Gad is Eliasaph son of Deuel.
His company as counted: forty-five thousand six hundred and fifty.
The total of all those counted for the division of Reuben, company by company: one hundred and fifty-one thousand four hundred and fifty. These set out second.
Then the tent of meeting sets out, with the camp of the Levites in its midst. They go exactly as they camp — each man in his place, under his standard.
The standard of the division of Ephraim is to the west, arranged in companies. The leader of the people of Ephraim is Elishama son of Ammihud.
His company as counted: forty thousand five hundred.
Next to him is the tribe of Manasseh. The leader of the people of Manasseh is Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
His company as counted: thirty-two thousand two hundred.
Then the tribe of Benjamin. The leader of the people of Benjamin is Abidan son of Gideoni.
His company as counted: thirty-five thousand four hundred.
The total of all those counted for the division of Ephraim, company by company: one hundred and eight thousand one hundred. These set out third.
The standard of the division of Dan is to the north, arranged in companies. The leader of the people of Dan is Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
His company as counted: sixty-two thousand seven hundred.
Camping next to him is the tribe of Asher. The leader of the people of Asher is Pagiel son of Ochran.
His company as counted: forty-one thousand five hundred.
Then the tribe of Naphtali. The leader of the people of Naphtali is Ahira son of Enan.
His company as counted: fifty-three thousand four hundred.
The total of the division of Dan: one hundred and fifty-seven thousand six hundred. These set out last, under their standards.
These are the Israelites counted by their ancestral houses. The total of all those counted in the divisions, company by company: six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty.
But the Levites are not counted among the Israelites, as YHWH commands Moses.
The Israelites do everything YHWH commands Moses — that is how they camp under their standards, and that is how they set out, each man by his clan and ancestral house.
These are the generations of Aaron and Moses at the time YHWH speaks with Moses on Mount Sinai.
The names of Aaron’s sons: Nadab the firstborn, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
These are the names of Aaron’s sons — the anointed priests, those ordained to serve as priests.

But Nadab and Abihu die before YHWH when they offer unauthorized fire before YHWH in the wilderness of Sinai. They have no sons. So Eleazar and Ithamar serve as priests in the lifetime of their father Aaron.
YHWH speaks to Moses:
“Bring the tribe of Levi near and present them to Aaron the priest, that they may serve him.
They are to carry out his duties and the duties of the whole congregation before the tent of meeting — doing the work of the tabernacle.
They are to take care of all the furnishings of the tent of meeting and fulfill the obligations of the Israelites as they do the work of the tabernacle.
Assign the Levites to Aaron and his sons — they are entirely given to him from among the Israelites.
Appoint Aaron and his sons to carry out the duties of the priesthood. Any outsider who comes near is to be put to death.”
YHWH speaks to Moses:
“I have taken the Levites from among the Israelites in place of every firstborn who opens the womb among the Israelites. The Levites are mine.
Every firstborn belongs to me. When I struck down every firstborn in Egypt, I set apart for myself every firstborn in Israel — human and animal alike. They are mine. I am YHWH.”
YHWH speaks to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai:
“Count the Levites by their ancestral houses and clans. Count every male a month old and upward.”
Moses counts them according to the word of YHWH, as he is commanded.
These are the sons of Levi by name: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
The names of the sons of Gershon by their clans: Libni and Shimei.
The sons of Kohath by their clans: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
The sons of Merari by their clans: Mahli and Mushi. These are the clans of the Levites by their ancestral houses.
From Gershon come the clans of the Libnites and the Shimeites — these are the Gershonite clans.
The males counted from a month old and upward: seven thousand five hundred.
The Gershonite clans camp on the west, behind the tabernacle.
The leader of the Gershonite ancestral house is Eliasaph son of Lael.
At the tent of meeting the Gershonites are responsible for the tabernacle, the tent, its covering, and the curtain at the entrance to the tent of meeting,
the hangings of the courtyard and the curtain at the entrance to the courtyard surrounding the tabernacle and the altar, and the ropes for all the work connected with these.
From Kohath come the clans of the Amramites, the Izharites, the Hebronites, and the Uzzielites — these are the Kohathite clans.
The males counted from a month old and upward: eight thousand six hundred. They are responsible for the care of the sanctuary.
The Kohathite clans camp on the south side of the tabernacle.
The leader of the Kohathite ancestral house is Elizaphan son of Uzziel.
They are responsible for the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, the vessels used in sanctuary ministry, the curtain, and everything connected with their service.
The chief leader over the leaders of the Levites is Eleazar son of Aaron the priest. He oversees those responsible for the care of the sanctuary.
From Merari come the clans of the Mahlites and the Mushites — these are the Merarite clans.
The males counted from a month old and upward: six thousand two hundred.
The leader of the Merarite ancestral house is Zuriel son of Abihail. They camp on the north side of the tabernacle.
The Merarites are assigned responsibility for the frames of the tabernacle, its crossbars, posts, bases, all its equipment, and everything connected with their use,
along with the posts of the surrounding courtyard, their bases, tent pegs, and ropes.

Those camping to the front of the tabernacle — on the east, toward the sunrise — are Moses and Aaron and his sons. They are responsible for the care of the sanctuary on behalf of the Israelites. Any outsider who comes near is to be put to death.
The total of all the Levites counted by Moses and Aaron at YHWH’s command, by their clans — every male a month old and upward: twenty-two thousand.
YHWH says to Moses: “Count every firstborn male of the Israelites a month old and upward and make a list of their names.
Take the Levites for me — I am YHWH — in place of all the firstborn among the Israelites, and the livestock of the Levites in place of all the firstborn among the livestock of the Israelites.”
Moses counts all the firstborn among the Israelites, as YHWH commands him.
The total of all firstborn males a month old and upward, listed by name: twenty-two thousand two hundred and seventy-three.
YHWH speaks to Moses:
“Take the Levites in place of all the firstborn of Israel, and the livestock of the Levites in place of their livestock. The Levites are mine. I am YHWH.
For the redemption of the two hundred and seventy-three firstborn Israelites who exceed the number of the Levites,
collect five shekels for each one, reckoning by the sanctuary shekel — twenty gerahs to the shekel.
Give the redemption money for the surplus to Aaron and his sons.”
Moses collects the redemption money from those who exceed the number redeemed by the Levites.
He collects the money from the firstborn Israelites: one thousand three hundred and sixty-five shekels, reckoned by the sanctuary shekel.
Moses gives the redemption money to Aaron and his sons, according to the word of YHWH — just as YHWH commands Moses.
YHWH speaks to Moses and Aaron:
“Take a census of the Kohathites among the Levites, by their clans and their ancestral houses,
from thirty years old up to fifty years old — everyone who enters the service to do the work at the tent of meeting.
This is the work of the Kohathites at the tent of meeting: the care of the most holy things.
When the camp is to set out, Aaron and his sons go in and take down the screening curtain and cover the ark of the testimony with it.
Over this they put a covering of fine leather and spread a cloth of solid blue on top, then set its carrying poles in place.
Over the table of the Presence they spread a blue cloth and lay on it the plates, the dishes, the bowls, and the pitchers for the drink offering; the bread of the regular offering remains on it.
Over all these they spread a scarlet cloth and cover that with a covering of fine leather, then put the poles in place.
They take a blue cloth and cover the lampstand used for light, together with its lamps, its wick trimmers, its trays, and all the oil vessels that serve it.
They put it and all its accessories within a covering of fine leather and place it on a carrying frame.
Over the gold altar they spread a blue cloth and cover it with a covering of fine leather, then put its poles in place.
They take all the utensils of ministry used in the sanctuary, put them in a blue cloth, cover that with a covering of fine leather, and place them on a carrying frame.
They remove the ashes from the bronze altar and spread a purple cloth over it.

They place on it all the utensils used for ministering at the altar — the fire pans, the meat forks, the shovels, and the basins — all the altar’s utensils. They spread a covering of fine leather over it and put its poles in place.

After Aaron and his sons have finished wrapping the holy furnishings and all the holy articles, and when the camp is ready to move, only then do the Kohathites come in to carry them. But they must not touch the holy things — or they will die. These are the things the Kohathites carry at the tent of meeting.

The oversight of Eleazar son of Aaron the priest: the oil for the light, the fragrant incense, the regular grain offering, and the anointing oil. He has charge of the entire tabernacle and everything in it — its holy furnishings and all its articles.”
YHWH speaks to Moses and Aaron:
“Do not let the clans of the Kohathites be cut off from among the Levites.
Do this for them so that they may live and not die when they approach the most holy things: Aaron and his sons are to go in and assign to each man his specific work and what he is to carry.
But the Kohathites must not go in to look at the holy things even for a moment — or they will die.”
YHWH speaks to Moses:
“Take a census of the Gershonites as well, by their ancestral houses and clans.
Count them from thirty years old up to fifty years old — all who come to serve, to do the work at the tent of meeting.
This is the service of the Gershonite clans: what they do and what they carry.
They carry the curtains of the tabernacle and the tent of meeting, its covering, the outer covering of fine leather, and the curtain for the entrance to the tent of meeting,

the hangings of the courtyard and the curtain for the gate of the courtyard that surrounds the tabernacle and the altar, their ropes, and all the equipment for their service. They do everything connected with these things.

All the service of the Gershonites — everything they carry, everything they do — is to be done at the command of Aaron and his sons. You are to assign to them as their responsibility all they are to carry.
This is the service of the Gershonite clans at the tent of meeting. Their duties are under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
“As for the Merarites, count them by their clans and ancestral houses.
Count them from thirty years old up to fifty years old — everyone who comes to serve, to do the work at the tent of meeting.
This is what they are responsible to carry as all their service at the tent of meeting: the frames of the tabernacle, its crossbars, posts, and bases;

the posts of the surrounding courtyard with their bases, tent pegs, and ropes, along with all their equipment and everything related to their use. You are to assign to each man by name the specific items he is to carry.
This is the service of the Merarite clans — all their work at the tent of meeting — under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.”
Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of the congregation count the Kohathites by their clans and ancestral houses —
from thirty years old up to fifty years old: everyone who enters service for work at the tent of meeting.
Those counted from their clans: two thousand seven hundred and fifty.
These are the ones counted from the Kohathite clans — all who serve at the tent of meeting — counted by Moses and Aaron at the command of YHWH through Moses.
The Gershonites are counted by their clans and ancestral houses —
from thirty years old up to fifty years old: everyone who enters service for work at the tent of meeting.
Those counted from their clans and ancestral houses: two thousand six hundred and thirty.
These are the ones counted from the Gershonite clans — all who serve at the tent of meeting — counted by Moses and Aaron at the command of YHWH.
The Merarites are counted by their clans and ancestral houses —
from thirty years old up to fifty years old: everyone who enters service for work at the tent of meeting.
Those counted from their clans: three thousand two hundred.
These are the ones counted from the Merarite clans, whom Moses and Aaron count at the command of YHWH through Moses.
All the Levites counted by Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of Israel — by their clans and ancestral houses —
from thirty years old up to fifty years old: everyone who comes to do the work of service and the work of carrying at the tent of meeting —
those counted: eight thousand five hundred and eighty.
At the command of YHWH through Moses, each man is assigned his work and what he is to carry. All of them are counted exactly as YHWH commands Moses.
YHWH speaks to Moses:
“Command the Israelites to send outside the camp anyone with a skin disease, anyone with a discharge, and anyone who is ritually unclean because of contact with a corpse.
Send both male and female outside the camp — so they do not defile the camp where I dwell among them.”
The Israelites do this, sending such people outside the camp. They do exactly as YHWH says to Moses.
YHWH speaks to Moses:
“Speak to the Israelites: when a man or woman commits any of the sins that people commit — acting unfaithfully against YHWH — that person incurs guilt.
They must confess the sin they have committed, make full restitution for the wrong, add a fifth of the value to it, and give it to the person they have wronged.

But if the wronged person has no kinsman-redeemer to whom restitution can be made, the restitution belongs to YHWH and goes to the priest — in addition to the ram of atonement by which he makes atonement for them.
Every sacred contribution of all the holy things that the Israelites bring to a priest will belong to him.
What any man gives to the priest will be the priest’s.”
YHWH speaks to Moses:
“Speak to the Israelites and say to them: if a man’s wife goes astray and is unfaithful to him,
and if a man has lain with her sexually, but it is hidden from her husband’s eyes and she has been defiled in secret with no witness against her and she was not caught —
and if a spirit of jealousy comes over him so that he is jealous about his wife who has defiled herself; or if a spirit of jealousy comes over him though she has not defiled herself —

then the man brings his wife to the priest and brings an offering for her: one-tenth of an ephah of barley flour. He pours no oil on it and adds no frankincense, for it is a grain offering of jealousy, a grain offering of remembrance that calls iniquity to mind.
The priest brings her forward and has her stand before YHWH.
The priest takes holy water in a clay jar and puts some dust from the tabernacle floor into the water.

The priest has the woman stand before YHWH, loosens the hair of her head, and places in her hands the reminder offering — the grain offering of jealousy. The priest himself holds in his hand the water of bitterness that brings a curse.

The priest then puts her under oath and says to the woman: ‘If no man has lain with you and you have not gone astray into uncleanness while under your husband’s authority, be immune from this water of bitterness that brings a curse.
But if you have gone astray while under your husband’s authority, if you have defiled yourself and some man other than your husband has lain with you’ —
here the priest puts the woman under the oath of the curse and says to her — ‘may YHWH make you a curse and an oath among your people when he causes your womb to discharge and your belly to swell;
may this water that brings a curse enter your body so that your belly swells and your womb discharges.’ The woman says: ‘Amen. Amen.’
The priest writes these curses on a scroll and washes them off into the water of bitterness.
He makes the woman drink the water of bitterness that brings a curse, and the water that brings a curse enters her causing bitter pain.
The priest takes the grain offering of jealousy from the woman’s hand, waves it before YHWH, and brings it to the altar.
The priest takes a handful of the grain offering as its memorial portion and burns it on the altar, then makes the woman drink the water.

When he makes her drink the water: if she has defiled herself and been unfaithful to her husband, the water that brings a curse enters her causing bitter pain — her belly swells and her womb discharges — and she becomes a curse among her people.
But if the woman has not defiled herself and is clean, she is free from harm and will conceive children.
This is the law of jealousy, when a wife goes astray while under her husband’s authority and defiles herself,
or when a spirit of jealousy comes over a man and he is jealous about his wife. He presents her before YHWH, and the priest carries out this entire law for her.
The man will be free from guilt, but that woman will bear the consequences of her iniquity.”
YHWH speaks to Moses:
“Speak to the Israelites and say to them: when a man or woman wants to make a special vow — the vow of a Nazirite, consecrating themselves to YHWH —
they must abstain from wine and other fermented drink. They must not drink vinegar made from wine or from other fermented drink, must not drink grape juice, and must not eat grapes or raisins.
Throughout the entire period of their Nazirite vow they must not eat anything that comes from the grapevine — not even the seeds or the skins.
During the whole period of their vow, no razor may touch their head. They are to be holy until the days of their consecration to YHWH are complete; they must let the locks of their hair grow freely.
Throughout the days of their consecration to YHWH they must not go near a dead body.
Even if their own father or mother, their brother or sister, dies, they must not make themselves unclean because of them — for the crown of their consecration to God is on their head.
Throughout the days of their consecration they are holy to YHWH.
If someone dies suddenly beside them, defiling the crown of their consecration, they must shave their head on the day of their cleansing — the seventh day.
On the eighth day they bring two doves or two young pigeons to the priest at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
The priest offers one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, making atonement because of the defilement from the dead. That same day they rededicate their head as holy.

They must rededicate themselves to YHWH for the full period of the Nazirite vow and bring a year-old male lamb as a guilt offering. The previous days do not count, because the consecration was defiled.
This is the law of the Nazirite when the period of consecration is complete. They are brought to the entrance of the tent of meeting.

There they present their offering to YHWH: a year-old male lamb without defect as a burnt offering, a year-old female lamb without defect as a sin offering, a ram without defect as a fellowship offering,
together with a basket of unleavened bread — loaves of the finest flour mixed with olive oil and thin loaves brushed with olive oil — along with their grain offerings and drink offerings.
The priest presents all this before YHWH and makes the sin offering and the burnt offering.
He presents the ram as a fellowship offering to YHWH, together with the basket of unleavened bread. The priest makes the grain offering and the drink offering as well.
Then the Nazirite shaves the consecrated head at the entrance to the tent of meeting and puts the hair in the fire under the fellowship offering.
After the Nazirite has shaved, the priest takes the boiled shoulder of the ram, one unleavened loaf from the basket, and one unleavened thin loaf, and places them in the hands of the Nazirite.

The priest waves them before YHWH as a wave offering. They are holy and belong to the priest, together with the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the presentation offering. After that the Nazirite may drink wine.

This is the law of the Nazirite who vows an offering to YHWH in keeping with the consecration, in addition to whatever else the person can afford. They must fulfill the vow exactly as the law of the Nazirite requires.”
YHWH speaks to Moses:
“Tell Aaron and his sons: this is how you are to bless the Israelites. Say to them:
May YHWH bless you and keep you;
may YHWH make his face shine upon you and be gracious to you;
may YHWH lift his face toward you and give you peace.”
So they put my name on the Israelites, and I will bless them.
On the day Moses finishes setting up the tabernacle, he anoints it and consecrates it along with all its furnishings. He also anoints and consecrates the altar and all its utensils.
Then the leaders of Israel come forward—the heads of families, the same tribal leaders who oversaw the census.
They bring before the LORD six covered wagons and twelve oxen—one wagon for every two leaders and one ox apiece—and present them in front of the tabernacle.
The LORD says to Moses,
"Accept these from them. They are to be used for the work at the tent of meeting. Give them to the Levites according to each man's service."
Moses receives the wagons and oxen and gives them to the Levites.
He gives two wagons and four oxen to the sons of Gershon, as their work requires.
He gives four wagons and eight oxen to the sons of Merari, as their work requires, all under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
But he gives nothing to the sons of Kohath, because their duty is to carry the holy things on their own shoulders.
When the altar is anointed, the leaders bring their dedication offerings before it.
The LORD says to Moses, "Let each leader bring his offering on a separate day for the dedication of the altar."
On the first day, Nahshon son of Amminadab—leader of the sons of Judah—comes forward.
His offering is one silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels—both by the sanctuary shekel—filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold pan of ten shekels, filled with incense;
one young bull, one ram, one male lamb in its first year for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the fellowship offering: two bulls, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs in their first year. This is the offering of Nahshon son of Amminadab.
On the second day, Nethanel son of Zuar—leader of the sons of Issachar—comes forward.
His offering is one silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels—both by the sanctuary shekel—filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold pan of ten shekels, filled with incense;
one young bull, one ram, one male lamb in its first year for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the fellowship offering: two bulls, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs in their first year. This is the offering of Nethanel son of Zuar.
On the third day, Eliab son of Helon—leader of the sons of Zebulun—comes forward.
His offering is one silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels—both by the sanctuary shekel—filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold pan of ten shekels, filled with incense;
one young bull, one ram, one male lamb in its first year for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the fellowship offering: two bulls, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs in their first year. This is the offering of Eliab son of Helon.
On the fourth day, Elizur son of Shedeur—leader of the sons of Reuben—comes forward.
His offering is one silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels—both by the sanctuary shekel—filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold pan of ten shekels, filled with incense;
one young bull, one ram, one male lamb in its first year for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the fellowship offering: two bulls, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs in their first year. This is the offering of Elizur son of Shedeur.
On the fifth day, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai—leader of the sons of Simeon—comes forward.
His offering is one silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels—both by the sanctuary shekel—filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold pan of ten shekels, filled with incense;
one young bull, one ram, one male lamb in its first year for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the fellowship offering: two bulls, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs in their first year. This is the offering of Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
On the sixth day, Eliasaph son of Deuel—leader of the sons of Gad—comes forward.
His offering is one silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels—both by the sanctuary shekel—filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold pan of ten shekels, filled with incense;
one young bull, one ram, one male lamb in its first year for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the fellowship offering: two bulls, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs in their first year. This is the offering of Eliasaph son of Deuel.
On the seventh day, Elishama son of Ammihud—leader of the sons of Ephraim—comes forward.
His offering is one silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels—both by the sanctuary shekel—filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold pan of ten shekels, filled with incense;
one young bull, one ram, one male lamb in its first year for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the fellowship offering: two bulls, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs in their first year. This is the offering of Elishama son of Ammihud.
On the eighth day, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur—leader of the sons of Manasseh—comes forward.
His offering is one silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels—both by the sanctuary shekel—filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold pan of ten shekels, filled with incense;
one young bull, one ram, one male lamb in its first year for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
