Offer one lamb in the morning and the other at twilight,
together with a grain offering of a tenth of an ephah of the finest flour mixed with a quarter of a hin of oil from pressed olives.
This is the regular burnt offering instituted at Mount Sinai as a pleasing aroma, a food offering presented to the LORD.
The accompanying drink offering is to be a quarter of a hin of fermented drink with each lamb. Pour out the drink offering to the LORD at the sanctuary.
Offer the second lamb at twilight, along with the same grain offering and drink offering as in the morning. This is a food offering, an aroma pleasing to the LORD.
"On the Sabbath day, make an offering of two lambs a year old without defect, together with its drink offering and a grain offering of two-tenths of an ephah of the finest flour mixed with olive oil.
This is the burnt offering for every Sabbath, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its drink offering."
"On the first of every month, present to the LORD a burnt offering of two young bulls, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, all without defect.
With each bull there is to be a grain offering of three-tenths of an ephah of the finest flour mixed with oil; with the ram, two-tenths;
and with each lamb, a tenth. This is for a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma, a food offering presented to the LORD.

With each bull there is to be a drink offering of half a hin of wine; with the ram, a third of a hin; and with each lamb, a quarter of a hin. This is the burnt offering for each month throughout the year.
Besides the regular burnt offering with its drink offering, one male goat is to be presented to the LORD as a sin offering."
"The LORD’s Passover is to be held on the fourteenth day of the first month.
On the fifteenth day of this month there is to be a festival; for seven days eat bread made without yeast.
On the first day hold a sacred assembly and do no regular work.
Present to the LORD a food offering consisting of a burnt offering of two young bulls, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, all without defect.
With each bull present a grain offering of three-tenths of an ephah of the finest flour mixed with oil; with the ram, two-tenths;
and with each of the seven lambs, one tenth.
Include one male goat as a sin offering to make atonement for you.
Offer these in addition to the regular morning burnt offering.
In this way present the food offering every day for seven days as an aroma pleasing to the LORD; it is to be offered in addition to the regular burnt offering and its drink offering.
On the seventh day hold a sacred assembly and do no regular work."
"On the day of firstfruits, when you present to the LORD an offering of new grain during the Festival of Weeks, hold a sacred assembly and do no regular work.
Present a burnt offering of two young bulls, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old as an aroma pleasing to the LORD.
With each bull there is to be a grain offering of three-tenths of an ephah of the finest flour mixed with oil; with the ram, two-tenths;
and with each of the seven lambs, one tenth.
Include one male goat to make atonement for you.
Offer these together with their drink offerings, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its grain offering. Be sure the animals are without defect."
"On the first day of the seventh month hold a sacred assembly and do no regular work. It is a day of trumpet blasts for you.
As an aroma pleasing to the LORD, present a burnt offering of one young bull, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, all without defect.
With the bull present a grain offering of three-tenths of an ephah of the finest flour mixed with oil; with the ram, two-tenths;
and with each of the seven lambs, one tenth.
Include one male goat as a sin offering to make atonement for you.
These are in addition to the monthly and daily burnt offerings with their prescribed grain offerings and drink offerings as stated. They are food offerings presented to the LORD, a pleasing aroma."
"On the tenth day of this seventh month hold a sacred assembly. Deny yourselves and do no work.
Present to the LORD a burnt offering of one young bull, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, all without defect, as an aroma pleasing to him.
With the bull present a grain offering of three-tenths of an ephah of the finest flour mixed with oil; with the ram, two-tenths;
and with each of the seven lambs, one tenth.
Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the sin offering for atonement and the regular burnt offering with its grain offering, and their drink offerings."
"On the fifteenth day of the seventh month hold a sacred assembly and do no regular work. Celebrate a festival to the LORD for seven days.
Present as a food offering, as an aroma pleasing to the LORD, a burnt offering of thirteen young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all without defect.
With each of the thirteen bulls present a grain offering of three-tenths of an ephah of the finest flour mixed with oil; with each of the two rams, two-tenths;
and with each of the fourteen lambs, one tenth.
Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
"On the second day present twelve young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all without defect.
With the bulls, rams, and lambs, present their grain offerings and drink offerings according to the number specified.
Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offerings.
"On the third day present eleven bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all without defect.
With the bulls, rams, and lambs, present their grain offerings and drink offerings according to the number specified.
Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
"On the fourth day present ten bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all without defect.
With the bulls, rams, and lambs, present their grain offerings and drink offerings according to the number specified.
Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
"On the fifth day present nine bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all without defect.
With the bulls, rams, and lambs, present their grain offerings and drink offerings according to the number specified.
Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
"On the sixth day present eight bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all without defect.
With the bulls, rams, and lambs, present their grain offerings and drink offerings according to the number specified.
Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
"On the seventh day present seven bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all without defect.
With the bulls, rams, and lambs, present their grain offerings and drink offerings according to the number specified.
Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
"On the eighth day hold a closing assembly and do no regular work.
Present as a food offering, as an aroma pleasing to the LORD, a burnt offering of one bull, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, all without defect.
With the bull, the ram, and the lambs, present their grain offerings and drink offerings according to the number specified.
Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering."
"In addition to what you vow and your freewill offerings, offer these to the LORD at your appointed festivals: your burnt offerings, grain offerings, drink offerings, and fellowship offerings."
Moses tells the Israelites everything the LORD commands him.
Moses says to the heads of the tribes of Israel: "This is what the LORD commands:
When a man makes a vow to the LORD or takes an oath to bind himself with a pledge, he must not break his word. He must do everything he has said."
"When a young woman still living in her father’s house makes a vow to the LORD or binds herself with a pledge,
and her father hears about her vow or pledge but says nothing to her, then all her vows and every pledge by which she has bound herself will stand.
But if her father forbids her when he hears about it, none of her vows or pledges will be binding. The LORD will release her because her father has forbidden her.
"If she marries after she makes a vow or after her lips utter a rash promise by which she binds herself,
and her husband hears about it but says nothing to her when he learns of it, then her vows or the pledges by which she bound herself will stand.
But if her husband forbids her when he hears about it, he nullifies the vow that binds her or the rash promise by which she bound herself, and the LORD will release her.
"Any vow or obligation taken by a widow or divorced woman will be binding on her.
"If a woman living with her husband makes a vow or binds herself with a pledge under oath
and her husband hears about it but says nothing to her and does not forbid her, then all her vows or pledges will stand.
But if her husband nullifies them when he hears about them, then none of the vows or pledges that came from her lips will stand. Her husband has nullified them, and the LORD will release her.
Her husband may confirm or nullify any vow she makes or any sworn pledge to deny herself.
But if her husband says nothing to her about it from day to day, then he confirms all her vows or pledges; he confirms them by saying nothing to her when he hears about them.
If he nullifies them some time after he heard of them, he is responsible for her guilt."
These are the regulations the LORD gave Moses concerning relationships between a man and his wife, and between a father and his daughter while she is still young and living in his house.
The LORD says to Moses,
"Avenge the Israelites on the Midianites, and then you will be gathered to your people."
Moses speaks to the people: "Arm some of your men to go to war against Midian so that the LORD’s vengeance may fall on them.
Send into battle a thousand men from each of the tribes of Israel."
So twelve thousand men are equipped for battle—a thousand from each tribe.
Moses sends them into battle—a thousand from each tribe—along with Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest, who takes with him the holy vessels and the trumpets for signaling.
They wage war against Midian as the LORD commanded Moses, and they kill every man.
Among those they kill are the five kings of Midian: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba. They also kill Balaam son of Beor with the sword.
The Israelites take the Midianite women and children captive and carry off all their herds, flocks, and goods.
They burn all the towns where the Midianites had settled, and all their camps.
They take all the plunder and spoils—including people and animals—
and bring them to Moses and Eleazar the priest and the whole Israelite assembly at the camp on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho.
Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the leaders of the community go out to meet them outside the camp.
Moses is angry with the army officers—the commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds—who are returning from the battle.
"Have you allowed all the women to live?" he asks them.
"They were the ones who followed Balaam’s advice and enticed the Israelites to be unfaithful to the LORD in the Peor incident, so that a plague struck the LORD’s people.
Now kill all the boys. And kill every woman who has slept with a man.
But spare every young woman who has never slept with a man.
"Anyone who has killed someone or touched someone who was killed must stay outside the camp seven days. Purify yourselves and your captives on the third day and the seventh day.
Purify every garment, everything made of leather, everything woven from goat hair, and everything made of wood."
Then Eleazar the priest says to the soldiers who have gone into battle, "This is what the law the LORD gave Moses requires:
Gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin, and lead—

everything that can withstand fire must be put through fire, and then it will be clean. But it must also be purified with the water of cleansing. Everything that cannot withstand fire must be put through water.
Wash your clothes on the seventh day and you will be clean. Then you may come into the camp."
The LORD says to Moses,
"You and Eleazar the priest and the family heads of the community are to count all the people and animals that were captured.
Divide the spoils equally between the soldiers who took part in the battle and the rest of the community.
From the soldiers who fought in the battle, set apart as a tribute for the LORD one out of every five hundred—whether people, cattle, donkeys, or sheep.
Take this tribute from their half share and give it to Eleazar the priest as the LORD’s part.

From the Israelites’ half, select one out of every fifty—whether people, cattle, donkeys, sheep, or other animals—and give them to the Levites, who are responsible for the care of the LORD’s tabernacle."
Moses and Eleazar the priest do as the LORD commands Moses.
The plunder remaining from what the soldiers captured is: 675,000 sheep,
72,000 cattle,
61,000 donkeys,
and 32,000 young women who have never slept with a man.
The half share of those who fought in the battle is: 337,500 sheep,
of which the tribute for the LORD is 675;
36,000 cattle, of which the tribute for the LORD is 72;
30,500 donkeys, of which the tribute for the LORD is 61;
16,000 people, of which the tribute for the LORD is 32.
Moses gives the tribute to Eleazar the priest as the LORD’s part, as the LORD commanded Moses.
The half belonging to the Israelites, which Moses sets apart from that of the fighting men—
the community’s half—is: 337,500 sheep,
36,000 cattle,
30,500 donkeys,
and 16,000 people.

From the Israelites’ half, Moses selects one out of every fifty people and animals, as the LORD commanded him, and gives them to the Levites, who are responsible for the care of the LORD’s tabernacle.
Then the officers who commanded the army—the commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds—approach Moses
and say to him, "Your servants have counted the soldiers under our command, and not one is missing.
So we have brought as an offering to the LORD the gold articles each of us acquired—armlets, bracelets, signet rings, earrings, and necklaces—to make atonement for ourselves before the LORD."
Moses and Eleazar the priest receive the gold from them—all the crafted articles.
All the gold from the commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds that Moses and Eleazar present as a gift to the LORD weighs 16,750 shekels.
Each soldier had taken plunder for himself.
Moses and Eleazar the priest receive the gold from the commanders of thousands and hundreds and bring it into the tent of meeting as a memorial for the Israelites before the LORD.
The Reubenites and Gadites, who have very large herds and flocks, see that the lands of Jazer and Gilead are well suited for livestock.
So they come to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the leaders of the community and say,
"Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo, and Beon—
the land the LORD has subdued before the community of Israel—is suitable for livestock, and we have livestock."
"If we have found favor in your sight," they say, "let this land be given to us as our possession. Do not make us cross the Jordan."
Moses says to the Gadites and Reubenites, "Should your fellow Israelites go to war while you sit here?
Why do you want to turn the hearts of the Israelites away from crossing over into the land the LORD has given them?
This is what your ancestors did when I sent them from Kadesh Barnea to look at the land.
After going up to the Valley of Eshcol and seeing the land, they turned the hearts of the Israelites away from entering the land the LORD had given them.
The LORD’s anger was aroused that day, and he swore this oath:
"Because they have not followed me wholeheartedly, not one of those who were twenty years old or more when they came up from Egypt will see the land I promised on oath to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—
not one except Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite and Joshua son of Nun, for they followed the LORD wholeheartedly."
The LORD’s anger burns against Israel, and he makes them wander in the wilderness for forty years, until the whole generation that had done evil in his sight is gone.
"And here you are—a brood of sinners risen up in place of your fathers—making the LORD even more angry with Israel.
If you turn away from following him, he will again leave all this people in the wilderness, and you will be the cause of their destruction."
Then they come up to Moses and say, "We will build pens here for our livestock and cities for our women and children.

But we will arm ourselves and lead the Israelites into their land until we have brought them to their place. Meanwhile our women and children will live in the fortified cities, for protection from the inhabitants of the land.
We will not return to our homes until each of the Israelites has received their inheritance.
We will not receive any inheritance with them on the other side of the Jordan, because our inheritance has come to us on the east side of the Jordan."
Moses says to them, "If you will do this—if you will arm yourselves before the LORD for battle,
and if all of you who are armed cross over the Jordan before the LORD until he has driven his enemies out before him—
then when the land is subdued before the LORD, you may return and be free from your obligation to the LORD and to Israel. And this land will be your possession before the LORD.
"But if you fail to do this, you will be sinning against the LORD; and you may be sure that your sin will find you out.
Build cities for your women and children and pens for your flocks, but do what you have promised."
The Gadites and Reubenites say to Moses, "We will do what the LORD has said.
Our children, our women, our livestock, and all our other animals will remain here in the towns of Gilead.
But we will arm ourselves for battle and go over before the LORD to fight, as the LORD has said."
Then Moses gives orders about them to Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun and to the family heads of the Israelite tribes.

He says to them, "If the Gadites and Reubenites, every man armed for battle, cross over the Jordan with you before the LORD, then when the land is subdued before you, give them the land of Gilead as their possession.
But if they do not cross over with you armed, they must accept their possession among you in Canaan."
The Gadites and Reubenites answer, "We will do what the LORD has said:
we will cross over before the LORD into Canaan armed, and the possession of our inheritance will remain with us on this side of the Jordan."

Moses gives to the Gadites, the Reubenites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan—the whole land with its cities and the territory around them.
The Gadites rebuild Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer,
Atroth Shophan, Jazer, Jogbehah,
Beth Nimrah, and Beth Haran—fortified cities—and pens for flocks.
The Reubenites rebuild Heshbon, Elealeh, and Kiriathaim,
as well as Nebo and Baal Meon (whose names are changed) and Sibmah. They give new names to the cities they rebuild.
The descendants of Makir son of Manasseh go to Gilead, capture it, and drive out the Amorites who are there.
So Moses gives Gilead to the Makirites, the descendants of Manasseh, and they settle there.
Jair, a descendant of Manasseh, captures their settlements and calls them Havvoth Jair—the Tent Villages of Jair.
And Nobah captures Kenath and its surrounding villages and calls it Nobah after himself.
Here are the stages of the journey of the Israelites as they come out of Egypt by their divisions under the leadership of Moses and Aaron.
At the LORD’s command Moses records the stages of the journey. These are the stages by their marching orders:
The Israelites set out from Rameses on the fifteenth day of the first month, the day after the Passover. They march out defiantly in full view of all the Egyptians,
while the Egyptians are burying all their firstborn, whom the LORD has struck down among them; for the LORD has brought judgment on their gods.
They set out from Rameses and camp at Succoth.
They set out from Succoth and camp at Etham, on the edge of the wilderness.
They set out from Etham, turn back to Pi-hahiroth, to the east of Baal-zephon, and camp near Migdol.
They set out from Pi-hahiroth, pass through the sea into the wilderness, and travel a three-day journey in the wilderness of Etham. They camp at Marah.
They set out from Marah and come to Elim, where there are twelve springs and seventy palm trees. They camp there.
They set out from Elim and camp by the Red Sea.
They set out from the Red Sea and camp in the wilderness of Sin.
They set out from the wilderness of Sin and camp at Dophkah.
They set out from Dophkah and camp at Alush.
They set out from Alush and camp at Rephidim, where there is no water for the people to drink.
They set out from Rephidim and camp in the wilderness of Sinai.
They set out from the wilderness of Sinai and camp at Kibroth-hattaavah.
They set out from Kibroth-hattaavah and camp at Hazeroth.
They set out from Hazeroth and camp at Rithmah.
They set out from Rithmah and camp at Rimmon-perez.
They set out from Rimmon-perez and camp at Libnah.
They set out from Libnah and camp at Rissah.
They set out from Rissah and camp at Kehelathah.
They set out from Kehelathah and camp at Mount Shepher.
They set out from Mount Shepher and camp at Haradah.
They set out from Haradah and camp at Makheloth.
They set out from Makheloth and camp at Tahath.
They set out from Tahath and camp at Terah.
They set out from Terah and camp at Mithkah.
They set out from Mithkah and camp at Hashmonah.
They set out from Hashmonah and camp at Moseroth.
They set out from Moseroth and camp at Bene-jaakan.
They set out from Bene-jaakan and camp at Hor-haggidgad.
They set out from Hor-haggidgad and camp at Jotbathah.
They set out from Jotbathah and camp at Abronah.
They set out from Abronah and camp at Ezion-geber.
They set out from Ezion-geber and camp at Kadesh, in the wilderness of Zin.
They set out from Kadesh and camp at Mount Hor, on the edge of the land of Edom.
At the LORD’s command, Aaron the priest goes up Mount Hor, where he dies on the first day of the fifth month of the fortieth year after the Israelites came out of Egypt.
Aaron is a hundred and twenty-three years old when he dies on Mount Hor.
The Canaanite king of Arad, who lives in the Negev of Canaan, hears that the Israelites are coming.
They set out from Mount Hor and camp at Zalmonah.
They set out from Zalmonah and camp at Punon.
They set out from Punon and camp at Oboth.
They set out from Oboth and camp at Iye-abarim, on the border of Moab.
They set out from Iyim and camp at Dibon-gad.
They set out from Dibon-gad and camp at Almon-diblathaim.
They set out from Almon-diblathaim and camp in the mountains of Abarim, near Nebo.
They set out from the mountains of Abarim and camp on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho.
There on the plains of Moab they camp along the Jordan from Beth-jeshimoth to Abel-shittim.
On the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho, the LORD speaks to Moses:
"When you cross the Jordan into Canaan,
drive out all the inhabitants before you.
Destroy all their carved images and cast idols,
and demolish all their high places.
Take possession of the land and settle in it,
for I have given you the land to possess.
Distribute it among the clans by lot.
To a larger group give a larger portion;
to a smaller group, a smaller one.
Whatever falls to them by lot will be theirs.
Distribute it according to your ancestral tribes.
But if you do not drive out the inhabitants,
those you allow to remain will become barbs in your eyes
and thorns in your sides—
they will give you trouble in the land where you will live.
And then I will do to you
what I plan to do to them."
The LORD says to Moses,
"Give this command to the Israelites: when you enter Canaan, the land that will be allotted to you as an inheritance will have these boundaries:
"Your southern side will include some of the wilderness of Zin along the border of Edom. On the east, your southern boundary will begin at the end of the Dead Sea.
It will cross to the south of Scorpion Pass, continue on to Zin, and go south of Kadesh Barnea. Then it will go to Hazar-addar and over to Azmon.
From Azmon it will turn, join the Wadi of Egypt, and end at the Mediterranean Sea.
"Your western boundary will be the coast of the Mediterranean Sea. This will be your boundary on the west.
"For your northern boundary, run a line from the Mediterranean Sea to Mount Hor.
From Mount Hor draw a line to Lebo-hamath, and the boundary will come out at Zedad.
Then it will continue to Ziphron and end at Hazar-enan. This will be your northern boundary.
"For your eastern boundary, draw a line from Hazar-enan to Shepham.
The boundary will go down from Shepham to Riblah, on the east side of Ain. From there it will continue along the slopes east of the Sea of Kinnereth.
Then the boundary will go down along the Jordan and end at the Dead Sea. These will be your boundaries on all sides."
Moses commands the Israelites: "Assign this land by lot as an inheritance. The LORD has ordered that it be given to the nine and a half tribes,
because the families of the tribe of Reuben, the tribe of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have already received their inheritance.
These two and a half tribes have received their inheritance east of the Jordan across from Jericho, toward the sunrise."
The LORD says to Moses,
"These are the names of the men who are to assign the land for you as an inheritance: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun.
And appoint one leader from each tribe to help assign the land.
These are the names of the men: from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
from the tribe of Simeon, Shemuel son of Ammihud;
from the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad son of Kislon;
from the tribe of Dan, Bukki son of Jogli;
from the tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph, Hanniel son of Ephod;
from the tribe of Ephraim son of Joseph, Kemuel son of Shiphtan;
from the tribe of Zebulun, Elizaphan son of Parnach;
from the tribe of Issachar, Paltiel son of Azzan;
from the tribe of Asher, Ahihud son of Shelomi;
from the tribe of Naphtali, Pedahel son of Ammihud."
These are the ones the LORD commands to assign the inheritance to the Israelites in the land of Canaan.
On the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho, the LORD says to Moses,
"Command the Israelites to give the Levites towns to live in from the inheritance the Israelites will possess. And give the Levites pasturelands around the towns.
Then the Levites will have towns to live in and pasturelands for the cattle, flocks, and all their other animals.
The pasturelands around the towns that you give the Levites will extend a thousand cubits from the town wall.

Outside the town, measure two thousand cubits on the east side, two thousand on the south side, two thousand on the west side, and two thousand on the north side, with the town in the center. This will be the pastureland for their towns.
"Six of the towns you give the Levites will be cities of refuge, to which a person who has killed someone may flee. In addition, give them forty-two other towns.
In all you must give the Levites forty-eight towns, together with their pasturelands.

The towns you give the Levites from the land the Israelites possess are to be given in proportion to the inheritance of each tribe: take many towns from a tribe that has many, but few from one that has few."
Then the LORD says to Moses:
"Speak to the Israelites and say to them: when you cross the Jordan into Canaan,
select some towns to be your cities of refuge, where a person who has killed someone accidentally may flee.
They will be places of refuge from the avenger, so that anyone accused of murder may not die before standing trial before the assembly.
These six towns you give will be your cities of refuge.
Give three on this side of the Jordan and three in Canaan as cities of refuge.
These six towns will be a place of refuge for Israelites and for foreigners residing among them—so that anyone who has killed another accidentally can flee there."
"If anyone strikes someone a fatal blow with an iron object, that person is a murderer; the murderer is to be put to death.
Or if anyone is holding a stone and strikes someone a fatal blow with it, that person is a murderer; the murderer is to be put to death.
Or if anyone is holding a wooden object and strikes someone a fatal blow with it, that person is a murderer; the murderer is to be put to death.
The avenger of blood shall put the murderer to death; when the avenger meets the murderer, the avenger shall put them to death.
If anyone with malice pushes another person or throws something at them intentionally so that they die,

or if out of enmity strikes another person with their fist so that the person dies, that person is to be put to death; that person is a murderer. The avenger of blood shall put the murderer to death when they meet.
"But if without enmity someone suddenly shoves another or throws something at them unintentionally,
or without seeing them drops on them a stone heavy enough to kill them, and they die—though they were not their enemy and they meant no harm—
then the assembly must judge between the accused and the avenger of blood according to these regulations.

The assembly must protect the one accused of murder from the avenger of blood and send them back to the city of refuge they fled to. The accused must stay there until the death of the high priest, who was anointed with the holy oil.
"But if the accused ever goes outside the limits of the city of refuge they fled to
and the avenger of blood finds them outside the city, the avenger of blood may kill the accused without being guilty of murder.
The accused must stay in the city of refuge until the death of the high priest; only after the death of the high priest may they return to their own property."
"This is to be a legal requirement for you throughout the generations to come, wherever you live."
"Anyone who kills a person is to be put to death as a murderer only on the testimony of witnesses. But no one is to be put to death on the testimony of only one witness.
"Do not accept a ransom for the life of a murderer, who deserves to die. They are to be put to death.
"Do not accept a ransom for anyone who has fled to a city of refuge and so allow them to go back and live on their own land before the death of the high priest.
"Do not pollute the land where you are. Bloodshed pollutes the land, and atonement cannot be made for the land on which blood has been shed, except by the blood of the one who shed it.
Do not defile the land where you live and where I dwell, for I, the LORD, dwell among the Israelites."

The family heads of the clan of Gilead son of Makir, the son of Manasseh, who belong to the clans of the descendants of Joseph, come forward and speak before Moses and the leaders—the family heads of the Israelites.

They say, "When the LORD commanded my lord to give the land as an inheritance by lot to the Israelites, my lord was commanded by the LORD to give the inheritance of our brother Zelophehad to his daughters.

Now suppose they marry men from other Israelite tribes; then their inheritance will be taken from our ancestral inheritance and added to that of the tribe they marry into. And so part of the inheritance allotted to us will be taken away.

When the Year of Jubilee for the Israelites comes, their inheritance will be added to that of the tribe into which they marry, and their property will be taken from the tribal inheritance of our ancestors."
Then at the LORD’s command Moses gives this ruling to the Israelites: "What the tribe of the descendants of Joseph is saying is right.
This is what the LORD commands for Zelophehad’s daughters: they may marry anyone they please, as long as they marry within a clan of their father’s tribe.
No inheritance in Israel is to pass from one tribe to another, for every Israelite shall keep the tribal inheritance of their ancestors.
Every daughter who inherits land in any Israelite tribe must marry someone in her father’s tribal clan, so that every Israelite will possess the inheritance of their ancestors.
No inheritance may pass from one tribe to another, for each Israelite tribe is to keep the land it inherits."
So Zelophehad’s daughters do as the LORD commanded Moses.
Zelophehad’s daughters—Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah—marry their cousins on their father’s side.
They marry within the clans of the descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, and their inheritance remains in their father’s tribal clan.
These are the commands and regulations the LORD gave through Moses to the Israelites on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho.
These are the words Moses speaks to all Israel on the east side of the Jordan — in the wilderness, in the Arabah opposite Suph, between Paran and Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, and Dizahab.
It is an eleven-day journey from Horeb by the way of Mount Seir to Kadesh-barnea.
In the fortieth year, on the first day of the eleventh month, Moses speaks to the people of Israel everything YHWH has commanded him to say to them —
after he has defeated Sihon king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon, and Og king of Bashan, who ruled in Ashtaroth and in Edrei.
East of the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses undertakes to set out this instruction:
"YHWH our God said to us at Horeb: 'You have stayed at this mountain long enough.

Break camp and set out for the hill country of the Amorites — and to all their neighbors in the Arabah, the hill country, the lowlands, the Negev, and the coast: the land of Canaan, and Lebanon, as far as the great river, the Euphrates.
Look — I have set this land before you. Go in and take possession of the land that YHWH swore to give to your fathers — to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob — and to their descendants after them.'"
"At that time I said to you: 'I cannot carry you alone.
YHWH your God has multiplied you until you are as many as the stars of the sky.
May YHWH, the God of your fathers, multiply you a thousand times over and bless you as he has promised!
But how can I carry your burden, your disputes, and your quarrels all by myself?
Choose from your tribes wise, discerning, and experienced men, and I will appoint them as your heads.'
You answered me: 'The plan is good.'

So I took the heads of your tribes — wise and experienced men — and appointed them as your leaders: commanders of thousands, commanders of hundreds, commanders of fifties, commanders of tens, and officers over your tribes.
I instructed your judges at that time: 'Hear the disputes that come between your people. Judge rightly between a man and his fellow Israelite, and between a man and a foreigner among you.
Show no partiality in judgment — hear the small and the great alike. Do not be intimidated by anyone, for the judgment belongs to God. Any case too hard for you, bring to me — I will hear it.'
At that time I gave you all the instructions about everything you were to do."

"Then we set out from Horeb and traveled through that whole vast and dreadful wilderness you saw, on the road to the hill country of the Amorites, just as YHWH our God commanded us. And we arrived at Kadesh-barnea.
I said to you: 'You have come to the hill country of the Amorites, which YHWH our God is giving us.
Look — YHWH your God has set this land before you. Go up and take possession of it, as YHWH, the God of your fathers, told you. Do not be afraid. Do not lose heart.'
Then all of you came to me and said: 'Let us send men ahead of us to scout out the land — to report back about the route and the towns we will find.'
The plan seemed good to me, so I chose twelve men from among you, one from each tribe.
They set out, went up into the hill country, and came to the Wadi Eshcol and explored it.
They gathered fruit from the land and brought it back to us, and gave their report: 'The land that YHWH our God is giving us is good.'"
"But you were unwilling to go up. You rebelled against the command of YHWH your God.
You grumbled in your tents and said: 'Because YHWH hated us, he brought us out of Egypt to hand us over to the Amorites and destroy us!

Where can we go? Our brothers have made our hearts melt — they report that the people are bigger and taller than we are, and their cities are great and fortified sky-high. We even saw the Anakites there!'
I said to you: 'Do not be terrified. Do not be afraid of them.
YHWH your God goes before you. He will fight for you — just as he did for you in Egypt, right before your eyes,
and in the wilderness too. There you saw how YHWH your God carried you, as a father carries his son, all the way you traveled until you arrived at this place.'
But for all that, you did not trust YHWH your God,
who went ahead of you on the journey — in fire by night and in cloud by day — to scout out a camping place and to show you the route you should take."
"YHWH heard your complaints and was furious. He swore an oath:
'Not one person of this evil generation will see the good land I swore to give your fathers —
no one except Caleb son of Jephunneh. He will see it. To him and his descendants I will give the land he walked on, because he followed YHWH wholeheartedly.'
YHWH was also angry with me on your account, saying: 'You too will not enter there.
Joshua son of Nun, who stands before you — he will enter. Strengthen him, for he will lead Israel to inherit the land.'
'And your little ones, who you said would be taken captive, and your children who today do not yet know good from evil — they will enter the land. I will give it to them and they will possess it.
But as for you — turn around and set out for the wilderness, on the road to the Red Sea.'"

"Then you answered me: 'We have sinned against YHWH. We ourselves will go up and fight, just as YHWH our God commanded us.' Each of you buckled on his weapons, treating the ascent into the hill country as a simple thing.
But YHWH said to me: 'Tell them: Do not go up and do not fight — for I am not among you. If you do, you will be struck down before your enemies.'
I told you this, but you would not listen. You rebelled against YHWH's command and presumptuously went up into the hill country.
The Amorites who lived in those hills came out against you and chased you like a swarm of bees. They drove you back from Seir all the way to Hormah.
You came back and wept before YHWH, but YHWH did not listen to your voice and gave you no attention.
So you stayed in Kadesh many days — all the time you remained there."
"Then we turned and set out for the wilderness by the road to the Red Sea, as YHWH told me. We circled around Mount Seir for many days.
Then YHWH said to me:
'You have circled this mountain long enough. Turn north.
Give the people this command: You are about to pass through the territory of your brothers, the sons of Esau who live in Seir. They will be afraid of you — so be very careful.
Do not provoke them, for I will not give you any of their land — not even enough for a footstep — because I have given Mount Seir to Esau as his possession.
You may purchase food from them with silver so that you can eat; purchase water from them with silver so that you can drink.'

For YHWH your God has blessed you in everything your hands have done. He has watched over your journey through this great wilderness. These forty years YHWH your God has been with you — you have lacked nothing.

So we passed through the territory of our brothers, the sons of Esau who live in Seir, turning away from the Arabah road, away from Elath and Ezion-geber. We turned and traveled the road toward the wilderness of Moab."
"YHWH said to me: 'Do not harass Moab or provoke them to war, for I will not give you any of their land as a possession. I have given Ar to the sons of Lot as their possession.'
(The Emim previously lived there — a great and numerous people, as tall as the Anakites.
Like the Anakites, they are considered Rephaim, though the Moabites call them Emim.
The Horites previously lived in Seir too, but the sons of Esau dispossessed them, destroying them and settling in their place — just as Israel did in the land YHWH gave them.)
"Now rise up — cross the Wadi Zered." So we crossed the Wadi Zered.

The time from when we left Kadesh-barnea until we crossed the Wadi Zered was thirty-eight years — until the entire generation of fighting men had perished from the camp, as YHWH had sworn concerning them.
Indeed, the hand of YHWH was against them, routing them from the camp until they were gone.
"When all the fighting men among the people had died,
YHWH said to me:
'Today you are to cross the border of Moab at Ar.

When you approach the territory of the Ammonites, do not harass them or provoke them to war, for I will not give you any of the Ammonites' land as a possession — I have given it to the sons of Lot as their possession.'
(That land also is considered the land of the Rephaim — Rephaim previously lived there, though the Ammonites called them Zamzummim.
They were a great, numerous, and tall people — as tall as the Anakites. But YHWH destroyed them before the Ammonites, and they dispossessed them and settled in their place.
He did the same for the sons of Esau who live in Seir when he destroyed the Horites before them. They dispossessed them and have lived in their place to this day.
And as for the Avvim, who lived in villages as far as Gaza — the Caphtorites who came from Caphtor destroyed them and settled in their place.)
'Rise up, set out, and cross the Arnon valley. Look — I am handing over Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land to you. Begin to take possession. Engage him in battle.
This very day I will begin to put the dread and fear of you upon the peoples under all heaven. When they hear about you they will tremble and writhe with anguish before you.'"
"So I sent messengers from the wilderness of Kedemoth to Sihon king of Heshbon with peaceful words, saying:
'Let me pass through your land. I will travel only on the highway — I will turn neither right nor left.
Sell me food to eat for silver, and water to drink for silver. Only let me pass through on foot,
as the sons of Esau who live in Seir allowed me, and the Moabites who live in Ar — until I cross the Jordan into the land that YHWH our God is giving us.'
But Sihon king of Heshbon would not let us pass through, for YHWH your God had made his spirit stubborn and his heart hard, in order to give him into your hand — as is now evident.
YHWH said to me: 'Look — I have already begun to hand over Sihon and his land to you. Begin now — take possession of his land.'
Then Sihon came out against us — he and all his people — to fight at Jahaz.
YHWH our God delivered him into our hands, and we struck him down — him, his sons, and all his people.
We captured all his cities at that time and devoted every city to destruction — men, women, and children — leaving no survivor.
We kept only the livestock as plunder for ourselves, along with the spoil of the cities we captured.
From Aroer on the rim of the Arnon valley, and from the city in the valley itself, all the way to Gilead — not a city was too strong for us. YHWH our God gave it all over to us.
But you did not approach the territory of the Ammonites — neither the bank of the Jabbok, nor the cities of the hill country, nor anything that YHWH our God had forbidden us."
"Then we turned and went up the road to Bashan. Og king of Bashan came out against us — he and all his people — to fight at Edrei.
YHWH said to me: 'Do not be afraid of him, for I am handing him over to you — him and all his people and his land. Do to him what you did to Sihon king of the Amorites who ruled in Heshbon.'
So YHWH our God also gave Og king of Bashan and all his people into our hands. We struck them down until no survivor was left.
We captured all his cities at that time — there was not a city we did not take: sixty cities, the whole region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
All these cities were fortified with high walls, double gates, and bars — in addition to a great many unwalled villages.
We devoted them to destruction, just as we had done to Sihon king of Heshbon — every city: men, women, and children.
But all the livestock and the spoil of the cities we took for ourselves as plunder.
So at that time we took from the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan the territory from the Arnon valley to Mount Hermon —
(the Sidonians call Hermon "Sirion," and the Amorites call it "Senir") —
all the cities of the plateau, all of Gilead, and all of Bashan as far as Salecah and Edrei — towns of Og's kingdom in Bashan.
(Only Og king of Bashan was left of the Rephaim. His bed was a bed of iron — it stands in Rabbah of the Ammonites to this day — nine cubits long and four cubits wide, measured by the standard cubit.)
"At that time we took possession of this land. From Aroer on the edge of the Arnon valley, with half the hill country of Gilead and its cities, I gave to the Reubenites and the Gadites.
The rest of Gilead and all of Bashan — the kingdom of Og — I gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh. All that region of Argob — all of Bashan — was formerly called the land of the Rephaim.
(Jair the Manassite took the entire region of Argob as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites and named it after himself — Havvoth-jair — as it is known to this day.)
To Machir I gave Gilead.
To the Reubenites and Gadites I gave the territory from Gilead down to the Arnon valley — the middle of the valley as the boundary — and to the Jabbok river, which borders Ammon;
also the Arabah with the Jordan as the boundary, from Kinnereth down to the Sea of the Arabah — the Salt Sea — below the slopes of Pisgah on the east.
I commanded you at that time: 'YHWH your God has given you this land to possess. All your fighting men must cross over armed ahead of your fellow Israelites.
But your wives, your children, and your livestock — I know you have much livestock — may remain in the towns I have given you,

until YHWH gives rest to your brothers as he has to you, and they too have taken possession of the land YHWH your God is giving them beyond the Jordan. After that, each man may return to the possession I have given him.'"
"I also commanded Joshua at that time: 'Your own eyes have seen everything YHWH your God has done to these two kings. YHWH will do the same to every kingdom you are about to enter.
Do not be afraid of them — YHWH your God himself will fight for you.'
At that time I pleaded with YHWH:
'O Lord YHWH — you have only begun to show your servant your greatness and your mighty hand. What god is there in heaven or on earth who can do the works and the mighty deeds that you do?
Let me cross over and see the good land that is beyond the Jordan — that beautiful hill country, and Lebanon.'
But YHWH was angry with me on your account and would not listen. YHWH said to me: 'Enough of this — speak to me no more about this matter.
Go up to the top of Pisgah and look out to the west, the north, the south, and the east. Look carefully with your own eyes — for you will not cross this Jordan.
Commission Joshua. Strengthen him and encourage him, for he will cross over before this people and will give them possession of the land you will see.'
So we remained in the valley opposite Beth-peor."
"Now, Israel, listen to the statutes and the judgments I am teaching you to follow, so that you may live and go in and take possession of the land that YHWH, the God of your fathers, is giving you.
You must not add to the word I command you, and you must not subtract from it — so that you may keep the commands of YHWH your God that I am giving you.
Your own eyes saw what YHWH did at Baal-peor: YHWH your God destroyed from among you every person who followed the Baal of Peor.
But all of you who held fast to YHWH your God are alive today — every one of you.
Look — I have taught you statutes and judgments just as YHWH my God commanded me, so that you may follow them in the land you are entering to possess.

Observe and keep them carefully, for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the peoples. When they hear all these statutes, they will say: 'Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.'
For what great nation is there that has a god so near to it as YHWH our God is to us whenever we call on him?
And what great nation has statutes and judgments as righteous as all this instruction I am setting before you today?"

"Only take care. Guard yourself carefully, lest you forget the things your eyes have seen — lest they depart from your heart all the days of your life. Make them known to your children and your children's children:

the day you stood before YHWH your God at Horeb, when YHWH said to me: 'Gather the people to me — I will let them hear my words, so that they may learn to fear me all the days they live on the earth, and so teach their children.'
You came near and stood at the foot of the mountain. The mountain burned with fire to the heart of heaven — darkness, cloud, and thick darkness.
Then YHWH spoke to you out of the fire. You heard the sound of words, but saw no form — only a voice.
He declared to you his covenant — the Ten Words — which he commanded you to keep, and wrote them on two tablets of stone.
YHWH commanded me at that time to teach you statutes and judgments, so that you might do them in the land you are crossing over to possess."
"So be very careful — since you saw no form on the day YHWH spoke to you at Horeb out of the fire —
lest you act corruptly by making for yourselves an idol in any image whatsoever: the form of a man or a woman,
the form of any animal on the earth, or the form of any bird that flies in the sky,
the form of anything that creeps on the ground, or the form of any fish in the waters below the earth.

And lest you lift your eyes to heaven and see the sun, the moon, the stars — all the host of heaven — and be drawn astray to bow down to them and serve them. YHWH your God has allotted these to all the peoples under all the heavens.
But YHWH took you and brought you out of the iron furnace — Egypt — to be a people of his own inheritance, as you are today.
Now YHWH was angry with me because of you, and he swore that I would not cross the Jordan and would not enter the good land that YHWH your God is giving you as an inheritance.
I am going to die in this land. I will not cross the Jordan. But you will cross over and take possession of that good land.
Take care, then, lest you forget the covenant of YHWH your God that he made with you — and make for yourselves an idol in any form, which YHWH your God has forbidden you.
For YHWH your God is a consuming fire — a jealous God."

"When you have had children and grandchildren and have grown old in the land — if you act corruptly by making an idol in any form, and do what is evil in the eyes of YHWH your God, provoking him to anger:
I call heaven and earth as witnesses against you this day: you will be swiftly swept off the land you are crossing the Jordan to possess. You will not live long in it — you will be utterly destroyed.
YHWH will scatter you among the peoples, and only a handful of you will survive among the nations where YHWH drives you.
There you will serve gods made by human hands — wood and stone — that can neither see nor hear, neither eat nor smell.
But from there you will seek YHWH your God, and you will find him — when you search for him with all your heart and with all your soul.
When you are in distress and all these things come upon you in the days to come, you will return to YHWH your God and listen to his voice.
For YHWH your God is a merciful God. He will not abandon you or destroy you. He will not forget the covenant with your fathers that he swore to them."

"Ask now about the former days, before your time — from the day God created humanity on the earth, and from one end of heaven to the other: has anything as great as this ever happened, or has anything like it ever been heard of?
Has any people heard the voice of God speaking out of fire — as you have heard — and survived?

Or has any god ever attempted to take a nation for himself from the midst of another nation, by trials, by signs, by wonders, by war, by a strong hand, by an outstretched arm, and by great terrors — like everything YHWH your God did for you in Egypt before your eyes?
You were shown all this so that you would know: YHWH alone is God — there is no other beside him.
From heaven he let you hear his voice to discipline you; on earth he let you see his great fire; and from the midst of that fire you heard his words.
And because he loved your fathers and chose their descendants after them, he brought you out of Egypt with his presence — with his great power —
to drive out before you nations greater and mightier than you and to bring you in and give you their land as an inheritance — as it is today.
Therefore know today — take it to your heart — that YHWH is God in heaven above and on the earth below. There is no other.

Keep his statutes and his commandments, which I am commanding you today, so that it may go well with you and with your children after you — and so that you may live long in the land that YHWH your God is giving you for all time."
Then Moses sets apart three cities on the east side of the Jordan,
so that a killer who has killed his neighbor unintentionally — without previous hostility — could flee there and find sanctuary: Bezer in the wilderness, on the plateau, for the Reubenites;
Ramoth in Gilead for the Gadites; and Golan in Bashan for the Manassites.
This is the instruction Moses sets before the people of Israel.
These are the testimonies, the statutes, and the judgments Moses spoke to the people of Israel when they came out of Egypt —
east of the Jordan, in the valley opposite Beth-peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites who ruled in Heshbon, whom Moses and the people of Israel defeated when they came out of Egypt.
They took possession of his land and the land of Og king of Bashan — the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan —
from Aroer on the edge of the Arnon valley to Mount Siyon (that is, Hermon),
and all the Arabah east of the Jordan as far as the Sea of the Arabah, below the slopes of Pisgah.
Moses calls all Israel together and says to them: "Listen, Israel, to the statutes and judgments I speak in your hearing today. Learn them. Be careful to follow them.
YHWH our God made a covenant with us at Horeb.
It was not with our fathers that YHWH made this covenant, but with us — with all of us who are alive here today.
YHWH spoke to you face to face at the mountain out of the fire.
(I stood between YHWH and you at that time to declare to you the word of YHWH — because you were afraid of the fire and did not go up the mountain.) He said:"
"I am YHWH your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
You shall have no other gods before me.
You shall not make for yourself an idol, or any likeness of what is in heaven above, or what is on the earth below, or what is in the water under the earth.

You shall not bow down to them or serve them — for I, YHWH your God, am a jealous God, bringing the consequences of the fathers' sin upon the children to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me,
but showing covenant faithfulness to the thousands who love me and keep my commands.
You shall not take the name of YHWH your God in vain, for YHWH will not leave unpunished the one who takes his name in vain.
Observe the Sabbath day and keep it holy, as YHWH your God commanded you.
Six days you shall labor and do all your work,

but the seventh day is a Sabbath to YHWH your God. You shall not do any work — you, your son or daughter, your male or female servant, your ox or donkey, or any of your livestock, or the foreigner who lives within your gates — so that your male and female servant may rest as well as you.

Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and YHWH your God brought you out from there with a strong hand and an outstretched arm. Therefore YHWH your God commanded you to keep the Sabbath day.
Honor your father and your mother, as YHWH your God commanded you — so that your days may be long and things may go well with you in the land that YHWH your God is giving you.
You shall not murder.
You shall not commit adultery.
You shall not steal.
You shall not give false testimony against your neighbor.
You shall not covet your neighbor's wife. You shall not covet your neighbor's house, his field, his male servant or female servant, his ox or donkey — or anything that belongs to your neighbor."

These words YHWH speaks to your whole assembly at the mountain — out of the fire, the cloud, and the thick darkness — with a great voice that does not continue. He writes them on two tablets of stone and gives them to me.
When you hear the voice out of the darkness, with the mountain burning with fire, all the heads of your tribes and your elders come to me.
You say: 'YHWH our God has shown us his glory and his greatness, and we have heard his voice out of the fire. Today we have seen that God speaks with a human being — and that person lives.
But now, why should we die? This great fire will consume us. If we hear the voice of YHWH our God any more, we will die.
For who is there of all flesh who has heard the voice of the living God speaking out of the middle of the fire as we have — and survived?
Go near and hear everything YHWH our God says, and tell us everything YHWH our God tells you. We will hear it and we will do it.'
YHWH hears your words when you speak to me, and says to me: 'I have heard the words these people have spoken to you. Everything they said was good.
If only they had such a heart — to fear me and keep all my commands always — so that things would go well with them and with their children forever!
Go and tell them to return to their tents.
But you — stand here with me, and I will tell you all the commandments, the statutes, and the judgments you are to teach them, so that they may do them in the land I am giving them to possess.'
You must be careful, then, to do as YHWH your God has commanded you. You shall not turn aside to the right or to the left.
You shall walk in all the way that YHWH your God has commanded you, so that you may live, and it may go well with you, and you may live long in the land you are going to possess.
"Now this is the commandment — the statutes and judgments — that YHWH your God commanded me to teach you to follow in the land you are crossing over to possess,

so that you may fear YHWH your God — you, your son, and your grandson — by keeping all his statutes and commandments that I am commanding you, all the days of your life, and so that your days may be long.

Hear, therefore, Israel — be careful to do this, so that it may go well with you and you may multiply greatly — just as YHWH, the God of your fathers, promised you: a land flowing with milk and honey."
Hear, O Israel:
YHWH our God — YHWH is one.
Love YHWH your God with all your heart,
with all your soul,
and with all your strength.
These words that I command you today must be on your heart.
Impress them on your children. Speak of them when you sit in your house and when you walk along the road — when you lie down and when you rise up.
Bind them as a sign on your hand. Let them be a reminder on your forehead between your eyes.
Write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates.
"And when YHWH your God brings you into the land he swore to your fathers — to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob — to give you: great and fine cities you did not build,
houses full of every good thing you did not fill, cisterns already cut that you did not carve, vineyards and olive trees you did not plant — and you eat and are full:
take care that you do not forget YHWH, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
It is YHWH your God you must fear. Him you shall serve. By his name alone shall you swear.
You shall not go after other gods — the gods of the peoples who are around you,
for YHWH your God in your midst is a jealous God — lest the anger of YHWH your God burn against you and he destroy you from the face of the earth."
"Do not test YHWH your God as you tested him at Massah.
You shall carefully keep the commandments of YHWH your God, and his testimonies and his statutes that he has commanded you.
Do what is right and good in the sight of YHWH, so that it may go well with you and you may enter and take possession of the good land that YHWH swore to give to your fathers,
driving out all your enemies before you — as YHWH has said."
"When your son asks you in time to come: 'What is the meaning of the testimonies and statutes and judgments that YHWH our God commanded you?' —
you shall say to your son: 'We were slaves to Pharaoh in Egypt, and YHWH brought us out of Egypt with a strong hand.
YHWH showed great and terrible signs and wonders against Egypt — against Pharaoh and all his household — right before our eyes.
He brought us out from there in order to bring us in and give us the land he had sworn to give our fathers.
YHWH commanded us to do all these statutes — to fear YHWH our God — for our good always, and for our preservation, as it is to this day.
It will be righteousness for us when we are careful to do all this commandment before YHWH our God, just as he commanded us.'"

"When YHWH your God brings you into the land you are entering to possess and drives out before you many nations — the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites: seven nations greater and mightier than you —
and when YHWH your God hands them over to you and you defeat them, you must devote them to complete destruction. Make no covenant with them and show them no mercy.
Do not intermarry with them. Do not give your daughters to their sons or take their daughters for your sons,
for they would turn your sons away from following me to serve other gods. Then YHWH's anger would burn against you and he would destroy you quickly.
Instead, this is what you must do to them: tear down their altars, smash their sacred pillars, cut down their Asherah poles, and burn their carved images in the fire."
"For you are a holy people to YHWH your God. YHWH your God has chosen you to be his treasured possession out of all the peoples on the face of the earth.
It was not because you were more numerous than all the other peoples that YHWH set his love on you and chose you — for you are the fewest of all peoples.

It was because YHWH loved you, and because he kept his oath to your fathers, that YHWH brought you out with a strong hand and ransomed you from the house of slavery — from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.
Know therefore that YHWH your God — he is God, the faithful God who keeps covenant faithfulness for those who love him and keep his commandments, to a thousand generations,
but who repays to their face those who hate him and destroys them. He will not be slow to repay those who hate him — he will repay them to their face.
You shall therefore keep the commandment and the statutes and the judgments that I command you today, to do them."
"And because you listen to these judgments — keeping and doing them — YHWH your God will keep with you the covenant and the faithfulness he swore to your fathers.

He will love you, bless you, and multiply you. He will bless the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your ground — your grain and your new wine and your olive oil, the young of your cattle and the lambs of your flock — in the land he swore to your fathers to give you.
You will be blessed above all peoples. There will not be a barren male or female among you, nor among your livestock.
YHWH will take away from you all sickness, and none of the dreadful diseases of Egypt that you knew will he put on you — he will put them on all who hate you.
You shall consume all the peoples that YHWH your God gives over to you. Your eye shall not pity them, and you shall not serve their gods — for that would be a snare to you."
"If you say in your heart: 'These nations are more than I am — how can I drive them out?'
you shall not be afraid of them. You must remember very well what YHWH your God did to Pharaoh and to all Egypt:
the great trials your eyes saw, the signs, the wonders, the strong hand, the outstretched arm by which YHWH your God brought you out. So YHWH your God will do to all the peoples you now dread.
Moreover, YHWH your God will send the hornet among them until those who remain, who hide from you, are destroyed.
Do not be in dread of them, for YHWH your God is in your midst — a great and awesome God.
YHWH your God will clear away these nations before you little by little. You will not be able to make a quick end of them, lest the wild animals multiply against you.
But YHWH your God will give them over to you and throw them into great confusion until they are destroyed.
He will hand their kings over to you, and you shall make their names perish from under heaven. No one will be able to stand against you until you have destroyed them.
The carved images of their gods you shall burn with fire. Do not covet the silver or the gold on them and take it for yourself — lest you be ensnared by it, for it is an abomination to YHWH your God.
And you shall not bring an abominable thing into your house and become devoted to destruction like it. You shall utterly detest and abhor it, for it is set apart for destruction."
"You shall be careful to do the whole commandment I am commanding you today — so that you may live and multiply and go in and possess the land that YHWH swore to give your fathers.

And you shall remember the whole way YHWH your God led you through the wilderness these forty years — to humble you, to test you, to know what was in your heart: whether you would keep his commandments or not.

He humbled you. He let you hunger. Then he fed you with manna — which neither you nor your fathers had known — to make you know that a person does not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of YHWH.
Your clothing did not wear out on you and your feet did not swell these forty years.
Know in your heart, then, that as a man disciplines his son, YHWH your God disciplines you.
So keep the commandments of YHWH your God — walk in his ways and fear him."
"For YHWH your God is bringing you into a good land — a land of streams and springs, of deep waters flowing in valleys and hills;
a land of wheat and barley, of vines and fig trees and pomegranates, a land of olive oil and honey;
a land in which you will eat bread without scarcity — you will lack nothing in it; a land whose stones are iron and from whose hills you may mine copper.
You shall eat and be full, and you shall bless YHWH your God for the good land he has given you."
"Take care lest you forget YHWH your God by failing to keep his commandments and his judgments and his statutes, which I command you today —
lest, when you have eaten and are full and have built good houses and settled in them,
and when your herds and your flocks multiply, and your silver and gold multiply, and all that you have multiplies,
your heart grows proud and you forget YHWH your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery,
who led you through the great and terrifying wilderness — with its fiery serpents and scorpions and thirsty ground where there was no water — who brought water for you out of the hard rock,
who fed you in the wilderness with manna that your fathers did not know — to humble you and to test you, to do you good in the end.
Beware lest you say in your heart: 'My own power and the strength of my hand have produced this wealth for me.'
Remember instead that it is YHWH your God who gives you power to produce wealth — so that he may confirm his covenant that he swore to your fathers, as it is this day.
And if you ever forget YHWH your God and go after other gods and serve them and bow down to them, I warn you plainly today that you will certainly perish.
Like the nations that YHWH is destroying before you, so you will perish — because you would not listen to the voice of YHWH your God."
"Listen, Israel: you are about to cross the Jordan today to go in and dispossess nations greater and mightier than you — great cities fortified to the sky,
a people great and tall, the sons of the Anakites, whom you know. You have heard it said: 'Who can stand before the sons of Anak?'

Know today that YHWH your God goes over before you as a consuming fire. He will destroy them and bring them down before you. You will drive them out and destroy them quickly, as YHWH has promised you.

Do not say in your heart, after YHWH your God has thrust them out before you: 'It was because of my righteousness that YHWH brought me in to possess this land.' No — it is because of the wickedness of these nations that YHWH is driving them out before you.

It is not because of your righteousness or the uprightness of your heart that you are going in to possess their land, but because of the wickedness of these nations that YHWH your God is driving them out before you — and in order to confirm the word that YHWH swore to your fathers, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Know, then, that YHWH your God is not giving you this good land to possess because of your righteousness, for you are a stiff-necked people."
"Remember and do not forget how you provoked YHWH your God to anger in the wilderness. From the day you left the land of Egypt until you came to this place, you have been rebelling against YHWH.
Even at Horeb you provoked YHWH to anger — and YHWH was so angry with you that he was ready to destroy you.

When I went up the mountain to receive the stone tablets — the tablets of the covenant that YHWH made with you — I remained on the mountain forty days and forty nights. I ate no bread and drank no water.
YHWH gave me the two stone tablets written by the finger of God, and on them were all the words YHWH had spoken to you at the mountain out of the fire, on the day of the assembly.
And at the end of forty days and forty nights, YHWH gave me the two stone tablets — the tablets of the covenant.

Then YHWH said to me: 'Rise up and go down from here quickly, for your people whom you brought from Egypt have acted corruptly. They have turned aside quickly from the way I commanded them. They have made themselves a cast image.'
YHWH also said to me: 'I have seen this people — they are a stiff-necked people.
Leave me alone, and I will destroy them and blot out their name from under heaven. Then I will make of you a nation mightier and more numerous than they.'
So I turned and went down the mountain while it was burning with fire — both tablets of the covenant in my two hands.
I looked, and there you had sinned against YHWH your God. You had made yourselves a calf of cast metal and had turned aside quickly from the way that YHWH had commanded you.
So I took hold of the two tablets and threw them out of my two hands, smashing them before your eyes.

Then I threw myself before YHWH as before — lying face down forty days and forty nights, eating no bread and drinking no water — because of all the sin you had committed in doing what was evil in the eyes of YHWH, provoking him to anger.
For I dreaded the anger and the fierce wrath of YHWH — he was so enraged against you that he was going to destroy you. But YHWH listened to me that time too.
YHWH was so furious with Aaron that he was ready to destroy him. But I also interceded for Aaron at that time.
The sinful thing you had made — the calf — I took and burned it with fire, ground it to dust, and threw its dust into the stream that ran down the mountain."
"At Taberah and Massah and Kibroth-hattaavah as well, you provoked YHWH to anger.

And when YHWH sent you from Kadesh-barnea, saying: 'Go up and take possession of the land I have given you' — you rebelled against the command of YHWH your God and did not trust him or obey his voice.
You have been rebellious against YHWH from the day I knew you.
So I lay before YHWH for those forty days and forty nights, because YHWH said he would destroy you.
And I prayed to YHWH: 'O Lord YHWH, do not destroy your people — your inheritance — whom you redeemed through your greatness, whom you brought out of Egypt with a strong hand.
Remember your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Do not look at the stubbornness of this people, or at their wickedness, or at their sin,
lest the land from which you brought us out say: YHWH was not able to bring them into the land he promised them, and because he hated them he brought them out to kill them in the wilderness.
For they are your people and your inheritance, whom you brought out by your great power and your outstretched arm.'"
"At that time YHWH said to me: 'Carve two stone tablets like the first ones and come up to me on the mountain. Also make an ark of wood.
I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke. Then you shall put them in the ark.'
So I made an ark of acacia wood, carved two stone tablets like the first ones, and went up the mountain with the two tablets in my hand.
He wrote on the tablets, just as before, the Ten Words that YHWH had spoken to you at the mountain out of the fire on the day of the assembly. And YHWH gave them to me.
I turned and went down the mountain and put the tablets in the ark I had made. There they are — just as YHWH commanded me."
(The people of Israel traveled from Beeroth-bene-jaakan to Moserah. There Aaron died and was buried, and Eleazar his son became priest in his place.
From there they traveled to Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah to Jotbathah — a land with streams of water.
At that time YHWH set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the ark of the covenant of YHWH, to stand before YHWH to minister to him, and to bless in his name, to this day.
Therefore Levi has no portion or inheritance with his brothers. YHWH is his inheritance, as YHWH your God said to him.)
"I myself had stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights, as I had before. And YHWH listened to me that time too — YHWH was not willing to destroy you.
YHWH said to me: 'Rise up and go on your way before the people, so that they may go in and possess the land that I swore to their fathers to give them.'
And now, Israel — what does YHWH your God ask of you
but to fear YHWH your God,
to walk in all his ways,
to love him,
to serve YHWH your God with all your heart and with all your soul,
and to keep the commandments of YHWH and his statutes that I am commanding you today — for your own good?
Behold, to YHWH your God belong heaven and the highest heavens, the earth and everything in it.
Yet it was only to your fathers that YHWH set his heart in love — he chose their descendants after them, you above all peoples, as it is today.
Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be stiff-necked no longer.
For YHWH your God is God of gods and Lord of lords — the great, the mighty, and the awesome God, who shows no partiality and accepts no bribe.
He executes justice for the fatherless and the widow, and he loves the foreigner among you, giving him food and clothing.
Love the foreigner, therefore — for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
It is YHWH your God you must fear. Him you shall serve. To him you shall hold fast, and by his name you shall swear.
He is your praise, and he is your God — the one who has done for you these great and awesome things that your eyes have seen.
Your fathers went down to Egypt seventy persons strong. Now YHWH your God has made you as numerous as the stars of the sky."
"Love YHWH your God, therefore, and always keep his charge, his statutes, his judgments, and his commandments.
Know today — it is not your children who have not known or seen — the discipline of YHWH your God: his greatness, his strong hand, his outstretched arm,
his signs, and his deeds that he did in Egypt against Pharaoh king of Egypt and against all his land;
and what he did to the army of Egypt — to their horses and chariots — how he made the waters of the Red Sea flow over them as they pursued you, and how YHWH destroyed them, to this day;
and what he did to you in the wilderness until you came to this place;

and what he did to Dathan and Abiram the sons of Eliab, son of Reuben — how the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them with their households, their tents, and every living thing that followed them, in the midst of all Israel.
It is your own eyes that have seen all the great work of YHWH that he did."
"You shall therefore keep the whole commandment that I command you today — so that you may be strong enough to go in and possess the land you are crossing over to possess,
and so that you may live long in the land that YHWH swore to give to your fathers and to their descendants — a land flowing with milk and honey.
For the land you are entering to possess is not like the land of Egypt, from which you came, where you sowed your seed and watered it on foot like a vegetable garden.
But the land you are crossing over to possess is a land of hills and valleys that drinks water from the rain of heaven —
a land that YHWH your God cares for. The eyes of YHWH your God are always on it, from the beginning of the year to its end.
And if you will indeed obey my commandments that I command you today — loving YHWH your God and serving him with all your heart and with all your soul —
he will give the rain of your land in its season: the early rain and the later rain. And you will gather your grain and your new wine and your olive oil.
He will give grass in your fields for your livestock, and you will eat and be full.
Take care lest your heart be deceived, and you turn aside and serve other gods and bow down to them.

Then YHWH's anger will burn against you, and he will shut up the heavens so there will be no rain, and the ground will yield no fruit, and you will perish quickly off the good land that YHWH is giving you."
"You shall therefore put these words of mine on your heart and on your soul. Bind them as a sign on your hand. Let them be a reminder between your eyes.
Teach them to your children — speaking of them when you sit in your house and when you walk along the road, when you lie down and when you rise up.
Write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates,
so that your days and the days of your children may be multiplied in the land that YHWH swore to give your fathers — as long as the heavens are above the earth.
For if you are careful to keep all this commandment that I command you to do — loving YHWH your God, walking in all his ways, and holding fast to him —
then YHWH will drive out all these nations before you, and you will dispossess nations greater and mightier than you.
Every place on which the sole of your foot treads will be yours. Your territory will extend from the wilderness and Lebanon, from the Euphrates River to the western sea.
No one will be able to stand against you. YHWH your God will put the fear and dread of you on all the land you tread on, as he has told you."
