Elon, Timnah, Ekron,
Eltekeh, Gibbethon, Baalath,
Jehud, Bene-berak, Gath-rimmon,
and Me-jarkon and Rakkon with the territory over against Joppa.

When the territory of the people of Dan is lost to them, the people of Dan go up and fight against Leshem, and after capturing it and striking it with the edge of the sword they take possession of it and settle in it, calling Leshem, Dan, after the name of Dan their ancestor.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the people of Dan according to their clans, these cities with their villages.
When they finish distributing the land for inheritance by its boundaries, the people of Israel give an inheritance among them to Joshua the son of Nun.
By the command of YHWH they give him the city that he asks, Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim. And he rebuilds the city and settles in it.

These are the inheritances that Eleazar the priest and Joshua the son of Nun and the heads of the fathers' houses of the tribes of the people of Israel distribute by lot at Shiloh before YHWH, at the entrance of the tent of meeting. So they finish dividing the land.
Then YHWH says to Joshua:
“Speak to the people of Israel: 'Appoint the cities of refuge, of which I spoke to you through Moses,
that the manslayer who strikes any person without intent or unknowingly may flee there. They shall be for you a refuge from the avenger of blood.

He shall flee to one of these cities and shall stand at the entrance of the gate of the city and explain his case in the ears of the elders of that city. Then they shall take him into the city and give him a place, and he shall remain with them.
And if the avenger of blood pursues him, they shall not give the manslayer into his hand, because he struck his neighbor unknowingly and did not hate him in time past.

And he shall remain in that city until he has stood before the congregation for judgment, until the death of him who is high priest at that time. Then the manslayer may return to his own town and his own home, to the town from which he fled.'“
So they set apart Kedesh in Galilee in the hill country of Naphtali, and Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, and Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron) in the hill country of Judah.

And beyond the Jordan east of Jericho, they appoint Bezer in the wilderness on the tableland from the tribe of Reuben, and Ramoth in Gilead from the tribe of Gad, and Golan in Bashan from the tribe of Manasseh.

These are the cities designated for all the people of Israel, and for the stranger sojourning among them, that anyone who kills a person without intent may flee there, so that he may not die by the hand of the avenger of blood, until he stands before the congregation.
Then the heads of the fathers' houses of the Levites come to Eleazar the priest and to Joshua the son of Nun and to the heads of the fathers' houses of the tribes of the people of Israel.
And they say to them at Shiloh in the land of Canaan: “YHWH commanded through Moses that we be given cities to dwell in, with their pasturelands for our livestock.“
So by command of YHWH the people of Israel give to the Levites the following cities and pasturelands out of their inheritance.
The lot comes out for the clans of the Kohathites. So those Levites who are descendants of Aaron the priest receive by lot from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin, thirteen cities.
And the rest of the Kohathites receive by lot from the clans of the tribe of Ephraim, from the tribe of Dan, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, ten cities.
The Gershonites receive by lot from the clans of the tribe of Issachar, from the tribe of Asher, from the tribe of Naphtali, and from the half-tribe of Manasseh in Bashan, thirteen cities.
The Merarites according to their clans receive from the tribe of Reuben, the tribe of Gad, and the tribe of Zebulun, twelve cities.
These cities and their pasturelands the people of Israel give by lot to the Levites, just as YHWH had commanded through Moses.
They give out of the tribe of the people of Judah and the tribe of the people of Simeon these cities, which are mentioned by name,
which go to the descendants of Aaron, one of the clans of the Kohathites who belong to the Levites; since the lot is theirs first.
They give them Kiriath-arba (Arba being the father of Anak), that is, Hebron, in the hill country of Judah, along with the pasturelands around it.
But the fields of the city and its villages had been given to Caleb the son of Jephunneh as his possession.
And to the descendants of Aaron the priest they give Hebron, the city of refuge for the manslayer, with its pasturelands, Libnah with its pasturelands,
Jattir with its pasturelands, Eshtemoa with its pasturelands,
Holon with its pasturelands, Debir with its pasturelands,
Ain with its pasturelands, Juttah with its pasturelands, and Beth-shemesh with its pasturelands — nine cities out of these two tribes;
then out of the tribe of Benjamin, Gibeon with its pasturelands, Geba with its pasturelands,
Anathoth with its pasturelands, and Almon with its pasturelands — four cities.
The cities of the descendants of Aaron, the priests, are in all thirteen cities with their pasturelands.
As to the rest of the Kohathites belonging to the Kohathite clans of the Levites, the cities allotted to them are out of the tribe of Ephraim.
They are given Shechem, the city of refuge for the manslayer, with its pasturelands in the hill country of Ephraim, Gezer with its pasturelands,
Kibzaim with its pasturelands, and Beth-horon with its pasturelands — four cities;
and out of the tribe of Dan, Elteke with its pasturelands, Gibbethon with its pasturelands,
Aijalon with its pasturelands, Gath-rimmon with its pasturelands — four cities;
and out of the half-tribe of Manasseh, Taanach with its pasturelands, and Gath-rimmon with its pasturelands — two cities.
The cities of the clans of the rest of the Kohathites are ten in all with their pasturelands.

And to the Gershonites, one of the clans of the Levites, are given out of the half-tribe of Manasseh, Golan in Bashan with its pasturelands, the city of refuge for the manslayer, and Beeshterah with its pasturelands — two cities;
and out of the tribe of Issachar, Kishion with its pasturelands, Daberath with its pasturelands,
Jarmuth with its pasturelands, En-gannim with its pasturelands — four cities;
and out of the tribe of Asher, Mishal with its pasturelands, Abdon with its pasturelands,
Helkath with its pasturelands, and Rehob with its pasturelands — four cities;
and out of the tribe of Naphtali, Kedesh in Galilee with its pasturelands, the city of refuge for the manslayer, Hammoth-dor with its pasturelands, and Kartan with its pasturelands — three cities.
The cities of the several clans of the Gershonites are in all thirteen cities with their pasturelands.
And to the rest of the Levites, the Merarite clans, are given out of the tribe of Zebulun, Jokneam with its pasturelands, Kartah with its pasturelands,
Dimnah with its pasturelands, Nahalal with its pasturelands — four cities;
and out of the tribe of Reuben, Bezer with its pasturelands, Jahaz with its pasturelands,
Kedemoth with its pasturelands, and Mephaath with its pasturelands — four cities;
and out of the tribe of Gad, Ramoth in Gilead with its pasturelands, the city of refuge for the manslayer, Mahanaim with its pasturelands,
Heshbon with its pasturelands, and Jazer with its pasturelands — four cities in all.
The cities given to the Merarite clans, that is, to the rest of the Levitical clans, are in all twelve cities.
The cities of the Levites in the midst of the possession of the people of Israel are in all forty-eight cities with their pasturelands.
These cities each had their pasturelands around them. So it is with all these cities.
And YHWH gives to Israel all the land
that he swore to give to their fathers,
and they take possession of it and dwell in it.
And YHWH gives them rest on every side,
just as he swore to their fathers.
Not one of all their enemies stands before them;
YHWH gives all their enemies into their hand.
Not one word fails
of all the good word that YHWH spoke to the house of Israel;
all comes to pass.
At that time Joshua summons the Reubenites and the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh
and says to them: “You have kept all that Moses the servant of YHWH commanded you and have obeyed my voice in all that I have commanded you.
You have not forsaken your brothers these many days, down to this day, but have kept the charge of the commandment of YHWH your God.

And now YHWH your God has given rest to your brothers, as he promised them. Therefore turn and go to your tents in the land where your possession lies, which Moses the servant of YHWH gave you beyond the Jordan.

Only be very careful to observe the commandment and the law that Moses the servant of YHWH commanded you, to love YHWH your God, and to walk in all his ways and to keep his commandments and to cling to him and to serve him with all your heart and with all your soul.“
So Joshua blesses them and sends them away, and they go to their tents.

Now to the one half of the tribe of Manasseh Moses had given a possession in Bashan, but to the other half Joshua had given a possession beside their brothers in the land west of the Jordan. And when Joshua sends them away to their tents and blesses them,

he says to them: “Return to your tents with much wealth and with very much livestock, with silver, gold, bronze, and iron, and with much clothing. Divide the spoil of your enemies with your brothers.“

So the people of Reuben and the people of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh return home, parting from the people of Israel at Shiloh, which is in the land of Canaan, to go to the land of Gilead, their own land of which they had possessed themselves by command of YHWH through Moses.

And when they come to the region of the Jordan that is in the land of Canaan, the people of Reuben and the people of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh build there an altar by the Jordan, an altar of imposing size.

And the people of Israel hear it said: “Behold, the people of Reuben and the people of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh have built the altar at the frontier of the land of Canaan, in the region about the Jordan, on the side that belongs to the people of Israel.“
And when the people of Israel hear of it, the whole assembly of the people of Israel gathers at Shiloh to make war against them.
Then the people of Israel send to the people of Reuben and the people of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh, in the land of Gilead, Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest,
and with him ten chiefs, one from each of the tribal families of Israel, every one of them the head of a family among the clans of Israel.
And they come to the people of Reuben, the people of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, in the land of Gilead, and they say to them:

“Thus says the whole congregation of YHWH: 'What is this breach of faith that you have committed against the God of Israel in turning away this day from following YHWH by building yourselves an altar this day in rebellion against YHWH?
Have we not had enough of the sin at Peor from which even yet we have not cleansed ourselves, and for which there came a plague upon the congregation of YHWH,
that you too must turn away this day from following YHWH? And if you too rebel against YHWH today then tomorrow he will be angry with the whole congregation of Israel.

But now, if the land of your possession is unclean, pass over into YHWH's land where YHWH's tabernacle stands, and take for yourselves a possession among us. Only do not rebel against YHWH or make us as rebels by building yourselves an altar other than the altar of YHWH our God.
Did not Achan the son of Zerah break faith in the matter of the devoted things, and wrath fell upon all the congregation of Israel? And he did not perish alone for his iniquity.'“
Then the people of Reuben, the people of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh answer and say to the heads of the families of Israel:
“The Mighty One, God, YHWH! The Mighty One, God, YHWH!
He knows; and let Israel itself know!
If it was in rebellion or in breach of faith against YHWH,
do not spare us today.
For building an altar to turn away from following YHWH, or if to offer burnt offerings or grain offerings or peace offerings on it, may YHWH himself take vengeance.
No, but we did it from fear that in time to come your children might say to our children: 'What have you to do with YHWH, the God of Israel?
For YHWH has made the Jordan a boundary between us and you, you people of Reuben and people of Gad. You have no portion in YHWH.' So your children might make our children cease to worship YHWH.
Therefore we said: 'Let us now build an altar, not for burnt offering, nor for sacrifice,

but to be a witness between us and you, and between our generations after us, that we do perform the service of YHWH in his presence with our burnt offerings and sacrifices and peace offerings, so your children will not say to our children in time to come, “You have no portion in YHWH.“'

And we thought: 'If this should be said to us or to our descendants in time to come, we should say, “Behold, the copy of the altar of YHWH, which our fathers made, not for burnt offerings, nor for sacrifice, but to be a witness between us and you.“'

Far be it from us that we should rebel against YHWH and turn away this day from following YHWH by building an altar for burnt offering, for grain offering, or for sacrifice, other than the altar of YHWH our God that stands before his tabernacle.“

When Phinehas the priest and the chiefs of the congregation, the heads of the families of Israel who were with him, hear the words that the people of Reuben and the people of Gad and the people of Manasseh spoke, it is good in their eyes.

And Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest says to the people of Reuben and the people of Gad and the people of Manasseh: “Today we know that YHWH is in our midst, because you have not committed this breach of faith against YHWH. Now you have delivered the people of Israel from the hand of YHWH.“

Then Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest, and the chiefs, return from the people of Reuben and the people of Gad in the land of Gilead to the land of Canaan, to the people of Israel, and bring back word to them.

And the report is good in the eyes of the people of Israel. And the people of Israel bless God and speak no more of making war against them to destroy the land where the people of Reuben and the people of Gad were settled.
The people of Reuben and the people of Gad call the altar Witness, “For,“ they say, “it is a witness between us that YHWH is God.“
A long time afterward, when YHWH has given rest to Israel from all their surrounding enemies, and Joshua is old and well advanced in years,
Joshua summons all Israel, its elders and heads, its judges and officers, and says to them: “I am now old and well advanced in years.
And you have seen all that YHWH your God has done to all these nations for your sake, for it is YHWH your God who has fought for you.
Behold, I have allotted to you as an inheritance for your tribes those nations that remain, along with all the nations that I have already cut off, from the Jordan to the Great Sea in the west.
YHWH your God will push them back before you and drive them out of your sight. And you shall possess their land, just as YHWH your God promised you.
Therefore, be very strong to keep and to do all that is written in the Book of the Law of Moses, turning aside from it neither to the right hand nor to the left,
that you may not mix with these nations remaining among you or make mention of the names of their gods or swear by them or serve them or bow down to them,
but you shall cling to YHWH your God just as you have done to this day.
For YHWH has driven out before you great and strong nations, and as for you, no man has been able to stand before you to this day.
One man of you puts to flight a thousand, since it is YHWH your God who fights for you, just as he promised you.
Be very careful, therefore, to love YHWH your God.
For if you turn back and cling to the remnant of these nations remaining among you and make marriages with them, so that you associate with them and they with you,

know for certain that YHWH your God will no longer drive out these nations before you, but they shall be a snare and a trap for you, a whip on your sides and thorns in your eyes, until you perish from off this good land that YHWH your God has given you.
And behold, this day I am going the way of all the earth.
And you know in all your hearts and in all your souls
that not one word has failed
of all the good words that YHWH your God promised concerning you.
All have come to pass for you; not one of them has failed.
But just as all the good things came to pass for you,
so YHWH will bring upon you all the evil things
until he has destroyed you from off this good land
that YHWH your God has given you,
if you transgress the covenant of YHWH your God,
which he commanded you,
and go and serve other gods and bow down to them.
Then the anger of YHWH will be kindled against you,
and you shall perish quickly from off the good land
that he has given to you.“
Joshua gathers all the tribes of Israel to Shechem and summons the elders of Israel, its heads, its judges, and its officers. And they present themselves before God.
And Joshua says to all the people: “Thus says YHWH, the God of Israel: 'Long ago, your fathers lived beyond the Euphrates, Terah, the father of Abraham and of Nahor; and they served other gods.
Then I took your father Abraham from beyond the River and led him through all the land of Canaan, and made his offspring many. I gave him Isaac.
And to Isaac I gave Jacob and Esau. And I gave Esau the hill country of Seir to possess, but Jacob and his children went down to Egypt.
And I sent Moses and Aaron, and I plagued Egypt with what I did in the midst of it, and afterward I brought you out.
Then I brought your fathers out of Egypt, and you came to the sea. And the Egyptians pursued your fathers with chariots and horsemen to the Red Sea.

And when they cried to YHWH, he put darkness between you and the Egyptians and made the sea come upon them and cover them; and your eyes saw what I did in Egypt. And you lived in the wilderness a long time.

Then I brought you to the land of the Amorites, who lived on the other side of the Jordan. And they fought with you, and I gave them into your hand, and you took possession of their land, and I destroyed them before you.
Then Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, arose and fought against Israel. And he sent and invited Balaam the son of Beor to curse you,
but I would not listen to Balaam. Indeed, he blessed you. So I delivered you out of his hand.

And you went over the Jordan and came to Jericho, and the leaders of Jericho fought against you, and also the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. And I gave them into your hand.
And I sent the hornet before you, which drove them out before you, the two kings of the Amorites; it was not by your sword or by your bow.
I gave you a land on which you had not laboured and cities that you had not built, and you dwell in them. You eat the fruit of vineyards and olive orchards that you did not plant.'
Now therefore fear YHWH and serve him
in sincerity and in faithfulness.
Put away the gods that your fathers served
beyond the River and in Egypt,
and serve YHWH.
And if it is evil in your eyes to serve YHWH,
choose this day whom you will serve,
whether the gods your fathers served
in the region beyond the River,
or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you dwell.
But as for me and my house,
we will serve YHWH.
Then the people answer: “Far be it from us that we should forsake YHWH to serve other gods,

for it is YHWH our God who brought us and our fathers up from the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery, and who did those great signs in our sight and preserved us in all the way that we went and among all the peoples through whom we passed.
And YHWH drove out before us all the peoples, the Amorites who lived in the land. Therefore we also will serve YHWH, for he is our God.“
But Joshua says to the people: “You are not able to serve YHWH, for he is a holy God. He is a jealous God; he will not forgive your transgressions or your sins.
If you forsake YHWH and serve foreign gods, then he will turn and do you harm and consume you, after having done you good.“
And the people say to Joshua: “No, but we will serve YHWH.“
Then Joshua says to the people: “You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen YHWH, to serve him.“ And they say: “We are witnesses.“
“Then put away the foreign gods that are among you, and incline your heart to YHWH, the God of Israel.“
And the people say to Joshua: “YHWH our God we will serve, and his voice we will obey.“
So Joshua makes a covenant with the people that day, and puts in place for them a statute and a rule at Shechem.
And Joshua writes these words in the Book of the Law of God. And he takes a large stone and sets it up there under the oak in the sanctuary of YHWH.

And Joshua says to all the people: “Behold, this stone shall be a witness against us, for it has heard all the words of YHWH that he spoke to us. Therefore it shall be a witness against you, lest you deal falsely with your God.“
So Joshua sends the people away, every man to his inheritance.
After these things Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of YHWH, dies, being a hundred and ten years old.
And they bury him in his own inheritance at Timnath-serah, which is in the hill country of Ephraim, north of the mountain of Gaash.
Israel serves YHWH all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders who outlive Joshua and who have known all the work that YHWH did for Israel.

As for the bones of Joseph, which the people of Israel brought up from Egypt, they bury them at Shechem, in the piece of land that Jacob bought from the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem for a hundred pieces of money. It becomes an inheritance of the descendants of Joseph.
And Eleazar the son of Aaron dies, and they bury him at Gibeah, the town of Phinehas his son, which had been given him in the hill country of Ephraim.
After Joshua dies, the Israelites inquire of YHWH: “Who will go up first for us against the Canaanites, to fight against them?”
YHWH says: “Judah goes up. Look — I have given the land into his hand.”
Judah says to his brother Simeon: “Come up with me into my allotted land. Let us fight against the Canaanites together. Then I will go with you into yours.” So Simeon goes with him.
Judah goes up, and YHWH gives the Canaanites and the Perizzites into their hand. They strike down ten thousand men at Bezek.
They find Adoni-bezek at Bezek and fight him, striking down the Canaanites and the Perizzites.
Adoni-bezek flees, but they pursue him and catch him. They cut off his thumbs and big toes.
Adoni-bezek says: “Seventy kings with their thumbs and big toes cut off used to gather scraps under my table. As I have done, so God has repaid me.” They bring him to Jerusalem, and there he dies.
The men of Judah fight against Jerusalem and take it. They put it to the sword and set the city on fire.
Afterwards the men of Judah go down to fight against the Canaanites who live in the hill country, the Negev, and the Shephelah.
Judah goes against the Canaanites living in Hebron — Hebron’s old name is Kiriath-arba — and they strike down Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.
From there they go up against the inhabitants of Debir. Debir’s old name is Kiriath-sepher.
Caleb says: “Whoever strikes down Kiriath-sepher and captures it — to him I will give my daughter Achsah as wife.”
Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother, captures it. So Caleb gives him his daughter Achsah as wife.
When she comes to him, she urges him to ask her father for a field. She gets down from her donkey, and Caleb says to her: “What is it you want?”
She says: “Give me a blessing. Since you have settled me in the land of the Negev, give me springs of water as well.” So Caleb gives her the upper springs and the lower springs.

The descendants of the Kenite, Moses’ father-in-law, go up from the City of Palms with the men of Judah into the wilderness of Judah, which is in the Negev near Arad. They go and live among the people there.
Then Judah goes with his brother Simeon, and they strike down the Canaanites living in Zephath. They devote it to destruction, and so the city is named Hormah.
Judah also takes Gaza with its territory, Ashkelon with its territory, and Ekron with its territory.
YHWH is with Judah, and they take possession of the hill country. But they cannot drive out those who live in the plain, because they have iron chariots.
They give Hebron to Caleb, as Moses had promised. He drives out from there the three sons of Anak.
But the Benjaminites do not drive out the Jebusites who live in Jerusalem. The Jebusites still live among the Benjaminites in Jerusalem to this day.
The house of Joseph also goes up — against Bethel — and YHWH is with them.
They send spies to Bethel. Bethel’s old name is Luz.
The spies see a man coming out of the city and say to him: “Show us the way into the city, and we will deal kindly with you.”
So he shows them the way in, and they put the city to the sword. But the man and his whole family they let go free.
The man goes to the land of the Hittites, builds a city, and names it Luz. That is its name to this day.

Manasseh does not drive out the inhabitants of Beth-shean and its villages, Taanach and its villages, the inhabitants of Dor and its villages, the inhabitants of Ibleam and its villages, the inhabitants of Megiddo and its villages. The Canaanites are determined to live in this land.
When Israel grows strong, they put the Canaanites to forced labor, but they do not drive them out completely.
Ephraim does not drive out the Canaanites living in Gezer. The Canaanites live among them in Gezer.
Zebulun does not drive out the inhabitants of Kitron or the inhabitants of Nahalol. The Canaanites live among them and are put to forced labor.
Asher does not drive out the inhabitants of Acco, Sidon, Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik, or Rehob.
So the Asherites live among the Canaanites who live in the land, because they cannot drive them out.

Naphtali does not drive out the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh or Beth-anath. They live among the Canaanites who live in the land, but the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath are put to forced labor for them.
The Amorites press the Danites back into the hill country. They will not allow them to come down to the plain.
The Amorites are determined to live in Mount Heres, in Aijalon, and in Shaalbim. But when the hand of the house of Joseph grows heavy, they too are put to forced labor.
The territory of the Amorites runs from the Ascent of Akrabbim, from the Rock and upward.
The angel of YHWH goes up from Gilgal to Bochim and says:
“I brought you up from Egypt and led you into the land I swore to give your ancestors. I said: I will never break my covenant with you;
and as for you — you must make no covenant with the inhabitants of this land. You must tear down their altars. But you have not obeyed my voice. What is this you have done?
So now I tell you: I will not drive them out before you. They will be thorns in your sides, and their gods will be a snare to you.”
When the angel of YHWH speaks these words to all the Israelites, the people lift up their voices and weep.
They name the place Bochim, and there they sacrifice to YHWH.
When Joshua dismisses the people, the Israelites go each to his own inheritance to take possession of the land.
The people serve YHWH all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders who outlive Joshua — who have seen all the great work YHWH did for Israel.
Joshua son of Nun, the servant of YHWH, dies at one hundred and ten years old.
They bury him in the territory of his inheritance, at Timnath-heres in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
That whole generation also is gathered to its ancestors, and another generation rises after them who do not know YHWH or the work he has done for Israel.
The Israelites do what is evil in the eyes of YHWH. They serve the Baals.

They abandon YHWH, the God of their ancestors, who brought them out of the land of Egypt. They go after other gods — the gods of the peoples around them — and bow down to them, and they provoke YHWH to anger.
They abandon YHWH and serve the Baal and the Ashtaroth.
The anger of YHWH burns against Israel. He hands them over to plunderers who plunder them. He sells them into the hand of their enemies all around, and they can no longer stand before their enemies.
Wherever they go out, the hand of YHWH is against them for harm — just as YHWH has said, and just as YHWH has sworn to them. They are in terrible distress.
Then YHWH raises up judges, and the judges rescue them from the hand of those who plunder them.

Yet they will not listen even to their judges. They prostitute themselves to other gods and bow down to them. They turn aside quickly from the way their ancestors walked — the way of obeying the commands of YHWH. They do not do as their ancestors did.

When YHWH raises up judges for them, YHWH is with the judge and rescues them from the hand of their enemies all the days of the judge — for YHWH is moved to pity by their groaning under those who oppress and crush them.

But when the judge dies, they turn back and act more corruptly than their ancestors — going after other gods to serve them and bow down to them. They give up none of their practices and none of their stubborn ways.
So the anger of YHWH burns against Israel, and he says:
“Because this nation has violated my covenant, which I commanded their ancestors, and has not listened to my voice,
I will no longer drive out before them any of the nations Joshua left when he died.
Through them I will test Israel — whether they will keep the way of YHWH and walk in it, as their ancestors kept it, or not.”
So YHWH leaves these nations alone. He does not drive them out at once, and he does not give them into the hand of Joshua.
These are the nations YHWH leaves alone to test by them all the Israelites who have not known any of the wars of Canaan —
only so that the generations of Israel will learn war, those who have not known it before:
the five lords of the Philistines, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites who live in the mountains of Lebanon, from Mount Baal-hermon to Lebo-hamath.
They are left to test Israel, to know whether Israel will obey the commands of YHWH that he gave their ancestors through Moses.
So the Israelites live among the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
They take the daughters of these peoples as wives, give their own daughters to their sons, and serve their gods.
The Israelites do what is evil in the eyes of YHWH. They forget YHWH their God and serve the Baals and the Asherahs.
So the anger of YHWH burns against Israel, and he sells them into the hand of Cushan-rishathaim, king of Aram-naharaim. The Israelites serve Cushan-rishathaim eight years.
Then the Israelites cry out to YHWH, and YHWH raises up a deliverer for them — Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother — and he rescues them.
The Spirit of YHWH comes upon him. He judges Israel and goes out to war. YHWH gives Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram into his hand, and his hand prevails over Cushan-rishathaim.
The land has rest for forty years. Then Othniel son of Kenaz dies.
Once again the Israelites do what is evil in the eyes of YHWH, and YHWH strengthens Eglon king of Moab against Israel — because they have done what is evil in the eyes of YHWH.
Eglon gathers to himself the Ammonites and the Amalekites. He goes and strikes Israel, and they take possession of the City of Palms.
The Israelites serve Eglon king of Moab eighteen years.
The Israelites cry out to YHWH, and YHWH raises up a deliverer for them: Ehud son of Gera, the Benjaminite, a left-handed man. The Israelites send tribute through him to Eglon king of Moab.
Ehud makes himself a sword with two edges, a cubit long, and he straps it under his clothes on his right thigh.
He presents the tribute to Eglon king of Moab. Eglon is a very fat man.
When Ehud finishes presenting the tribute, he sends away the people who carried it.
But he himself turns back at the carved stones near Gilgal and says: “I have a secret word for you, O king.” The king says, “Silence!” and all his attendants leave him.
Ehud comes to him while he is sitting alone in his cool upper room, and Ehud says: “I have a word from God for you.” The king rises from his seat.
Ehud reaches with his left hand, takes the sword from his right thigh, and drives it into Eglon’s belly.
Even the hilt goes in after the blade. The fat closes over the blade, for he does not pull the sword out of the belly — and the filth comes out.
Ehud goes out to the porch, shuts the doors of the upper room behind him, and locks them.
After he leaves, the king’s servants come and see — look, the doors of the upper room are locked. They say: “He must be relieving himself in the cool chamber.”
They wait until they are embarrassed. Still the doors of the upper room are not opened. So they take the key and open them — and there is their master, fallen to the floor, dead.
While they have been delaying, Ehud has escaped. He passes the carved stones and gets away to Seirah.
When he arrives, he blows the ram’s horn in the hill country of Ephraim, and the Israelites come down with him from the hills, with Ehud leading them.
He says to them: “Follow me — for YHWH has given your enemies the Moabites into your hand.” They go down after him, seize the fords of the Jordan against Moab, and allow no one to cross over.
They strike down about ten thousand Moabites at that time — every strong, able-bodied man. Not one escapes.
So Moab is subdued that day under the hand of Israel, and the land has rest for eighty years.
After him comes Shamgar son of Anath, who strikes down six hundred Philistines with an ox-goad. He too rescues Israel.
After Ehud dies, the Israelites again do what is evil in the eyes of YHWH.
So YHWH sells them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who reigns in Hazor. The commander of his army is Sisera, who lives in Harosheth-hagoyim.
The Israelites cry out to YHWH — for Jabin has nine hundred iron chariots, and he oppresses the Israelites harshly for twenty years.
Now Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lappidoth, is judging Israel at that time.
She sits under the Palm of Deborah, between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, and the Israelites come up to her for judgment.

She sends and summons Barak son of Abinoam from Kedesh-naphtali, and says to him: “Has not YHWH the God of Israel commanded you? — ‘Go, march to Mount Tabor, and take with you ten thousand men from the people of Naphtali and Zebulun.
I will draw out Sisera, Jabin’s army commander, to the Wadi Kishon, with his chariots and his troops, and I will give him into your hand.’”
Barak says to her: “If you go with me, I will go. But if you will not go with me, I will not go.”
She says:
“I will surely go with you. Only — the honor will not be yours on the road you are taking. For YHWH will sell Sisera into the hand of a woman.”
Then Deborah rises and goes with Barak to Kedesh. Barak calls Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh, and ten thousand men go up at his heels. Deborah goes up with him.

Now Heber the Kenite has separated himself from the Kenites — from the descendants of Hobab, the father-in-law of Moses — and has pitched his tent as far away as the oak in Zaanannim, which is near Kedesh.
They tell Sisera that Barak son of Abinoam has gone up to Mount Tabor.
So Sisera calls out all his chariots — nine hundred iron chariots — and all the troops with him, from Harosheth-hagoyim to the Wadi Kishon.
Deborah says to Barak: “Get up! For this is the day YHWH gives Sisera into your hand. Has not YHWH gone out before you?” So Barak comes down from Mount Tabor with ten thousand men behind him.
YHWH throws Sisera and all his chariots and all his army into a panic before Barak by the edge of the sword. Sisera leaps down from his chariot and flees on foot.
Barak pursues the chariots and the army as far as Harosheth-hagoyim, and all the army of Sisera falls by the edge of the sword. Not one is left.
Sisera flees on foot to the tent of Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite — for there is peace between Jabin king of Hazor and the house of Heber the Kenite.
Jael comes out to meet Sisera and says to him: “Turn aside, my lord, turn aside to me. Do not be afraid.” So he turns aside into her tent, and she covers him with a rug.
He says to her: “Please give me a little water to drink, for I am thirsty.” She opens a skin of milk, gives him a drink, and covers him again.
He says to her: “Stand at the entrance of the tent. If anyone comes and asks you, ‘Is there a man here?’ you are to say, ‘No.’”

Then Jael wife of Heber takes a tent peg in her hand and a hammer in her other hand. She comes to him softly and drives the peg through his temple, down into the ground — for he is fast asleep from weariness. So he dies.

Just then Barak comes pursuing Sisera. Jael comes out to meet him and says to him: “Come, I will show you the man you are looking for.” He goes in with her, and there is Sisera, fallen dead, the tent peg through his temple.
So on that day God subdues Jabin king of Canaan before the Israelites.
The hand of the Israelites grows steadily heavier on Jabin king of Canaan, until they destroy Jabin king of Canaan.
On that day Deborah sings — she and Barak son of Abinoam:
“When leaders lead in Israel,
when the people willingly offer themselves —
bless YHWH!
Hear, kings! Give ear, princes!
I — to YHWH, I will sing.
I will make music to YHWH the God of Israel.
YHWH, when you went out from Seir,
when you marched from the land of Edom,
the earth shook,
the heavens also dripped —
yes, the clouds dripped water.
The mountains quaked before YHWH,
the One of Sinai,
before YHWH, the God of Israel.
In the days of Shamgar son of Anath,
in the days of Jael,
the highways were abandoned.
Travelers walked the winding side-paths.
The villages were empty in Israel — empty,
until I, Deborah, arose,
arose as a mother in Israel.
They chose new gods —
then war came to the gates.
Was a shield seen, or a spear,
among forty thousand in Israel?
My heart goes out to Israel’s commanders,
to the willing among the people —
bless YHWH!
You who ride on tawny donkeys,
you who sit on saddle-blankets,
you who walk along the road —
sing!
Above the voices of those at the watering places,
they recount the righteous acts of YHWH,
the righteous acts of his villages in Israel.
Then the people of YHWH went down to the gates.
Awake, awake, Deborah!
Awake, awake, raise a song!
Rise up, Barak,
lead away your captives, son of Abinoam!
Then the survivors came down to the nobles;
the people of YHWH came down to me with the mighty.
From Ephraim came down those whose root is in Amalek;
after you, Benjamin, with your kinsmen.
From Machir commanders came down,
and from Zebulun those who wield the officer’s staff.
The chiefs of Issachar are with Deborah —
as Issachar, so Barak —
into the valley they were sent at his heels.
Among the divisions of Reuben — great searchings of heart.
Why did you sit among the sheepfolds,
to hear the bleating of the flocks?
Among the divisions of Reuben — great searchings of heart.
Gilead stayed beyond the Jordan.
And Dan — why did he linger by the ships?
Asher sat at the coast of the sea,
settling down by his harbors.
Zebulun is a people who scorned their lives to the death,
Naphtali too — on the heights of the field.
Kings came, they fought;
then the kings of Canaan fought
at Taanach by the waters of Megiddo —
no plunder of silver did they take.
From the heavens the stars fought;
from their courses they fought against Sisera.
The wadi Kishon swept them away —
the ancient wadi, the wadi Kishon.
March on, my soul, in strength!
Then thundered the hoofs of the horses
with the galloping, the galloping of his stallions.
‘Curse Meroz,’ says the angel of YHWH —
‘curse bitterly its inhabitants,
because they did not come to the help of YHWH,
to the help of YHWH against the mighty.’
Most blessed of women is Jael,
the wife of Heber the Kenite —
of tent-dwelling women, most blessed.
He asked water; she gave milk.
In a noble bowl she brought him curds.
Her hand she put to the tent peg,
her right hand to the workman’s hammer.
She struck Sisera; she crushed his head;
she shattered and pierced his temple.
Between her feet he sank, he fell, he lay still.
Between her feet he sank, he fell.
Where he sank, there he fell — destroyed.
Through the window she peered,
the mother of Sisera, through the lattice she cried:
‘Why is his chariot so long in coming?
Why are the hoofbeats of his chariots delayed?’
The wisest of her ladies answer her —
she even returns the answer to herself:
‘Are they not finding, dividing the plunder?
A girl, two girls for every man!
Plunder of dyed cloth for Sisera,
plunder of dyed cloth embroidered,
dyed cloth, doubly embroidered, for the necks of the plunderers!’
So perish all your enemies, YHWH!
But let those who love him be like the sun
going out in its strength.”
And the land has rest for forty years.
The Israelites do what is evil in the eyes of YHWH, and YHWH gives them into the hand of Midian for seven years.
The hand of Midian prevails over Israel. To escape the Midianites, the Israelites make for themselves the hideouts in the mountains, the caves, and the strongholds.
Whenever Israel has sown, the Midianites come up — with the Amalekites and the people of the East they come up against them.
They camp against them and destroy the produce of the land as far as Gaza. They leave no food in Israel — no sheep, no ox, no donkey.
They come up with their livestock and their tents; they come like locusts in number. Both they and their camels are without number. They come into the land to lay it waste.
So Israel is brought very low by Midian, and the Israelites cry out to YHWH.
When the Israelites cry out to YHWH because of Midian,
YHWH sends a prophet to the Israelites, and he says to them:
“This is what YHWH the God of Israel says: I brought you up from Egypt, and led you out of the house of slavery.
I rescued you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of all who oppressed you. I drove them out before you, and gave you their land.
And I said to you: I am YHWH your God. Do not fear the gods of the Amorites in whose land you live. But you have not obeyed my voice.”
The angel of YHWH comes and sits under the oak at Ophrah, which belongs to Joash the Abiezrite. His son Gideon is beating out wheat in a winepress to hide it from the Midianites.
The angel of YHWH appears to him and says: “YHWH is with you, mighty warrior.”

Gideon says to him: “Excuse me, my lord — if YHWH is with us, then why has all this happened to us? And where are all his wonders that our ancestors told us about — ‘Did not YHWH bring us up from Egypt?’ But now YHWH has abandoned us; he has given us into the open hand of Midian.”
YHWH turns to him and says: “Go in this strength of yours and rescue Israel from the hand of Midian. Am I not sending you?”
He says to him: “Excuse me, my Lord — how can I rescue Israel? Look — my clan is the weakest in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father’s house.”
YHWH says to him: “Because I will be with you. You will strike down Midian as one man.”
He says to him: “If I have found favor in your eyes, give me a sign that it is you who speaks with me.
Please do not depart from here until I come back to you and bring out my offering and set it before you.” He says: “I will stay until you come back.”
Gideon goes in and prepares a young goat and unleavened cakes from an ephah of flour. He puts the meat in a basket and the broth in a pot, brings it to him under the oak, and presents it.
The angel of God says to him: “Take the meat and the unleavened cakes, lay them on this rock, and pour out the broth.” He does so.

The angel of YHWH stretches out the tip of the staff in his hand and touches the meat and the unleavened cakes. Fire comes up from the rock and consumes the meat and the unleavened cakes. The angel of YHWH vanishes from his sight.
Then Gideon sees that it is the angel of YHWH, and Gideon says: “Oh no, my Lord YHWH! — for I have seen the angel of YHWH face to face.”
YHWH says to him: “Peace to you. Do not be afraid. You will not die.”
So Gideon builds an altar there to YHWH and names it “YHWH is Peace.” To this day it is still there at Ophrah of the Abiezrites.

That same night YHWH says to him: “Take your father’s bull — the second bull, seven years old — and tear down the altar of the Baal that belongs to your father, and cut down the Asherah pole beside it.
Build an altar to YHWH your God on the top of this stronghold, with the stones laid in order. Take the second bull and offer it as a whole burnt offering, with the wood of the Asherah you cut down.”
So Gideon takes ten of his servants and does as YHWH has told him. But because he is too afraid of his father’s household and of the men of the city to do it by day, he does it by night.
When the men of the city get up early in the morning — look — the altar of the Baal is torn down, and the Asherah beside it is cut down. The second bull is offered on the altar that has been built.
They say to one another: “Who has done this thing?” After they investigate and inquire, they say: “Gideon son of Joash has done this thing.”
The men of the city say to Joash: “Bring out your son. He must die — because he has torn down the altar of the Baal, and because he has cut down the Asherah beside it.”

But Joash says to all who stand against him: “Will you contend for the Baal? Will you yourselves rescue him? Whoever contends for him will be put to death by morning. If he is a god, let him contend for himself, because someone has torn down his altar.”
So on that day they call Gideon “Jerubbaal” — let Baal contend with him — because he has torn down his altar.
All the Midianites and the Amalekites and the people of the East gather together, cross over, and camp in the Valley of Jezreel.
The Spirit of YHWH clothes Gideon. He blows the ram’s horn, and the Abiezrites are mustered to follow him.
He sends messengers throughout Manasseh, and they too are mustered to follow him. He sends messengers to Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, and they come up to meet them.
Gideon says to God: “If you really are going to rescue Israel through me, as you have said —

look, I am setting a fleece of wool on the threshing floor. If there is dew on the fleece alone, and on all the ground it is dry, then I will know that you will rescue Israel through me, as you have said.”
And so it happens. He gets up early the next day, squeezes the fleece, and wrings dew out of it — a bowlful of water.

Gideon says to God: “Do not let your anger burn against me; let me speak just once more. Let me test, please, just once more with the fleece: let it be dry on the fleece alone, and on all the ground let there be dew.”
God does so that night: the fleece alone is dry, and there is dew on all the ground.
Jerubbaal — who is Gideon — gets up early, with all the people who are with him, and they camp by the spring of Harod. The camp of Midian is north of them, by the hill of Moreh in the valley.
YHWH says to Gideon:
“The people with you are too many for me to give Midian into their hand — for Israel might boast against me, saying, ‘My own hand has saved me.’
So now, proclaim in the ears of the people: ‘Whoever is afraid and trembling — let him go back and leave Mount Gilead.’”
Twenty-two thousand of the people turn back, and ten thousand remain.

YHWH says to Gideon: “The people are still too many. Take them down to the water, and I will sift them for you there. The one of whom I say to you, ‘This one shall go with you’ — he shall go with you. And every one of whom I say to you, ‘This one shall not go with you’ — he shall not go.”
So he takes the people down to the water. YHWH says to Gideon: “Everyone who laps the water with his tongue as a dog laps — set him by himself. And everyone who kneels down to drink — likewise.”
The number of those who lap, putting their hand to their mouth, is three hundred men. All the rest of the people kneel to drink water.
YHWH says to Gideon: “By the three hundred men who lapped I will rescue you and give Midian into your hand. Let all the rest of the people go, each to his own place.”

So they take the people’s provisions and their ram’s horns in their own hands. He sends every man of Israel to his tent but keeps the three hundred men with him. The camp of Midian is below him in the valley.
That night YHWH says to him: “Get up, go down against the camp, for I have given it into your hand.
But if you are afraid to go down, go down with Purah your servant to the camp.

You will hear what they are saying, and afterwards your hands will be strengthened, and you will go down against the camp.” So he goes down with Purah his servant to the edge of the armed men in the camp.
The Midianites and the Amalekites and all the people of the East are spread in the valley like locusts in number; their camels are without number, like the sand on the seashore in multitude.

When Gideon arrives, a man is telling a dream to his fellow. He says: “Look — I had a dream. A round loaf of barley bread came tumbling into the camp of Midian. It came to the tent, struck it, and it fell — turned it upside down — and the tent collapsed.”
His fellow answers and says: “This is nothing other than the sword of Gideon son of Joash, the man of Israel. God has given Midian and all the camp into his hand.”
When Gideon hears the telling of the dream and its interpretation, he bows down in worship. He returns to the camp of Israel and says: “Get up! For YHWH has given the camp of Midian into your hand.”
He divides the three hundred men into three companies. He puts a ram’s horn in every man’s hand, and empty jars with torches inside the jars.
He says to them: “Look at me — and do likewise. When I come to the edge of the camp, what I do, you do as well.
When I blow the ram’s horn — I and all who are with me — then you also blow the ram’s horns around the whole camp, and shout: ‘For YHWH and for Gideon!’”

Gideon and the hundred men with him come to the edge of the camp at the beginning of the middle watch — just as they have freshly set the watch. They blow the ram’s horns and smash the jars in their hands.

The three companies blow the ram’s horns and break the jars. They hold the torches in their left hands and the ram’s horns in their right hands to blow, and they shout: “A sword for YHWH and for Gideon!”
Every man stands in his place around the camp, and the whole camp runs — they cry out and flee.

When the three hundred ram’s horns blow, YHWH sets every man’s sword against his fellow throughout the whole camp. The camp flees as far as Beth-shittah toward Zererah, as far as the border of Abel-meholah, by Tabbath.
The men of Israel are called out from Naphtali and from Asher and from all Manasseh, and they pursue Midian.

Gideon sends messengers throughout the hill country of Ephraim, saying: “Come down to meet Midian. Seize the waters before them as far as Beth-barah and the Jordan.” So all the men of Ephraim are mustered, and they seize the waters as far as Beth-barah and the Jordan.

They capture two princes of Midian — Oreb and Zeeb. They kill Oreb at the Rock of Oreb, and Zeeb they kill at the Winepress of Zeeb. They pursue Midian, and the heads of Oreb and Zeeb they bring to Gideon beyond the Jordan.
The men of Ephraim say to him: “What is this you have done to us — not calling us when you went to fight against Midian?” And they quarrel sharply with him.
He says to them: “What have I done now compared with you? Are not the gleanings of Ephraim better than the vintage of Abiezer?
Into your hand God has given the princes of Midian — Oreb and Zeeb. What was I able to do compared with you?” When he says this, their anger against him subsides.
Gideon comes to the Jordan and crosses over — he and the three hundred men with him — exhausted, but still in pursuit.
He says to the men of Succoth: “Please give some loaves of bread to the people following me, for they are exhausted, and I am pursuing Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian.”
The officials of Succoth say: “Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your hand, that we should give bread to your army?”
Gideon says: “Very well — when YHWH gives Zebah and Zalmunna into my hand, I will thresh your flesh with the thorns of the wilderness and with briers.”
He goes up from there to Penuel and speaks to them in the same way. The men of Penuel answer him as the men of Succoth answered.
So he says also to the men of Penuel: “When I return safely, I will tear down this tower.”

Zebah and Zalmunna are in Karkor with their armies — about fifteen thousand men, all who are left of the whole army of the people of the East. A hundred and twenty thousand swordsmen have already fallen.
Gideon goes up by the route of the tent-dwellers east of Nobah and Jogbehah, and strikes the camp while the camp is at ease.
Zebah and Zalmunna flee, and he pursues them. He captures the two kings of Midian — Zebah and Zalmunna — and throws the whole camp into a panic.
Then Gideon son of Joash returns from the battle by the Ascent of Heres.
He catches a young man from among the men of Succoth and questions him. The young man writes down for him the officials of Succoth and its elders — seventy-seven men.

He comes to the men of Succoth and says: “Look — Zebah and Zalmunna, about whom you mocked me, saying, ‘Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your hand that we should give bread to your weary men?’”
He takes the elders of the city, and thorns of the wilderness and briers, and with them he disciplines the men of Succoth.
The tower of Penuel he tears down, and the men of the city he kills.
He says to Zebah and Zalmunna: “What kind of men were they, the ones you killed at Tabor?” They say: “They were like you. Each one had the look of a king’s son.”
He says: “They were my brothers — my mother’s sons. As YHWH lives — if you had let them live, I would not kill you.”
He says to Jether his firstborn: “Get up — kill them.” But the boy does not draw his sword, because he is afraid — he is still young.

Zebah and Zalmunna say: “Get up yourself, and fall on us — for as the man, so is his strength.” So Gideon gets up and kills Zebah and Zalmunna. He takes the crescent ornaments that were on the necks of their camels.
The men of Israel say to Gideon: “Rule over us — you and your son and your grandson — for you have rescued us from the hand of Midian.”
Gideon says to them:
“I will not rule over you, and my son will not rule over you. YHWH will rule over you.”
Gideon says to them: “I will make one request of you: give me, each of you, an earring from his plunder.” (The enemy had golden earrings, because they were Ishmaelites.)
They say: “We will gladly give them.” They spread out a garment, and each man throws on it an earring from his plunder.

The weight of the golden earrings he requests comes to seventeen hundred shekels of gold — not counting the crescent ornaments, the pendants, and the purple garments that were on the kings of Midian, and not counting the chains that were on the necks of their camels.
Gideon makes from it an ephod and sets it up in his city, in Ophrah. All Israel prostitutes itself to it there, and it becomes a snare to Gideon and to his household.
So Midian is subdued before the Israelites, and they do not lift up their heads again. The land has rest for forty years in the days of Gideon.
Jerubbaal son of Joash goes and lives in his own house.
Gideon has seventy sons of his own descent, for he has many wives.
His concubine in Shechem also bears him a son, and he gives him the name Abimelech.
Gideon son of Joash dies at a good old age, and is buried in the tomb of Joash his father, in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.
After Gideon dies, the Israelites turn back and prostitute themselves to the Baals. They make Baal-berith their god.
The Israelites do not remember YHWH their God — the one who rescued them from the hand of all their enemies on every side.
They do not show kindness to the house of Jerubbaal-Gideon for all the good he had done for Israel.
Abimelech son of Jerubbaal goes to Shechem, to his mother’s brothers, and speaks to them and to all the clan of his mother’s father, saying:

“Speak now in the hearing of all the citizens of Shechem: ‘Which is better for you — that seventy men, all the sons of Jerubbaal, should rule over you, or that one man should rule over you?’ Remember also that I am your bone and your flesh.”
His mother’s brothers speak all these words about him in the hearing of all the citizens of Shechem, and their hearts incline to follow Abimelech, for they say: “He is our brother.”
They give him seventy pieces of silver from the temple of Baal-berith, and with them Abimelech hires worthless and reckless men, who follow him.
He goes to his father’s house at Ophrah and kills his brothers — the sons of Jerubbaal, seventy men — on one stone. But Jotham, the youngest son of Jerubbaal, is left, because he hides himself.
All the citizens of Shechem and all Beth-millo gather together. They go and make Abimelech king at the oak of the pillar in Shechem.
When Jotham is told, he goes and stands on the top of Mount Gerizim. He lifts up his voice and calls out to them:
“Listen to me, citizens of Shechem,
that God may listen to you.
The trees once went out
to anoint a king over themselves.
They said to the olive: ‘Reign over us.’
But the olive said to them:
‘Shall I leave my fatness —
by which gods and humans are honored —
to go and sway over the trees?’
The trees said to the fig:
‘Come — you, reign over us.’
But the fig said to them:
‘Shall I leave my sweetness
and my good fruit
to go and sway over the trees?’
The trees said to the vine:
‘Come — you, reign over us.’
But the vine said to them:
‘Shall I leave my new wine
that gladdens gods and humans,
to go and sway over the trees?’
Then all the trees said to the bramble:
‘Come — you, reign over us.’
The bramble said to the trees:
‘If in truth you are anointing me king over you,
come, take refuge in my shade.
But if not — let fire come out of the bramble
and devour the cedars of Lebanon.’”
“Now then — if you have acted in truth and integrity in making Abimelech king, if you have done well by Jerubbaal and his house, and if you have done to him as his hands deserved —
because my father fought for you and risked his life and rescued you from the hand of Midian,

but today you have risen up against my father’s house and killed his sons — seventy men on one stone — and made Abimelech, the son of his slave woman, king over the citizens of Shechem because he is your brother —
if then you have acted in truth and integrity with Jerubbaal and with his house this day, then rejoice in Abimelech, and let him rejoice in you.
But if not — let fire come out from Abimelech and consume the citizens of Shechem and Beth-millo; and let fire come out from the citizens of Shechem and from Beth-millo and consume Abimelech.”
Then Jotham flees and runs away. He goes to Beer and stays there because of Abimelech his brother.
Abimelech rules over Israel three years.
Then God sends an evil spirit between Abimelech and the citizens of Shechem, and the citizens of Shechem deal treacherously with Abimelech —

so that the violence done to the seventy sons of Jerubbaal might come back, and their blood be laid on Abimelech their brother who killed them, and on the citizens of Shechem who strengthened his hands to kill his brothers.
The citizens of Shechem set up ambushes against him on the mountaintops, and they rob all who pass by them on the road. It is reported to Abimelech.
Gaal son of Ebed comes with his brothers, and passes through to Shechem. The citizens of Shechem put their trust in him.
They go out into the field, gather the grapes from their vineyards, tread them, and hold festivities. They go into the house of their god, eat and drink, and curse Abimelech.

Gaal son of Ebed says: “Who is Abimelech, and who is Shechem, that we should serve him? Is he not the son of Jerubbaal, and Zebul his officer? Serve the men of Hamor the father of Shechem! Why should we serve him?
If only this people were in my hand! Then I would remove Abimelech.” He says of Abimelech: “Build up your army, and come out!”
When Zebul, the ruler of the city, hears the words of Gaal son of Ebed, his anger burns.
He sends messengers to Abimelech secretly, saying: “Look — Gaal son of Ebed and his brothers have come to Shechem, and they are stirring up the city against you.
So now, get up by night, you and the people with you, and lie in wait in the field.
In the morning, as soon as the sun rises, get up early and rush against the city. Look — when he and the people with him come out against you, you do to him whatever your hand finds.”
Abimelech gets up by night, and all the people with him, and they lie in ambush against Shechem in four companies.
Gaal son of Ebed comes out and stands at the entrance of the gate of the city. Abimelech and the people with him get up from ambush.
When Gaal sees the people, he says to Zebul: “Look — people are coming down from the mountaintops.” Zebul says to him: “The shadows of the mountains look like men to you.”
Gaal speaks again, saying: “Look — people are coming down from the navel of the land, and one company is coming from the direction of the Diviners’ Oak.”
Zebul says to him: “Where is your mouth now? — you who said, ‘Who is Abimelech that we should serve him?’ Are not these the very people you despised? Go out now and fight them.”
Gaal goes out at the head of the citizens of Shechem and fights Abimelech.
Abimelech pursues him, and he flees before him. Many fall wounded, all the way to the entrance of the gate.
Abimelech stays at Arumah, and Zebul drives Gaal and his brothers out, so that they can no longer live in Shechem.
The next day the people go out into the field. It is reported to Abimelech.
He takes his army, divides it into three companies, and lies in ambush in the field. When he sees that the people are coming out of the city, he gets up against them and strikes them.
Abimelech and the company with him rush forward and stand at the entrance of the gate of the city, while the two other companies rush against all who are in the field and strike them.
Abimelech fights against the city all that day. He captures the city, kills the people in it, tears down the city, and sows it with salt.
When all the citizens of the Tower of Shechem hear of it, they go into the stronghold of the house of El-berith.
Abimelech is told that all the citizens of the Tower of Shechem are gathered together.

Abimelech goes up to Mount Zalmon, he and all the people with him. He takes an axe in his hand, cuts down a branch from the trees, lifts it up, and lays it on his shoulder. He says to the people with him: “What you have seen me do — quickly, do as I have done.”

So each of the people also cuts down his branch. They follow Abimelech, set them up against the stronghold, and set the stronghold on fire over them, so that all the people of the Tower of Shechem also die — about a thousand men and women.
Then Abimelech goes to Thebez. He encamps against Thebez and captures it.
But there is a strong tower in the middle of the city. All the men and women — all the citizens of the city — flee there and shut themselves in. They go up on the roof of the tower.
Abimelech comes to the tower and fights against it. He draws near to the door of the tower to burn it down with fire.
But a certain woman drops an upper millstone on Abimelech’s head and shatters his skull.
He quickly calls to the young man, his armor-bearer, and says to him: “Draw your sword and kill me, so they will not say of me: ‘A woman killed him.’” His young man pierces him through, and he dies.
When the men of Israel see that Abimelech is dead, they go away — each to his own place.
So God repays the evil of Abimelech, the evil he did to his father in killing his seventy brothers.
And all the evil of the men of Shechem God brings back on their own heads. On them comes the curse of Jotham son of Jerubbaal.
After Abimelech, Tola son of Puah, son of Dodo — a man of Issachar — rises to rescue Israel. He lives in Shamir, in the hill country of Ephraim.
He judges Israel twenty-three years. Then he dies and is buried in Shamir.
After him rises Jair the Gileadite, and he judges Israel twenty-two years.
He has thirty sons, who ride on thirty donkeys, and they have thirty towns, which are called Havvoth-jair to this day — they are in the land of Gilead.
Then Jair dies and is buried in Kamon.

The Israelites again do what is evil in the eyes of YHWH. They serve the Baals and the Ashtaroth, the gods of Aram, the gods of Sidon, the gods of Moab, the gods of the Ammonites, and the gods of the Philistines. They abandon YHWH and do not serve him.
So the anger of YHWH burns against Israel, and he sells them into the hand of the Philistines and into the hand of the Ammonites.
They crush and oppress the Israelites that year. For eighteen years they oppress all the Israelites who are beyond the Jordan, in the land of the Amorites — which is in Gilead.
The Ammonites also cross the Jordan to fight against Judah, against Benjamin, and against the house of Ephraim, and Israel is greatly distressed.
The Israelites cry out to YHWH, saying: “We have sinned against you — we have abandoned our God and served the Baals.”
YHWH says to the Israelites:
“Did I not rescue you from Egypt and from the Amorites, from the Ammonites and from the Philistines?
The Sidonians, Amalek, and Maon oppressed you, and you cried out to me, and I rescued you from their hand.
But you have abandoned me and served other gods — therefore I will rescue you no more.
Go and cry out to the gods you have chosen. Let them rescue you in the time of your distress.”
The Israelites say to YHWH: “We have sinned. Do to us whatever seems good in your eyes. Only — please rescue us this day.”
They put away the foreign gods from their midst and serve YHWH. And his soul grows impatient at the misery of Israel.
The Ammonites are called out and camp in Gilead. The Israelites gather together and camp at Mizpah.
The people, the leaders of Gilead, say to one another: “Who is the man who will begin the fight against the Ammonites? He will be head over all the inhabitants of Gilead.”
Jephthah the Gileadite is a mighty warrior. He is the son of a prostitute. Gilead is the father of Jephthah.

Gilead’s wife also bears him sons, and when the wife’s sons grow up, they drive Jephthah out and say to him: “You shall not have an inheritance in our father’s house, for you are the son of another woman.”
So Jephthah flees from his brothers and lives in the land of Tob. Worthless men gather around Jephthah and go out with him.
Some time later, the Ammonites make war against Israel.
When the Ammonites make war against Israel, the elders of Gilead go to bring Jephthah from the land of Tob.
They say to Jephthah: “Come and be our commander, so we can fight the Ammonites.”
Jephthah says to the elders of Gilead: “Did you not hate me and drive me out of my father’s house? Why do you come to me now, when you are in distress?”
The elders of Gilead say to Jephthah: “That is exactly why we have turned to you now — that you may go with us, fight the Ammonites, and become our head — over all the inhabitants of Gilead.”
Jephthah says to the elders of Gilead: “If you bring me back to fight the Ammonites and YHWH gives them to me, will I be your head?”
The elders of Gilead say to Jephthah: “YHWH will be a witness between us — if we do not act according to your word.”
So Jephthah goes with the elders of Gilead. The people make him head and commander over them. Jephthah speaks all his words before YHWH at Mizpah.
Jephthah sends messengers to the king of the Ammonites, saying: “What is there between you and me, that you have come against me to fight against my land?”

The king of the Ammonites says to Jephthah’s messengers: “Because Israel took my land when they came up from Egypt — from the Arnon to the Jabbok, and to the Jordan. Now then, give it back peacefully.”
Jephthah sends messengers again to the king of the Ammonites,
and says to him: “This is what Jephthah says: Israel did not take the land of Moab or the land of the Ammonites.
When Israel came up from Egypt, they went through the wilderness to the Red Sea, and came to Kadesh.

Then Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying: ‘Let us pass through your land.’ But the king of Edom would not listen. They also sent to the king of Moab, but he refused. So Israel stayed at Kadesh.

Then they went through the wilderness and went around the land of Edom and the land of Moab. They came to the eastern side of the land of Moab and camped beyond the Arnon. They did not enter the territory of Moab — for the Arnon is the border of Moab.
Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, the king of Heshbon, and Israel said to him: ‘Let us pass through your land to our place.’
But Sihon did not trust Israel to cross his territory. Sihon gathered all his people, camped at Jahaz, and fought against Israel.
YHWH the God of Israel gave Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and they struck them down. Israel took possession of all the land of the Amorites, the inhabitants of that country.
They took possession of all the territory of the Amorites — from the Arnon to the Jabbok, and from the wilderness to the Jordan.
So now YHWH the God of Israel has dispossessed the Amorites from before his people Israel — and you would possess them?
Do you not possess what your god Chemosh gives you to possess? And whomever YHWH our God has dispossessed before us — them we possess.
Are you really better than Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab? Did he ever contend against Israel? Did he ever fight against them?
While Israel has lived in Heshbon and its towns, in Aroer and its towns, and in all the cities along the banks of the Arnon, for three hundred years — why did you not recover them during that time?
I have not sinned against you. You are doing me wrong by making war against me. Let YHWH the Judge decide today between the Israelites and the Ammonites.”
But the king of the Ammonites does not listen to the words of Jephthah that he sent him.
Then the Spirit of YHWH comes upon Jephthah. He passes through Gilead and Manasseh, then through Mizpeh of Gilead, and from Mizpeh of Gilead he crosses over to the Ammonites.
Jephthah makes a vow to YHWH and says: “If you really give the Ammonites into my hand,
then whoever comes out — whoever comes out of the doors of my house to meet me when I return safely from the Ammonites — shall be YHWH’s, and I will offer him up as a burnt offering.”
So Jephthah crosses over to the Ammonites to fight against them, and YHWH gives them into his hand.
He strikes them down from Aroer to the entrance of Minnith — twenty cities — and as far as Abel-keramim. It is a very great blow. So the Ammonites are subdued before the Israelites.
Jephthah comes to his home at Mizpah, and look — his daughter is coming out to meet him, with tambourines and dances. She is his only child. Besides her he has neither son nor daughter.
When he sees her, he tears his clothes and says: “Oh, my daughter! You have brought me very low — you have become the cause of my trouble! I have opened my mouth to YHWH, and I cannot take it back.”
She says to him: “My father, you have opened your mouth to YHWH. Do to me as has come out of your mouth — now that YHWH has avenged you on your enemies, the Ammonites.”
She says to her father: “Let this thing be done for me: leave me alone for two months, that I may go down on the mountains and bewail my virginity — I and my companions.”
He says: “Go.” He sends her away for two months. She and her companions go and bewail her virginity on the mountains.
At the end of two months she returns to her father, and he does to her as he had vowed. She has never known a man. And it becomes a custom in Israel —
that the daughters of Israel, year by year, go to lament the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite, four days in the year.

The men of Ephraim are called out. They cross over to Zaphon and say to Jephthah: “Why did you cross over to fight the Ammonites and not call us to go with you? We will burn your house over you with fire!”
Jephthah says to them: “I and my people had a great quarrel with the Ammonites. I called to you, but you did not rescue me from their hand.

When I saw that you were no deliverer, I took my life in my hand and crossed over against the Ammonites, and YHWH gave them into my hand. Why then have you come up against me today to fight against me?”

So Jephthah gathers all the men of Gilead and fights with Ephraim. The men of Gilead strike Ephraim down — because they had said: “You Gileadites are fugitives of Ephraim — in the midst of Ephraim and Manasseh!”

The Gileadites seize the fords of the Jordan against the Ephraimites. Whenever a fugitive of Ephraim says, “Let me cross over,” the men of Gilead say to him: “Are you an Ephraimite?” If he says, “No,”

they say to him: “Then say ‘Shibboleth.’” And he says “Sibboleth” — because he cannot pronounce it correctly. They seize him and slaughter him at the fords of the Jordan. Forty-two thousand of Ephraim fall at that time.
Jephthah judges Israel six years. Then Jephthah the Gileadite dies and is buried in one of the cities of Gilead.
After him, Ibzan of Bethlehem judges Israel.
He has thirty sons. Thirty daughters he sends outside the clan, and thirty daughters he brings in for his sons from outside. He judges Israel seven years.
Then Ibzan dies and is buried in Bethlehem.
After him, Elon the Zebulunite judges Israel. He judges Israel ten years.
Then Elon the Zebulunite dies and is buried in Aijalon in the land of Zebulun.
After him, Abdon son of Hillel the Pirathonite judges Israel.
He has forty sons and thirty grandsons, who ride on seventy donkeys. He judges Israel eight years.
Then Abdon son of Hillel the Pirathonite dies and is buried in Pirathon in the land of Ephraim, in the hill country of the Amalekites.
The Israelites again do what is evil in the eyes of YHWH, and YHWH gives them into the hand of the Philistines for forty years.
There is a man from Zorah, of the clan of the Danites, whose name is Manoah. His wife is barren and has not borne a child.
The angel of YHWH appears to the woman and says to her:
“Look — you are barren and have not borne,
but you will conceive and bear a son.
So now, be careful: drink no wine or strong drink,
and eat nothing unclean.
For look — you will conceive and bear a son.
No razor shall come upon his head,
for the boy shall be a Nazirite to God from the womb;
and he will begin to rescue Israel from the hand of the Philistines.”

The woman comes and tells her husband: “A man of God came to me. His appearance was like the appearance of the angel of God — very awesome. I did not ask him where he was from, and he did not tell me his name.

He said to me: ‘Look — you will conceive and bear a son. So now, drink no wine or strong drink, and eat nothing unclean — for the boy will be a Nazirite to God from the womb until the day of his death.’”
Manoah entreats YHWH and says: “Oh, my Lord — let the man of God you sent come to us again, and teach us what we are to do for the boy who will be born.”
God listens to the voice of Manoah, and the angel of God comes again to the woman as she sits in the field. Manoah her husband is not with her.
The woman hurries and runs and tells her husband: “Look — the man who came to me the other day has appeared to me.”
Manoah gets up and follows his wife. He comes to the man and says to him: “Are you the man who spoke to the woman?” He says: “I am.”
Manoah says: “Now when your word comes true, what is to be the rule for the boy and his work?”
The angel of YHWH says to Manoah: “Of all that I said to the woman she is to be careful.
She is not to eat anything that comes from the grapevine. She is not to drink wine or strong drink. She is not to eat anything unclean. All that I have commanded her she is to keep.”
Manoah says to the angel of YHWH: “Please let us detain you and prepare a young goat before you.”
The angel of YHWH says to Manoah: “Even if you detain me, I will not eat your food. And if you prepare a burnt offering, offer it up to YHWH.” — for Manoah does not yet know it is the angel of YHWH.
Manoah says to the angel of YHWH: “What is your name? When your word comes true, we want to honor you.”
The angel of YHWH says to him: “Why do you ask my name? It is wonderful.”
So Manoah takes the young goat and the grain offering and offers it on the rock to YHWH. And he does a wonderful thing while Manoah and his wife look on.
As the flame goes up from the altar toward heaven, the angel of YHWH goes up in the flame of the altar. Manoah and his wife see it and fall on their faces to the ground.
The angel of YHWH does not appear again to Manoah and his wife. Then Manoah knows that it was the angel of YHWH.
Manoah says to his wife: “We shall surely die — for we have seen God.”

But his wife says to him: “If YHWH had wanted to kill us, he would not have accepted from our hand a burnt offering and a grain offering, and he would not have shown us all these things, and at this time he would not have let us hear such things.”
The woman bears a son, and she names him Samson. The boy grows, and YHWH blesses him.
The Spirit of YHWH begins to stir him in Mahaneh-dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol.
Samson goes down to Timnah and sees a woman in Timnah, one of the daughters of the Philistines.
He comes up and tells his father and his mother: “I have seen a woman in Timnah, one of the daughters of the Philistines. Now then, get her for me as a wife.”

His father and his mother say to him: “Is there no woman among the daughters of your brothers, or among all my people, that you have to go and take a wife from the uncircumcised Philistines?” Samson says to his father: “Get her for me — for she is right in my eyes.”
His father and his mother do not know that this is from YHWH — that he is seeking an occasion against the Philistines. In those days the Philistines are ruling over Israel.
Samson goes down with his father and his mother to Timnah. They come to the vineyards of Timnah, and look — a young lion comes roaring out to meet him.
The Spirit of YHWH rushes upon him, and he tears the lion apart as one tears apart a young goat — with nothing in his hand. But he does not tell his father or his mother what he has done.
He goes down and speaks to the woman, and she is right in Samson’s eyes.
After some time he returns to take her, and turns aside to see the carcass of the lion — and look, a swarm of bees is in the body of the lion, and honey.

He scrapes it into his hands and goes, eating as he walks. When he comes to his father and his mother, he gives them some, and they eat. But he does not tell them that he scraped the honey from the body of the lion.
His father goes down to the woman, and Samson holds a feast there — for that is what the young men do.
When they see him, they choose thirty companions to be with him.

Samson says to them: “Let me put a riddle to you. If you can tell me the answer during the seven days of the feast and figure it out, I will give you thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothes.
