David speaks to YHWH the words of this song on the day YHWH delivers him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul.
He says:
"YHWH is my rock and my fortress and my deliverer,
my God, my rock, in whom I take refuge —
my shield, the horn of my salvation,
my stronghold and my refuge,
my savior; you save me from violence.
I call upon YHWH, who is worthy to be praised,
and I am saved from my enemies.
For the waves of death encompass me,
the torrents of destruction assail me;
the cords of Sheol entangle me,
the snares of death confront me.
In my distress I call upon YHWH;
to my God I call.
From his temple he hears my voice,
and my cry comes to his ears.
Then the earth reels and rocks;
the foundations of the heavens tremble
and quake, because he is angry.
Smoke goes up from his nostrils,
devouring fire from his mouth;
glowing coals blaze out from him.
He bows the heavens and comes down;
thick darkness is under his feet.
He rides on a cherub and flies;
he is seen on the wings of the wind.
He makes darkness his canopy around him,
thick clouds, a gathering of water.
Out of the brightness before him
coals of fire blaze forth.
YHWH thunders from heaven;
the Most High utters his voice.
He sends out arrows and scatters them;
lightning, and he routs them.
The channels of the sea are seen;
the foundations of the world are laid bare
at the rebuke of YHWH,
at the blast of the breath of his nostrils.
He reaches from on high, he takes me;
he draws me out of many waters.
He rescues me from my strong enemy,
from those who hate me —
for they are too mighty for me.
They confront me in the day of my calamity,
but YHWH is my support.
He brings me out into a broad place;
he rescues me, because he delights in me.
YHWH deals with me according to my righteousness;
according to the cleanness of my hands he rewards me.
For I keep the ways of YHWH
and do not wickedly depart from my God.
All his rules are before me,
and from his statutes I do not turn aside.
I am blameless before him,
and I keep myself from guilt.
YHWH rewards me according to my righteousness,
according to my cleanness in his sight.
With the merciful you show yourself merciful;
with the blameless you show yourself blameless;
with the pure you deal purely,
and with the crooked you make yourself seem tortuous.
You save a humble people,
but your eyes are on the haughty to bring them down.
For you are my lamp, O YHWH,
and YHWH lightens my darkness.
By you I can run against a troop,
and by my God I can leap over a wall.
This God — his way is perfect;
the word of YHWH proves true;
he is a shield for all who take refuge in him.
For who is God but YHWH?
And who is a rock except our God?
This God is my strong refuge
and makes my way blameless.
He makes my feet like the feet of a deer
and sets me secure on the heights.
He trains my hands for war,
so that my arms can bend a bow of bronze.
You give me the shield of your salvation,
and your condescension makes me great.
You give a wide place for my steps under me,
and my feet do not slip.
I pursue my enemies and destroy them,
and do not turn back until they are consumed.
I consume them; I thrust them through,
and they do not rise;
they fall under my feet.
You equip me with strength for battle;
you make those who rise against me sink under me.
You make my enemies turn their backs to me;
those who hate me I destroy.
They look, but there is none to save;
they cry to YHWH, but he does not answer.
I beat them fine as the dust of the earth;
I crush them and stamp them down like mud in the streets.
You deliver me from strife with my people;
you keep me as the head of the nations;
a people I had not known serve me.
Foreigners come cringing to me;
as soon as they hear, they obey me.
Foreigners lose heart
and come trembling out of their strongholds.
YHWH lives — blessed is my rock!
Exalted is my God, the rock of my salvation —
the God who gives me vengeance
and brings down peoples under me,
who brings me out from my enemies.
You exalt me above those who rise against me;
you deliver me from the man of violence.
For this I praise you, O YHWH, among the nations,
and sing praises to your name.
Great salvation he brings to his king
and shows steadfast love to his anointed —
to David and his offspring forever."
The Last Words of David · 23:1–7
These are the last words of David:
The oracle of David son of Jesse,
the oracle of the man raised on high,
the anointed of the God of Jacob,
the sweet psalmist of Israel:
"The Spirit of YHWH speaks through me,
his word is on my tongue.
The God of Israel has spoken,
the Rock of Israel has said to me:
When one rules justly over men,
ruling in the fear of God,
he dawns on them like the morning light,
like the sun rising on a cloudless morning,
like rain that makes grass sprout from the earth.
For is not my house established with God?
He has made with me an everlasting covenant,
ordered in all things and secure.
For all my salvation and all my desire,
will he not cause it to flourish?
But worthless men are all like thorns that are thrown away,
for they cannot be taken with the hand;
but the man who touches them
arms himself with iron and the shaft of a spear,
and they are utterly consumed with fire in their place."
David's Mighty Men · 23:8–39
These are the names of the mighty men of David: Josheb-basshebeth the Tahchemonite is chief of the three. He wields his spear against eight hundred and kills them at one time.
Next to him among the three mighty men is Eleazar son of Dodo, son of Ahohi. He is with David when they defy the Philistines who are gathered there for battle, and the men of Israel withdraw.

He rises and strikes down the Philistines until his hand is weary and his hand clings to the sword. YHWH brings about a great victory that day, and the troops come back after him only to strip the slain.
Next to him is Shammah son of Agee the Hararite. The Philistines gather together at Lehi, where there is a plot of ground full of lentils, and the troops flee from the Philistines.
But Shammah takes his stand in the middle of the plot and defends it and strikes down the Philistines, and YHWH brings about a great victory.
Three of the thirty chief men go down at harvest time to David at the cave of Adullam, while a band of Philistines is encamped in the Valley of Rephaim.
David is then in the stronghold, while the garrison of the Philistines is then at Bethlehem.
David has a longing and says, "Oh, that someone would give me water to drink from the well of Bethlehem that is by the gate!"

So the three mighty men break through the camp of the Philistines and draw water from the well of Bethlehem that is by the gate. They carry it and bring it to David. But he will not drink it and pours it out to YHWH
and says, "YHWH forbid that I should do this. Shall I drink the blood of the men who went at the risk of their lives?" So he will not drink it. These things the three mighty men do.
Now Abishai the brother of Joab, son of Zeruiah, is chief of the thirty. He wields his spear against three hundred men and kills them and wins a name beside the three.
He is the most renowned of the thirty and becomes their commander, though he does not attain to the three.
And Benaiah son of Jehoiada is a valiant man, a great fighter from Kabzeel. He strikes down two ariels of Moab. He also goes down and strikes down a lion in a pit on a day when snow falls.

And he strikes down an Egyptian, a handsome man. The Egyptian has a spear in his hand, but Benaiah goes down to him with a staff, wrenches the spear out of the Egyptian's hand, and kills him with his own spear.
These things Benaiah son of Jehoiada does, and wins a name beside the three mighty men.
He is renowned among the thirty, but he does not attain to the three. And David sets him over his bodyguard.
Asahel the brother of Joab is among the thirty: Elhanan son of Dodo of Bethlehem,
Shammah of Harod, Elika of Harod,
Helez the Paltite, Ira son of Ikkesh of Tekoa,
Abiezer of Anathoth, Mebunnai the Hushathite,
Zalmon the Ahohite, Maharai of Netophah,
Heleb son of Baanah of Netophah, Ittai son of Ribai of Gibeah of the people of Benjamin,
Benaiah of Pirathon, Hiddai of the brooks of Gaash,
Abi-albon the Arbathite, Azmaveth of Bahurim,
Eliahba the Shaalbonite, the sons of Jashen, Jonathan,
Shammah the Hararite, Ahiam son of Sharar the Hararite,
Eliphelet son of Ahasbai, son of the Maacathite, Eliam son of Ahithophel the Gilonite,
Hezro of Carmel, Paarai the Arbite,
Igal son of Nathan of Zobah, Bani the Gadite,
Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai of Beeroth, the armor-bearer of Joab son of Zeruiah,
Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,
Uriah the Hittite — thirty-seven in all.
The Census · 24:1–9
The anger of YHWH burns against Israel again, and he incites David against them, saying, "Go, number Israel and Judah."
The king says to Joab and the commanders of the army who are with him, "Go through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, and number the people, that I may know how many there are."

But Joab says to the king, "May YHWH your God add to the people a hundred times as many as they are, while the eyes of my lord the king still see it. But why does my lord the king delight in this thing?"
But the king's word prevails against Joab and the commanders of the army. So Joab and the commanders go out from the king's presence to number the people of Israel.
They cross the Jordan and begin from Aroer, and from the city that is in the middle of the valley, toward Gad and on to Jazer.
Then they come to Gilead, and to Kadesh in the land of the Hittites, and they come to Dan, and from Dan they go around to Sidon,
and come to the fortress of Tyre and to all the cities of the Hivites and Canaanites, and they go out to the Negeb of Judah at Beersheba.
So when they have gone through all the land, they come to Jerusalem at the end of nine months and twenty days.
And Joab gives the sum of the numbering of the people to the king: in Israel there are eight hundred thousand valiant men who draw the sword, and the men of Judah are five hundred thousand.
David's Conscience and God's Judgment · 24:10–17

But David's heart strikes him after he has numbered the people. And David says to YHWH, "I have sinned greatly in what I have done. But now, O YHWH, please take away the iniquity of your servant, for I have acted very foolishly."
When David rises in the morning, the word of YHWH comes to the prophet Gad, David's seer:
"Go and say to David, 'Thus says YHWH: Three things I offer you. Choose one of them, that I may do it to you.'"

So Gad comes to David and tells him, and says to him, "Shall three years of famine come to you in your land? Or will you flee three months before your foes while they pursue you? Or shall there be three days of pestilence in your land? Now consider and decide what answer I shall return to him who sent me."
Then David says to Gad, "I am in great distress. Let us fall into the hand of YHWH, for his mercy is great; but let me not fall into the hand of man."
So YHWH sends a pestilence on Israel from the morning until the appointed time. And there die of the people from Dan to Beersheba seventy thousand men.

And when the angel stretches out his hand toward Jerusalem to destroy it, YHWH relents over the disaster and says to the angel who is working destruction among the people, "It is enough. Now stay your hand." The angel of YHWH is then by the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.

Then David speaks to YHWH when he sees the angel who is striking the people, and says, "Behold, I have sinned, and I have done wickedly. But these sheep, what have they done? Please let your hand be against me and against my father's house."
The Threshing Floor of Araunah · 24:18–25
And Gad comes to David that day and says to him, "Go up, raise an altar to YHWH on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite."
So David goes up at Gad's word, as YHWH commanded.
And when Araunah looks down and sees the king and his servants coming toward him, Araunah goes out and bows before the king with his face to the ground.

And Araunah says, "Why has my lord the king come to his servant?" David says, "To buy the threshing floor from you, in order to build an altar to YHWH, that the plague may be averted from the people."
Then Araunah says to David, "Let my lord the king take and offer up what seems good to him. Here are the oxen for the burnt offering and the threshing sledges and the yokes of the oxen for the wood.
All this, O king, Araunah gives to the king." And Araunah says to the king, "May YHWH your God accept you."

But the king says to Araunah, "No, but I will buy it from you for a price. I will not offer burnt offerings to YHWH my God that cost me nothing." So David buys the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.
And David builds there an altar to YHWH and offers burnt offerings and peace offerings. So YHWH responds to the plea for the land, and the plague is averted from Israel.
The Old King and the Shunammite · 1:1–4
King David is old, deep in years. His servants pile blankets on him, but he cannot get warm.
So his servants say to him, "Let a young woman be sought for my lord the king — a virgin who will attend the king and care for him. She will lie in your arms and warm my lord the king."
They search throughout all the territory of Israel for a beautiful young woman and find Abishag the Shunammite, whom they bring to the king.
The young woman is very beautiful. She cares for the king and serves him, but the king does not know her.
Adonijah Seizes His Chance · 1:5–10
Now Adonijah, the son of Haggith, lifts himself up and says, "I will be king." He secures chariots and horsemen for himself and fifty men to run before him.
His father has never at any time displeased him by asking, "Why have you done this?" He is also a very handsome man, and his mother bore him after Absalom.
He confers with Joab son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, and they give their support to Adonijah.
But Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and David's mighty men are not with Adonijah.
Adonijah sacrifices sheep, oxen, and fattened cattle at the stone of Zoheleth beside En-rogel. He invites all his brothers, the king's sons, and all the men of Judah, the king's servants —
but Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, the mighty men, and his brother Solomon he does not invite.
Bathsheba and Nathan Move · 1:11–27
Then Nathan says to Bathsheba, Solomon's mother, "Have you not heard that Adonijah son of Haggith has become king, and our lord David does not even know it?
Come now, let me give you counsel so you can save your life and the life of your son Solomon.

Go at once to King David and say to him: 'Did you not, my lord the king, swear to your servant that Solomon your son would reign after you, and that he would sit on your throne? Why then has Adonijah become king?'
While you are still speaking there with the king, I will come in after you and confirm your words."
So Bathsheba goes to the king in his private chamber. The king is very old, and Abishag the Shunammite is attending him.
Bathsheba bows low and does obeisance to the king. "What is it you want?" he asks.
She says to him, "My lord, you swore to your servant by YHWH your God: 'Solomon your son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne.'
And now Adonijah has become king, and you, my lord the king, do not know it.

He has sacrificed oxen, fattened cattle, and sheep in abundance. He has invited all the king's sons, Abiathar the priest, and Joab the commander of the army — but Solomon your servant he has not invited.
Now, my lord the king, the eyes of all Israel are on you, watching for you to tell them who shall sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.
Otherwise, when my lord the king lies down with his fathers, my son Solomon and I will be counted as criminals."
She is still speaking with the king when Nathan the prophet arrives.
The servants announce him: "Nathan the prophet is here." He comes before the king and bows with his face to the ground.
"My lord the king," Nathan says, "have you said, 'Adonijah shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne'?

For he has gone down today and sacrificed oxen, fattened cattle, and sheep in abundance. He has invited all the king's sons, the army commanders, and Abiathar the priest. Even now they are eating and drinking before him and shouting, 'Long live King Adonijah!'
But me your servant, and Zadok the priest, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and your servant Solomon — none of us has he invited.
Has this thing come about by my lord the king's command, and you have not told your servants who should sit on your throne after you?"
David Commands Solomon's Anointing · 1:28–40
Then King David says, "Call Bathsheba to me." She comes into the king's presence and stands before him.
The king swears: "As YHWH lives, who has redeemed my soul from every adversity,
as I swore to you by YHWH, the God of Israel — Solomon your son shall reign after me and shall sit on my throne in my place — I will fulfill this oath this very day."
Bathsheba bows her face to the ground and does obeisance to the king and says, "May my lord King David live forever!"
Then King David says, "Call to me Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada." They come before the king.
The king says to them, "Take with you the servants of your lord and have Solomon my son ride on my own mule, and bring him down to Gihon.
There let Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anoint him king over Israel. Blow the shofar and shout, 'Long live King Solomon!'
Then come up after him, and let him come and sit on my throne, for he shall be king in my place. I have commanded him to be ruler over Israel and over Judah."
Benaiah son of Jehoiada answers the king: "Amen! So may YHWH, the God of my lord the king, say it so.
As YHWH has been with my lord the king, so may he be with Solomon, and make his throne greater than the throne of my lord King David."
So Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada go down with the Cherethites and the Pelethites and have Solomon ride on King David's own mule, escorting him to Gihon.
Zadok the priest takes the horn of oil from the tent and anoints Solomon. The shofar sounds, and all the people shout, "Long live King Solomon!"
All the people stream up after him, playing on pipes and rejoicing with such great joy that the earth itself shakes from the noise.
Solomon Is King · 1:41–53
Adonijah and all the guests with him hear it just as they are finishing their feast. When Joab hears the sound of the shofar, he says, "What is this uproar in the city?"
He is still speaking when Jonathan son of Abiathar the priest arrives. "Come in," Adonijah says, "for you are a man of worth — surely you bring good news."
Jonathan answers Adonijah, "Not so. Our lord King David has made Solomon king.
The king sent with him Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites and Pelethites, and they had him ride on the king's own mule.
Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anointed him king at Gihon, and they came up from there rejoicing, and the whole city is in an uproar. That is the noise you have heard.
Solomon is now seated on the royal throne,

and the king's servants have come to congratulate our lord King David, saying: 'May your God make the name of Solomon even more famous than yours, and make his throne greater than your throne.' And the king bowed in worship on his bed.
Moreover, the king said, 'Blessed be YHWH, the God of Israel, who has granted one of my own offspring to sit on my throne today while my own eyes see it.'"
At this, all of Adonijah's guests are seized with fear. Every man rises and goes his own way.
Adonijah himself is afraid of Solomon. He rises and goes and takes hold of the horns of the altar.

It is reported to Solomon: "Adonijah is afraid of King Solomon and has laid hold of the horns of the altar and says, 'Let King Solomon first swear to me that he will not put his servant to death with the sword.'"
Solomon says, "If he proves himself a man of worth, not a hair of his shall fall to the ground. But if evil is found in him, he will die."
So King Solomon sends for him, and they bring him down from the altar. He comes and bows before King Solomon, and Solomon says to him, "Go to your house."
When David's time to die draws near, he charges his son Solomon.
“I am going the way of all the earth,“ he says. “Be strong, and show yourself a man.
Keep the charge of YHWH your God —
walking in his ways,
keeping his statutes, his commandments,
his ordinances and his testimonies,
as written in the Law of Moses —
so that you may prosper in all you do,
in every direction you turn.

Then YHWH will fulfill the word he spoke concerning me: 'If your sons watch their way, walking before me in faithfulness with all their heart and with all their soul, you will never lack a man on the throne of Israel.'

You know what Joab son of Zeruiah did to me — how he dealt with the two commanders of Israel's armies, Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether, whom he murdered in peacetime for blood that had been shed in war. He put that war-blood on the belt at his waist and the sandals on his feet.
Act according to your wisdom, but do not let his grey head go down to Sheol in peace.
But deal loyally with the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite. Let them be among those who eat at your table, for they showed me that same loyalty when I fled from your brother Absalom.

With you also is Shimei son of Gera, the Benjaminite from Bahurim, who cursed me with a grievous curse on the day I went to Mahanaim. When he came down to meet me at the Jordan, I swore to him by YHWH: 'I will not put you to death with the sword.'
But you must not leave him unpunished. You are a wise man; you will know what to do to him. Bring his grey head down to Sheol in blood.“
Then David lies down with his fathers and is buried in the city of David.
David reigned over Israel forty years in all — seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
Solomon sits on the throne of his father David, and his kingdom is firmly established.
Adonijah son of Haggith comes to Bathsheba, Solomon's mother. “Do you come in peace?“ she asks. “In peace,“ he says.
“I have something to say to you.“ “Speak,“ she says.
“You know that the kingdom was mine,“ he says, “and that all Israel looked to me to be their king. But the kingdom has turned about and gone to my brother — it was his from YHWH.
Now I have one request of you; do not refuse me.“ “Speak,“ she says.
“Please ask King Solomon — he will not refuse you — to give me Abishag the Shunammite as my wife.“
“Very well,“ Bathsheba says. “I will speak to the king on your behalf.“

Bathsheba goes to King Solomon to speak to him for Adonijah. The king rises to meet her and bows to her, then sits back on his throne. A seat is brought for the queen mother, and she sits at his right hand.
“I have one small request to make of you,“ she says. “Do not refuse me.“ “Ask, mother,“ the king says. “I will not refuse you.“
“Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to Adonijah your brother as his wife.“

King Solomon answers his mother: “Why do you ask Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? Ask him the kingdom as well — for he is my older brother, and Abiathar the priest and Joab son of Zeruiah are on his side.“
Then King Solomon swears by YHWH: “May God do so to me, and worse, if Adonijah does not pay for this request with his life.
Now therefore, as YHWH lives — who has established me and set me on the throne of David my father, who has built me a house as he promised — Adonijah shall be put to death today.“
King Solomon sends Benaiah son of Jehoiada, who strikes Adonijah down, and he dies.

To Abiathar the priest the king says, “Go to Anathoth, to your own field. You deserve death, but I will not put you to death now, because you carried the ark of the Lord YHWH before my father David, and you shared in all that my father suffered.“
So Solomon removes Abiathar from serving as priest before YHWH, fulfilling the word that YHWH had spoken against the house of Eli at Shiloh.
When the news reaches Joab — for Joab had followed Adonijah, though not Absalom — Joab flees to the tent of YHWH and grasps the horns of the altar.
It is reported to King Solomon that Joab has fled to the tent of YHWH and is beside the altar. Solomon sends Benaiah son of Jehoiada with orders: “Go, cut him down.“

Benaiah comes to the tent of YHWH and says, “The king says, 'Come out.'“ But Joab says, “No — I will die here.“ Benaiah brings the king's word back: “This is what Joab said; this is how he answered me.“
The king says to Benaiah: “Do as he says. Cut him down and bury him, and take away from me and my father's house the innocent blood that Joab shed.

YHWH will return his bloodshed on his own head, because he attacked and killed two men more righteous and better than himself — Abner son of Ner, commander of Israel's army, and Amasa son of Jether, commander of Judah's army — without my father David's knowledge.
Their blood shall come back on Joab's head and on his descendants forever. But for David, and for his descendants, his house and his throne, there shall be peace from YHWH forever.“
Then Benaiah son of Jehoiada goes up and cuts Joab down and kills him. He is buried at his house in the wilderness.
The king appoints Benaiah son of Jehoiada over the army in Joab's place, and appoints Zadok the priest in place of Abiathar.
The king summons Shimei and says to him, “Build yourself a house in Jerusalem and live there. Do not go out from there in any direction.
On the day you leave and cross the Kidron Valley, know for certain you will die. Your blood will be on your own head.“
“What you say is right,“ Shimei answers the king. “Your servant will do exactly as my lord the king has spoken.“ And Shimei lives in Jerusalem for many days.
But three years later, two of Shimei's servants run away to Achish son of Maacah, king of Gath. When Shimei is told, “Your servants are in Gath,“ —
he rises, saddles his donkey, and travels to Gath to find them. He goes to Achish and brings his servants back from Gath.
Solomon is told that Shimei has gone from Jerusalem to Gath and returned.

The king summons Shimei and says: “Did I not make you swear by YHWH and warn you clearly: 'On the day you go out in any direction, know that you will die'? And you said, 'What you say is right; I will obey.'
Why then have you not kept the oath you swore to YHWH and the command I laid on you?“
The king says further: “You know in your own heart all the evil you did to my father David. YHWH will return that evil on your own head.
But King Solomon shall be blessed, and the throne of David established before YHWH forever.“
The king commands Benaiah son of Jehoiada, who goes out and strikes Shimei down, and he dies. The kingdom is now firmly in Solomon's hand.

Solomon makes a marriage alliance with Pharaoh king of Egypt and brings Pharaoh's daughter into the city of David, until he finishes building his own house, the house of YHWH, and the wall around Jerusalem.
The people, however, are still sacrificing at the high places, because no house has yet been built for the name of YHWH.
Solomon loves YHWH, walking in the statutes of his father David — yet he too sacrifices and makes offerings at the high places.
The king goes to Gibeon to sacrifice there, for that is the great high place. On that altar Solomon offers a thousand burnt offerings.
At Gibeon YHWH appears to Solomon in a dream by night. God says, “Ask whatever you want me to give you.“

Solomon says, “You have shown great steadfast love to your servant my father David, because he walked before you in faithfulness and righteousness and in uprightness of heart toward you. You have kept this great steadfast love for him and given him a son to sit on his throne this very day.
And now, YHWH my God, you have made your servant king in place of my father David, though I am only a young child. I do not know how to go out or come in.
Your servant stands in the midst of your people whom you have chosen — a great people, too numerous to be counted or numbered.
Give your servant therefore a listening heart — a heart that hears — to govern your people and to discern between good and evil. For who can govern this great people of yours?“
The request pleases the Lord — that Solomon asked for this.
God says to him, “Because you asked for this — because you did not ask for long life for yourself, nor for riches, nor for the lives of your enemies, but asked for understanding to discern justice —
I now do as you have asked. I give you a wise and discerning heart, so that none like you has ever been before you, and none like you shall arise after you.
I also give you what you did not ask — both riches and honor — so that no other king shall compare with you all your days.
And if you walk in my ways, keeping my statutes and commandments as your father David walked, I will also lengthen your days.“
Then Solomon wakes — and it is a dream. He comes to Jerusalem and stands before the ark of the covenant of YHWH and offers burnt offerings and peace offerings and makes a feast for all his servants.
Then two women who work as prostitutes come to the king and stand before him.
One woman says: “Please, my lord — this woman and I live in the same house. I gave birth to a child while she was in the house.
On the third day after I gave birth, this woman also gave birth. We were alone together — no one else was in the house, just the two of us.
This woman's son died in the night, because she lay on him.
She got up in the middle of the night and took my son from beside me while I slept, and laid him against her breast, and laid her dead son against mine.
When I rose in the morning to nurse my child, he was dead. But when I looked at him closely in the morning light, he was not the child I had borne.“
The other woman says, “No — the living child is mine and the dead one is yours.“ The first says, “No — the dead child is yours and the living one is mine.“ And so they argue before the king.
The king says, “One says, 'This is my son who is alive, and your son is the dead one,' and the other says, 'No — your son is dead and my son is the living one.'“
Then the king says, “Bring me a sword.“ A sword is brought before the king.
The king says, “Cut the living child in two, and give half to one and half to the other.“

The woman whose son was the living child says to the king — for her compassion blazes for her son — “Please, my lord, give her the living child! Do not kill him!“ But the other says, “He shall be neither mine nor yours. Cut him in two.“
The king speaks: “Give the living child to the first woman. Do not kill him. She is his mother.“
All Israel hears of the judgment the king has rendered, and they stand in awe of him — for they see that the wisdom of God is in him to execute justice.
King Solomon is king over all Israel.
These are his chief officers: Azariah son of Zadok — the priest;
Elihoreph and Ahijah sons of Shisha — secretaries; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud — the recorder;
Benaiah son of Jehoiada — over the army; Zadok and Abiathar — priests;
Azariah son of Nathan — over the district governors; Zabud son of Nathan — priest and king's personal friend;
Ahishar — over the palace household; Adoniram son of Abda — over the forced labor.
Solomon also has twelve officers over all Israel who provide food for the king and his household. Each man is responsible for one month of the year.
These are their names: Ben-hur, in the hill country of Ephraim;
Ben-deker, in Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth-shemesh, and Elon-beth-hanan;
Ben-hesed, in Arubboth — which includes Socoh and all the land of Hepher;
Ben-abinadab, in all of Naphath-dor — he is married to Taphath, Solomon's daughter;
Baana son of Ahilud, in Taanach and Megiddo, and all Beth-shean beside Zarethan below Jezreel, from Beth-shean to Abel-meholah, as far as beyond Jokneam;
Ben-geber, in Ramoth-gilead — with the villages of Jair son of Manasseh in Gilead, and the region of Argob in Bashan, sixty great cities with walls and bronze bars;
Ahinadab son of Iddo, in Mahanaim;
Ahimaaz, in Naphtali — he too has taken a daughter of Solomon, Basemath, as his wife;
Baana son of Hushai, in Asher and Bealoth;
Jehoshaphat son of Paruah, in Issachar;
Shimei son of Ela, in Benjamin;
Geber son of Uri, in the land of Gilead — the country of Sihon king of the Amorites and of Og king of Bashan. He is the one governor over the whole district.
Judah and Israel are as numerous as the sand by the sea. They eat and drink and are glad.
Solomon rules over all the kingdoms from the Euphrates to the land of the Philistines and to the border of Egypt. They bring tribute and serve Solomon all the days of his life.
Solomon's daily provision is thirty cors of fine flour and sixty cors of meal,
ten fat oxen and twenty pasture-fed cattle and a hundred sheep, besides deer, gazelles, roebucks, and fattened fowl.
For he has dominion over all the region west of the Euphrates from Tiphsah to Gaza — over all the kings west of the river — and he has peace on every side.
Throughout his reign Judah and Israel live in safety — every man under his own vine and under his own fig tree, from Dan to Beersheba.
Solomon has four thousand stalls for his chariot horses and twelve thousand horsemen.
Those district governors provide food for King Solomon and for all who come to the king's table, each in his appointed month, and they let nothing be lacking.
Barley and straw for the horses and swift steeds they bring to wherever it is needed, each according to his duty.
God gives Solomon wisdom and understanding beyond all measure, and a breadth of mind as vast as the sand on the seashore.
Solomon's wisdom surpasses the wisdom of all the people of the east and all the wisdom of Egypt.
He is wiser than any man — wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol — and his fame spreads to all the surrounding nations.
He composes three thousand proverbs, and his songs number a thousand and five.
He speaks of trees, from the cedar of Lebanon to the hyssop growing from the wall. He speaks of beasts, and of birds, and of crawling things, and of fish.
People come from every nation to hear the wisdom of Solomon, sent by all the kings of the earth who have heard of his wisdom.
Now Hiram king of Tyre sends his servants to Solomon when he hears that Solomon has been anointed king in place of his father, for Hiram has always loved David.
Solomon sends word back to Hiram:
“You know that my father David could not build a house for the name of YHWH his God because of the warfare surrounding him on every side, until YHWH put his enemies under the soles of his feet.
But now YHWH my God has given me rest on every side. There is no adversary, no misfortune.
Therefore I intend to build a house for the name of YHWH my God, as YHWH said to my father David: 'Your son, whom I will set on your throne in your place, shall build the house for my name.'

So command that cedars of Lebanon be cut for me. My servants will work alongside yours, and I will pay you wages for your servants according to whatever you set. For you know that none of us knows how to cut timber like the Sidonians.“
When Hiram hears the words of Solomon, he is greatly pleased and says, “Blessed be YHWH today, who has given David a wise son to rule over this great people.“
Hiram sends word to Solomon: “I have heard the message you sent me. I will do all you desire regarding cedar and cypress timber.

My servants will bring it down from Lebanon to the sea, and I will make it into rafts to sail by sea to whatever place you direct me. There I will have them broken up, and you shall receive them. You in turn shall fulfill my wish by providing food for my household.“
So Hiram supplies Solomon with all the cedar and cypress timber he desires,
and Solomon gives Hiram twenty thousand cors of wheat as food for his household, and twenty thousand cors of beaten oil. This is what Solomon gives Hiram year after year.
YHWH gives Solomon wisdom as he promised him, and there is peace between Hiram and Solomon, and the two of them make a treaty.
King Solomon conscripts forced labor from all Israel; thirty thousand men in all.
He sends them to Lebanon in shifts of ten thousand a month — one month in Lebanon, two months at home — with Adoniram in charge of the forced labor.
Solomon also has seventy thousand burden-bearers and eighty thousand stonecutters in the hill country,
besides three thousand three hundred chief officers who oversee the work and manage the workers.
At the king's command they quarry great, costly stones to lay the foundation of the house with dressed stone.
Solomon's builders, Hiram's builders, and the men of Gebal cut the timber and shape the stone to build the house.

In the four hundred and eightieth year after the people of Israel came out of the land of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon's reign over Israel, in the month of Ziv, which is the second month, he begins to build the house of YHWH.
The house that King Solomon builds for YHWH is sixty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high.
The vestibule in front of the main hall of the house is twenty cubits wide, corresponding to the width of the house, and ten cubits deep in front of the house.
He makes for the house windows with recessed frames.
He also builds against the wall of the house a structure all around — against the walls of the house, surrounding the main hall and the inner sanctuary — and he makes side chambers all around.

The lowest story of the side structure is five cubits wide, the middle story six cubits wide, and the third story seven cubits wide, for around the outside of the house he makes offsets in the wall so that the supporting beams do not need to be inserted into the house walls.
The house is built with stone dressed at the quarry, so that no hammer, axe, or any iron tool is heard in the house while it is being built.
The entrance to the lowest story of the side chambers is on the south side of the house, with stairs leading up to the middle story and from the middle story to the third.
So he builds the house and finishes it, roofing it with beams and planks of cedar.
The side chambers, each five cubits high, are built all along the outside of the house, and they are attached to the house by timbers of cedar.
The word of YHWH comes to Solomon:
“Concerning this house you are building —
if you walk in my statutes
and obey my ordinances
and keep all my commandments,
walking in them,
then I will fulfill my word with you
that I spoke to your father David.
I will dwell among the children of Israel
and will not forsake my people Israel.“
So Solomon builds the house and finishes it.

He lines the interior walls of the house with cedar boards — from the floor of the house to the rafters of the ceiling, he covers them on the inside with wood — and he covers the floor of the house with cypress planks.
He builds twenty cubits of the rear of the house with cedar boards from floor to rafters, and this inner section he builds as the inner sanctuary — the Most Holy Place.
The house in front of the inner sanctuary — the main hall — is forty cubits long.
The cedar inside the house is carved with gourds and open flowers. All is cedar; no stone can be seen.
He prepares the inner sanctuary inside the house to set the ark of the covenant of YHWH there.
The inner sanctuary is twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and twenty cubits high, and he overlays it with pure gold. He also makes an altar of cedar.
Solomon overlays the inside of the house with pure gold, and he draws chains of gold across, in front of the inner sanctuary, and overlays it with gold.
He overlays the whole house with gold, until all the house is completely covered. He also overlays with gold the entire altar that belongs to the inner sanctuary.
In the inner sanctuary he makes two cherubim of olivewood, each ten cubits high.
Five cubits is the length of one wing of a cherub and five cubits the length of the other wing — ten cubits from wingtip to wingtip.
The other cherub also measures ten cubits — both cherubim have the same measure and the same form.
The height of one cherub is ten cubits, and so is the height of the other.

He sets the cherubim inside the innermost house. The wings of the cherubim are spread out so that a wing of one touches one wall, and a wing of the other touches the other wall; their wings toward the center of the room touch each other wing to wing.
He overlays the cherubim with gold.
Around all the walls of the house, inside and outside, he carves figures of cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers.
The floor of the house, both inner and outer rooms, he overlays with gold.
For the entrance to the inner sanctuary he makes doors of olivewood; the doorpost is five-sided.
He covers the two doors of olivewood with carvings of cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers, and overlays them with gold, hammering the gold onto the cherubim and palm trees.
For the entrance to the main hall he makes doorposts of olivewood, squared,
and two doors of cypress wood; the two leaves of the one door can fold, and the two leaves of the other door can fold.
On them he carves cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers, and overlays them with gold evenly applied over the carvings.
He builds the inner court with three courses of dressed stone and one course of cedar beams.
In the fourth year the foundation of the house of YHWH is laid, in the month of Ziv.
And in the eleventh year, in the month of Bul — which is the eighth month — the house is finished in all its parts and according to all its specifications. He spends seven years building it.
Solomon also builds his own house, and it takes him thirteen years to complete it.
He builds the House of the Forest of Lebanon — one hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high — set on four rows of cedar pillars with cedar beams on the pillars.
The ceiling above is cedar over forty-five beams, fifteen in each row.
There are three rows of window frames, window opposite window, in three tiers.
All the doorways and doorposts have rectangular frames, and the windows face each other in three tiers.
He also makes the Hall of Pillars — fifty cubits long and thirty cubits wide, with a porch in front and pillars and a canopy before them.
He makes the Hall of the Throne — the Hall of Judgment — where he is to rule and decide cases. It is paneled with cedar from floor to floor.
His own dwelling, in the other court behind the hall, is built in the same fashion. He also makes a house like this hall for Pharaoh's daughter, whom he has married.
All these structures are made of costly dressed stone, cut to size, from the foundation to the eaves, and from the outside to the great court.
The foundations are set with large, costly stones — stones of eight cubits and stones of ten cubits.
Above are costly dressed stones and cedar.
The great court around it has three courses of dressed stone and one course of cedar beams, as in the inner court of the house of YHWH and in the vestibule of the house.
King Solomon sends for Hiram from Tyre.

He is the son of a widow of the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre, a worker in bronze. He is full of wisdom, understanding, and skill for making every work in bronze. He comes to King Solomon and does all his work.
He casts two pillars of bronze. Each pillar is eighteen cubits high, and a line of twelve cubits would encircle each.
He also makes two capitals of molten bronze to set on the tops of the pillars; the height of one capital is five cubits, and the height of the other capital is five cubits.
There are lattices of checker-work with wreaths of chainwork for the capitals on the tops of the pillars: seven for one capital and seven for the other.
So he makes the two pillars, and with two rows of pomegranates all around upon the one network to cover the capitals on the tops of the pillars; he does the same for the second capital.
The capitals on top of the pillars in the vestibule are of lily-work, four cubits high.
On the two pillars are also capitals above, close to the round projection beside the network; and there are two hundred pomegranates in rows all around on each capital.
He sets up the pillars at the vestibule of the main hall. He sets up the right pillar and calls its name Jachin, and he sets up the left pillar and calls its name Boaz.
On the top of the pillars is lily-work. So the work of the pillars is finished.
He makes the molten sea — ten cubits from brim to brim, circular in shape, five cubits high, and a line of thirty cubits encircles it.
Under its brim all around are gourds, ten to a cubit, encircling the sea all around; the gourds are in two rows, cast when it is cast.
It stands on twelve oxen — three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east — and the sea is set on top of them. All their hindquarters are toward the center.
Its thickness is a handbreadth, and its brim is made like the brim of a cup, like the flower of a lily. It holds two thousand baths.
He also makes ten bronze stands. Each stand is four cubits long, four cubits wide, and three cubits high.
This is the design of the stands: they have panels, and the panels are set between frames.
On the panels between the frames are lions, oxen, and cherubim; on the frames also, above and below the lions and oxen, are wreaths of hammered work.
Each stand has four bronze wheels with bronze axles, and its four feet have supports; the supports are cast with wreaths on each side.
The opening at the top is a cubit and a half deep; its opening is round, as a pedestal is made, a cubit and a half. At its opening there are carvings with frames of square, not round, shape.
The four wheels are under the panels; the axles of the wheels are part of the stands. The height of a wheel is a cubit and a half.
The wheels are made like chariot wheels — their axles, rims, spokes, and hubs are all of cast bronze.
There are four supports at the four corners of each stand; the supports are part of the stand itself.
At the top of the stand there is a round band half a cubit high; and at the top of the stand its supports and its panels are part of the stand itself.
On the surfaces of its supports and on its panels he engraves cherubim, lions, and palm trees, each in its place, with wreaths all around.
He makes the ten stands in this way — all of them with the same casting, the same measure, and the same form.
He also makes ten basins of bronze, each basin holding forty baths; each basin measures four cubits, and there is one basin for each of the ten stands.
He sets five of the stands on the south side of the house and five on the north side. He sets the sea on the south side of the house, toward the southeast.
Hiram also makes the pots, the shovels, and the basins. So Hiram finishes all the work he does for King Solomon on the house of YHWH:
the two pillars, the two bowl-shaped capitals on the tops of the pillars, the two sets of network covering the two bowl-shaped capitals on the tops of the pillars,
the four hundred pomegranates for the two networks, two rows of pomegranates for each network, to cover the two bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars,
the ten stands, and the ten basins on the stands,
and the one sea, and the twelve oxen beneath the sea,
and the pots, the shovels, and the basins. All these vessels that Hiram makes for King Solomon for the house of YHWH are of burnished bronze.
In the plain of the Jordan the king casts them, in the clay ground between Succoth and Zarethan.
Solomon leaves all the vessels unweighed, because there are so many of them; the weight of the bronze is beyond reckoning.
So Solomon makes all the vessels that are in the house of YHWH: the golden altar, the golden table for the bread of the Presence,
the lampstands of pure gold, five on the south side and five on the north, before the inner sanctuary; the flowers, the lamps, and the tongs, of gold;

the cups, snuffers, basins, dishes for incense, and fire pans, of pure gold; the hinges, both for the doors of the innermost house — the Most Holy Place — and for the doors of the main hall of the temple, of gold.

Thus all the work that King Solomon does on the house of YHWH is finished. Solomon brings in the things that his father David had dedicated — the silver, the gold, and the vessels — and stores them in the treasuries of the house of YHWH.

Then Solomon assembles the elders of Israel and all the heads of the tribes, the leaders of the ancestral houses of the people of Israel, before King Solomon in Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of YHWH out of the city of David, which is Zion.
All the men of Israel assemble to King Solomon at the feast in the month Ethanim, which is the seventh month.
All the elders of Israel come, and the priests take up the ark.
They bring up the ark of YHWH, the tent of meeting, and all the holy vessels that were in the tent. The priests and Levites bring them up.
And King Solomon and all the congregation of Israel who have gathered before him are with him before the ark, sacrificing sheep and oxen that cannot be counted or numbered for multitude.
Then the priests bring the ark of the covenant of YHWH to its place in the inner sanctuary of the house — the Most Holy Place — under the wings of the cherubim.
The cherubim spread their wings over the place of the ark, so that the cherubim make a covering over the ark and its poles.
The poles extend so far that the ends of the poles are seen from the Holy Place before the inner sanctuary, but they cannot be seen from outside. And they are there to this day.
There is nothing in the ark except the two stone tablets that Moses put there at Horeb, where YHWH made a covenant with the people of Israel when they came out of the land of Egypt.
When the priests come out of the Holy Place, a cloud fills the house of YHWH,
and the priests cannot stand to minister because of the cloud, for the glory of YHWH fills the house of YHWH.
Then Solomon says:
“YHWH has said that he would dwell in thick darkness.
I have indeed built you an exalted house,
a place for you to dwell in forever.“
Then the king turns around and blesses all the assembly of Israel, while all the assembly of Israel stands.
He says: “Blessed be YHWH, the God of Israel, who with his hand has fulfilled what he promised with his mouth to my father David, saying,

“'Since the day I brought my people Israel out of Egypt, I chose no city out of all the tribes of Israel in which to build a house, so that my name might be there. But I chose David to be over my people Israel.'
Now it was in the heart of my father David to build a house for the name of YHWH, the God of Israel.
But YHWH said to my father David: 'You have done well that it was in your heart to build a house for my name.
Nevertheless, you shall not build the house, but your son who shall be born of you shall build the house for my name.'

Now YHWH has fulfilled his promise that he made. For I have risen in the place of my father David, and I sit on the throne of Israel, as YHWH promised. I have built the house for the name of YHWH, the God of Israel.
And I have provided there a place for the ark, in which is the covenant of YHWH that he made with our fathers when he brought them out of the land of Egypt.“
Then Solomon stands before the altar of YHWH in the presence of all the assembly of Israel and spreads out his hands toward heaven.
He says: “YHWH, God of Israel, there is no God like you, in heaven above or on earth beneath — keeping covenant and showing steadfast love to your servants who walk before you with all their heart.
You have kept with your servant David my father what you promised him. You spoke it with your mouth and have fulfilled it with your hand this day.

Now therefore, YHWH, God of Israel, keep for your servant David my father what you promised him: 'You shall not lack a man to sit before me on the throne of Israel, if only your sons pay careful attention to their way, to walk before me as you have walked before me.'
Now therefore, O God of Israel, let your word be confirmed, which you have spoken to your servant my father David.
“But will God indeed dwell on the earth? Behold, heaven and the highest heaven cannot contain you; how much less this house that I have built!
Yet have regard to the prayer of your servant and to his plea, O YHWH my God, listening to the cry and to the prayer that your servant prays before you this day,
that your eyes may be open night and day toward this house — the place of which you have said, 'My name shall be there' — that you may listen to the prayer that your servant prays toward this place.
And listen to the plea of your servant and of your people Israel when they pray toward this place. Hear in heaven your dwelling place, and when you hear, forgive.
“If a man sins against his neighbor and is made to take an oath and comes and swears his oath before your altar in this house,
then hear in heaven and act, and judge your servants, condemning the guilty by bringing his conduct on his own head, and vindicating the righteous by rewarding him according to his righteousness.
“When your people Israel are defeated before the enemy because they have sinned against you, and if they turn again to you and acknowledge your name and pray and plead with you in this house,
then hear in heaven and forgive the sin of your people Israel and bring them back to the land you gave to their fathers.
“When heaven is shut up and there is no rain because they have sinned against you, if they pray toward this place and acknowledge your name and turn from their sin when you afflict them,

then hear in heaven and forgive the sin of your servants, your people Israel, when you teach them the good way they should walk, and send rain on your land, which you have given to your people as an inheritance.

“If there is famine in the land, if there is pestilence or blight or mildew or locust or caterpillar, if their enemy besieges them in any of their cities, whatever plague or whatever sickness there is,
whatever prayer, whatever plea is made by any man or by all your people Israel, each knowing the plague of his own heart and stretching out his hands toward this house,
then hear in heaven your dwelling place and forgive and act and render to each whose heart you know, according to all his ways — for you, you alone, know the hearts of all the children of men —
that they may fear you all the days that they live in the land you gave to our fathers.
“Likewise, when a foreigner who is not of your people Israel comes from a far country for the sake of your name —
for they shall hear of your great name and your mighty hand and your outstretched arm — when he comes and prays toward this house,

hear in heaven your dwelling place and do according to all for which the foreigner calls to you, in order that all the peoples of the earth may know your name and fear you, as do your people Israel, and that they may know that this house I have built is called by your name.
“If your people go out to battle against their enemy, by whatever way you shall send them, and they pray to YHWH toward the city you have chosen and the house I have built for your name,
then hear in heaven their prayer and their plea and maintain their cause.

“If they sin against you — for there is no one who does not sin — and you are angry with them and give them to an enemy so that they are carried away captive to the land of the enemy, far off or near,

yet if they take it to heart in the land to which they have been carried captive, and repent and plead with you in the land of their captors, saying, 'We have sinned and have done wrong; we have acted wickedly,'

if they repent with all their heart and with all their soul in the land of their enemies who carried them captive, and pray to you toward their land, which you gave to their fathers, the city you have chosen, and the house I have built for your name,
then hear in heaven your dwelling place their prayer and their plea, and maintain their cause

and forgive your people who have sinned against you and all their transgressions that they have committed against you, and grant them compassion in the sight of those who carried them captive, that they may have compassion on them.
For they are your people and your heritage, whom you brought out of Egypt, from the midst of the iron furnace.
Let your eyes be open to the plea of your servant and to the plea of your people Israel, giving ear to them whenever they call to you.
For you separated them from among all the peoples of the earth to be your heritage, as you declared through Moses your servant, when you brought our fathers out of Egypt, O Lord YHWH.“
Now as Solomon finishes offering all this prayer and plea to YHWH, he rises from before the altar of YHWH, where he has been kneeling with his hands spread out toward heaven.
He stands and blesses all the assembly of Israel with a loud voice:
“Blessed be YHWH, who has given rest to his people Israel,
according to all that he promised.
Not one word has failed
of all his good promise,
which he spoke by Moses his servant.
May YHWH our God be with us, as he was with our fathers. May he not leave us or forsake us,
that he may incline our hearts to him, to walk in all his ways and to keep his commandments, his statutes, and his ordinances, which he commanded our fathers.

Let these words of mine, with which I have pleaded before YHWH, be near to YHWH our God day and night, that he may maintain the cause of his servant and the cause of his people Israel, as each day requires,
so that all the peoples of the earth may know that YHWH is God; there is no other.
Let your heart therefore be wholly true to YHWH our God, walking in his statutes and keeping his commandments, as it is this day.“
Then the king and all Israel with him offer sacrifice before YHWH.
Solomon offers as peace offerings to YHWH twenty-two thousand oxen and a hundred and twenty thousand sheep. So the king and all the people of Israel dedicate the house of YHWH.

The same day the king consecrates the middle of the court that is before the house of YHWH, for there he offers the burnt offering and the grain offering and the fat pieces of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar that is before YHWH is too small to receive the burnt offering and the grain offering and the fat pieces of the peace offerings.
So Solomon holds the feast at that time, and all Israel with him — a great assembly, from Lebo-hamath to the Brook of Egypt — before YHWH our God, seven days.

On the eighth day he sends the people away, and they bless the king and go to their homes, joyful and glad of heart for all the goodness that YHWH has shown to David his servant and to Israel his people.
When Solomon has finished building the house of YHWH and the king's house and everything Solomon desired to make,
YHWH appears to Solomon a second time, as he had appeared to him at Gibeon.

YHWH says to him: “I have heard your prayer and your plea that you made before me. I have consecrated this house that you have built, to put my name there forever. My eyes and my heart will be there for all time.

And as for you, if you will walk before me as your father David walked, with integrity of heart and uprightness, doing according to all that I have commanded you and keeping my statutes and my ordinances,
then I will establish your royal throne over Israel forever, as I promised your father David, saying: 'You shall not lack a man on the throne of Israel.'
But if you turn aside from following me, you or your children, and do not keep my commandments and my statutes that I have set before you, and if you go and serve other gods and bow down to them,

then I will cut off Israel from the land I have given them, and this house that I have consecrated for my name I will cast out of my sight, and Israel will become a proverb and a byword among all peoples.
And this house will become a heap of ruins. Everyone passing by it will be appalled and will hiss, and they will say: 'Why has YHWH done this to this land and to this house?'

And they will say: 'Because they abandoned YHWH their God who brought their fathers out of the land of Egypt and took hold of other gods and worshipped them and served them. Therefore YHWH has brought all this disaster on them.'“
At the end of twenty years, in which Solomon built the two houses — the house of YHWH and the king's house —
Hiram king of Tyre had supplied Solomon with cedar and cypress timber and gold, as much as he desired, Solomon gives Hiram twenty cities in the land of Galilee.
But when Hiram comes from Tyre to see the cities that Solomon has given him, they do not please him.
He says, “What are these cities that you have given me, my brother?“ So they are called the land of Cabul to this day.
Hiram had sent to the king one hundred and twenty talents of gold.
This is the account of the forced labor that King Solomon drafted to build the house of YHWH and his own house and the Millo and the wall of Jerusalem and Hazor and Megiddo and Gezer.
Pharaoh king of Egypt had gone up and captured Gezer and burned it with fire, killing the Canaanites who lived in the city, and given it as dowry to his daughter, Solomon's wife.
So Solomon rebuilt Gezer and Lower Beth-horon
and Baalath and Tamar in the wilderness, in the land of Judah,

and all the store cities that Solomon had, and the cities for his chariots, and the cities for his horsemen, and whatever Solomon desired to build in Jerusalem, in Lebanon, and in all the land of his dominion.
All the people who were left of the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites — who were not of the people of Israel —
their descendants who were left after them in the land, whom the people of Israel were unable to devote to destruction — these Solomon drafted to be slaves and so they remain to this day.
But of the people of Israel Solomon made no slaves. They were his soldiers, his officials, his commanders, his captains, his chariot commanders, and his horsemen.
These are the chief officers who are over Solomon's work: five hundred and fifty, who have charge of the people who carry on the work.
But Pharaoh's daughter comes up from the city of David to her own house that Solomon builds for her. Then he builds the Millo.
Three times a year Solomon offers burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar he built to YHWH, making offerings with it before YHWH. So he finished the house.
King Solomon builds a fleet of ships at Ezion-geber, which is near Eloth on the shore of the Red Sea, in the land of Edom.
Hiram sends with the fleet his servants, seamen who know the sea, together with the servants of Solomon.
They go to Ophir and bring back from there gold — four hundred and twenty talents — and they bring it to King Solomon.
Now when the queen of Sheba hears of the fame of Solomon concerning the name of YHWH, she comes to test him with hard questions.
She arrives in Jerusalem with a very great retinue — camels bearing spices, very much gold, and precious stones — and when she comes to Solomon, she speaks with him about all that is on her mind.
Solomon answers all her questions; there is nothing hidden from the king that he cannot explain to her.
When the queen of Sheba sees all the wisdom of Solomon, the house he has built,

the food of his table, the seating of his officials, the attendance of his servants, their clothing, his cupbearers, and his burnt offerings that he makes at the house of YHWH, there is no more breath in her.
She says to the king: “The report was true that I heard in my own land about your words and your wisdom.
I did not believe the reports until I came and my own eyes saw it. And behold, the half was not told me. Your wisdom and prosperity surpass the report that I heard.
Happy are your men! Happy are your servants, who continually stand before you and hear your wisdom!
Blessed be YHWH your God, who has delighted in you and set you on the throne of Israel! Because YHWH loved Israel forever, he has made you king to execute justice and righteousness.“

Then she gives the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold, a very great quantity of spices, and precious stones. Never again came such an abundance of spices as those that the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.
Moreover, the fleet of Hiram, which brought gold from Ophir, brought from Ophir a very great amount of almug wood and precious stones.
The king made of the almug wood supports for the house of YHWH and for the king's house, lyres also and harps for the singers. No such almug wood came again or has been seen to this day.

And King Solomon gives to the queen of Sheba all that she desired, whatever she asked, besides what was given her by the bounty of King Solomon. Then she turns and goes back to her own land with her servants.
Now the weight of gold that comes to Solomon in one year is six hundred and sixty-six talents of gold,
besides that which comes from the explorers and the business of the merchants, and from all the kings of the west and from the governors of the land.
King Solomon makes two hundred large shields of beaten gold — six hundred shekels of gold go into each shield.
And he makes three hundred shields of beaten gold — three minas of gold go into each shield — and the king puts them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
The king also makes a great ivory throne and overlays it with the finest gold.
The throne has six steps, and the top of the throne is round at the back, with armrests on each side of the seat, and two lions standing beside the armrests.
Twelve lions stand there, one on each end of a step on the six steps. Nothing like it was ever made in any kingdom.
All King Solomon's drinking vessels are of gold, and all the vessels of the House of the Forest of Lebanon are of pure gold. Silver is not considered as anything in the days of Solomon.
For the king has a fleet of ships of Tarshish at sea with Hiram's fleet. Once every three years the fleet of ships of Tarshish comes bringing gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.
Thus King Solomon exceeds all the kings of the earth in riches and in wisdom.
And the whole earth seeks the presence of Solomon to hear his wisdom, which God has put into his mind.
Every one of them brings his present — articles of silver and gold, garments, myrrh, spices, horses, and mules — so much year by year.
Solomon also gathers chariots and horsemen. He has fourteen hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, whom he stations in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.
The king makes silver as common in Jerusalem as stone, and he makes cedar as plentiful as the sycamore of the Shephelah.
Solomon's horses are imported from Egypt and from Kue — the king's traders receive them from Kue at a set price.

A chariot could be imported from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver and a horse for a hundred and fifty shekels. Likewise through them these were exported to all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Syria.
King Solomon loves many foreign women — the daughter of Pharaoh, as well as Moabite, Ammonite, Edomite, Sidonian, and Hittite women,

from the nations of which YHWH said to the people of Israel, “You shall not enter into marriage with them, neither shall they with you, for surely they will turn your heart after their gods.“ To these Solomon clings in love.
He has seven hundred wives, who are princesses, and three hundred concubines, and his wives turn his heart away.
When Solomon is old, his wives turn his heart after other gods, and his heart is not wholly true to YHWH his God, as was the heart of his father David.
For Solomon goes after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, and after Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites.
So Solomon does what is evil in the sight of YHWH and does not wholly follow YHWH, as his father David had done.
Then Solomon builds a high place for Chemosh the abomination of Moab, and for Molech the abomination of the Ammonites, on the mountain east of Jerusalem.
And so he does for all his foreign wives, who make offerings and sacrifice to their gods.
YHWH is angry with Solomon, because his heart has turned away from YHWH, the God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice
and had commanded him concerning this thing — not to go after other gods. But he did not keep what YHWH commanded.

Therefore YHWH says to Solomon, “Since this has been your practice and you have not kept my covenant and my statutes that I have commanded you, I will surely tear the kingdom from you and give it to your servant.
Yet for the sake of your father David I will not do it in your days, but I will tear it out of the hand of your son.
However, I will not tear away all the kingdom, but I will give one tribe to your son, for the sake of my servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem that I have chosen.“
YHWH raises up an adversary against Solomon — Hadad the Edomite. He was of the royal house of Edom.
For when David was in Edom, and Joab the commander of the army went up to bury the slain and struck down every male in Edom —
for Joab and all Israel had stayed there six months, until he had cut off every male in Edom —
Hadad fled to Egypt, together with some Edomites of his father's servants. Hadad was still a small child at that time.
They set out from Midian and came to Paran and took men with them from Paran and came to Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt, who gave him a house and assigned him an allowance of food and gave him land.
Hadad finds great favor in the sight of Pharaoh, so that Pharaoh gives him in marriage the sister of his own wife, the sister of Tahpenes the queen.
The sister of Tahpenes bears him Genubath his son, whom Tahpenes weans in Pharaoh's house. And Genubath was in Pharaoh's house among the sons of Pharaoh.
But when Hadad hears in Egypt that David slept with his fathers and that Joab the commander of the army was dead, Hadad says to Pharaoh, “Let me depart, so that I may go to my own country.“
Pharaoh says to him, “What have you lacked with me, that you are now seeking to go to your own country?“ He says, “Nothing, but still — let me go.“
God also raises up as adversary against Solomon Rezon son of Eliada, who had fled from his master Hadadezer king of Zobah.
He gathered men around himself and became leader of a marauding band, after David killed the men of Zobah. And they went to Damascus and lived there and made him king in Damascus.
He was an adversary of Israel all the days of Solomon, doing harm as Hadad did. He loathed Israel and reigned over Syria.
Jeroboam son of Nebat, an Ephraimite of Zeredah, a servant of Solomon, also lifts up his hand against the king. His mother's name is Zeruah, a widow.
This is the account of why he lifts his hand against the king. Solomon built the Millo and closed up the breach of the city of David his father.
The man Jeroboam is very able, and when Solomon sees that the young man is industrious, he puts him in charge of all the forced labor of the house of Joseph.

And at that time, when Jeroboam goes out of Jerusalem, the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite finds him on the road. Now Ahijah has clothed himself with a new garment, and the two of them are alone in the open country.
Ahijah takes hold of the new garment that is on him and tears it into twelve pieces.
He says to Jeroboam, “Take for yourself ten pieces, for thus says YHWH, the God of Israel: 'Behold, I am about to tear the kingdom from the hand of Solomon and will give you ten tribes.
But he shall have one tribe, for the sake of my servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel.

This is because he has forsaken me and worshipped Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, Chemosh the god of Moab, and Milcom the god of the Ammonites, and has not walked in my ways, doing what is right in my sight and keeping my statutes and my ordinances, as David his father did.

Nevertheless, I will not take the whole kingdom out of his hand, but I will make him ruler all the days of his life, for the sake of my servant David whom I chose, who kept my commandments and my statutes.
But I will take the kingdom out of his son's hand and will give it to you — ten tribes.
Yet to his son I will give one tribe, that David my servant may always have a lamp before me in Jerusalem, the city where I have chosen to put my name.
And I will take you, and you shall reign over all that your soul desires, and you shall be king over Israel.

And if you will listen to all that I command you and will walk in my ways and do what is right in my eyes by keeping my statutes and my commandments, as David my servant did, I will be with you and will build you a sure house, as I built for David, and I will give Israel to you.
And I will afflict the offspring of David because of this, but not forever.'“
Solomon seeks to kill Jeroboam, but Jeroboam rises and flees to Egypt, to Shishak king of Egypt, and is in Egypt until the death of Solomon.
Now the rest of the acts of Solomon, and all that he did, and his wisdom — are they not written in the Book of the Acts of Solomon?
The time that Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel is forty years.
Solomon lies down with his fathers and is buried in the city of David his father. Rehoboam his son reigns in his place.
Rehoboam goes to Shechem, for all Israel has come to Shechem to make him king.
When Jeroboam son of Nebat hears of it — for he is still in Egypt, where he had fled from King Solomon — Jeroboam returns from Egypt.
They send and call him. Jeroboam and all the assembly of Israel come and speak to Rehoboam:
“Your father made our yoke heavy. Now therefore lighten the hard service of your father and his heavy yoke on us, and we will serve you.“
He says to them, “Go away for three days, then come back to me.“ So the people go away.
Then King Rehoboam takes counsel with the old men who had stood before his father Solomon while he was still alive: “How do you advise me to answer this people?“
They say to him, “If you will be a servant to this people today and serve them and speak good words to them when you answer them, they will be your servants forever.“
But he abandons the counsel of the old men and takes counsel with the young men who had grown up with him and stood before him.
He says to them, “What do you advise that we answer this people who have said to me, 'Lighten the yoke that your father put on us'?“

The young men who had grown up with him say to him: “Thus shall you speak to this people who said to you, 'Your father made our yoke heavy, but you lighten it for us' — say to them: 'My little finger is thicker than my father's waist.
And now, whereas my father laid on you a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions.'“
Jeroboam and all the people come to Rehoboam on the third day, as the king said, “Come to me again on the third day.“
The king answers the people harshly. He abandons the counsel of the old men

and speaks to them according to the counsel of the young men: “My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add to your yoke. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions.“
So the king does not listen to the people, for it is a turn of affairs brought about by YHWH so that he might fulfill his word, which YHWH spoke by Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat.
When all Israel sees that the king does not listen to them, the people answer the king:
“What portion do we have in David?
We have no inheritance in the son of Jesse.
To your tents, O Israel!
Look now to your own house, David.“
So Israel goes to their tents.
But Rehoboam reigns over the people of Israel who live in the cities of Judah.
When King Rehoboam sends Adoram, who is over the forced labor, all Israel stones him to death with stones. King Rehoboam hurries to mount his chariot to flee to Jerusalem.
So Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David to this day.

When all Israel hears that Jeroboam has returned, they send and call him to the assembly and make him king over all Israel. There is none that follows the house of David except the tribe of Judah alone.

When Rehoboam comes to Jerusalem, he assembles all the house of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin — one hundred and eighty thousand chosen warriors — to fight against the house of Israel to restore the kingdom to Rehoboam son of Solomon.
But the word of God comes to Shemaiah the man of God:
“Say to Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all the house of Judah and Benjamin and the rest of the people:

“Thus says YHWH: You shall not go up or fight against your relatives the people of Israel. Every man return to his home, for this thing is from me.'“ So they listen to the word of YHWH and go home again, according to the word of YHWH.
Then Jeroboam built Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim and settled there. And he went out from there and built Penuel.
And Jeroboam says in his heart, “Now the kingdom will return to the house of David.

If this people go up to offer sacrifices in the house of YHWH at Jerusalem, the heart of this people will turn again to their lord, to Rehoboam king of Judah, and they will kill me and return to Rehoboam king of Judah.“
So the king takes counsel and makes two calves of gold. He says to the people, “You have gone up to Jerusalem long enough. Behold your gods, O Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt.“
He sets one in Bethel and the other he puts in Dan.
Then this thing becomes a sin, for the people go as far as Dan to worship before the one there.
He also makes temples on high places and appoints priests from among all the people who are not of the Levites.

And Jeroboam appoints a feast on the fifteenth day of the eighth month — like the feast that is in Judah — and he offers sacrifices on the altar. So he does in Bethel, sacrificing to the calves that he has made. And he places in Bethel the priests of the high places that he has made.

He goes up to the altar that he has made in Bethel on the fifteenth day in the eighth month, in the month that he devised from his own heart. And he institutes a feast for the people of Israel and goes up to the altar to make offerings.
And behold, a man of God comes out of Judah by the word of YHWH to Bethel. Jeroboam is standing by the altar to make offerings.

The man cries out against the altar by the word of YHWH: “O altar, altar, thus says YHWH: 'Behold, a son shall be born to the house of David — Josiah by name — and he shall sacrifice on you the priests of the high places who make offerings on you, and human bones shall be burned on you.'“
He gives a sign the same day: “This is the sign that YHWH has spoken: Behold, the altar shall be torn apart, and the ashes that are on it shall be poured out.“

When the king hears the word of the man of God, which he cries against the altar at Bethel, Jeroboam stretches out his hand from the altar, saying, “Seize him!“ And his hand, which he stretched out against him, withers so that he cannot draw it back to himself.
The altar also is torn apart and the ashes poured out from the altar, according to the sign that the man of God has given by the word of YHWH.

The king says to the man of God, “Entreat now the favor of YHWH your God, and pray for me, that my hand may be restored to me.“ And the man of God entreats YHWH, and the king's hand is restored to him and became as before.
The king says to the man of God, “Come home with me and refresh yourself, and I will give you a reward.“
