The man of God says to the king, “If you give me half your house, I will not go in with you. And I will not eat bread or drink water in this place,
for so was it commanded me by the word of YHWH, saying, 'You shall neither eat bread nor drink water nor return by the way you came.'“
So he goes another way and does not return by the way he came to Bethel.
Now an old prophet lives in Bethel. His sons come and tell him all that the man of God has done that day in Bethel. They also tell their father the words that he spoke to the king.
Their father says to them, “Which way did he go?“ His sons show him the way the man of God who came from Judah had gone.
He says to his sons, “Saddle the donkey for me.“ So they saddle the donkey for him and he mounts it.
He goes after the man of God and finds him sitting under an oak. He says to him, “Are you the man of God who came from Judah?“ And he says, “I am.“
Then he says to him, “Come home with me and eat bread.“
He says, “I may not return with you, or go in with you, neither will I eat bread nor drink water with you in this place,
for it was said to me by the word of YHWH: You shall neither eat bread nor drink water there, nor return by the way you came.“

He says to him, “I also am a prophet as you are, and an angel spoke to me by the word of YHWH, saying, 'Bring him back with you into your house that he may eat bread and drink water.'“ But he lied to him.
So he goes back with him and eats bread in his house and drinks water.
As they sit at the table, the word of YHWH comes to the prophet who brought him back.
He cries to the man of God who came from Judah: “Thus says YHWH: 'Because you have disobeyed the word of YHWH and have not kept the commandment that YHWH your God commanded you,
but have come back and have eaten bread and drunk water in the place of which he said to you, “Eat no bread and drink no water,“ your body shall not come to the tomb of your fathers.'“
After he had eaten bread and drunk, the old prophet saddles the donkey for the man of God.
As the man of God goes, a lion meets him on the road and kills him. His body is thrown on the road, and the donkey stands beside it; the lion also stands beside the body.
People passing by see the body thrown on the road and the lion standing beside the body, and they come and tell it in the city where the old prophet lives.

When the prophet who had brought him back from the way hears of it, he says, “It is the man of God who disobeyed the word of YHWH; therefore YHWH has given him to the lion, which has torn him and killed him, according to the word that YHWH spoke to him.“
He speaks to his sons: “Saddle the donkey for me.“ And they saddle it.
He goes and finds the body thrown in the road, with the donkey and the lion standing beside the body. The lion has not eaten the body or torn the donkey.
The prophet takes up the body of the man of God and lays it on the donkey and brings it back to the city to mourn and to bury him.
He lays the body in his own tomb and mourns over him: “Alas, my brother!“
After he has buried him, he says to his sons, “When I die, bury me in the tomb in which the man of God is buried; lay my bones beside his bones.
For the saying that he called out by the word of YHWH against the altar in Bethel and against all the houses of the high places that are in the cities of Samaria will surely come to pass.“
After this thing Jeroboam does not turn from his evil way, but makes priests for the high places again from among all the people. Whoever wishes, he ordains as priest for the high places.
This thing becomes sin to the house of Jeroboam, so as to cut it off and to destroy it from the face of the earth.
At that time Abijah the son of Jeroboam falls sick.

Jeroboam says to his wife, “Arise, and disguise yourself, so they will not know you are the wife of Jeroboam, and go to Shiloh. Behold, Ahijah the prophet is there, who said of me that I should be king over this people.
Take with you ten loaves, some cakes, and a jar of honey, and go to him. He will tell you what shall happen to the child.“
Jeroboam's wife does so. She arises and goes to Shiloh and comes to the house of Ahijah. Now Ahijah cannot see, for his eyes are dim because of his age.
YHWH says to Ahijah, “Behold, the wife of Jeroboam is coming to inquire of you concerning her son, for he is sick. Thus and thus shall you say to her.“

When she comes in, she pretends to be another woman. But when Ahijah hears the sound of her feet as she comes in at the door, he says, “Come in, wife of Jeroboam. Why do you pretend to be another? For I am charged with heavy news for you.
Go, tell Jeroboam, “Thus says YHWH, the God of Israel: 'Because I exalted you from among the people and made you leader over my people Israel,

and tore the kingdom away from the house of David and gave it to you — and yet you have not been like my servant David, who kept my commandments and followed me with all his heart, doing only what was right in my eyes —
but you have done evil above all who were before you and have gone and made for yourself other gods and metal images, provoking me to anger and casting me behind your back —

therefore behold: I will bring disaster upon the house of Jeroboam and will cut off from Jeroboam every male, both bond and free in Israel, and will burn up the house of Jeroboam as a man burns up dung until it is all gone.
Anyone belonging to Jeroboam who dies in the city the dogs shall eat, and anyone who dies in the open country the birds of the heavens shall eat, for YHWH has spoken it.'“
“Arise therefore and go to your house. When your feet enter the city, the child shall die.

And all Israel shall mourn for him and bury him, for he alone of Jeroboam's family shall come to the grave, because in him there is found something pleasing to YHWH, the God of Israel, in the house of Jeroboam.
Moreover, YHWH will raise up for himself a king over Israel who shall cut off the house of Jeroboam today. And henceforth, even now.

And YHWH will strike Israel as a reed is shaken in the water, and root up Israel out of this good land that he gave to their fathers and scatter them beyond the Euphrates, because they have made their Asherah poles, provoking YHWH to anger.
And he will give Israel up because of the sins of Jeroboam, which he sinned and made Israel to sin.“
Jeroboam's wife arises and departs and comes to Tirzah. As she comes to the threshold of the house, the child dies.
And all Israel buries him and mourns for him, according to the word of YHWH, which he spoke by his servant Ahijah the prophet.
Now the rest of the acts of Jeroboam — how he warred and how he reigned — behold, they are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
The time that Jeroboam reigned was twenty-two years. He lies down with his fathers, and Nadab his son reigns in his place.

Now Rehoboam the son of Solomon reigns in Judah. Rehoboam is forty-one years old when he becomes king, and he reigns seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city that YHWH chose out of all the tribes of Israel to put his name there. His mother's name is Naamah the Ammonite.
Judah does what is evil in the sight of YHWH, and they provoke him to jealousy with their sins that they commit — more than all their fathers had done.
For they also build for themselves high places and pillars and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every green tree.
And there are also male cult prostitutes in the land. They do according to all the abominations of the nations that YHWH drove out before the people of Israel.
In the fifth year of King Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt comes up against Jerusalem.
He takes away the treasures of the house of YHWH and the treasures of the king's house. He takes away everything. He also takes away all the shields of gold that Solomon had made.
King Rehoboam makes shields of bronze in their place and commits them to the hands of the officers of the guard who keep the door of the king's house.
And as often as the king goes into the house of YHWH, the guard carries them and brings them back to the guardroom.
Now the rest of the acts of Rehoboam and all that he did — are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
And there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continually.
Rehoboam lies down with his fathers and is buried with his fathers in the city of David. His mother's name is Naamah the Ammonite. Abijam his son reigns in his place.
In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam son of Nebat, Abijam begins to reign over Judah.
He reigns three years in Jerusalem. His mother's name is Maacah the daughter of Abishalom.
He walks in all the sins of his father which he committed before him, and his heart is not wholly true to YHWH his God, as the heart of David his father.
Nevertheless, for David's sake YHWH his God gives him a lamp in Jerusalem, raising up his son after him and establishing Jerusalem,
because David did what was right in the eyes of YHWH and did not turn aside from anything that he commanded him all the days of his life, except in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.
Now there is war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days of his life.
The rest of the acts of Abijam and all that he did — are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah? There is also war between Abijam and Jeroboam.
Abijam lies down with his fathers, and they bury him in the city of David. Asa his son reigns in his place.
In the twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Asa begins to reign over Judah.
He reigns forty-one years in Jerusalem. His mother's name is Maacah the daughter of Abishalom.
Asa does what is right in the eyes of YHWH, as his father David did.
He puts away the male cult prostitutes from the land and removes all the idols that his fathers had made.
He also removes Maacah his mother from being queen mother because she has made an abominable image for Asherah. Asa cuts down her image and burned it at the brook Kidron.
The high places are not taken away. Nevertheless, the heart of Asa is wholly true to YHWH all his days.
He brings into the house of YHWH the sacred gifts of his father and his own sacred gifts — silver, gold, and vessels.
There is war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.
Baasha king of Israel goes up against Judah and builds Ramah, to prevent any from going out or coming in to Asa king of Judah.

Then Asa takes all the silver and gold that are left in the treasures of the house of YHWH and the treasures of the king's house and gives them into the hands of his servants. King Asa sends them to Ben-hadad the son of Tabrimmon, the son of Hezion, king of Syria, who lived in Damascus, saying,

“Let there be a covenant between me and you, as there was between my father and your father. Behold, I am sending to you a present of silver and gold. Go, break your covenant with Baasha king of Israel, that he may withdraw from me.“
Ben-hadad listens to King Asa and sends the commanders of his armies against the cities of Israel and conquers Ijon, Dan, Abel-beth-maacah, and all Chinneroth, with all the land of Naphtali.
When Baasha hears of it, he stops building Ramah and lives in Tirzah.

Then King Asa makes a proclamation to all Judah — none is exempt — and they carry away the stones of Ramah and its timber, with which Baasha had been building, and with them King Asa builds Geba of Benjamin and Mizpah.

Now the rest of all the acts of Asa, all his might, and all that he did, and the cities that he built — are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah? But in his old age he is diseased in his feet.
Asa lies down with his fathers and is buried with his fathers in the city of David his father. Jehoshaphat his son reigns in his place.
Nadab the son of Jeroboam begins to reign over Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah, and he reigns over Israel two years.
He does what is evil in the sight of YHWH and walks in the way of his father and in his sin which he made Israel to sin.

Baasha the son of Ahijah, of the house of Issachar, conspires against him, and Baasha strikes him down at Gibbethon, which belongs to the Philistines, for Nadab and all Israel are laying siege to Gibbethon.
So Baasha kills him in the third year of Asa king of Judah and reigns in his place.

And as soon as he is king, he kills all the house of Jeroboam. He leaves to the house of Jeroboam not one that breathes, until he has destroyed it, according to the word of YHWH that he spoke by his servant Ahijah the Shilonite.
It is for the sins of Jeroboam that he sinned and that he made Israel to sin, and because of the provocation with which he provoked YHWH, the God of Israel, to anger.
Now the rest of the acts of Nadab and all that he did — are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
There is war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.
In the third year of Asa king of Judah, Baasha the son of Ahijah begins to reign over all Israel at Tirzah, and he reigns twenty-four years.
He does what is evil in the sight of YHWH and walks in the way of Jeroboam and in his sin which he made Israel to sin.
The word of YHWH comes to Jehu the son of Hanani against Baasha:

“Since I exalted you out of the dust and made you leader over my people Israel, and you have walked in the way of Jeroboam and have made my people Israel to sin, provoking me to anger with their sins,
behold, I will utterly sweep away Baasha and his house, and I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat.
Anyone belonging to Baasha who dies in the city the dogs shall eat, and anyone who belongs to him who dies in the field the birds of the heavens shall eat.“
Now the rest of the acts of Baasha and what he did, and his might — are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
Baasha lies down with his fathers and is buried at Tirzah, and Elah his son reigns in his place.

Moreover, the word of YHWH came by the prophet Jehu the son of Hanani against Baasha and his house, both because of all the evil that he did in the sight of YHWH, provoking him to anger with the work of his hands — in being like the house of Jeroboam — and also because he destroyed it.
In the twenty-sixth year of Asa king of Judah, Elah the son of Baasha begins to reign over Israel at Tirzah, and he reigns two years.
But his servant Zimri, commander of half his chariots, conspires against him. When he is at Tirzah, drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza, who is over the household at Tirzah,
Zimri comes in and strikes him down and kills him — in the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah — and reigns in his place.
When he begins to reign, as soon as he sits on his throne, he strikes down all the house of Baasha. He does not leave a single male of his relatives or his friends.
Thus Zimri destroys all the house of Baasha, according to the word of YHWH, which he spoke against Baasha through Jehu the prophet,
for all the sins of Baasha and the sins of Elah his son, which they sinned and which they made Israel to sin, provoking YHWH the God of Israel to anger with their idols.
Now the rest of the acts of Elah and all that he did — are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
In the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, Zimri reigns seven days in Tirzah. Now the people are encamped against Gibbethon, which belongs to the Philistines.
The people who are encamped hear it said, “Zimri has conspired, and he has killed the king.“ Therefore all Israel makes Omri, the commander of the army, king over Israel that day in the camp.
So Omri goes up from Gibbethon, and all Israel with him, and they besiege Tirzah.
When Zimri sees that the city is taken, he goes into the citadel of the king's house and burns the king's house over himself with fire and dies,
because of his sins that he committed, doing evil in the sight of YHWH, walking in the way of Jeroboam, and for his sin which he did, making Israel to sin.
Now the rest of the acts of Zimri and the conspiracy that he made — are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
Then the people of Israel are divided into two halves. Half of the people follow Tibni the son of Ginath, to make him king, and half follow Omri.
But the people who follow Omri overcome the people who follow Tibni the son of Ginath. So Tibni dies, and Omri reigns.
In the thirty-first year of Asa king of Judah, Omri begins to reign over Israel — twelve years. He reigns six years in Tirzah.
He buys the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver, and he builds on the hill and calls the name of the city that he builds Samaria, after the name of Shemer, the owner of the hill.
Omri does what is evil in the sight of YHWH and does more evil than all who were before him.
For he walks in all the way of Jeroboam the son of Nebat and in the sins that he made Israel to sin, provoking YHWH the God of Israel to anger with their idols.
Now the rest of the acts of Omri that he did, and the might that he showed — are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
Omri lies down with his fathers and is buried in Samaria, and Ahab his son reigns in his place.
In the thirty-eighth year of Asa king of Judah, Ahab the son of Omri begins to reign over Israel. Ahab the son of Omri reigns over Israel in Samaria twenty-two years.
Ahab the son of Omri does evil in the sight of YHWH, more than all who were before him.

And as if it had been a light thing for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, he takes for his wife Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians, and goes and serves Baal and worships him.
He erects an altar for Baal in the house of Baal, which he builds in Samaria.
Ahab also makes an Asherah. Ahab does more to provoke YHWH, the God of Israel, to anger than all the kings of Israel who were before him.

In his days Hiel of Bethel builds Jericho. He lays its foundation at the cost of Abiram his firstborn, and sets up its gates at the cost of his youngest son Segub, according to the word of YHWH, which he spoke by Joshua the son of Nun.
Now Elijah the Tishbite, of Tishbe in Gilead, says to Ahab, “As YHWH the God of Israel lives, before whom I stand, there shall be neither dew nor rain these years, except by my word.“
The word of YHWH comes to him:
“Depart from here and turn eastward and hide yourself by the brook Cherith, which is east of the Jordan.
You shall drink from the brook, and I have commanded the ravens to feed you there.“
So he goes and does according to the word of YHWH. He goes and lives by the brook Cherith that is east of the Jordan.
The ravens bring him bread and meat in the morning, and bread and meat in the evening, and he drinks from the brook.
After a while the brook dries up, because there is no rain in the land.
Then the word of YHWH comes to him:
“Arise, go to Zarephath, which belongs to Sidon, and dwell there. Behold, I have commanded a widow there to feed you.“

So he arises and goes to Zarephath. When he comes to the gate of the city, behold, a widow is there gathering sticks. He calls to her and says, “Bring me a little water in a vessel, that I may drink.“
As she goes to bring it, he calls to her and says, “Bring me a morsel of bread in your hand.“

She says, “As YHWH your God lives, I have nothing baked — only a handful of flour in a jar and a little oil in a jug. And now I am gathering a couple of sticks that I may go in and prepare it for myself and my son, that we may eat it and die.“
Elijah says to her, “Do not fear. Go and do as you have said. But first make me a little cake of it and bring it to me, and afterward make something for yourself and your son.
For thus says YHWH, the God of Israel: The jar of flour shall not be spent, and the jug of oil shall not run dry, until the day that YHWH sends rain upon the earth.“
She goes and does as Elijah says. And she and he and her household eat for many days.
The jar of flour is not spent, neither does the jug of oil run dry, according to the word of YHWH that he spoke by Elijah.
After this the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, becomes ill. His illness is so severe that there is no breath left in him.
She says to Elijah, “What have you against me, O man of God? You have come to me to bring my sin to remembrance and to cause the death of my son!“
He says to her, “Give me your son.“ He takes him from her arms and carries him up into the upper chamber where he is lodging and lays him on his own bed.
He cries out to YHWH: “O YHWH my God, have you brought calamity even upon the widow with whom I sojourn, by killing her son?“
Then he stretches himself upon the child three times and cries to YHWH: “O YHWH my God, let this child's soul come into him again.“
YHWH listens to the voice of Elijah. The soul of the child comes into him again, and he revives.
Elijah takes the child and brings him down from the upper chamber into the house and gives him to his mother. Elijah says, “See, your son lives.“
The woman says to Elijah, “Now I know that you are a man of God, and that the word of YHWH in your mouth is truth.“
After many days the word of YHWH comes to Elijah, in the third year: “Go, show yourself to Ahab, and I will send rain upon the earth.“
So Elijah goes to show himself to Ahab. The famine is severe in Samaria.
Ahab calls Obadiah, who is over the household — and Obadiah fears YHWH greatly.
For when Jezebel cuts off the prophets of YHWH, Obadiah takes a hundred prophets and hides them by fifties in a cave and feeds them with bread and water.
Ahab says to Obadiah, “Go through the land to all the springs of water and to all the valleys. Perhaps we may find grass and save the horses and mules alive, and not lose some of the animals.“
So they divide the land between them to pass through it. Ahab goes in one direction by himself and Obadiah goes in another direction by himself.
As Obadiah is on the way, behold, Elijah meets him. Obadiah recognizes him and falls on his face and says, “Is it you, my lord Elijah?“
He answers him, “It is I. Go, tell your lord, 'Behold, Elijah is here.'“
He says, “How have I sinned, that you would give your servant into the hand of Ahab, to kill me?

As YHWH your God lives, there is no nation or kingdom where my lord has not sent to seek you. And when they said, 'He is not here,' he would take an oath of the kingdom or nation that they had not found you.
And now you say, 'Go, tell your lord, “Behold, Elijah is here.“'

And as soon as I have gone from you, the Spirit of YHWH will carry you I know not where. And so, when I come and tell Ahab and he cannot find you, he will kill me, although I your servant have feared YHWH from my youth.
Has it not been told my lord what I did when Jezebel killed the prophets of YHWH — how I hid a hundred men of YHWH's prophets by fifties in a cave and fed them with bread and water?
And now you say, 'Go, tell your lord, “Behold, Elijah is here.“'He will kill me.“
Elijah says, “As YHWH of hosts lives, before whom I stand, I will surely show myself to him today.“
So Obadiah goes to meet Ahab and tells him. Ahab goes to meet Elijah.
When Ahab sees Elijah, Ahab says to him, “Is it you, you troubler of Israel?“
Elijah answers, “I have not troubled Israel, but you have — you and your father's house, because you have abandoned the commandments of YHWH and followed the Baals.
Now therefore send and gather all Israel to me at Mount Carmel, and the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal and the four hundred prophets of Asherah, who eat at Jezebel's table.“
So Ahab sends to all the people of Israel and gathers the prophets together at Mount Carmel.

Elijah comes near to all the people and says, “How long will you go limping between two different opinions? If YHWH is God, follow him; but if Baal, then follow him.“ And the people answer him not a word.
Then Elijah says to the people, “I, even I only, am left as a prophet of YHWH, while Baal's prophets are four hundred and fifty men.

Let two bulls be given to us, and let them choose one bull for themselves and cut it in pieces and lay it on the wood but put no fire to it. I will prepare the other bull and lay it on the wood and put no fire to it.
And you call upon the name of your god, and I will call upon the name of YHWH, and the God who answers by fire — he is God.“ All the people answer, “It is well spoken.“
Then Elijah says to the prophets of Baal, “Choose for yourselves one bull and prepare it first, for you are many, and call upon the name of your god, but put no fire to it.“

So they take the bull that is given them and prepare it and call upon the name of Baal from morning until noon, crying, “O Baal, answer us!“ But there is no voice, and no one answers. And they limp around the altar that they have made.
At noon Elijah mocks them, saying, “Cry aloud, for he is a god. Either he is musing, or he is relieving himself, or he is on a journey, or perhaps he is asleep and must be awakened.“
And they cry aloud and cut themselves after their custom with swords and lances, until the blood gushes out upon them.
And as midday passes, they rave on until the time of the offering of the oblation. But there is no voice. No one answers. No one pays attention.
Then Elijah says to all the people, “Come near to me.“ And all the people come near to him. And he repairs the altar of YHWH that had been thrown down.
Elijah takes twelve stones, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Jacob, to whom the word of YHWH came, saying, “Israel shall be your name.“
With the stones he builds an altar in the name of YHWH. And he makes a trench around the altar, as great as would contain two seahs of seed.
He arranges the wood and cuts the bull in pieces and lays it on the wood. He says, “Fill four jars with water and pour it on the burnt offering and on the wood.“
He says, “Do it a second time.“ And they do it a second time. He says, “Do it a third time.“ And they do it a third time.
The water runs around the altar and fills the trench also with water.

At the time of the offering of the oblation, Elijah the prophet comes near and says: “O YHWH, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, let it be known this day that you are God in Israel and that I am your servant and that I have done all these things at your word.
Answer me, YHWH, answer me — that this people may know that you, YHWH, are God, and that you have turned their hearts back.“
Then the fire of YHWH falls and consumes the burnt offering and the wood and the stones and the dust, and licks up the water that is in the trench.
When all the people see it, they fall on their faces and say, “YHWH, he is God! YHWH, he is God!“
Elijah says to them, “Seize the prophets of Baal; let not one of them escape.“ They seize them, and Elijah brings them down to the brook Kishon and slaughters them there.
Elijah says to Ahab, “Go up, eat and drink, for there is the sound of the rushing of rain.“
So Ahab goes up to eat and drink. And Elijah goes up to the top of Carmel. He bows himself down on the earth and puts his face between his knees.
He says to his servant, “Go up and look toward the sea.“ He goes up and looks and says, “There is nothing.“ He says, “Go again,“ seven times.
At the seventh time he says, “Behold, a little cloud like a man's hand is rising from the sea.“ Elijah says, “Go up and say to Ahab, 'Prepare your chariot and go down lest the rain stop you.'“
And in a little while the heavens grow black with clouds and wind, and there is a great rain. Ahab rides and goes to Jezreel.
And the hand of YHWH is on Elijah, and he girds up his loins and runs before Ahab to the entrance of Jezreel.
Ahab tells Jezebel all that Elijah has done — and all that he killed all the prophets with the sword.
Then Jezebel sends a messenger to Elijah, saying, “So may the gods do to me and more also, if I do not make your life as the life of one of them by this time tomorrow.“
Then he is afraid, and he rises and runs for his life. He comes to Beersheba, which belongs to Judah, and leaves his servant there.

But he himself goes a day's journey into the wilderness and comes and sits down under a broom tree. He asks that he might die, saying, “It is enough; now, O YHWH, take away my life, for I am no better than my fathers.“
He lies down and sleeps under a broom tree. And behold, an angel touches him and says to him, “Arise and eat.“
He looks, and behold, there is at his head a cake baked on hot stones and a jar of water. He eats and drinks and lies down again.
The angel of YHWH comes again a second time and touches him and says, “Arise and eat, for the journey is too great for you.“
He arises and eats and drinks, and goes in the strength of that food forty days and forty nights to Horeb, the mountain of God.
There he comes to a cave and lodges in it. And behold, the word of YHWH comes to him, and he says to him, “What are you doing here, Elijah?“

He says, “I have been very jealous for YHWH, the God of hosts. For the people of Israel have forsaken your covenant, thrown down your altars, and killed your prophets with the sword, and I, even I only, am left, and they seek my life, to take it away.“

He says, “Go out and stand on the mountain before YHWH.“ And behold, YHWH passes by, and a great and strong wind tears the mountains and breaks in pieces the rocks before YHWH — but YHWH is not in the wind. After the wind, an earthquake — but YHWH is not in the earthquake.
After the earthquake, a fire — but YHWH is not in the fire. And after the fire, a sound of thin silence.
When Elijah hears it, he wraps his face in his cloak and goes out and stands at the entrance of the cave. And behold, a voice comes to him and says, “What are you doing here, Elijah?“

He says, “I have been very jealous for YHWH, the God of hosts. For the people of Israel have forsaken your covenant, thrown down your altars, and killed your prophets with the sword, and I, even I only, am left, and they seek my life, to take it away.“
YHWH says to him, “Go, return on your way to the wilderness of Damascus. When you arrive, anoint Hazael to be king over Syria.
And Jehu the son of Nimshi you shall anoint to be king over Israel, and Elisha the son of Shaphat of Abel-meholah you shall anoint to be prophet in your place.
And the one who escapes from the sword of Hazael shall Jehu put to death, and the one who escapes from the sword of Jehu shall Elisha put to death.
Yet I will leave seven thousand in Israel — all the knees that have not bowed to Baal and every mouth that has not kissed him.“
So he departs from there and finds Elisha the son of Shaphat, who is plowing with twelve yoke of oxen in front of him. He passes by him and throws his cloak over him.
Elisha leaves the oxen and runs after Elijah and says, “Let me kiss my father and my mother, and then I will follow you.“ Elijah says to him, “Go back — for what have I done to you?“

Elisha turns back from him and takes the yoke of oxen and slaughters them and boiled their flesh with the yokes of the oxen and gave it to the people, and they ate. Then he arose and went after Elijah and assisted him.
Ben-hadad the king of Syria gathers all his army together — thirty-two kings are with him, and horses and chariots — and he goes up and besieges Samaria and fights against it.
He sends messengers into the city to Ahab king of Israel and says to him, “Thus says Ben-hadad:
Your silver and your gold are mine; your wives also and your best children are mine.“
The king of Israel answers, “As you say, my lord, O king, I am yours, and all that I have.“
The messengers come again and say, “Thus says Ben-hadad: 'I sent to you, saying, 'Your silver and your gold, your wives and your children, you shall deliver to me.
Nevertheless I will send my servants to you tomorrow about this time, and they shall search your house and the houses of your servants and lay hands on whatever pleases them and take it away.'“

Then the king of Israel calls all the elders of the land and says, “Mark, now, and see how this man is seeking trouble. For he sent to me for my wives and my children, my silver and my gold, and I did not refuse him.“
All the elders and all the people say to him, “Do not listen or consent.“
So he says to the messengers of Ben-hadad, “Tell my lord the king: All that you first demanded of your servant I will do, but this thing I cannot do.“ The messengers depart and bring him word again.
Ben-hadad sends to him and says, “The gods do so to me and more also, if the dust of Samaria shall suffice for handfuls for all the people who follow me.“
The king of Israel answers, “Tell him, 'Let not him who straps on his armor boast himself as he who takes it off.'“
When Ben-hadad hears this message — as he was drinking with the kings in the booths — he says to his servants, “Take your positions.“ And they take their positions against the city.

And behold, a prophet comes near to Ahab king of Israel and says, “Thus says YHWH: Have you seen all this great multitude? Behold, I will give it into your hand this day, and you shall know that I am YHWH.“
Ahab says, “By whom?“ He says, “Thus says YHWH: By the servants of the district governors.“ Then he says, “Who shall begin the battle?“ He answers, “You.“
Then he musters the servants of the district governors — two hundred and thirty-two. After them he musters all the people of Israel, seven thousand.
They go out at noon, while Ben-hadad was drinking himself drunk in the booths — he and the thirty-two kings who helped him.
The servants of the district governors go out first. Ben-hadad sends out scouts who report to him, “Men are coming out from Samaria.“
He says, “If they have come out for peace, take them alive. If they have come out for war, take them alive.“
So these go out from the city — the servants of the district governors and the army behind them.
Each strikes down his man. The Syrians flee, and Israel pursues them, but Ben-hadad king of Syria escapes on a horse with horsemen.
The king of Israel goes out and strikes the horses and chariots and strikes the Syrians with a great blow.
Then the prophet comes near to the king of Israel and says to him, “Come, strengthen yourself, and consider well what you have to do, for in the spring the king of Syria will come up against you.“

The servants of the king of Syria say to him, “Their gods are gods of the hills, and so they were stronger than we. But let us fight against them in the plain, and surely we shall be stronger than they.
And do this: remove the kings, each from his post, and put commanders in their places.

Muster an army like the army you have lost, horse for horse, and chariot for chariot. Then we will fight against them in the plain, and surely we shall be stronger than they.“ He listens to their voice and does so.
In the spring, Ben-hadad musters the Syrians and goes up to Aphek to fight against Israel.
And the people of Israel are mustered and were provisioned and go against them. The people of Israel encamp before them like two little flocks of goats, but the Syrians fill the country.

A man of God comes near and says to the king of Israel, “Thus says YHWH: Because the Syrians have said, 'YHWH is a god of the hills but he is not a god of the valleys,' therefore I will give all this great multitude into your hand, and you shall know that I am YHWH.“
They encamp opposite one another for seven days. Then on the seventh day the battle is joined. And the people of Israel strike down of the Syrians a hundred thousand foot soldiers in one day.
The rest flee into the city of Aphek, and the wall falls upon twenty-seven thousand men who are left. Ben-hadad also flees and enters an inner chamber in the city.

His servants say to him, “Behold now, we have heard that the kings of the house of Israel are merciful kings. Let us put sackcloth on our loins and ropes on our heads and go out to the king of Israel. Perhaps he will spare your life.“

So they tie sackcloth on their loins and put ropes on their heads and come to the king of Israel and say, “Your servant Ben-hadad says, 'Please let me live.'“ Ahab says, “Does he still live? He is my brother.“

Now the men were watching for a sign, and they quickly picked up on it and said, “Yes, Ben-hadad is your brother.“ He says, “Go and bring him.“ So Ben-hadad comes out to him, and he causes him to come up into the chariot.

Ben-hadad says to him, “The cities that my father took from your father I will restore, and you may establish markets for yourself in Damascus, as my father did in Samaria.“ Ahab says, “I will let you go on these terms.“ So he makes a covenant with him and lets him go.
A certain man of the sons of the prophets says to his fellow at the command of YHWH, “Strike me, please.“ But the man refuses to strike him.
Then he says to him, “Because you have not obeyed the voice of YHWH, as soon as you have left me a lion will strike you down.“ And as soon as he had left him a lion meets him and strikes him down.
Then he finds another man and says, “Strike me, please.“ And the man strikes him — he strikes him and wounds him.
So the prophet goes away and waits for the king by the way, disguising himself with a bandage over his eyes.

As the king passes, he cries to the king and says, “Your servant went out into the midst of the battle, and behold, a soldier turned and brought a man to me and said, 'Guard this man; if by any means he is missing, your life shall be for his life, or you shall pay a talent of silver.'
And as your servant was busy here and there, he was gone.“ The king of Israel says to him, “So shall your judgment be; you yourself have decided it.“
Then he hurries to take the bandage away from his eyes, and the king of Israel recognizes him as one of the prophets.
He says to him, “Thus says YHWH: 'Because you have let go out of your hand the man whom I had devoted to destruction, therefore your life shall go for his life, and your people for his people.'“
The king of Israel goes to his house resentful and sullen and comes to Samaria.
Now Naboth the Jezreelite has a vineyard in Jezreel, beside the palace of Ahab king of Samaria.

Ahab says to Naboth, “Give me your vineyard, that I may have it for a vegetable garden, because it is near my house, and I will give you a better vineyard for it; or, if it seems good to you, I will give you its value in money.“
But Naboth says to Ahab, “YHWH forbid that I should give you the inheritance of my fathers.“

Ahab goes into his house resentful and sullen because of what Naboth the Jezreelite has said to him — for he said, “I will not give you the inheritance of my fathers.“ He lies down on his bed and turns away his face and will not eat.
His wife Jezebel comes to him and says to him, “Why is your spirit so resentful that you eat no food?“

He says to her, “Because I spoke to Naboth the Jezreelite and said to him, 'Give me your vineyard for money, or else, if you please, I will give you another vineyard for it.' And he answered, 'I will not give you my vineyard.'“
Jezebel his wife says to him, “Do you now govern Israel? Arise and eat bread and let your heart be cheerful. I will give you the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite.“
So she writes letters in Ahab's name and seals them with his seal and sends them to the elders and the leaders who lived with Naboth in his city.
She writes in the letters: “Proclaim a fast, and set Naboth at the head of the people.
And set two worthless men opposite him and let them bring a charge against him, saying, 'You have cursed God and the king.' Then take him out and stone him to death.“
The men of his city — the elders and the leaders who lived in his city — do as Jezebel has sent word to them. As it is written in the letters she sent to them,
they proclaim a fast and set Naboth at the head of the people.

Then the two worthless men come in and sit opposite him. And the worthless men bring a charge against Naboth in the presence of the people, saying, “Naboth cursed God and the king.“ So they take him outside the city and stone him to death with stones.
Then they send to Jezebel, saying, “Naboth has been stoned; he is dead.“

As soon as Jezebel hears that Naboth had been stoned and is dead, she says to Ahab, “Arise, take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, which he refused to give you for money, for Naboth is not alive, but dead.“
As soon as Ahab hears that Naboth is dead, Ahab rises to go down to the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, to take possession of it.
Then the word of YHWH comes to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,
“Arise, go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who is in Samaria; behold, he is in the vineyard of Naboth, where he has gone to take possession.

And you shall say to him: 'Thus says YHWH: Have you killed and also taken possession?' And you shall say to him: 'Thus says YHWH: In the place where dogs licked up the blood of Naboth shall dogs lick your blood — even yours.'“
Ahab says to Elijah, “Have you found me, O my enemy?“ Elijah answers, “I have found you, because you have sold yourself to do what is evil in the sight of YHWH.
Behold, I will bring disaster upon you. I will utterly burn you up and will cut off from Ahab every male, bond or free, in Israel.

And I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha the son of Ahijah, for the anger to which you have provoked me, and because you have made Israel to sin.
And of Jezebel YHWH also said, 'The dogs shall eat Jezebel within the walls of Jezreel.'
Anyone belonging to Ahab who dies in the city the dogs shall eat, and anyone of his who dies in the open country the birds of the heavens shall eat.“
There was none who sold himself to do what was evil in the sight of YHWH like Ahab, whom Jezebel his wife incited.
He acted very abominably in going after idols, as the Amorites had done, whom YHWH cast out before the people of Israel.
When Ahab hears these words, he tears his clothes and puts sackcloth on his flesh and fasts and lies in sackcloth and goes about dejectedly.
And the word of YHWH comes to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,

“Have you seen how Ahab has humbled himself before me? Because he has humbled himself before me, I will not bring the disaster in his days; but in his son's days I will bring the disaster upon his house.“
For three years Syria and Israel continue without war.
But in the third year Jehoshaphat the king of Judah comes down to the king of Israel.
The king of Israel says to his servants, “Do you know that Ramoth-gilead belongs to us, and we keep quiet and do not take it out of the hand of the king of Syria?“
He says to Jehoshaphat, “Will you go with me to battle at Ramoth-gilead?“ Jehoshaphat says to the king of Israel, “I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses.“
Jehoshaphat also says to the king of Israel, “Inquire first for the word of YHWH.“

Then the king of Israel gathers the prophets together — about four hundred men — and says to them, “Shall I go to battle against Ramoth-gilead, or shall I refrain?“ They say, “Go up, for the Lord will give it into the hand of the king.“
But Jehoshaphat says, “Is there not here another prophet of YHWH of whom we may inquire?“

The king of Israel says to Jehoshaphat, “There is yet one man by whom we may inquire of YHWH, Micaiah the son of Imlah, but I hate him, for he never prophesies good concerning me, but evil.“ Jehoshaphat says, “Let not the king say so.“
Then the king of Israel summons an officer and says, “Bring quickly Micaiah the son of Imlah.“

Now the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat the king of Judah are sitting on their thrones, arrayed in their robes, at the threshing floor at the entrance of the gate of Samaria, and all the prophets are prophesying before them.
Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah makes for himself horns of iron and says, “Thus says YHWH: 'With these you shall push the Syrians until they are destroyed.'“
And all the prophets prophesy so and say, “Go up to Ramoth-gilead and triumph; YHWH will give it into the hand of the king.“

The messenger who went to summon Micaiah says to him, “Behold, the words of the prophets with one accord are favorable to the king. Let your word be like the word of one of them, and speak favorably.“
But Micaiah says, “As YHWH lives, what YHWH says to me, that I will speak.“

When he comes to the king, the king says to him, “Micaiah, shall we go to Ramoth-gilead to battle, or shall we refrain?“ He answers him, “Go up and triumph; YHWH will give it into the hand of the king.“
The king says to him, “How many times shall I make you swear that you speak nothing but the truth to me in the name of YHWH?“
Micaiah says, “I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains, as sheep that have no shepherd. YHWH said, 'These have no master; let each return to his home in peace.'“
The king of Israel says to Jehoshaphat, “Did I not tell you that he would not prophesy good concerning me, but evil?“
Micaiah says, “Therefore hear the word of YHWH: I saw YHWH sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven standing beside him on his right hand and on his left.
YHWH says, 'Who will entice Ahab so that he will go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead?' One says one thing, and another says another.
Then a spirit comes forward and stands before YHWH, saying, 'I will entice him.'
YHWH says to him, 'By what means?' He says, 'I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.' YHWH says, 'You are to entice him, and you shall succeed. Go out and do so.'
And now behold, YHWH has put a lying spirit in the mouth of all these your prophets; YHWH has declared disaster for you.“
Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah comes near and strikes Micaiah on the cheek and says, “How did the Spirit of YHWH go from me to speak to you?“
Micaiah says, “Behold, you shall see on that day when you go into an inner chamber to hide yourself.“
The king of Israel says, “Seize Micaiah and take him back to Amon the governor of the city and to Joash the king's son,
and say, 'Thus says the king, “Put this fellow in prison and feed him with meager rations of bread and water until I come in peace.“'
Micaiah says, “If you return in peace, YHWH has not spoken by me.“ And he says, “Hear, all you peoples!“
So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat the king of Judah go up to Ramoth-gilead.
The king of Israel says to Jehoshaphat, “I will disguise myself and go into battle, but you wear your robes.“ So the king of Israel disguises himself and goes into battle.
Now the king of Syria had commanded the thirty-two captains of his chariots, “Fight with neither small nor great, but only with the king of Israel.“
When the captains of the chariots see Jehoshaphat, they say, “It is surely the king of Israel.“ So they turn to fight against him. Jehoshaphat cries out.
When the captains of the chariots see that it is not the king of Israel, they turn back from pursuing him.

But a certain man draws his bow at random and strikes the king of Israel between the scale armor and the breastplate. Ahab says to the driver of his chariot, “Turn around and carry me out of the battle, for I am wounded.“
The battle continues that day, and the king is propped up in his chariot facing the Syrians, until at evening he dies. The blood from his wound flows into the bottom of the chariot.
About sunset a cry goes through the army, “Every man to his city, and every man to his country!“
So the king dies and is brought to Samaria, and they bury the king in Samaria.
They wash the chariot by the pool of Samaria, and the dogs lick up his blood, and the prostitutes wash themselves in it, according to the word of YHWH that he had spoken.
Now the rest of the acts of Ahab and all that he did, the ivory house that he built and all the cities that he built — are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
So Ahab lies down with his fathers, and Ahaziah his son reigns in his place.
Jehoshaphat the son of Asa begins to reign over Judah in the fourth year of Ahab king of Israel.
Jehoshaphat is thirty-five years old when he begins to reign and he reigns twenty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother's name is Azubah the daughter of Shilhi.

He walks in all the way of Asa his father. He does not turn aside from it, doing what is right in the sight of YHWH. Yet the high places are not taken away, and the people still sacrifice and make offerings on the high places.
Jehoshaphat also makes peace with the king of Israel.
Now the rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat and his might that he showed and how he warred — are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
He exterminated from the land the remnant of the male cult prostitutes who remained in the days of his father Asa.
There was no king in Edom; a deputy was king.
Jehoshaphat makes ships of Tarshish to go to Ophir for gold, but they do not go, for the ships are wrecked at Ezion-geber.
Then Ahaziah the son of Ahab says to Jehoshaphat, “Let my servants go with your servants in the ships,“ but Jehoshaphat is not willing.
Jehoshaphat lies down with his fathers and is buried with his fathers in the city of David his father. Jehoram his son reigns in his place.
Ahaziah the son of Ahab begins to reign over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigns two years over Israel.
He does what is evil in the sight of YHWH and walks in the way of his father and in the way of his mother and in the way of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin.
He serves Baal and worships him and provokes YHWH, the God of Israel, to anger in every way that his father had done.
After the death of Ahab, Moab rebels against Israel.

Ahaziah falls through the lattice in his upper chamber in Samaria and is injured. He sends messengers and says to them, "Go, inquire of Baal-zebub the god of Ekron whether I shall recover from this injury."

But the angel of YHWH says to Elijah the Tishbite, "Arise, go up to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria and say to them, 'Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are going to inquire of Baal-zebub the god of Ekron?
Now therefore, thus says YHWH: You shall not come down from the bed to which you have gone up, but you shall surely die.'" So Elijah goes.
The messengers return to the king, and he says to them, "Why have you returned?"

They say to him, "There came a man to meet us, and he said to us, 'Go back to the king who sent you, and say to him, Thus says YHWH: Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are sending to inquire of Baal-zebub the god of Ekron? Therefore you shall not come down from the bed to which you have gone up, but you shall surely die.'"
He says to them, "What kind of man was he who came to meet you and spoke these words to you?"
They answer him, "He wore a garment of hair, with a belt of leather around his waist." He says, "It is Elijah the Tishbite."
Then the king sends to him a captain of fifty men with his fifty. He goes up to Elijah, who is sitting on the top of a hill, and says to him, "O man of God, the king says, 'Come down.'"
But Elijah answers the captain of fifty, "If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty." Then fire comes down from heaven and consumes him and his fifty.
The king sends to him another captain of fifty men with his fifty. He speaks to him and says, "O man of God, this is the king's order, 'Come down quickly.'"
But Elijah answers them, "If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty." Then the fire of God comes down from heaven and consumes him and his fifty.

Again the king sends the captain of a third fifty with his fifty. The third captain of fifty goes up and comes and falls on his knees before Elijah and entreats him: "O man of God, please let my life — and the life of these fifty servants of yours — be precious in your sight.
Behold, fire came down from heaven and consumed the two former captains of fifty men with their fifties, but now let my life be precious in your sight."
The angel of YHWH says to Elijah, "Go down with him; do not be afraid of him." So he rises and goes down with him to the king.

He says to him, "Thus says YHWH: Because you have sent messengers to inquire of Baal-zebub the god of Ekron — is it because there is no God in Israel to inquire of his word? — therefore you shall not come down from the bed to which you have gone up, but you shall surely die."
So he dies according to the word of YHWH that Elijah had spoken. Jehoram begins to reign in his place, in the second year of Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, because Ahaziah has no son.
Now the rest of the acts of Ahaziah that he did — are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
Now when YHWH was about to take Elijah up to heaven by a whirlwind, Elijah and Elisha set out from Gilgal.
Elijah says to Elisha, "Please stay here, for YHWH has sent me as far as Bethel." But Elisha says, "As YHWH lives and as you yourself live, I will not leave you." So they go down to Bethel.
The sons of the prophets who are in Bethel come out to Elisha and say to him, "Do you know that today YHWH will take away your master from over you?" He says, "Yes, I know it; keep quiet."
Elijah says to him, "Elisha, please stay here, for YHWH has sent me to Jericho." But he says, "As YHWH lives and as you yourself live, I will not leave you." So they come to Jericho.
The sons of the prophets who are at Jericho draw near to Elisha and say to him, "Do you know that today YHWH will take away your master from over you?" He says, "Yes, I know it; keep quiet."
Then Elijah says to him, "Please stay here, for YHWH has sent me to the Jordan." But he says, "As YHWH lives and as you yourself live, I will not leave you." So the two of them go on.
Fifty men of the sons of the prophets also go and stand at some distance from them, as they both stand by the Jordan.
Then Elijah takes his cloak and rolls it up and strikes the water, and the water is parted to the one side and to the other, until the two of them could go over on dry ground.
When they have crossed over, Elijah says to Elisha, "Ask what I shall do for you, before I am taken from you." Elisha says, "Please let a double portion of your spirit be upon me."
Elijah says, "You have asked a hard thing. Yet if you see me as I am being taken from you, it shall be so for you, but if you do not see me, it shall not be so."
And as they still went on and talked, behold, a chariot of fire and horses of fire separate the two of them. And Elijah goes up by a whirlwind into heaven.
Elisha sees it and cries, "My father, my father! The chariots of Israel and its horsemen!" And he sees him no more. Then he takes hold of his own clothes and tears them in two pieces.
He takes up the cloak of Elijah that has fallen from him and goes back and stands on the bank of the Jordan.

Then he takes the cloak of Elijah that has fallen from him and strikes the water, saying, "Where is YHWH, the God of Elijah?" And when he has struck the water, the water is parted to the one side and to the other, and Elisha goes over.
Now when the sons of the prophets who are at Jericho see him opposite them, they say, "The spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha." And they come to meet him and bow to the ground before him.

They say to him, "Behold now, there are with your servants fifty strong men. Please let them go and seek your master. Perhaps the Spirit of YHWH has cast him onto some mountain or into some valley." He says, "You shall not send."
But when they urge him until he is embarrassed, he says, "Send." They send fifty men. For three days they seek but do not find him.
When they come back to him — for he stayed at Jericho — he says to them, "Did I not say to you, 'Do not go'?"
Now the men of the city say to Elisha, "Behold, the situation of this city is pleasant, as my lord sees, but the water is bad and the land is unfruitful."
He says, "Bring me a new bowl, and put salt in it." So they bring it to him.
Then he goes to the spring of water and throws salt in it and says, "Thus says YHWH: I have healed this water; from now on neither death nor miscarriage shall come from it."
So the water is healed to this day, according to the word that Elisha spoke.
From there he goes up to Bethel. While he is going up on the way, some small boys come out of the city and jeer at him, saying, "Go up, you baldhead! Go up, you baldhead!"
He turns around and looks at them and curses them in the name of YHWH. Two she-bears come out of the woods and tear forty-two of the boys.
From there he goes on to Mount Carmel, and from there he returns to Samaria.
In the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, Jehoram the son of Ahab begins to reign over Israel in Samaria and reigns twelve years.
He does what is evil in the sight of YHWH, though not like his father and mother, for he puts away the pillar of Baal that his father made.
Nevertheless he clings to the sin of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, which he made Israel to sin; he does not depart from it.
Now Mesha king of Moab was a sheep breeder, and he used to deliver to the king of Israel a hundred thousand lambs and the wool of a hundred thousand rams.
But when Ahab died, the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.
King Jehoram marches out of Samaria at that time and musters all Israel.

He goes and sends to Jehoshaphat king of Judah: "The king of Moab has rebelled against me. Will you go with me to battle against Moab?" He says, "I will go. I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses."
Then he says, "By which way shall we go up?" Jehoshaphat answers, "By the way of the wilderness of Edom."
So the king of Israel, the king of Judah, and the king of Edom set out. After making a circuit of seven days' journey, there is no water for the army or for the animals that follow them.
The king of Israel says, "Alas! YHWH has called these three kings together only to give them into the hand of Moab."

But Jehoshaphat says, "Is there no prophet of YHWH here, through whom we may inquire of YHWH?" One of the king of Israel's servants answers, "Elisha the son of Shaphat is here — who poured water on the hands of Elijah."
Jehoshaphat says, "The word of YHWH is with him." So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat and the king of Edom go down to him.

Elisha says to the king of Israel, "What have I to do with you? Go to the prophets of your father and to the prophets of your mother." The king of Israel says to him, "No; it is YHWH who has called these three kings together to give them into the hand of Moab."
Elisha says, "As YHWH of hosts lives, before whom I stand, were it not that I have regard for Jehoshaphat the king of Judah, I would neither look at you nor see you.
But now bring me a musician." And when the musician plays, the hand of YHWH comes upon him.
He says, "Thus says YHWH: I will make this dry streambed full of pools.
For thus says YHWH: You shall not see wind or rain, yet that streambed shall be filled with water, so that you shall drink, you, your livestock, and your animals."
"This is a light thing in the sight of YHWH. He will also give Moab into your hand.
You shall attack every fortified city and every choice city, and shall fell every good tree and stop up all springs of water and ruin every good piece of land with stones."
The next morning, about the time of offering the sacrifice, behold, water came from the direction of Edom, until the country was filled with water.
When all the Moabites hear that the kings have come up to fight against them, all who are able to put on armor, from the youngest to the oldest, are called out and are drawn up at the border.
When they rise early in the morning and the sun shines on the water, the Moabites see the water opposite them as red as blood.
They say, "This is blood; the kings have surely fought together and struck one another down. Now then, Moab, to the spoil!"
But when they come to the camp of Israel, the Israelites rise and strike the Moabites, till they flee before them. And they strike Moab repeatedly.

They overthrow the cities, and on every good piece of land every man throws a stone until it is covered. They stop up every spring of water and fell every good tree, until only its stones are left in Kir-hareseth. And the slingers surround and attack it.
When the king of Moab sees that the battle is going against him, he takes with him seven hundred swordsmen to break through, opposite the king of Edom, but they cannot.
Then he takes his oldest son who was to reign in his place and offers him for a burnt offering on the wall. And great wrath comes against Israel. They withdraw from him and return to their own land.

Now the wife of one of the sons of the prophets cries to Elisha, "Your servant my husband is dead, and you know that your servant feared YHWH, but the creditor has come to take my two children to be his slaves."
Elisha says to her, "What shall I do for you? Tell me; what do you have in the house?" She says, "Your servant has nothing in the house except a jar of oil."
He says, "Go outside, borrow vessels from all your neighbors, empty vessels and not too few.
Then go in and shut the door behind yourself and your sons and pour into all these vessels. And when one is full, set it aside."
So she goes from him and shuts the door behind herself and her sons. And they keep bringing vessels to her, and she keeps pouring.
When the vessels are full, she says to her son, "Bring me another vessel." But he says to her, "There is not another." And the oil stops.
She comes and tells the man of God, and he says, "Go, sell the oil and pay your debt, and you and your sons can live on the rest."
One day Elisha goes on to Shunem, where a wealthy woman lives, who urges him to eat some food. And whenever he passes that way, he turns in there to eat food.
She says to her husband, "Behold now, I know that this is a holy man of God who is continually passing our way.
Let us make a small room on the roof with walls and put there for him a bed, a table, a chair, and a lamp, so that whenever he comes to us, he can go in there."
One day he comes there and turns into the chamber and rests there.
He says to Gehazi his servant, "Call this Shunammite." When he calls her, she stands before him.

He says to him, "Say now to her, 'See, you have taken all this trouble for us; what is to be done for you? Would you have a word spoken on your behalf to the king or to the commander of the army?'" She answers, "I dwell among my own people."
He says, "What then is to be done for her?" Gehazi answers, "Well, she has no son, and her husband is old."
He says, "Call her." And when he calls her, she stands in the doorway.
He says, "At this season, about this time next year, you shall embrace a son." She says, "No, my lord, O man of God; do not lie to your servant."
But the woman conceives and bears a son about that time the following spring, as Elisha had said to her.
When the child has grown, he goes out one day to his father among the reapers.
He says to his father, "Oh, my head, my head!" The father says to his servant, "Carry him to his mother."
When he has lifted him and brought him to his mother, the child sits on her lap until noon, and then he dies.
She goes up and lays him on the bed of the man of God and shuts the door behind him and goes out.
She calls to her husband and says, "Send me one of the servants and one of the donkeys, that I may quickly go to the man of God and come back again."
He says, "Why will you go to him today? It is neither new moon nor Sabbath." She says, "All is well."
Then she saddles the donkey and says to her servant, "Urge the animal on; do not slow down for me unless I tell you."
So she sets out and comes to the man of God at Mount Carmel. When the man of God sees her coming, he says to Gehazi his servant, "Look, there is the Shunammite.
Run at once to meet her and say to her, 'Is all well with you? Is all well with your husband? Is all well with the child?'" She answers, "All is well."

When she comes to the mountain to the man of God, she catches hold of his feet. Gehazi comes to push her away. But the man of God says, "Leave her alone, for she is in bitter distress, and YHWH has hidden it from me and has not told me."
She says, "Did I ask my lord for a son? Did I not say, 'Do not deceive me'?"

He says to Gehazi, "Tie up your garment and take my staff in your hand and go. If you meet anyone, do not greet him, and if anyone greets you, do not reply. And lay my staff on the face of the child."
Then the mother of the child says, "As YHWH lives and as you yourself live, I will not leave you." So he rises and follows her.
Gehazi goes on ahead and lays the staff on the face of the child, but there is no sound or sign of life. Therefore he returns to meet Elisha and tells him, "The child has not awakened."
When Elisha comes into the house, he sees the child lying dead on his bed.
So he goes in and shuts the door behind the two of them and prays to YHWH.
Then he goes up and lies on the child, putting his mouth on his mouth, his eyes on his eyes, and his hands on his hands. As he stretches himself upon him, the flesh of the child becomes warm.
Then he gets up again and walks once back and forth in the house, and goes up and stretches himself upon him. The child sneezes seven times, and the child opens his eyes.
He calls Gehazi and says, "Call this Shunammite." So he calls her. And when she comes to him, he says, "Pick up your son."
She comes and falls at his feet, bowing to the ground. Then she picks up her son and goes out.
Elisha returns to Gilgal. There is a famine in the land. As the sons of the prophets are sitting before him, he says to his servant, "Set on the large pot and boil stew for the sons of the prophets."
One of them goes out into the field to gather herbs and finds a wild vine and gathers from it his lap full of wild gourds and comes and cuts them into the pot of stew, not knowing what they were.
They pour it out for the men to eat. But as they eat, they cry out, "O man of God, there is death in the pot!" And they cannot eat it.
He says, "Then bring flour." And he throws it into the pot and says, "Pour it out for the men so they may eat." And there is nothing harmful in the pot.
A man comes from Baal-shalishah, bringing the man of God bread of the firstfruits — twenty loaves of barley and fresh ears of grain in his sack. Elisha says, "Give to the men so they may eat."
But his servant says, "How shall I set this before a hundred men?" He says, "Give them to the men so they may eat, for thus says YHWH: 'They shall eat and have some left.'"
So he sets it before them and they eat and have some left, according to the word of YHWH.
Naaman, commander of the army of the king of Syria, is a great man with his master and in high favor, because by him YHWH had given victory to Syria. He is a mighty man of valor, but he is a leper.
Now the Syrians on one of their raids had carried off a little girl from the land of Israel, and she works in the service of Naaman's wife.
She says to her mistress, "Would that my lord were with the prophet who is in Samaria! He would cure him of his leprosy."
So Naaman goes in and tells his lord, "Thus and so spoke the girl from the land of Israel."
The king of Syria says, "Go now, and I will send a letter to the king of Israel." He departs, taking with him ten talents of silver, six thousand shekels of gold, and ten changes of clothing.
He brings the letter to the king of Israel, which reads, "When this letter reaches you, know that I have sent to you Naaman my servant, that you may cure him of his leprosy."

When the king of Israel reads the letter, he tears his clothes and says, "Am I God, to kill and to make alive, that this man sends word to me to cure a man of his leprosy? Only consider, and see how he is seeking a quarrel with me."

But when Elisha the man of God hears that the king of Israel has torn his clothes, he sends to the king, saying, "Why have you torn your clothes? Let him come now to me, that he may know there is a prophet in Israel."
So Naaman comes with his horses and chariots and stands at the door of Elisha's house.
Elisha sends a messenger to him, saying, "Go and wash in the Jordan seven times, and your flesh shall be restored, and you shall be clean."
But Naaman is angry and goes away, saying, "Behold, I thought that he would surely come out to me and stand and call upon the name of YHWH his God and wave his hand over the place and cure the leper.
Are not Abana and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? Could I not wash in them and be clean?" So he turns and goes away in a rage.

But his servants come near and say to him, "My father, if the prophet had commanded you to do some great thing, would you not have done it? How much more then, when he says to you, 'Wash and be clean'?"
So he goes down and dips himself seven times in the Jordan, according to the word of the man of God, and his flesh is restored like the flesh of a little child, and he is clean.

Then he returns to the man of God, he and all his company, and he comes and stands before him. He says, "Behold, I know that there is no God in all the earth but in Israel; so accept now a present from your servant."
But he says, "As YHWH lives, before whom I stand, I will receive nothing." Naaman urges him to take it, but he refuses.
Then Naaman says, "If not, please let there be given to your servant two mule-loads of earth, for from now on your servant will not offer burnt offering or sacrifice to any god but YHWH.

In this matter may YHWH pardon your servant: when my master goes into the house of Rimmon to worship there, leaning on my arm, and I bow myself in the house of Rimmon — when I bow myself in the house of Rimmon, YHWH pardon your servant in this matter."
He says to him, "Go in peace." But when Naaman had gone from him a short distance,

Gehazi, the servant of Elisha the man of God, says, "See, my master has spared this Naaman the Syrian, in not accepting from his hand what he brought. As YHWH lives, I will run after him and get something from him."
So Gehazi hurries after Naaman. When Naaman sees someone running after him, he steps down from the chariot to meet him and says, "Is all well?"

He says, "All is well. My master has sent me to say, 'There have just come to me from the hill country of Ephraim two young men of the sons of the prophets. Please give them a talent of silver and two changes of clothing.'"

Naaman says, "Be pleased to accept two talents." And he urges him and ties up two talents of silver in two bags, with two changes of clothing, and lays them on two of his servants. And they carry them before Gehazi.
When he comes to the hill, he takes them from their hand and puts them in the house. He sends the men away, and they depart.
He goes in and stands before his master. Elisha says to him, "Where have you been, Gehazi?" He says, "Your servant went nowhere."

But he says to him, "Did not my heart go when the man turned from his chariot to meet you? Was it a time to accept money and garments, olive orchards and vineyards, sheep and oxen, male servants and female servants?
Therefore the leprosy of Naaman shall cling to you and to your descendants forever." So he goes out from his presence a leper, like snow.
Now the sons of the prophets say to Elisha, "See, the place where we dwell under your charge is too small for us.
Let us go to the Jordan and each of us get there a log, and let us make a place for us to dwell there." He says, "Go."
One of them says, "Be pleased to go with your servants." He answers, "I will go."
So he goes with them. And when they come to the Jordan, they cut down trees.
But as one was felling a log, his axehead falls into the water. He cries out, "Alas, my master! It was borrowed."
The man of God says, "Where did it fall?" He shows him the place. He cuts off a stick and throws it in there and makes the iron float.
He says, "Take it up." So he reaches out his hand and takes it.
Once when the king of Syria was warring against Israel, he takes counsel with his servants, saying, "At such and such a place shall be my camp."
But the man of God sends word to the king of Israel: "Beware that you do not pass this place, for the Syrians are going down there."
The king of Israel sends to the place about which the man of God told him — and thus he warned him — so that he was on his guard there, more than once or twice.
The mind of the king of Syria is greatly troubled because of this thing. He calls his servants and says to them, "Will you not show me who of us is for the king of Israel?"
One of his servants says, "None, my lord, O king; but Elisha, the prophet who is in Israel, tells the king of Israel the words that you speak in your bedroom."
"Go and see where he is," the king says, "that I may send and seize him." It is told him: "He is in Dothan."
So he sends horses and chariots and a great army there, and they come by night and surround the city.
When the servant of the man of God rises early in the morning and goes out, behold, an army with horses and chariots is all around the city. His servant says, "Alas, my master! What shall we do?"
He says, "Do not be afraid, for those who are with us are more than those who are with them."

Then Elisha prays and says, "O YHWH, please open his eyes that he may see." So YHWH opens the eyes of the young man, and he sees, and behold, the mountain is full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.
When the Syrians come down against him, Elisha prays to YHWH and says, "Please strike this people with blindness." So he strikes them with blindness in accordance with the prayer of Elisha.
Elisha says to them, "This is not the way, and this is not the city. Follow me, and I will bring you to the man whom you seek." And he leads them to Samaria.
As soon as they enter Samaria, Elisha says, "O YHWH, open the eyes of these men, that they may see." So YHWH opens their eyes and they see, and behold, they are in the middle of Samaria.
As soon as the king of Israel sees them, he says to Elisha, "My father, shall I strike them down? Shall I strike them down?"

He answers, "You shall not strike them down. Would you strike down those whom you have taken captive with your sword and with your bow? Set bread and water before them, that they may eat and drink and go to their master."
So he prepares a great feast for them. And when they have eaten and drunk, he sends them away and they go to their master. And the Syrians do not come again on raids into the land of Israel.
Afterward Ben-hadad king of Syria musters his entire army and marches up and besieges Samaria.
There is a great famine in Samaria, as they besiege it, until a donkey's head sells for eighty shekels of silver and a quarter of a kab of dove's dung for five shekels.
As the king of Israel is passing by on the wall, a woman cries out to him, "Help, my lord, O king!"
He says, "If YHWH will not help you, how shall I help you? From the threshing floor, or from the winepress?"
The king asks her, "What is your trouble?" She answers, "This woman said to me, 'Give your son, that we may eat him today, and we will eat my son tomorrow.'
So we boiled my son and ate him. And I said to her the next day, 'Give your son, that we may eat him.' But she has hidden her son."
When the king hears the words of the woman, he tears his clothes — as he passed by on the wall, the people look and behold, he has sackcloth beneath, against his body.
He says, "God do so to me and more also, if the head of Elisha the son of Shaphat remains on his shoulders today."

Elisha is sitting in his house and the elders are sitting with him. Now the king sends a man from his presence, but before the messenger arrives Elisha says to the elders, "Do you see how this murderer has sent to take off my head? Look, when the messenger comes, shut the door and hold the door fast against him. Is not the sound of his master's feet behind him?"
While he is still speaking with them, the messenger comes down to him and says, "This trouble is from YHWH! Why should I wait for YHWH any longer?"
But Elisha says, "Hear the word of YHWH: thus says YHWH, Tomorrow about this time a seah of fine flour shall be sold for a shekel, and two seahs of barley for a shekel, at the gate of Samaria."

Then the captain on whose hand the king leaned says to the man of God, "If YHWH himself should make windows in heaven, could this thing be?" But he says, "You shall see it with your own eyes, but you shall not eat of it."
Now there are four men who are lepers at the entrance to the gate. They say to one another, "Why are we sitting here until we die?

If we say, 'Let us enter the city,' the famine is in the city, and we shall die there. And if we sit here, we die also. So now come, let us go over to the camp of the Syrians. If they spare our lives we shall live, and if they kill us we shall but die."
So they arise at twilight to go to the camp of the Syrians. But when they come to the edge of the Syrian camp, there is no one there.

For YHWH had made the army of the Syrians hear the sound of chariots and of horses, the sound of a great army, so that they say to one another, "Behold, the king of Israel has hired against us the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Egypt to come against us."
So they flee away in the twilight and abandon their tents, their horses, and their donkeys, leaving the camp as it is, and flee for their lives.

When these lepers come to the edge of the camp, they go into a tent and eat and drink, and carry off silver and gold and clothing and go and hide them. Then they come back and enter another tent and carry off things from it and go and hide them.

Then they say to one another, "We are not doing right. This day is a day of good news. If we are silent and wait until the morning light, punishment will overtake us. Now therefore come; let us go and tell the king's household."

So they come and call to the gatekeepers of the city and tell them, "We came to the camp of the Syrians, and behold, there was no one to be seen or heard there, nothing but horses tied and donkeys tied and the tents as they were."
Then the gatekeepers call out and it is told within the king's household.

The king rises in the night and says to his servants, "I will tell you what the Syrians have done to us. They know that we are hungry. Therefore they have gone out of the camp to hide themselves in the open country, thinking, 'When they come out of the city, we shall take them alive and get into the city.'"

One of his servants answers, "Let some men take five of the remaining horses — seeing that those who are left here will fare like the whole multitude of Israel who have already perished — let us send and see."
So they take two horsemen, and the king sends them after the Syrian army, saying, "Go and see."

So they go after them as far as the Jordan, and behold, all the way is littered with garments and equipment that the Syrians had thrown away in their haste. And the messengers return and tell the king.
Then the people go out and plunder the camp of the Syrians. So a seah of fine flour was sold for a shekel and two seahs of barley for a shekel, according to the word of YHWH.

Now the king had appointed the captain on whose hand he leaned to have charge of the gate. And the people trampled him in the gate, so that he dies, as the man of God had said when the king came down to him.
For when the man of God had said to the king, "Two seahs of barley shall be sold for a shekel, and a seah of fine flour for a shekel, about this time tomorrow at the gate of Samaria,"
