the captain had answered the man of God, "If YHWH himself should make windows in heaven, could such a thing be?" And he had said, "You shall see it with your own eyes, but you shall not eat of it."
And so it happened to him, for the people trampled him in the gate and he dies.

Now Elisha has said to the woman whose son he had restored to life, "Arise and depart with your household and sojourn wherever you can, for YHWH has called for a famine, and it will come upon the land for seven years."
So the woman arises and does according to the word of the man of God. She goes with her household and sojourns in the land of the Philistines seven years.
At the end of the seven years, when the woman returns from the land of the Philistines, she goes to appeal to the king for her house and her land.
Now the king is talking with Gehazi the servant of the man of God, saying, "Tell me all the great things Elisha has done."

And while he is telling the king how Elisha had restored the dead to life, behold, the woman whose son he had restored to life appeals to the king for her house and her land. Gehazi says, "My lord, O king, here is the woman and here is her son whom Elisha restored to life."

When the king asks the woman, she tells him. So the king appoints an official for her, saying, "Restore all that was hers, together with all the produce of the fields from the day that she left the land until now."
Now Elisha comes to Damascus. Ben-hadad the king of Syria is sick. When it is told him, "The man of God has come here,"
the king says to Hazael, "Take a present with you and go to meet the man of God and inquire of YHWH through him, saying, 'Shall I recover from this sickness?'"

So Hazael goes to meet him and takes a present with him — every good thing of Damascus, forty camel-loads. He comes and stands before him and says, "Your son Ben-hadad king of Syria has sent me to you, saying, 'Shall I recover from this sickness?'"
Elisha says to him, "Go, say to him, 'You shall certainly recover,' but YHWH has shown me that he shall certainly die."
He fixes his gaze and stares at him until he is ashamed. And the man of God weeps.

Hazael says, "Why does my lord weep?" He answers, "Because I know the evil that you will do to the people of Israel. You will set on fire their fortresses, and you will kill their young men with the sword and dash in pieces their little ones and rip open their pregnant women."
Hazael says, "What is your servant, who is but a dog, that he should do this great thing?" Elisha answers, "YHWH has shown me that you are to be king over Syria."
Then he departs from Elisha and comes to his master, who says to him, "What did Elisha say to you?" He answers, "He told me that you would certainly recover."
But on the next day he takes the bed cloth and dips it in water and spreads it over his face, until he dies. And Hazael becomes king in his place.
In the fifth year of Joram the son of Ahab, king of Israel, when Jehoshaphat was king of Judah, Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat began to reign as king of Judah.
He is thirty-two years old when he becomes king, and he reigns eight years in Jerusalem.
He walks in the way of the kings of Israel, as the house of Ahab had done, for the daughter of Ahab is his wife. He does what is evil in the sight of YHWH.
Yet YHWH is not willing to destroy Judah, for the sake of David his servant, since he promised to give a lamp to him and to his sons forever.
In his days Edom revolts from the rule of Judah and sets up a king of their own.
Then Joram crosses over to Zair with all his chariots. He rises in the night and strikes the Edomites who had surrounded him and his chariot commanders, but his army flees home.
So Edom revolts from the rule of Judah to this day. Libnah also revolts at the same time.
Now the rest of the acts of Joram and all that he did — are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
So Joram lies down with his fathers and is buried with his fathers in the city of David. Ahaziah his son reigns in his place.
In the twelfth year of Joram the son of Ahab, king of Israel, Ahaziah the son of Jehoram, king of Judah, begins to reign.
Ahaziah is twenty-two years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns one year in Jerusalem. His mother's name is Athaliah; she is a granddaughter of Omri king of Israel.
He also walks in the way of the house of Ahab and does what is evil in the sight of YHWH, as the house of Ahab had done, for he is son-in-law to the house of Ahab.
He goes with Joram the son of Ahab to make war against Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth-gilead. The Syrians wound Joram,

and King Joram returns to be healed in Jezreel of the wounds that the Syrians had given him at Ramah, when he fought against Hazael king of Syria. Ahaziah the son of Jehoram, king of Judah, goes down to see Joram the son of Ahab in Jezreel, because he is sick.
Then Elisha the prophet calls one of the sons of the prophets and says to him, "Tie up your garments and take this flask of oil in your hand and go to Ramoth-gilead.
When you arrive, look there for Jehu the son of Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi. Go in and have him rise from among his brothers and lead him to an inner chamber.
Then take the flask of oil and pour it on his head and say, 'Thus says YHWH: I anoint you king over Israel.' Then open the door and flee; do not linger."
So the young man, the servant of the prophet, goes to Ramoth-gilead.
When he arrives, behold, the commanders of the army are in council. He says, "I have a word for you, O commander." Jehu says, "To which of us all?" And he says, "To you, O commander."
So he arises and goes inside. The young man pours the oil on his head and says to him, "Thus says YHWH, the God of Israel: I anoint you king over the people of YHWH, over Israel.
You shall strike down the house of Ahab your master, so that I may avenge on Jezebel the blood of my servants the prophets and the blood of all the servants of YHWH.
For the whole house of Ahab shall perish, and I will cut off from Ahab every male, bond or free, in Israel.
And I will make the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha the son of Ahijah.
And the dogs shall eat Jezebel in the plot of ground at Jezreel, and none shall bury her."' Then he opens the door and flees.
When Jehu comes out to the servants of his master, they say to him, "Is all well? Why did this mad fellow come to you?" He says to them, "You know the fellow and his talk."
They say, "That is not true; tell us now." He says, "Thus and so he spoke to me, saying, 'Thus says YHWH: I anoint you king over Israel.'"
Then in haste every man of them takes his garment and puts it under him on the bare steps, and they blow the trumpet and proclaim, "Jehu is king."
So Jehu the son of Jehoshaphat the son of Nimshi conspires against Joram. Now Joram with all Israel had been on guard at Ramoth-gilead against Hazael king of Syria,

but King Joram had returned to be healed in Jezreel of the wounds that the Syrians had given him, when he fought with Hazael king of Syria. And Jehu says, "If this is your decision, then let no one slip out of the city to go and tell the news in Jezreel."
Then Jehu rode in a chariot and went to Jezreel, for Joram lay there. Ahaziah king of Judah had come down to visit Joram.

Now the watchman is standing on the tower in Jezreel, and he sees the company of Jehu as he comes and says, "I see a company." Joram says, "Take a horseman and send to meet them, and let him say, 'Is it peace?'"

So a man on horseback goes to meet him and says, "Thus says the king: 'Is it peace?'" Jehu says, "What do you have to do with peace? Turn around and ride behind me." The watchman reports, "The messenger reached them, but he is not coming back."
Then he sends out a second horseman, who comes to them and says, "Thus says the king: 'Is it peace?'" Jehu answers, "What do you have to do with peace? Turn around and ride behind me."
Again the watchman reports, "He reached them, but he is not coming back. And the driving is like the driving of Jehu the son of Nimshi, for he drives furiously."

Joram says, "Make ready." His chariot is made ready. Joram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah set out, each in his chariot, and they go to meet Jehu. And they meet him in the property of Naboth the Jezreelite.
When Joram sees Jehu, he says, "Is it peace, Jehu?" He answers, "What peace can there be, so long as the whorings and sorceries of your mother Jezebel are so many?"
Joram reins about and flees, saying to Ahaziah, "Treachery, O Ahaziah!"
Jehu draws his bow with his full strength and strikes Joram between the shoulders, so that the arrow pierces his heart, and he sinks in his chariot.

Jehu says to Bidkar his aide, "Take him up and throw him on the plot of ground belonging to Naboth the Jezreelite. For remember, when you and I rode side by side behind Ahab his father, YHWH uttered this pronouncement against him:

"'As surely as I saw yesterday the blood of Naboth and the blood of his sons — declares YHWH — I will repay you on this very plot of ground.' Now therefore take him up and throw him on the plot of ground, in accordance with the word of YHWH."

When Ahaziah the king of Judah sees this, he flees in the direction of Beth-haggan. Jehu pursues him and says, "Shoot him also," in his chariot at the ascent of Gur, which is by Ibleam. And he flees to Megiddo and dies there.
His servants carry him in a chariot to Jerusalem and bury him in his tomb with his fathers in the city of David.
In the eleventh year of Joram the son of Ahab, Ahaziah began to reign over Judah.
When Jehu comes to Jezreel, Jezebel hears of it. She paints her eyes and adorns her head and looks out of the window.
As Jehu enters the gate, she says, "Is it peace, you Zimri, murderer of your master?"
He lifts up his face to the window and says, "Who is on my side? Who?" Two or three eunuchs look out at him.
He says, "Throw her down." So they throw her down. Some of her blood splatters on the wall and on the horses, and he tramples her underfoot.
Then he goes in and eats and drinks. He says, "See now to this cursed woman and bury her, for she is a king's daughter."
But when they go to bury her, they find no more of her than the skull and the feet and the palms of her hands.
When they come back and tell him, he says, "This is the word of YHWH, which he spoke by his servant Elijah the Tishbite: 'In the plot of ground at Jezreel the dogs shall devour the flesh of Jezebel,
and the corpse of Jezebel shall be as dung on the face of the field in the plot at Jezreel, so that no one can say, This is Jezebel.'"
Now Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria. Jehu writes letters and sends them to Samaria, to the rulers of Jezreel, to the elders, and to the guardians of the sons of Ahab, saying,
"Now then, as soon as this letter comes to you, seeing your master's sons are with you, and you have chariots and horses, a fortified city also, and weapons,
select the best and fittest of your master's sons and set him on his father's throne and fight for your master's house."
But they are exceedingly afraid and say, "Behold, the two kings could not stand before him. How then can we stand?"

So he who is over the palace and he who is over the city, together with the elders and the guardians, send word to Jehu: "We are your servants, and we will do all that you tell us. We will not make anyone king. Do whatever is good in your eyes."

Then he writes to them a second letter: "If you are on my side, and if you are ready to obey me, take the heads of your master's sons and come to me at Jezreel tomorrow at this time." Now the king's sons, seventy persons, were with the great men of the city, who were bringing them up.
As soon as the letter comes to them, they take the king's sons and slaughter them — seventy persons — and put their heads in baskets and send them to him at Jezreel.
When the messenger comes and tells him, "They have brought the heads of the king's sons," he says, "Lay them in two heaps at the entrance of the gate until morning."
Then in the morning when he goes out, he stands and says to all the people, "You are innocent. It was I who conspired against my master and killed him, but who struck down all these?
Know then that there shall fall to the earth nothing of the word of YHWH, which YHWH spoke concerning the house of Ahab, for YHWH has done what he said by his servant Elijah."
So Jehu strikes down all who remain of the house of Ahab in Jezreel, all his great men and his close friends and his priests, until he leaves him none remaining.
Then he sets out and goes to Samaria. On the way, when he was at Beth-eked of the Shepherds,
Jehu met the relatives of Ahaziah king of Judah and said, "Who are you?" They answer, "We are the relatives of Ahaziah, and we came down to visit the royal princes and the sons of the queen mother."
He says, "Take them alive." And they take them alive and slaughter them at the pit of Beth-eked — forty-two persons — and he leaves none of them.

When he departs from there, he meets Jehonadab the son of Rechab coming to meet him. He greets him and says to him, "Is your heart true to my heart as mine is to yours?" Jehonadab answers, "It is." Jehu says, "If it is, give me your hand." So he gave him his hand. Jehu took him up with him into the chariot.
Jehu says, "Come with me and see my zeal for YHWH." So he had him ride in his chariot.
When he comes to Samaria, he strikes down all who remained to Ahab in Samaria, until he had wiped them out, according to the word of YHWH that he spoke to Elijah.
Then Jehu assembles all the people and says to them, "Ahab served Baal a little, but Jehu will serve him much.

Now therefore call to me all the prophets of Baal, all his worshipers and all his priests. Let none be missing, for I have a great sacrifice to offer to Baal. Whoever is missing shall not live." But Jehu does it with cunning in order to destroy the worshipers of Baal.
Jehu orders, "Sanctify a solemn assembly for Baal." So they proclaim it.

Jehu sends throughout all Israel, and all the worshipers of Baal come, so that there is not a man left who did not come. And they enter the house of Baal, and the house of Baal is filled from one end to the other.
He says to the keeper of the wardrobe, "Bring out the vestments for all the worshipers of Baal." So he brings out the vestments for them.

Then Jehu goes into the house of Baal with Jehonadab the son of Rechab. He says to the worshipers of Baal, "Search and see that there is no servant of YHWH here among you, but only the worshipers of Baal."
When they go in to offer sacrifices and burnt offerings, Jehu posts eighty men outside and says, "The man who allows any of the men whom I give into your hands to escape shall forfeit his life."

As soon as he has finished offering the burnt offering, Jehu commands the guards and the officers, "Go in and strike them down; let not a man escape." So when they put them to the sword, the guards and the officers cast them out and went to the inner room of the house of Baal,
and they bring out the pillar that was in the house of Baal and burn it.
And they demolish the pillar of Baal and demolish the house of Baal and make it a latrine to this day.
Thus Jehu wipes out Baal from Israel.
But Jehu does not turn aside from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, which he made Israel to sin — the golden calves that were in Bethel and in Dan.

YHWH says to Jehu, "Because you have done well in carrying out what is right in my eyes, and have done to the house of Ahab according to all that was in my heart, your sons of the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Israel."
But Jehu was not careful to walk in the law of YHWH, the God of Israel, with all his heart. He did not turn from the sins of Jeroboam, which he made Israel to sin.
In those days YHWH began to cut off parts of Israel. Hazael defeated them throughout the territory of Israel:
from the Jordan eastward, all the land of Gilead, the Gadites, and the Reubenites, and the Manassites, from Aroer, which is by the Valley of the Arnon, that is, Gilead and Bashan.
Now the rest of the acts of Jehu and all that he did, and all his might — are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
Jehu lies down with his fathers and they bury him in Samaria. Jehoahaz his son reigns in his place.
The time that Jehu reigned over Israel in Samaria is twenty-eight years.
Now when Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah sees that her son is dead, she rises and destroys all the royal family.

But Jehosheba, the daughter of King Joram, sister of Ahaziah, takes Joash the son of Ahaziah and steals him away from among the king's sons who are being put to death — she puts him and his nurse in a bedroom. Thus she hides him from Athaliah, and he is not put to death.
He remains with her six years, hidden in the house of YHWH, while Athaliah reigns over the land.

But in the seventh year Jehoiada sends and brings the captains of hundreds of the Carites and of the guards, and has them come to him in the house of YHWH. He makes a covenant with them and puts them under oath in the house of YHWH and shows them the king's son.
He commands them: "This is the thing that you shall do: one third of you, those who come off duty on the Sabbath and guard the king's house
(another third being at the gate Sur, and a third at the gate behind the guards) — you shall guard the palace.
And the two divisions of you, which come on duty in force on the Sabbath and guard the house of YHWH —
shall surround the king, each with his weapons in his hand. Whoever approaches the ranks is to be put to death. Be with the king when he goes out and when he comes in."

The captains of hundreds do according to all that Jehoiada the priest commands. Each brings his men who are to go off duty on the Sabbath, with those who are to come on duty on the Sabbath. They come to Jehoiada the priest.
The priest delivers to the captains of hundreds the spears and shields that had been King David's, which were in the house of YHWH.
The guards stand, every man with his weapons in his hand, from the south side of the house to the north side of the house, around the altar and the house on behalf of the king.
Then he brings out the king's son and puts the crown on him and gives him the testimony. They proclaim him king and anoint him, and they clap their hands and say, "Long live the king!"
When Athaliah hears the noise of the guard and of the people, she goes into the house of YHWH to the people.

When she looks, there is the king standing by the pillar, according to the custom, with the captains and the trumpeters beside the king, and all the people of the land rejoicing and blowing trumpets. Athaliah tears her clothes and cries, "Treason! Treason!"

Then Jehoiada the priest commands the captains who are set over the army: "Bring her out between the ranks, and put to the sword anyone who follows her." For the priest says, "Let her not be put to death in the house of YHWH."
So they lay hands on her; she goes through the horses' entrance to the king's house, and she is put to death there.
Then Jehoiada makes a covenant between YHWH and the king and people, that they should be YHWH's people, and also between the king and the people.

Then all the people of the land go to the house of Baal and tear it down; his altars and his images they break in pieces, and they kill Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars. Jehoiada the priest posts guards over the house of YHWH.

Then he takes the captains, the Carites, the guards, and all the people of the land, and they bring the king down from the house of YHWH, marching through the gate of the guards to the king's house. And he takes his seat on the throne of the kings.
So all the people of the land rejoice, and the city is quiet after Athaliah has been put to death with the sword at the king's house.
Jehoash is seven years old when he begins to reign.
In the seventh year of Jehu, Jehoash begins to reign, and he reigns forty years in Jerusalem. His mother's name is Zibiah of Beersheba.
Jehoash does what is right in the eyes of YHWH all his days, because Jehoiada the priest instructs him.
Nevertheless, the high places are not taken away; the people continue to sacrifice and make offerings at the high places.

Jehoash says to the priests, "All the money of the sacred donations that is brought into the house of YHWH — the money for which each man is assessed, the money from the assessment of persons, and the money that a man's heart prompts him to bring into the house of YHWH —
let the priests take it, each from his donor, and let them repair the house wherever any need of repairs is discovered."
But by the twenty-third year of King Jehoash, the priests had made no repairs on the house.

Then King Jehoash summons Jehoiada the priest and the other priests and says to them, "Why are you not repairing the house? Now therefore take no more money from your donors but hand it over for the repair of the house."
So the priests agree that they shall take no more money from the people, and that they shall not repair the house.

Then Jehoiada the priest takes a chest and bores a hole in the lid of it and sets it beside the altar on the right side as one enters the house of YHWH. The priests who guard the threshold put in it all the money that is brought into the house of YHWH.
And whenever they see that there is much money in the chest, the king's secretary and the high priest come up and they count and bag the money that is found in the house of YHWH.
Then they give the money that is weighed out to the workmen who have the oversight of the house of YHWH. And they use it to pay the carpenters and the builders who worked on the house of YHWH,
and the masons and the stonecutters, as well as to buy timber and quarried stone for making repairs on the house of YHWH, and for any outlay for the repairs of the house.
But there are not made for the house of YHWH basins of silver, snuffers, bowls, trumpets, or any vessels of gold or of silver, from the money that is brought into the house of YHWH,
for that is given to the workmen who are repairing the house of YHWH with it.
They do not ask an accounting from the men into whose hand they deliver the money to pay out to the workmen, for they deal honestly.
The money from the guilt offerings and the money from the sin offerings is not brought into the house of YHWH; it belongs to the priests.
At that time Hazael king of Syria went up and fought against Gath and took it. But when Hazael set his face to go up against Jerusalem,

Jehoash king of Judah takes all the sacred gifts that Jehoshaphat and Jehoram and Ahaziah his fathers, the kings of Judah, had dedicated, and his own sacred gifts, and all the gold that was found in the treasuries of the house of YHWH and of the king's house, and sends these to Hazael king of Syria. Then Hazael turns away from Jerusalem.
Now the rest of the acts of Joash and all that he did — are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
His servants arise and make a conspiracy and strike down Joash at the house of Millo, on the way that goes down to Silla.

It is Jozacar the son of Shimeath and Jehozabad the son of Shomer, his servants, who strike him down, so that he dies. They bury him with his fathers in the city of David, and Amaziah his son reigns in his place.
In the twenty-third year of Joash the son of Ahaziah, king of Judah, Jehoahaz the son of Jehu begins to reign over Israel in Samaria and reigns seventeen years.
He does what is evil in the sight of YHWH and follows the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, which he made Israel to sin; he does not depart from them.
The anger of YHWH is kindled against Israel, and he gives them continually into the hand of Hazael king of Syria and into the hand of Ben-hadad the son of Hazael.
Then Jehoahaz seeks the favor of YHWH, and YHWH listens to him, for he sees the oppression of Israel, how the king of Syria oppresses them.
Therefore YHWH gives Israel a savior, so that they escape from the hand of the Syrians, and the people of Israel dwell in their homes as formerly.
Nevertheless, they do not depart from the sins of the house of Jeroboam, which he made Israel to sin, but walk in them. The Asherah also remains in Samaria.
For there are left to Jehoahaz an army of only fifty horsemen and ten chariots and ten thousand foot soldiers, for the king of Syria had destroyed them and made them like the dust at threshing.
Now the rest of the acts of Jehoahaz and all that he did, and his might — are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
So Jehoahaz lies down with his fathers, and they bury him in Samaria, and Joash his son reigns in his place.
In the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz begins to reign over Israel in Samaria and reigns sixteen years.
He also does what is evil in the sight of YHWH. He does not depart from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, which he made Israel to sin, but he walks in them.
Now the rest of the acts of Joash and all that he did, and the might with which he fought against Amaziah king of Judah — are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
So Joash lies down with his fathers, and Jeroboam sits on his throne. Joash is buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.

Now when Elisha falls sick with the illness of which he is to die, Joash king of Israel comes down to him and weeps before him, crying, "My father, my father! The chariots of Israel and its horsemen!"
Elisha says to him, "Take a bow and arrows." So he takes a bow and arrows.
Then he says to the king of Israel, "Draw the bow." And he draws it. Elisha puts his hands on the king's hands.

He says, "Open the east window." And he opens it. Then Elisha says, "Shoot!" And he shoots. He says, "YHWH's arrow of victory, the arrow of victory over Syria! For you shall fight the Syrians in Aphek until you have made an end of them."
Elisha says, "Take the arrows." And he takes them. He says to the king of Israel, "Strike the ground with them." He strikes three times and stops.

Then the man of God is angry with him and says, "You should have struck five or six times; then you would have struck down Syria until you had made an end of it, but now you will strike down Syria only three times."
So Elisha dies and they bury him. Now bands of Moabites used to invade the land in the spring of the year.
And as a man is being buried, behold, a marauding band is seen, and the man is thrown into the tomb of Elisha. As soon as the man touches the bones of Elisha, he revives and stands on his feet.
Now Hazael king of Syria oppresses Israel all the days of Jehoahaz.

But YHWH is gracious to them and has compassion on them and turns toward them, because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and has not been willing to destroy them, and he has not cast them from his presence until now.
When Hazael king of Syria dies, Ben-hadad his son becomes king in his place.

Then Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz takes again from Ben-hadad the son of Hazael the cities that he had taken from Jehoahaz his father in war. Three times Joash defeats him and recovers the cities of Israel.
In the second year of Joash the son of Joahaz, king of Israel, Amaziah the son of Joash, king of Judah, begins to reign.
He is twenty-five years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name is Jehoaddin of Jerusalem.
He does what is right in the eyes of YHWH, yet not like David his father. He does in all things as Joash his father had done.
But the high places are not removed; the people still sacrifice and make offerings on the high places.
As soon as the royal power is firmly in his hand, he strikes down his servants who had struck down the king his father.

But he does not put to death the children of the murderers, according to what is written in the Book of the Law of Moses, where YHWH commanded, "Fathers shall not be put to death because of their children, or children be put to death because of their fathers. But each one shall die for his own sin."
He struck down ten thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt and took Sela by storm, and called it Joktheel, which is its name to this day.
Then Amaziah sent messengers to Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz, son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, "Come, let us look one another in the face."

Jehoash king of Israel sends to Amaziah king of Judah, "A thistle on Lebanon sent to a cedar on Lebanon, saying, 'Give your daughter to my son for a wife.' And a wild beast of Lebanon passed by and trampled down the thistle.
You have indeed struck down Edom, and your heart has lifted you up. Be content with your glory and stay at home, for why should you provoke trouble so that you fall, you and Judah with you?"
But Amaziah would not listen. So Jehoash king of Israel went up, and he and Amaziah king of Judah faced one another in battle at Beth-shemesh, which belongs to Judah.
Judah is defeated before Israel, and every man flees to his home.

Jehoash king of Israel captures Amaziah king of Judah, the son of Jehoash, son of Ahaziah, at Beth-shemesh, and comes to Jerusalem and breaks down the wall of Jerusalem for four hundred cubits, from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate.
He seizes all the gold and silver and all the vessels that are found in the house of YHWH and in the treasuries of the king's house, also hostages, and he returns to Samaria.
Now the rest of the acts of Jehoash that he did, and his might, and how he fought with Amaziah king of Judah — are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
Jehoash lies down with his fathers and is buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel. Jeroboam his son reigns in his place.
Amaziah the son of Joash, king of Judah, lives fifteen years after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel.
Now the rest of the deeds of Amaziah — are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
They make a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem, and he flees to Lachish. But they send after him to Lachish and put him to death there.
And they bring him on horses; he is buried in Jerusalem with his fathers in the city of David.
All the people of Judah take Azariah, who is sixteen years old, and make him king in the place of his father Amaziah.
He built Elath and restored it to Judah, after the king lies down with his fathers.
In the fifteenth year of Amaziah the son of Joash, king of Judah, Jeroboam the son of Joash, king of Israel, begins to reign in Samaria and reigns forty-one years.
He does what is evil in the sight of YHWH. He does not depart from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, which he made Israel to sin.

He restores the border of Israel from Lebo-hamath as far as the Sea of the Arabah, according to the word of YHWH, the God of Israel, which he spoke by his servant Jonah the son of Amittai, the prophet, who was from Gath-hepher.
For YHWH sees that the affliction of Israel is very bitter, for there is none left, bond or free, and there is none to help Israel.
But YHWH has not said that he will blot out the name of Israel from under heaven, so he saves them by the hand of Jeroboam the son of Joash.

Now the rest of the acts of Jeroboam and all that he did, and his might, how he fought, and how he restored Damascus and Hamath to Judah in Israel — are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
Jeroboam lies down with his fathers, the kings of Israel, and Zechariah his son reigns in his place.
In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Azariah the son of Amaziah, king of Judah, begins to reign.
He is sixteen years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name is Jecoliah of Jerusalem.
He does what is right in the eyes of YHWH, according to all that his father Amaziah had done.
Nevertheless, the high places are not taken away. The people still sacrifice and make offerings on the high places.
YHWH strikes the king so that he is a leper to the day of his death, and he lives in a separate house. Jotham the king's son is over the household, governing the people of the land.
Now the rest of the acts of Azariah and all that he did — are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
Azariah lies down with his fathers, and they bury him with his fathers in the city of David. Jotham his son reigns in his place.
In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah king of Judah, Zechariah the son of Jeroboam reigns over Israel in Samaria six months.
He does what is evil in the sight of YHWH, as his fathers had done. He does not depart from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, which he made Israel to sin.
Shallum the son of Jabesh conspires against him and strikes him down at Ibleam and puts him to death and reigns in his place.
Now the rest of the deeds of Zechariah — behold, they are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
This was the promise of YHWH that he gave to Jehu: "Your sons shall sit on the throne of Israel to the fourth generation." And so it came to pass.
Shallum the son of Jabesh begins to reign in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah king of Judah, and he reigns one month in Samaria.
Then Menahem the son of Gadi came up from Tirzah and came to Samaria and struck down Shallum the son of Jabesh in Samaria and put him to death and reigned in his place.
Now the rest of the deeds of Shallum and the conspiracy that he made — behold, they are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.

At that time Menahem sacked Tiphsah and all who were in it and its territory from Tirzah on, because they did not open it to him. Therefore he sacked it and he ripped open all the women in it who were with child.
In the thirty-ninth year of Azariah king of Judah, Menahem the son of Gadi begins to reign over Israel and reigns ten years in Samaria.
He does what is evil in the sight of YHWH. He does not depart all his days from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, which he made Israel to sin.
Pul the king of Assyria came against the land, and Menahem gives Pul a thousand talents of silver that he might help him to confirm his hold on the royal power.

Menahem exacted the money from Israel, that is, from all the wealthy men, fifty shekels of silver from every man, to give to the king of Assyria. So the king of Assyria turned back and did not stay there in the land.
Now the rest of the deeds of Menahem and all that he did — are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
Menahem lies down with his fathers, and Pekahiah his son reigns in his place.
In the fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekahiah the son of Menahem begins to reign over Israel in Samaria and reigns two years.
He does what is evil in the sight of YHWH. He does not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, which he made Israel to sin.

Pekah the son of Remaliah, his captain, conspires against him with fifty men of the Gileadites and strikes him down in Samaria, in the citadel of the king's house; he puts him to death and reigns in his place.
Now the rest of the deeds of Pekahiah and all that he did — behold, they are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
In the fifty-second year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekah the son of Remaliah begins to reign over Israel in Samaria and reigns twenty years.
He does what is evil in the sight of YHWH. He does not depart from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, which he made Israel to sin.

In the days of Pekah king of Israel, Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria comes and captures Ijon, Abel-beth-maacah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, and Galilee, all the land of Naphtali, and he carries the people captive to Assyria.
Then Hoshea the son of Elah makes a conspiracy against Pekah the son of Remaliah and strikes him down and puts him to death and reigns in his place, in the twentieth year of Jotham the son of Uzziah.
Now the rest of the deeds of Pekah and all that he did — behold, they are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
In the second year of Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, Jotham the son of Uzziah, king of Judah, begins to reign.
He is twenty-five years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother's name is Jerusha the daughter of Zadok.
He does what is right in the eyes of YHWH, according to all that his father Uzziah had done.
Nevertheless, the high places are not removed. The people still sacrifice and make offerings on the high places. He built the upper gate of the house of YHWH.
Now the rest of the acts of Jotham and all that he did — are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
In those days YHWH begins to send Rezin the king of Syria and Pekah the son of Remaliah against Judah.
Jotham lies down with his fathers and is buried with his fathers in the city of David his father. Ahaz his son reigns in his place.
In the seventeenth year of Pekah the son of Remaliah, Ahaz the son of Jotham, king of Judah, begins to reign.
Ahaz is twenty years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns sixteen years in Jerusalem. He does not do what is right in the eyes of YHWH his God, as his father David had done,
but he walks in the way of the kings of Israel. He even burns his son as an offering, according to the despicable practices of the nations whom YHWH drove out before the people of Israel.
He sacrifices and makes offerings on the high places and on the hills and under every green tree.
Then Rezin the king of Syria and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, came up to wage war on Jerusalem. They besiege Ahaz but cannot conquer him.
At that time Rezin the king of Syria recovered Elath for Syria and drove the men of Judah from Elath. And the Edomites came to Elath, where they dwell to this day.

So Ahaz sends messengers to Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, saying, "I am your servant and your son. Come up and rescue me from the hand of the king of Syria and from the hand of the king of Israel, who are attacking me."
Ahaz also takes the silver and gold that is found in the house of YHWH and in the treasuries of the king's house and sends a present to the king of Assyria.
The king of Assyria listens to him. The king of Assyria marches up against Damascus and takes it, carrying its people captive to Kir, and puts Rezin to death.

When King Ahaz goes to Damascus to meet Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, he sees the altar that is at Damascus. King Ahaz sends to Uriah the priest a model of the altar and its pattern, exact in all its details.
Uriah the priest builds the altar; in accordance with all that King Ahaz has sent from Damascus — so Uriah the priest makes it, before King Ahaz arrives from Damascus.
When the king came from Damascus, the king views the altar. The king draws near to the altar and goes up on it
and burns his burnt offering and his grain offering and pours his drink offering and throws the blood of his peace offerings against the altar.
The bronze altar that was before YHWH he removes from the front of the house, from the place between his altar and the house of YHWH, and puts it on the north side of his new altar.

King Ahaz commands Uriah the priest: "On the great altar burn the morning burnt offering and the evening grain offering and the king's burnt offering and his grain offering, with the burnt offering of all the people of the land, and their grain offering and their drink offering. All the blood of the burnt offering and all the blood of the sacrifice shall you throw against it. But the bronze altar shall be for me to inquire by."
Uriah the priest does all this, as King Ahaz commanded.
King Ahaz cuts off the frames of the stands and removes the basin from them, and he takes down the sea from off the bronze oxen that were under it and puts it on a stone pedestal.
The covered way for the Sabbath that had been built inside the house and the outer entrance for the king he removes from the house of YHWH, because of the king of Assyria.
Now the rest of the acts of Ahaz that he did — are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
Ahaz lies down with his fathers and is buried with his fathers in the city of David. Hezekiah his son reigns in his place.
In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah, Hoshea the son of Elah begins to reign in Samaria over Israel and reigns nine years.
He does what is evil in the sight of YHWH, yet not as the kings of Israel who were before him.
Against him came up Shalmaneser king of Assyria. Hoshea becomes his vassal and pays him tribute.

But the king of Assyria finds treachery in Hoshea. For he had sent messengers to So, king of Egypt, and offered no tribute to the king of Assyria, as he had done year by year. Therefore the king of Assyria shut him up and bound him in prison.
Then the king of Assyria invaded all the land and came to Samaria and for three years he besieged it.

In the ninth year of Hoshea, the king of Assyria captured Samaria, and he carried the Israelites away to Assyria and placed them in Halah, and on the Habor, the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.

And this happened because the people of Israel had sinned against YHWH their God, who had brought them up out of the land of Egypt from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt — they had feared other gods
and walked in the customs of the nations whom YHWH drove out before the people of Israel, and in the customs that the kings of Israel had practiced.
Israel did things that were not right against YHWH their God. They built for themselves high places in all their towns, from watchtower to fortified city.
They set up for themselves pillars and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every green tree.
There they made offerings on all the high places, as the nations did whom YHWH carried away before them. And they did wicked things, provoking YHWH to anger.
They served idols, of which YHWH had said to them, "You shall not do this."

Yet YHWH warned Israel and Judah by every prophet and every seer, saying, "Turn from your evil ways and keep my commandments and my statutes, in accordance with all the Law that I commanded your fathers, and that I sent to you by my servants the prophets."
But they would not listen. They were stubborn — as their fathers had been who did not believe in YHWH their God.

They despised his statutes and his covenant that he made with their fathers and the warnings that he gave them. They went after false idols and became false, and they followed the nations that were around them, concerning whom YHWH had commanded them that they should not do as they did.
They abandoned all the commandments of YHWH their God, and made for themselves metal images of two calves; they made an Asherah and worshiped all the host of heaven and served Baal.
They burned their sons and their daughters as offerings and used divination and omens and sold themselves to do evil in the sight of YHWH, provoking him to anger.
Therefore YHWH is very angry with Israel and removes them out of his sight. None is left but the tribe of Judah only.
Judah also does not keep the commandments of YHWH their God, but walks in the customs that Israel has practiced.
YHWH rejects all the descendants of Israel and afflicts them and gives them into the hand of plunderers, until he has cast them out of his sight.
When he had torn Israel from the house of David, they made Jeroboam the son of Nebat king. Jeroboam drove Israel from following YHWH and made them commit great sin.
The people of Israel walked in all the sins that Jeroboam did. They did not depart from them,
until YHWH removed Israel out of his sight, as he had spoken by all his servants the prophets. So Israel was exiled from their own land to Assyria until this day.

The king of Assyria brought people from Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath, and Sepharvaim, and placed them in the cities of Samaria instead of the people of Israel. They take possession of Samaria and dwell in its cities.
When they first settle there, they do not fear YHWH. So YHWH sends lions among them, which kill some of them.

So the king of Assyria is told: "The nations that you have carried away and placed in the cities of Samaria do not know the law of the god of the land. Therefore he has sent lions among them, and behold, they are killing them because they do not know the law of the god of the land."
Then the king of Assyria commanded, "Send there one of the priests whom you carried away from there, and let him go and dwell there and teach them the law of the god of the land."
So one of the priests whom they had carried away from Samaria comes and dwells in Bethel and teaches them how they should fear YHWH.
But every nation still makes its own gods and puts them in the shrines of the high places that the Samaritans had made, every nation in the cities in which they dwell.
The men of Babylon make Succoth-benoth, the men of Cuth make Nergal, the men of Hamath make Ashima,
and the Avvites make Nibhaz and Tartak; and the Sepharvites burn their children in the fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech, the gods of Sepharvaim.
They also fear YHWH and appoint from among themselves all sorts of people as priests of the high places, who sacrifice for them in the shrines of the high places.
So they fear YHWH but also serve their own gods, after the manner of the nations from among whom they were carried away.

To this day they do according to the former manner. They do not fear YHWH, and they do not follow the statutes or the rules or the law or the commandment that YHWH commanded the children of Jacob, whom he named Israel.
YHWH made a covenant with them and commanded them: "You shall not fear other gods or bow yourselves to them or serve them or sacrifice to them.
But you shall fear YHWH, who brought you out of the land of Egypt with great power and with an outstretched arm. You shall bow yourselves to him and sacrifice to him.
And the statutes and the rules and the law and the commandment that he wrote for you, you shall always be careful to do. You shall not fear other gods.
The covenant that I have made with you, you shall not forget, and you shall not fear other gods.
But you shall fear YHWH your God, and he will deliver you out of the hand of all your enemies."
However, they do not listen, but they do according to their former manner.
So these nations fear YHWH and also serve their carved images. Their children do likewise, and their children's children — as their fathers did, so they do to this day.
In the third year of Hoshea son of Elah, king of Israel, Hezekiah the son of Ahaz, king of Judah, begins to reign.
He is twenty-five years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name is Abi the daughter of Zechariah.
He does what is right in the eyes of YHWH, according to all that David his father had done.

He removes the high places and breaks the pillars and cuts down the Asherah. He breaks in pieces the bronze serpent that Moses had made, for until those days the people of Israel had made offerings to it — it was called Nehushtan.
He trusts in YHWH the God of Israel, so that there was none like him among all the kings of Judah after him, nor among those who were before him.
He holds fast to YHWH. He does not depart from following him, but keeps the commandments that YHWH commanded Moses.
YHWH is with him; wherever he goes out, he prospers. He rebels against the king of Assyria and does not serve him.
He struck down the Philistines as far as Gaza and its territory, from watchtower to fortified city.
In the fourth year of King Hezekiah, which was the seventh year of Hoshea son of Elah, king of Israel, Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up against Samaria and besieged it.
At the end of three years he captures it. In the sixth year of Hezekiah, which was the ninth year of Hoshea king of Israel, Samaria is taken.
The king of Assyria carried the Israelites away to Assyria and put them in Halah, and on the Habor, the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes,
because they did not obey the voice of YHWH their God but transgressed his covenant — all that Moses the servant of YHWH commanded. They neither listened nor obeyed.
In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria comes up against all the fortified cities of Judah and takes them.

Hezekiah king of Judah sends to the king of Assyria at Lachish, saying, "I have done wrong; withdraw from me. Whatever you impose on me I will bear." The king of Assyria requires of Hezekiah king of Judah three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.
Hezekiah gives him all the silver that is found in the house of YHWH and in the treasuries of the king's house.
At that time Hezekiah strips the gold from the doors of the temple of YHWH and from the doorposts that Hezekiah king of Judah had overlaid and gives it to the king of Assyria.

The king of Assyria sends the Tartan, the Rab-saris, and the Rabshakeh with a great army from Lachish to King Hezekiah at Jerusalem. They go up and come to Jerusalem. When they arrive, they come and stand by the conduit of the upper pool, which is on the highway to the Washer's Field.
When they call for the king, there come out to them Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, who is over the household, and Shebnah the secretary, and Joah the son of Asaph, the recorder.
The Rabshakeh says to them, "Say to Hezekiah: 'Thus says the great king, the king of Assyria: On what do you rest this trust of yours?
Do you think that mere words are strategy and power for war? In whom do you now trust, that you have rebelled against me?
Behold, you are trusting now in Egypt, that broken reed of a staff, which will pierce the hand of any man who leans on it. Such is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who trust in him.
But if you say to me, "We trust in YHWH our God," is it not he whose high places and altars Hezekiah has removed, saying to Judah and to Jerusalem, "You shall worship before this altar in Jerusalem"?
Come now, make a wager with my master the king of Assyria: I will give you two thousand horses, if you are able on your part to put riders on them.
How then can you repulse a single captain among the least of my master's servants, when you trust in Egypt for chariots and for horsemen?
Moreover, is it without YHWH that I have come up against this place to destroy it? YHWH said to me, Go up against this land, and destroy it.'"

Then Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, and Shebnah, and Joah say to the Rabshakeh, "Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, for we understand it. Do not speak to us in the language of Judah within the hearing of the people who are on the wall."

But the Rabshakeh says to them, "Has my master sent me to speak these words to your master and to you, and not to the men sitting on the wall, who are doomed with you to eat their own dung and to drink their own urine?"
Then the Rabshakeh stands and calls out in a loud voice in the language of Judah: "Hear the word of the great king, the king of Assyria!
Thus says the king: 'Do not let Hezekiah deceive you, for he will not be able to deliver you out of my hand.
Do not let Hezekiah make you trust in YHWH, saying, YHWH will surely deliver us, and this city will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.'

Do not listen to Hezekiah, for thus says the king of Assyria: Make your peace with me and come out to me. Then each one of you will eat of his own vine and each one of his own fig tree and each one of you will drink the water of his own cistern,

until I come and take you away to a land like your own land, a land of grain and wine, a land of bread and vineyards, a land of olive trees and honey, that you may live, and not die. Do not listen to Hezekiah when he misleads you by saying, YHWH will deliver us.
Has any of the gods of the nations ever delivered his land out of the hand of the king of Assyria?
Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah? Have they delivered Samaria out of my hand?
Who among all the gods of the lands have delivered their lands out of my hand, that YHWH should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?'"
But the people are silent and answer him not a word, for the king's command was, "Do not answer him."

Then Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, and Shebna the secretary, and Joah the son of Asaph, the recorder, come to Hezekiah with their clothes torn and tell him the words of the Rabshakeh.
When King Hezekiah hears it, he tears his clothes and covers himself with sackcloth and goes into the house of YHWH.
He sends Eliakim, who was over the household, and Shebna the secretary and the senior priests, covered with sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah the son of Amoz.
They say to him, "Thus says Hezekiah: This day is a day of distress, of rebuke, and of disgrace; children have come to the point of birth and there is no strength to bring them forth.

It may be that YHWH your God heard all the words of the Rabshakeh, whom his master the king of Assyria has sent to mock the living God, and will rebuke the words that YHWH your God has heard; therefore lift up your prayer for the remnant that is left."
When the servants of King Hezekiah come to Isaiah,
Isaiah says to them, "Say to your master, 'Thus says YHWH: Do not be afraid because of the words that you have heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have reviled me.
Behold, I will put a spirit in him, so that he shall hear a rumor and return to his own land, and I will make him fall by the sword in his own land.'"
The Rabshakeh returns and finds the king of Assyria fighting against Libnah, for he had heard that the king had left Lachish.
When he heard it said of Tirhakah king of Cush, "Behold, he has set out to fight against you," the king of Assyria again sends messengers to Hezekiah, saying,
"Thus shall you speak to Hezekiah king of Judah: Do not let your God in whom you trust deceive you by promising that Jerusalem will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.
Behold, you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all lands, devoting them to destruction. Shall you be delivered?
Have the gods of the nations delivered them — the nations that my fathers destroyed — Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the people of Eden who were in Telassar?
Where is the king of Hamath, the king of Arpad, the king of the city of Sepharvaim, the king of Hena, or the king of Ivvah?'"
Hezekiah receives the letter from the hand of the messengers and reads it. And Hezekiah goes up to the house of YHWH and spreads it before YHWH.
Hezekiah prays before YHWH and says: "O YHWH, the God of Israel, enthroned above the cherubim, you are the God, you alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth; you have made heaven and earth.
Incline your ear, O YHWH, and hear; open your eyes, O YHWH, and see; hear the words of Sennacherib, which he has sent to mock the living God.
Truly, O YHWH, the kings of Assyria have laid waste the nations and their lands
and have cast their gods into the fire, for they were not gods, but the work of men's hands, wood and stone. Therefore they were destroyed.
So now, O YHWH our God, save us, please, from his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you, O YHWH, are God alone."
Then Isaiah the son of Amoz sends to Hezekiah, saying, "Thus says YHWH, the God of Israel: Your prayer to me about Sennacherib king of Assyria I have heard.
This is the word that YHWH has spoken concerning him:
"She despises you, she scorns you — the virgin daughter of Zion; she wags her head behind you — the daughter of Jerusalem.
"Whom have you mocked and reviled? Against whom have you raised your voice and lifted your eyes to the heights? Against the Holy One of Israel!

By your servants you have mocked YHWH and you have said, 'With my many chariots I have gone up the heights of the mountains, to the far recesses of Lebanon. I felled its tallest cedars, its choicest cypresses. I entered its farthest retreat, its densest forest.
I dug wells and drank foreign waters, and I dried up with the sole of my foot all the streams of Egypt.'
"Have you not heard that I determined it long ago? I planned from days of old what now I bring to pass: that you should make fortified cities crash into heaps of ruins,
while their inhabitants, shorn of strength, are dismayed and confounded, and have become like plants of the field and like tender grass, like grass on the housetops, blighted before it is grown.

"I know your sitting down and your going out and coming in, and your raging against me. Because you have raged against me and your arrogance has come into my ears, I will put my hook in your nose and my bit in your mouth, and I will turn you back on the way by which you came.

"This shall be the sign for you: this year you shall eat what grows of itself, and in the second year what springs of the same. Then in the third year sow and reap, and plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
The surviving remnant of the house of Judah shall again take root downward and bear fruit upward.
For out of Jerusalem shall go a remnant, and out of Mount Zion a band of survivors. The zeal of YHWH of hosts will do this.
"Therefore thus says YHWH concerning the king of Assyria: He shall not come into this city or shoot an arrow there, or come before it with a shield or cast up a siege mound against it.
By the way that he came, by the same he shall return, and he shall not come into this city, declares YHWH.
For I will defend this city to save it, for my own sake and for the sake of my servant David."
That night the angel of YHWH goes out and strikes down 185,000 in the camp of the Assyrians. When people rise early in the morning, behold, all of these are dead bodies.
Then Sennacherib king of Assyria departs and returns home and lives at Nineveh.
As he was worshiping in the house of Nisroch his god, Adrammelech and Sharezer, his sons, strike him down with the sword and escape into the land of Ararat. Esarhaddon his son reigns in his place.

In those days Hezekiah becomes sick and is at the point of death. The prophet Isaiah the son of Amoz comes to him and says to him, "Thus says YHWH: Set your house in order, for you shall die; you shall not recover."
Then Hezekiah turns his face to the wall and prays to YHWH, saying,
"Please, O YHWH, remember how I have walked before you in faithfulness and with a whole heart, and have done what is good in your sight." And Hezekiah weeps bitterly.
Before Isaiah had gone out of the middle court, the word of YHWH came to him:

"Turn back, and say to Hezekiah the leader of my people, Thus says YHWH, the God of David your father: I have heard your prayer; I have seen your tears. Behold, I will heal you. On the third day you shall go up to the house of YHWH.
I will add fifteen years to your life. I will deliver you and this city out of the hand of the king of Assyria, and I will defend this city for my own sake and for my servant David's sake."
Isaiah says, "Bring a cake of figs." They bring it and put it on the boil, and he recovers.
Hezekiah says to Isaiah, "What shall be the sign that YHWH will heal me, and that I shall go up to the house of YHWH on the third day?"
Isaiah says, "This shall be the sign to you from YHWH that YHWH will do the thing that he has promised: shall the shadow go forward ten steps, or go back ten steps?"
Hezekiah answers, "It is an easy thing for the shadow to lengthen ten steps. Rather let the shadow go back ten steps."
Isaiah the prophet calls to YHWH and he brings the shadow back ten steps, by which it had gone down on the steps of Ahaz.
At that time Merodach-baladan the son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sends envoys with letters and a present to Hezekiah, for he heard that Hezekiah had been sick.

Hezekiah welcomes them and shows them all his treasure house — the silver, the gold, the spices, the precious oil, his armory, all that is found in his storehouses. There is nothing in his house or in all his realm that Hezekiah does not show them.
Then Isaiah the prophet comes to King Hezekiah and says to him, "What did these men say? And from where did they come to you?" Hezekiah says, "They have come from a far country — from Babylon."
He says, "What have they seen in your house?" Hezekiah answers, "They have seen all that is in my house; there is nothing in my storehouses that I did not show them."
Then Isaiah says to Hezekiah, "Hear the word of YHWH:
Behold, the days are coming when all that is in your house, and that which your fathers have stored up till this day, shall be carried to Babylon. Nothing shall be left, says YHWH.
And some of your own sons who will come from you, whom you will father, shall be taken away, and they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon."
Then Hezekiah says to Isaiah, "The word of YHWH that you have spoken is good." For he thought, "Why not, if there will be peace and security in my days?"

Now the rest of the acts of Hezekiah and all his might and how he made the pool and the conduit and brought water into the city — are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
Hezekiah lies down with his fathers, and Manasseh his son reigns in his place.
Manasseh is twelve years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns fifty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother's name is Hephzibah.
He does what is evil in the sight of YHWH, according to the despicable practices of the nations whom YHWH drove out before the people of Israel.

For he rebuilds the high places that Hezekiah his father had destroyed, and he erects altars for Baal and makes an Asherah, as Ahab king of Israel had done, and worships all the host of heaven and serves them.
He builds altars in the house of YHWH, of which YHWH had said, "In Jerusalem will I put my name."
He builds altars for all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of YHWH.
He burns his son as an offering and uses fortune-telling and omens and deals with mediums and with necromancers. He does much evil in the sight of YHWH, provoking him to anger.

The carved image of Asherah that he had made he sets in the house of which YHWH had said to David and to Solomon his son, "In this house and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I will put my name forever.

I will not cause the feet of Israel to wander anymore out of the land that I gave to their fathers, if only they will be careful to do according to all that I have commanded them, and according to all the Law that my servant Moses commanded them."
But they do not listen. Manasseh leads them astray to do more evil than the nations had done whom YHWH destroyed before the people of Israel.
YHWH speaks by his servants the prophets, saying,
"Because Manasseh king of Judah has committed these abominations and has done things more evil than all that the Amorites did, who were before him, and has made Judah also to sin with his idols,
therefore thus says YHWH, the God of Israel: Behold, I am bringing upon Jerusalem and Judah such disaster that the ears of everyone who hears of it will tingle.
I will stretch over Jerusalem the measuring line of Samaria, and the plumb line of the house of Ahab, and I will wipe Jerusalem as one wipes a dish, wiping it and turning it upside down.
I will forsake the remnant of my heritage and give them into the hand of their enemies, and they shall become a prey and a spoil to all their enemies,
because they have done what is evil in my sight and have provoked me to anger, since the day their fathers came out of Egypt, even to this day."
Moreover, Manasseh sheds very much innocent blood, till he has filled Jerusalem from one end to another, besides the sin that he made Judah to sin so that they did what was evil in the sight of YHWH.
Now the rest of the acts of Manasseh and all that he did, and the sin that he committed — are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
Manasseh lies down with his fathers and is buried in the garden of his house, in the garden of Uzza. Amon his son reigns in his place.
Amon is twenty-two years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name is Meshullemeth the daughter of Haruz of Jotbah.
He does what is evil in the sight of YHWH, as Manasseh his father had done.
He walks in all the way that his father walked and serves the idols that his father served and worships them.
He abandons YHWH, the God of his fathers, and does not walk in the way of YHWH.
The servants of Amon conspire against him and put the king to death in his house.
But the people of the land strike down all those who had conspired against King Amon, and the people of the land make Josiah his son king in his place.
Now the rest of the acts of Amon that he did — are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
He is buried in his tomb in the garden of Uzza, and Josiah his son reigns in his place.
Josiah is eight years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns thirty-one years in Jerusalem. His mother's name is Jedidah the daughter of Adaiah of Bozkath.
He does what is right in the eyes of YHWH and walks in all the way of David his father, and he does not turn aside to the right or to the left.
In the eighteenth year of King Josiah, the king sends Shaphan the son of Azaliah, son of Meshullam, the secretary, to the house of YHWH, saying,
"Go up to Hilkiah the high priest, that he may count the money that has been brought into the house of YHWH, which the keepers of the threshold have collected from the people.
Let it be given to the workmen who have the oversight of the house of YHWH, and let them give it to the workmen who are at the house of YHWH, repairing the house —
that is, to the carpenters and to the builders and to the masons — and let them use it for buying timber and quarried stone to repair the house.
But no accounting shall be asked of them for the money that is delivered into their hand, for they deal honestly."
Hilkiah the high priest says to Shaphan the secretary, "I have found the Book of the Law in the house of YHWH." Hilkiah gives the book to Shaphan and he reads it.

Shaphan the secretary comes to the king and reports to the king, "Your servants have emptied out the money that was found in the house and have delivered it into the hand of the workmen who have the oversight of the house of YHWH."
Then Shaphan the secretary tells the king, "Hilkiah the priest has given me a book." And Shaphan reads it before the king.
When the king hears the words of the Book of the Law, he tears his clothes.
The king commands Hilkiah the priest and Ahikam the son of Shaphan and Achbor the son of Micaiah and Shaphan the secretary and Asaiah the king's servant, saying,

"Go, inquire of YHWH for me, and for the people, and for all Judah, concerning the words of this book that has been found. For great is the wrath of YHWH that is kindled against us, because our fathers have not obeyed the words of this book, to do according to all that is written concerning us."

So Hilkiah the priest, and Ahikam, and Achbor, and Shaphan, and Asaiah go to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum the son of Tikvah, son of Harhas, keeper of the wardrobe — now she lives in Jerusalem in the Second Quarter — and they speak with her.
She says to them, "Thus says YHWH, the God of Israel: 'Tell the man who sent you to me,
Thus says YHWH, Behold, I will bring disaster upon this place and upon its inhabitants, all the words of the book that the king of Judah has read.

Because they have forsaken me and have made offerings to other gods, that they might provoke me to anger with all the work of their hands, therefore my wrath will be kindled against this place and it will not be quenched.
But to the king of Judah, who sent you to inquire of YHWH, thus shall you say to him: Thus says YHWH, the God of Israel, concerning the words that you have heard:

Because your heart was penitent, and you humbled yourself before YHWH when you heard how I spoke against this place and against its inhabitants, that they should become a desolation and a curse, and you have torn your clothes and wept before me, I also have heard you, declares YHWH.

Therefore, behold, I will gather you to your fathers, and you shall be gathered to your grave in peace, and your eyes shall not see all the disaster that I will bring upon this place.'" And they bring back word to the king.
Then the king sends, and all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem are gathered to him.

The king goes up to the house of YHWH, and with him all the men of Judah and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem and the priests and the prophets, all the people, both small and great. He reads in their hearing all the words of the Book of the Covenant that had been found in the house of YHWH.

The king stands by the pillar and makes a covenant before YHWH, to walk after YHWH and to keep his commandments and his testimonies and his statutes with all his heart and all his soul, to perform the words of this covenant that were written in this book. And all the people join in the covenant.

The king commands Hilkiah the high priest and the priests of the second order and the keepers of the threshold to bring out of the temple of YHWH all the vessels made for Baal, for Asherah, and for all the host of heaven. He burns them outside Jerusalem in the fields of the Kidron and carries their ashes to Bethel.

He deposes the priests whom the kings of Judah had ordained to make offerings in the high places at the cities of Judah and around Jerusalem; those also who burned incense to Baal, to the sun and the moon and the constellations and all the host of the heavens.

He brings out the Asherah from the house of YHWH, outside Jerusalem, to the brook Kidron, and burns it at the brook Kidron and beats it to dust and casts the dust of it upon the graves of the common people.
He breaks down the houses of the male cult prostitutes that were in the house of YHWH, where the women wove hangings for the Asherah.

He brings all the priests out of the cities of Judah, and defiles the high places where the priests had made offerings, from Geba to Beersheba. He breaks down the high places of the gates that were at the entrance of the gate of Joshua the governor of the city, which were on one's left at the gate of the city.
However, the priests of the high places do not come up to the altar of YHWH in Jerusalem, but they eat unleavened bread among their brothers.
He defiles Topheth, which is in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, that no one might burn his son or his daughter as an offering to Molech.

He removes the horses that the kings of Judah had dedicated to the sun, at the entrance to the house of YHWH, by the chamber of Nathan-melech the chamberlain, which was in the precincts. He burns the chariots of the sun with fire.

The altars on the roof of the upper chamber of Ahaz, which the kings of Judah had made, and the altars that Manasseh had made in the two courts of the house of YHWH, the king beats down and breaks in pieces and casts the dust of them into the brook Kidron.

The king defiles the high places that were east of Jerusalem, to the south of the Mount of Corruption, which Solomon the king of Israel had built for Ashtoreth the abomination of the Sidonians, and for Chemosh the abomination of Moab, and for Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites.
He breaks in pieces the pillars and cuts down the Asherim and fills their places with the bones of men.

Moreover, the altar at Bethel, the high place erected by Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin — that altar also and the high place he breaks down and he burns the high place and beats it to dust. He also burns the Asherah.

As Josiah turned, he sees the tombs there on the mount. He sends and takes the bones out of the tombs and burns them on the altar and defiles it, according to the word of YHWH that the man of God proclaimed, who had predicted these things.

Then he says, "What is that monument that I see?" The men of the city tell him, "It is the tomb of the man of God who came from Judah and predicted these things that you have done against the altar at Bethel."
He says, "Let him be; let no man move his bones." So they let his bones alone, with the bones of the prophet who came out of Samaria.

Josiah also removes all the shrines of the high places that are in the cities of Samaria, which kings of Israel had made, provoking YHWH to anger. He does to them according to all that he had done at Bethel.
He sacrifices on the altars all the priests of the high places who were there and burns human bones on them. Then he returns to Jerusalem.
The king commands all the people, "Keep the Passover to YHWH your God, as it is written in this Book of the Covenant."
For no such Passover had been kept since the days of the judges who judged Israel, or during all the days of the kings of Israel or of the kings of Judah.
But in the eighteenth year of King Josiah this Passover is kept to YHWH in Jerusalem.

Moreover, Josiah puts away the mediums and the necromancers and the household gods and the idols and all the abominations that are seen in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem, that he might establish the words of the law that were written in the book that Hilkiah the priest found in the house of YHWH.
Before him there was no king like him, who turned to YHWH with all his heart and with all his soul and with all his might, according to all the Law of Moses, nor did any like him arise after him.
Still YHWH did not turn from the burning of his great wrath, by which his anger was kindled against Judah, because of all the provocations with which Manasseh had provoked him.
YHWH says, "I will remove Judah also out of my sight, as I have removed Israel, and I will cast off this city that I have chosen, Jerusalem, and the house of which I said, My name shall be there."
Now the rest of the acts of Josiah and all that he did — are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
In his days Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt went up to the king of Assyria to the river Euphrates. King Josiah goes to meet him, and Pharaoh Neco kills him at Megiddo, when he sees him.

His servants carry him dead in a chariot from Megiddo and bring him to Jerusalem and bury him in his own tomb. The people of the land take Jehoahaz the son of Josiah and anointed him and make him king in his father's place.
Jehoahaz is twenty-three years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns three months in Jerusalem. His mother's name is Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
He does what is evil in the sight of YHWH, according to all that his fathers had done.
Pharaoh Neco puts him in bonds at Riblah in the land of Hamath, that he might not reign in Jerusalem, and laid on the land a tribute of a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.
Pharaoh Neco makes Eliakim the son of Josiah king in the place of Josiah his father, and changed his name to Jehoiakim. But he took Jehoahaz away, and he comes to Egypt and dies there.

Jehoiakim gives the silver and the gold to Pharaoh, but he taxes the land to give the money according to the command of Pharaoh. He exacts the silver and the gold of the people of the land, from everyone according to his assessment, to give it to Pharaoh Neco.
Jehoiakim is twenty-five years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother's name is Zebidah the daughter of Pedaiah of Rumah.
He does what is evil in the sight of YHWH, according to all that his fathers had done.
In his days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up, and Jehoiakim becomes his servant for three years. Then he turns and rebels against him.

YHWH sends against him bands of the Chaldeans and bands of the Syrians and bands of the Moabites and bands of the Ammonites and sends them against Judah to destroy it, according to the word of YHWH that he spoke by his servants the prophets.
Surely this comes upon Judah at the command of YHWH, to remove them out of his sight, for the sins of Manasseh, according to all that he had done,
and also for the innocent blood that he had shed. For he filled Jerusalem with innocent blood, and YHWH would not pardon.
Now the rest of the deeds of Jehoiakim and all that he did — are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
So Jehoiakim lies down with his fathers, and Jehoiachin his son reigns in his place.
The king of Egypt does not come again out of his land, for the king of Babylon had taken all that belonged to the king of Egypt from the Brook of Egypt to the river Euphrates.
Jehoiachin is eighteen years old when he becomes king, and he reigns three months in Jerusalem. His mother's name is Nehushta the daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem.
He does what is evil in the sight of YHWH, according to all that his father had done.
At that time the servants of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up to Jerusalem, and the city is besieged.
Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to the city while his servants were besieging it.

Jehoiachin king of Judah gives himself up to the king of Babylon — himself and his mother and his servants and his officials and his palace officials. The king of Babylon takes him prisoner in the eighth year of his reign.

He carries off all the treasures of the house of YHWH and the treasures of the king's house, and cuts in pieces all the vessels of gold in the temple of YHWH, which Solomon king of Israel had made, as YHWH had foretold.

He carries away all Jerusalem and all the officials and all the mighty men of valor — ten thousand captives — and all the craftsmen and the smiths. None remained, except the poorest people of the land.
He carries away Jehoiachin to Babylon. The king's mother, the king's wives, his officials, and the chief men of the land — he takes into captivity from Jerusalem to Babylon.
All the men of valor — seven thousand — and the craftsmen and the metal workers — one thousand — all of them strong and fit for war, these also the king of Babylon brings captive to Babylon.
The king of Babylon makes Mattaniah, Jehoiachin's uncle, king in his place, and changes his name to Zedekiah.
Zedekiah is twenty-one years old when he becomes king, and he reigns eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother's name is Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
He does what is evil in the sight of YHWH, according to all that Jehoiakim had done.
For because of the anger of YHWH it comes to the point in Jerusalem and Judah that he cast them out from his presence. Zedekiah rebels against the king of Babylon.

In the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came with all his army against Jerusalem and laid siege to it. They built siegeworks all around it.
So the city is besieged until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
On the ninth day of the fourth month the famine was so severe in the city that there was no food for the people of the land.

Then a breach is made in the city, and all the men of war fled by night by the way of the gate between the two walls, by the king's garden, and the Chaldeans were around the city. They went in the direction of the Arabah.
But the army of the Chaldeans pursues the king and overtakes him in the plains of Jericho, and all his army is scattered from him.
Then they capture the king and bring him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah, and they pass sentence on him.
They slaughter the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and put out the eyes of Zedekiah and bound him in chains and took him to Babylon.
