In the fifth month, on the seventh day of the month — that was the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon — Nebuzaradan, the captain of the bodyguard, a servant of the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
He burns the house of YHWH and the king's house and all the houses of Jerusalem; every great house he burns down.
The whole army of the Chaldeans, who were with the captain of the guard, breaks down the walls around Jerusalem.

Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carried into exile the rest of the people who were left in the city and the deserters who had deserted to the king of Babylon, together with the rest of the multitude.
But the captain of the guard left some of the poorest of the land to be vinedressers and plowmen.
The pillars of bronze that were in the house of YHWH, and the stands and the bronze sea that were in the house of YHWH, the Chaldeans broke in pieces and carried the bronze to Babylon.
They took away the pots and the shovels and the snuffers and the dishes for incense and all the vessels of bronze used in the temple service,
the fire pans also and the bowls. What was of gold the captain of the guard took away as gold, and what was of silver, as silver.
As for the two pillars, the one sea, and the stands that Solomon had made for the house of YHWH, the bronze of all these vessels was beyond weight.

The height of the one pillar was eighteen cubits, and on it was a capital of bronze. The height of the capital was three cubits. A latticework and pomegranates, all of bronze, were all around the capital. And the second pillar had the same, with the latticework.
The captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest and Zephaniah the second priest and the three keepers of the threshold.

From the city he took an officer who had been in command of the men of war and five men of the king's council who were found in the city; and the secretary of the commander of the army, who mustered the people of the land; and sixty men of the people of the land who were found in the city.
Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
The king of Babylon struck them down and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah was taken into exile out of its land.
He appointed Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, governor over the people who remained in the land of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had left.

Now when all the captains of the forces in the open country and their men heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah governor, they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah — Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and Johanan the son of Kareah, and Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah the son of the Maacathite — they and their men.
Gedaliah swears to them and their men, saying, "Do not be afraid because of the Chaldean officials. Live in the land and serve the king of Babylon and it shall be well with you."

But in the seventh month, Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, son of Elishama, of the royal family, came with ten men and struck down Gedaliah and put him to death along with the Jews and the Chaldeans who were with him at Mizpah.
Then all the people, both small and great, and the captains of the forces arose and went to Egypt, for they were afraid of the Chaldeans.

In the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the year that he began to reign, graciously freed Jehoiachin king of Judah from prison.
He speaks kindly to him and gives him a seat above the seats of the kings who were with him in Babylon.
So Jehoiachin puts off his prison garments. Every day of his life he dined regularly at the king's table.
His allowance was a regular allowance from the king, a portion every day, all the days of his life.
From Adam to Abraham · 1:1–27
Adam, Seth, Enosh,
Kenan, Mahalalel, Jared,
Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech,
Noah — Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
The sons of Japheth: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
The sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
The sons of Javan: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Rodanim.
The sons of Ham: Cush, Egypt, Put, and Canaan.
The sons of Cush: Seba, Havilah, Sabta, Raamah, and Sabteca. The sons of Raamah: Sheba and Dedan.
Cush fathers Nimrod — the first on earth to become a mighty warrior.
Egypt fathers Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim,
Pathrusim, Casluhim — from whom the Philistines come — and Caphtorim.
Canaan fathers Sidon his firstborn, and Heth,
and the Jebusites, the Amorites, the Girgashites,
the Hivites, the Arkites, the Sinites,
the Arvadites, the Zemarites, and the Hamathites.
The sons of Shem: Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, Aram, Uz, Hul, Gether, and Meshech.
Arpachshad fathers Shelah, and Shelah fathers Eber.
Two sons are born to Eber. The name of the one is Peleg, for in his days the earth is divided; and his brother's name is Joktan.
Joktan fathers Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,
Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,
Ebal, Abimael, Sheba,
Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab — all these are the sons of Joktan.
Shem, Arpachshad, Shelah,
Eber, Peleg, Reu,
Serug, Nahor, Terah,
Abram — that is, Abraham.
The Sons of Abraham · 1:28–34
The sons of Abraham: Isaac and Ishmael.
These are their genealogies: the firstborn of Ishmael is Nebaioth; then Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, Tema,
Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah. These are the sons of Ishmael.
The sons of Keturah, Abraham's concubine: she bears Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. The sons of Jokshan: Sheba and Dedan.
The sons of Midian: Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these are the sons of Keturah.
Abraham fathers Isaac. The sons of Isaac: Esau and Israel.
The Sons of Esau and Seir · 1:35–54
The sons of Esau: Eliphaz, Reuel, Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
The sons of Eliphaz: Teman, Omar, Zephi, Gatam, Kenaz, Timna, and Amalek.
The sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.
The sons of Seir: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan.
The sons of Lotan: Hori and Homam; and Timna is Lotan's sister.
The sons of Shobal: Alian, Manahath, Ebal, Shephi, and Onam. The sons of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah.
The son of Anah: Dishon. The sons of Dishon: Hamran, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
The sons of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Jaakan. The sons of Dishan: Uz and Aran.
These are the kings who reign in the land of Edom before any king reigns over the Israelites: Bela son of Beor, whose city is named Dinhabah.
When Bela dies, Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah reigns in his place.
When Jobab dies, Husham from the land of the Temanites reigns in his place.
When Husham dies, Hadad son of Bedad reigns in his place — he defeats Midian in the field of Moab — and the name of his city is Avith.
When Hadad dies, Samlah from Masrekah reigns in his place.
When Samlah dies, Shaul from Rehoboth on the Euphrates reigns in his place.
When Shaul dies, Baal-hanan son of Achbor reigns in his place.
When Baal-hanan dies, Hadad reigns in his place; the name of his city is Pai, and his wife's name is Mehetabel daughter of Matred, daughter of Me-zahab.
Then Hadad dies. The chiefs of Edom are: chief Timna, chief Aliah, chief Jetheth,
chief Oholibamah, chief Elah, chief Pinon,
chief Kenaz, chief Teman, chief Mibzar,
chief Magdiel, and chief Iram. These are the chiefs of Edom.
The Sons of Israel · 2:1–2
These are the sons of Israel: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun,
Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.
The Line of Judah to David · 2:3–17
The sons of Judah: Er, Onan, and Shelah — three are born to him by Bath-shua the Canaanite woman. Er, Judah's firstborn, is wicked in the sight of the LORD, and he puts him to death.
Tamar, his daughter-in-law, bears him Perez and Zerah. Judah has five sons in all.
The sons of Perez: Hezron and Hamul.
The sons of Zerah: Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Dara — five in all.
The son of Carmi: Achar, who troubles Israel by violating the devoted thing.
The son of Ethan: Azariah.
The sons of Hezron who are born to him: Jerahmeel, Ram, and Chelubai.
Ram fathers Amminadab, and Amminadab fathers Nahshon, prince of the sons of Judah.
Nahshon fathers Salma, and Salma fathers Boaz.
Boaz fathers Obed, and Obed fathers Jesse.
Jesse fathers Eliab his firstborn, Abinadab the second, Shimea the third,
Nethanel the fourth, Raddai the fifth,
Ozem the sixth, David the seventh.
Their sisters are Zeruiah and Abigail. The sons of Zeruiah: Abishai, Joab, and Asahel — three.
Abigail bears Amasa, and the father of Amasa is Jether the Ishmaelite.
The Sons of Hezron: Caleb · 2:18–24
Caleb son of Hezron fathers children by his wife Azubah and by Jerioth; these are her sons: Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.

Hur fathers Uri, and Uri fathers Bezalel.
Afterward Hezron goes in to the daughter of Machir, father of Gilead, whom he marries when he is sixty years old; she bears him Segub.
Segub fathers Jair, who has twenty-three cities in the land of Gilead.
But Geshur and Aram take Havvoth-jair from them, with Kenath and its villages — sixty towns. All these are the sons of Machir, father of Gilead.
After Hezron dies in Caleb-ephrathah, Hezron's wife Abijah bears him Ashhur the father of Tekoa.

The sons of Jerahmeel, the firstborn of Hezron: Ram his firstborn, Bunah, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah.

The sons of Ram, the firstborn of Jerahmeel: Maaz, Jamin, and Eker.
The sons of Onam: Shammai and Jada. The sons of Shammai: Nadab and Abishur.
The name of Abishur's wife is Abihail, and she bears him Ahban and Molid.
The sons of Nadab: Seled and Appaim. Seled dies without sons.

Attai fathers Nathan, and Nathan fathers Zabad.
Zabad fathers Ephlal, and Ephlal fathers Obed.
Obed fathers Jehu, and Jehu fathers Azariah.

The sons of Caleb, the brother of Jerahmeel: Mesha his firstborn, who is the father of Ziph, and the sons of Mareshah the father of Hebron.

The son of Shammai: Maon, and Maon is the father of Beth-zur.

The Sons of David Born in Hebron · 3:1–4
These are the sons of David born to him in Hebron: the firstborn Amnon, by Ahinoam the Jezreelite; the second Daniel, by Abigail the Carmelite;
the third Absalom, son of Maacah daughter of Talmai king of Geshur; the fourth Adonijah, son of Haggith;
the fifth Shephatiah, by Abital; the sixth Ithream, by his wife Eglah.

Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet — nine.

Solomon's son is Rehoboam. Abijah is his son, Asa his son, Jehoshaphat his son,
Joram his son, Ahaziah his son, Joash his son,
Amaziah his son, Azariah his son, Jotham his son,
Ahaz his son, Hezekiah his son, Manasseh his son,
Amon his son, Josiah his son.

And Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, Hasadiah, and Jushab-hesed — five.

The sons of Neariah: Elioenai, Hizkiah, and Azrikam — three.

The sons of Judah: Perez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur, and Shobal.
Reaiah son of Shobal fathers Jahath, and Jahath fathers Ahumai and Lahad. These are the clans of the Zorathites.

Jabez calls out to the God of Israel, saying, "Oh that you would bless me and enlarge my border, and that your hand might be with me, and that you would keep me from harm so that it might not bring me pain!" And God grants what he asks.
Chelub, the brother of Shuhah, fathers Mehir, who is the father of Eshton.
Eshton fathers Beth-rapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah the father of Ir-nahash. These are the men of Recah.

The sons of Shelah son of Judah: Er the father of Lecah, Laadah the father of Mareshah, and the clans of the linen workers' guild at Beth-ashbea,
and Jokim, and the men of Cozeba, and Joash, and Saraph, who ruled in Moab and returned to Jashubi-lehem. (These are ancient records.)

The Sons of Simeon · 4:24–43
The sons of Simeon: Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul;
Shallum his son, Mibsam his son, Mishma his son.
The sons of Mishma: Hammuel his son, Zaccur his son, Shimei his son.
Shimei has sixteen sons and six daughters; but his brothers do not have many children, and all their clan does not multiply as much as the sons of Judah.
They live in Beersheba, Moladah, Hazar-shual,
Bilhah, Ezem, Tolad,
Bethuel, Hormah, Ziklag,
Beth-marcaboth, Hazar-susim, Beth-biri, and Shaaraim. These are their cities until David reigns.
And their villages are Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Tochen, and Ashan — five cities —
along with all their villages that surround these cities as far as Baal. These are their settlements, and they keep a genealogical record.
Meshobab, Jamlech, Joshah son of Amaziah,
Joel, Jehu son of Joshibiah, son of Seraiah, son of Asiel,
Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel, Benaiah,
Ziza son of Shiphi, son of Allon, son of Jedaiah, son of Shimri, son of Shemaiah —
these, who are listed by name, are princes in their clans; and their ancestral houses increase greatly.
They go to the entrance of Gedor, to the east side of the valley, seeking pasture for their flocks.
They find fertile and good pasture, and the land is broad, quiet, and peaceful; for the former inhabitants there belong to Ham.

These, recorded by name, come in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah and strike down the tents of Ham and the Meunim who are found there; they devote them to destruction to this day and settle in their place, because there is pasture there for their flocks.
And some of them — five hundred men of the sons of Simeon — go to Mount Seir, with Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel, the sons of Ishi, at their head.
They strike down the remnant of the Amalekites who escape, and they live there to this day.
The Sons of Reuben · 5:1–10

The sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel — for he is the firstborn, but because he defiles his father's bed, his birthright is given to the sons of Joseph son of Israel, so that he is not enrolled in the genealogy according to the birthright.
Though Judah becomes strong among his brothers and a ruler comes from him, yet the birthright belongs to Joseph —
the sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
The sons of Joel: Shemaiah his son, Gog his son, Shimei his son,
Micah his son, Reaiah his son, Baal his son,
Beerah his son, whom Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria carries away into exile; he is a prince of the Reubenites.
And his kinsmen by their clans, when the genealogy of their generations is recorded: the chief Jeiel, and Zechariah,
and Bela son of Azaz, son of Shema, son of Joel, who lives in Aroer, as far as Nebo and Baal-meon.
He also lives to the east as far as the entrance of the desert this side of the Euphrates, because their livestock has multiplied in the land of Gilead.
And in the days of Saul they make war against the Hagrites, who fall into their hand; and they dwell in their tents throughout all the region east of Gilead.
The Sons of Gad · 5:11–17
The sons of Gad live alongside them in the land of Bashan as far as Salecah.
Joel the chief, Shapham the second, Janai, and Shaphat in Bashan.
And their kinsmen by their ancestral houses: Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, and Eber — seven.
These are the sons of Abihail son of Huri, son of Jaroah, son of Gilead, son of Michael, son of Jeshishai, son of Jahdo, son of Buz.
Ahi son of Abdiel, son of Guni, is chief in their ancestral house.
And they live in Gilead, in Bashan and in its villages, and in all the pasturelands of Sharon to their limits.
All of these are enrolled by genealogies in the days of Jotham king of Judah and in the days of Jeroboam king of Israel.
The Transjordanian War Against the Hagrites · 5:18–22

The sons of Reuben, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have valiant men who carry shield and sword, and draw the bow, trained for war — forty-four thousand seven hundred and sixty, ready for military service.
They wage war against the Hagrites, Jetur, Naphish, and Nodab.
And they receive help against them, and the Hagrites and all who are with them are given into their hands, because they cry to God in the battle, and he grants their plea, because they trust in him.
They carry off their livestock: fifty thousand camels, two hundred fifty thousand sheep, and two thousand donkeys; and they take a hundred thousand persons captive.
For many fall slain, because the war is from God. And they dwell in their place until the exile.
The Half-Tribe of Manasseh · 5:23–26
The members of the half-tribe of Manasseh live in the land, from Bashan to Baal-hermon, Senir, and Mount Hermon; they are numerous.
These are the heads of their ancestral houses: Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel — mighty warriors, men of great renown, heads of their ancestral houses.
But they break faith with the God of their ancestors, and whore after the gods of the peoples of the land, whom God destroys before them.

So the God of Israel stirs up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria, the spirit of Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, and he takes them into exile — the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh — and brings them to Halah, Habor, Hara, and the river of Gozan, to this day.
The Sons of Levi · 6:1–3
The sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.

Eleazar fathers Phinehas, and Phinehas fathers Abishua,
and Abishua fathers Bukki, and Bukki fathers Uzzi,
and Uzzi fathers Zerahiah, and Zerahiah fathers Meraioth,
Meraioth fathers Amariah, and Amariah fathers Ahitub,
and Ahitub fathers Zadok, and Zadok fathers Ahimaaz,
and Ahimaaz fathers Azariah, and Azariah fathers Johanan,
and Johanan fathers Azariah — he is the one who serves as priest in the temple that Solomon builds in Jerusalem.
Azariah fathers Amariah, and Amariah fathers Ahitub,
and Ahitub fathers Zadok, and Zadok fathers Shallum,
and Shallum fathers Hilkiah, and Hilkiah fathers Azariah,

The sons of Levi: Gershom, Kohath, and Merari.

Joah his son, Iddo his son, Zerah his son, Jeatherai his son.

These are the men whom David puts in charge of the service of song in the house of the LORD after the ark rests there.

These are the men who serve, and their sons: Of the sons of the Kohathites: Heman the singer, son of Joel, son of Samuel,
son of Elkanah, son of Jeroham, son of Eliel, son of Toah,
son of Zuph, son of Elkanah, son of Mahath, son of Amasai,
son of Elkanah, son of Joel, son of Azariah, son of Zephaniah,
son of Tahath, son of Assir, son of Ebiasaph, son of Korah,
son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, son of Israel.

son of Michael, son of Baaseiah, son of Malchijah,
son of Ethni, son of Zerah, son of Adaiah,
son of Ethan, son of Zimmah, son of Shimei,
son of Jahath, son of Gershom, son of Levi.

son of Hashabiah, son of Amaziah, son of Hilkiah,
son of Amzi, son of Bani, son of Shemer,
son of Mahli, son of Mushi, son of Merari, son of Levi.
And their brothers the Levites are appointed for all the service of the tabernacle of the house of God.
Aaron and His Sons · 6:49–53

But Aaron and his sons make offerings on the altar of burnt offering and on the altar of incense, for all the work of the most holy place, and to make atonement for Israel, according to all that Moses the servant of God commands.
These are the sons of Aaron: Eleazar his son, Phinehas his son, Abishua his son,
Bukki his son, Uzzi his son, Zerahiah his son,
Meraioth his son, Amariah his son, Ahitub his son,
Zadok his son, Ahimaaz his son.
The Levitical Cities · 6:54–81
These are their dwelling places according to their settlements within their borders: to the sons of Aaron of the clans of the Kohathites, for the lot falls to them first,
they give Hebron in the land of Judah and its surrounding pasturelands.
But the fields of the city and its villages they give to Caleb son of Jephunneh.
To the sons of Aaron they give the cities of refuge: Hebron, Libnah with its pasturelands, Jattir, Eshtemoa with its pasturelands,
Hilen with its pasturelands, Debir with its pasturelands,
Ashan with its pasturelands, and Beth-shemesh with its pasturelands;
and from the tribe of Benjamin: Geba with its pasturelands, Alemeth with its pasturelands, and Anathoth with its pasturelands. All their cities throughout their clans are thirteen cities.
To the rest of the Kohathites are given by lot out of the clan of the tribe, out of the half-tribe, the half of Manasseh, ten cities.

To the Gershomites according to their clans are given out of the tribe of Issachar, out of the tribe of Asher, out of the tribe of Naphtali, and out of the tribe of Manasseh in Bashan, thirteen cities.
To the Merarites according to their clans are given by lot out of the tribe of Reuben, out of the tribe of Gad, and out of the tribe of Zebulun, twelve cities.
So the people of Israel give the Levites the cities with their pasturelands.
They give by lot out of the tribe of the sons of Judah, out of the tribe of the sons of Simeon, and out of the tribe of the sons of Benjamin, these cities that are mentioned by name.
And some of the clans of the sons of Kohath have cities of their territory out of the tribe of Ephraim.
They give them the cities of refuge: Shechem with its pasturelands in the hill country of Ephraim, Gezer with its pasturelands,
Jokmeam with its pasturelands, Beth-horon with its pasturelands,
Aijalon with its pasturelands, Gath-rimmon with its pasturelands;
and out of the half-tribe of Manasseh, Aner with its pasturelands, and Bileam with its pasturelands, for the rest of the clans of the sons of Kohath.
To the Gershomites are given out of the clan of the half-tribe of Manasseh: Golan in Bashan with its pasturelands and Ashtaroth with its pasturelands;
and out of the tribe of Issachar: Kedesh with its pasturelands, Daberath with its pasturelands,
Ramoth with its pasturelands, and Anem with its pasturelands;
and out of the tribe of Asher: Mashal with its pasturelands, Abdon with its pasturelands,
Hukok with its pasturelands, and Rehob with its pasturelands;
and out of the tribe of Naphtali: Kedesh in Galilee with its pasturelands, Hammon with its pasturelands, and Kiriathaim with its pasturelands.
To the rest of the Merarites are given out of the tribe of Zebulun: Rimmono with its pasturelands, Tabor with its pasturelands;
and beyond the Jordan at Jericho, on the east side of the Jordan, out of the tribe of Reuben: Bezer in the wilderness with its pasturelands, Jahzah with its pasturelands,
Kedemoth with its pasturelands, and Mephaath with its pasturelands;
and out of the tribe of Gad: Ramoth in Gilead with its pasturelands, Mahanaim with its pasturelands,
Heshbon with its pasturelands, and Jazer with its pasturelands.
The Sons of Issachar · 7:1–5
The sons of Issachar: Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron — four.

The sons of Tola: Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam, and Shemuel, heads of their ancestral houses — of Tola, mighty warriors of their generations. Their number in the days of David is twenty-two thousand six hundred.
The son of Uzzi: Izrahiah. And the sons of Izrahiah: Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Isshiah — five, all of them chiefs.
And along with them, by their generations, according to their ancestral houses, are units of the army for war, thirty-six thousand — for they have many wives and sons.
Their kinsmen belonging to all the clans of Issachar, mighty warriors, are enrolled by genealogies — in all eighty-seven thousand.
The Sons of Benjamin · 7:6–12
The sons of Benjamin: Bela, Becher, and Jediael — three.
The sons of Bela: Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri — five, heads of ancestral houses, mighty warriors; and their enrollment by genealogies is twenty-two thousand thirty-four.
The sons of Becher: Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth. All these are the sons of Becher.
And their enrollment by genealogies, according to their generations, as heads of their ancestral houses, mighty warriors, is twenty thousand two hundred.
The son of Jediael: Bilhan. And the sons of Bilhan: Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar.
All these are sons of Jediael according to their heads of ancestral houses, mighty warriors — seventeen thousand two hundred, ready for military service.
And Shuppim and Huppim are the sons of Ir; Hushim is the son of Aher.
The Sons of Naphtali · 7:13
The sons of Naphtali: Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, and Shallum — the sons of Bilhah.
The Sons of Manasseh · 7:14–19
The sons of Manasseh: Asriel, whom his Aramean concubine bears; she also bears Machir the father of Gilead.
And Machir takes a wife for Huppim and Shuppim. The name of his sister is Maacah. And the name of the second is Zelophehad; and Zelophehad has daughters.
And Maacah the wife of Machir bears a son, and she names him Peresh; and the name of his brother is Sheresh; and his sons are Ulam and Rakem.
The son of Ulam: Bedan. These are the sons of Gilead son of Machir, son of Manasseh.
And his sister Hammolecheth bears Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.
The sons of Shemida are Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam.
The Sons of Ephraim · 7:20–29
The sons of Ephraim: Shuthelah, and Bered his son, Tahath his son, Eleadah his son, Tahath his son,
Zabad his son, Shuthelah his son, and Ezer and Elead. Now the men of Gath who are born in the land kill them, because they come down to raid their livestock.
And Ephraim their father mourns many days, and his brothers come to comfort him.
And Ephraim goes in to his wife, and she conceives and bears a son. And he names him Beriah, because disaster has come upon his house.
His daughter is Sheerah, who builds both Lower and Upper Beth-horon, and Uzzen-sheerah.
Rephah is his son, Resheph his son, Telah his son, Tahan his son,
Ladan his son, Ammihud his son, Elishama his son,
Nun his son, Joshua his son.
Their possessions and settlements are Bethel and its towns, and to the east Naaran, and to the west Gezer and its towns, Shechem and its towns, and Ayyah and its towns.
And along the borders of the sons of Manasseh, Beth-shean and its towns, Taanach and its towns, Megiddo and its towns, Dor and its towns. In these live the sons of Joseph son of Israel.
The Sons of Asher · 7:30–40
The sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah; and Serah is their sister.
The sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel, who is the father of Birzaith.
Heber fathers Japhlet, Shomer, Hotham, and Shua their sister.
The sons of Japhlet: Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath — these are the sons of Japhlet.
The sons of Shemer: Ahi, Rohgah, Jehubbah, and Aram.
The sons of his brother Helem: Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal.
The sons of Zophah: Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, Imrah,
Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran, and Beera.
The sons of Jether: Jephunneh, Pispa, and Ara.
The sons of Ulla: Arah, Hanniel, and Rizia.
All these are sons of Asher, heads of ancestral houses, approved, mighty warriors, chiefs of the princes. Their enrollment by genealogies for service in war is twenty-six thousand men.
The Sons of Benjamin · 8:1–28
Benjamin fathers Bela his firstborn, Ashbel the second, Aharah the third,
Nohah the fourth, and Rapha the fifth.
And the sons of Bela are Addar, Gera, Abihud,
Abishua, Naaman, Ahoah,
Gera, Shephuphan, and Huram.
These are the sons of Ehud — these are the heads of the ancestral houses of the inhabitants of Geba, and they are carried into exile to Manahath:
Naaman, Ahijah, and Gera — that is, Heglam, who fathers Uzza and Ahihud.
And Shaharaim fathers sons in the country of Moab after he sends away his wives Hushim and Baara.
He fathers Jobab, Zibia, Mesha, Malcam,
Jeuz, Sachia, and Mirmah — these are his sons, heads of ancestral houses.
And by Hushim he fathers Abitub and Elpaal.
The sons of Elpaal: Eber, Misham, and Shemed, who builds Ono and Lod with its towns;
and Beriah and Shema, who are heads of ancestral houses of the inhabitants of Aijalon, who put to flight the inhabitants of Gath.
And Ahio, Shashak, and Jeremoth;
Zebadiah, Arad, Eder,
Michael, Ishpah, and Joha are sons of Beriah.
Zebadiah, Meshullam, Hizki, Heber,
Ishmerai, Izliah, and Jobab are the sons of Elpaal.
Jakim, Zichri, Zabdi,
Elienai, Zillethai, Eliel,
Adaiah, Beraiah, and Shimrath are the sons of Shimei.
Ishpan, Eber, Eliel,
Abdon, Zichri, Hanan,
Hananiah, Elam, Anthothijah,
Iphdeiah, and Penuel are the sons of Shashak.
Shamsherai, Shehariah, Athaliah,
Jaareshiah, Elijah, and Zichri are the sons of Jeroham.
These are the heads of ancestral houses, according to their generations, chiefs. These live in Jerusalem.
The Ancestors of Saul · 8:29–40
Jeiel the father of Gibeon lives in Gibeon, and the name of his wife is Maacah.
His firstborn son is Abdon, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Nadab,
Gedor, Ahio, Zecher,
and Mikloth, who fathers Shimeah. And these also live opposite their kinsmen in Jerusalem.
Ner fathers Kish, and Kish fathers Saul, and Saul fathers Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Esh-baal.
The son of Jonathan: Merib-baal; and Merib-baal fathers Micah.
The sons of Micah: Pithon, Melech, Tarea, and Ahaz.
Ahaz fathers Jehoaddah, and Jehoaddah fathers Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri; Zimri fathers Moza.
Moza fathers Binea; Raphah is his son, Eleasah his son, Azel his son.
Azel has six sons, and these are their names: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan — all these are the sons of Azel.
The sons of Eshek his brother: Ulam his firstborn, Jeush the second, and Eliphelet the third.
The sons of Ulam are mighty warriors, archers; they have many sons and grandsons — one hundred fifty. All these are sons of Benjamin.
The Returned Exiles · 9:1–9
So all Israel is enrolled by genealogies; and these are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel. And Judah is carried away into exile in Babylon because of their unfaithfulness.
Now the first to live again in their possessions in their cities are Israel, the priests, the Levites, and the temple servants.
And some of the sons of Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh live in Jerusalem:
Uthai son of Ammihud, son of Omri, son of Imri, son of Bani, from the sons of Perez son of Judah.
And of the Shilonites: Asaiah the firstborn, and his sons.
Of the sons of Zerah: Jeuel and their kinsmen — six hundred ninety.
Of the sons of Benjamin: Sallu son of Meshullam, son of Hodaviah, son of Hassenuah,
Ibneiah son of Jeroham, Elah son of Uzzi, son of Michri, and Meshullam son of Shephatiah, son of Reuel, son of Ibnijah;
and their kinsmen according to their generations — nine hundred fifty-six. All these are heads of ancestral houses according to their fathers' houses.
The Returned Priests · 9:10–13
Of the priests: Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, Jachin,
and Azariah son of Hilkiah, son of Meshullam, son of Zadok, son of Meraioth, son of Ahitub, the chief officer of the house of God;
and Adaiah son of Jeroham, son of Pashhur, son of Malchijah, and Maasai son of Adiel, son of Jahzerah, son of Meshullam, son of Meshillemith, son of Immer;
and their kinsmen, heads of their ancestral houses — one thousand seven hundred sixty, very able men for the work of the service of the house of God.
The Returned Levites · 9:14–16
Of the Levites: Shemaiah son of Hasshub, son of Azrikam, son of Hashabiah, of the sons of Merari;
and Bakbakkar, Heresh, Galal, and Mattaniah son of Mica, son of Zichri, son of Asaph;
and Obadiah son of Shemaiah, son of Galal, son of Jeduthun, and Berechiah son of Asa, son of Elkanah, who lives in the villages of the Netophathites.
The Gatekeepers · 9:17–27
The gatekeepers: Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, and Ahiman; and their brother Shallum is the chief;
stationed until now in the king's gate on the east side, these are the gatekeepers of the camps of the sons of Levi.

Shallum son of Kore, son of Ebiasaph, son of Korah, and his kinsmen of his ancestral house, the Korahites, are in charge of the work of the service, keepers of the thresholds of the tent; and their ancestors have been in charge of the camp of the LORD, keepers of the entrance.
And Phinehas son of Eleazar is their chief in former times; the LORD is with him.
Zechariah son of Meshelemiah is gatekeeper at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

All these, who are chosen as gatekeepers at the thresholds, are two hundred twelve. They are enrolled by genealogies in their villages. David and Samuel the seer establish them in their office of trust.
So they and their sons are in charge of the gates of the house of the LORD, that is, the house of the tent, as guards.
The gatekeepers are on the four sides, east, west, north, and south.
And their kinsmen who are in their villages come in every seven days, in turn, to be with these;
for the four chief gatekeepers, who are Levites, are in a position of trust, and they are over the chambers and the treasuries of the house of God.
And they spend the night around the house of God, for on them lies the duty of watching, and they have charge of opening it every morning.
Other Temple Servants · 9:28–34
Some of them are in charge of the utensils of service, for they count them when they bring them in and when they take them out.
Some of them are appointed over the furnishings and over all the utensils of the sanctuary, and over the fine flour, the wine, the oil, the incense, and the spices.
Some of the sons of the priests prepare the mixing of the spices.
And Mattithiah, one of the Levites, the firstborn of Shallum the Korahite, is in charge of making the flat cakes.
And some of their kinsmen of the sons of the Kohathites are in charge of the showbread, to prepare it every Sabbath.
Now these are the singers, the heads of ancestral houses of the Levites, who live in the chambers of the temple free from other service, for they are on duty day and night.
These are the heads of the ancestral houses of the Levites, according to their generations, chiefs; these live in Jerusalem.
The Ancestors of Saul Repeated · 9:35–44
In Gibeon lives Jeiel the father of Gibeon, and the name of his wife is Maacah.
His firstborn son is Abdon, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab,
Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah, and Mikloth.
Mikloth fathers Shimeam; and these also live opposite their kinsmen in Jerusalem.
Ner fathers Kish, and Kish fathers Saul, and Saul fathers Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Esh-baal.
The son of Jonathan: Merib-baal; and Merib-baal fathers Micah.
The sons of Micah: Pithon, Melech, Tahrea, and Ahaz.
Ahaz fathers Jarah, and Jarah fathers Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri; Zimri fathers Moza.
Moza fathers Binea; and Rephaiah is his son, Eleasah his son, Azel his son.
Azel has six sons and these are their names: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan — these are the sons of Azel.
The Death of Saul · 10:1–7
Now the Philistines fight against Israel; and the men of Israel flee before the Philistines and fall slain on Mount Gilboa.
The Philistines overtake Saul and his sons, and the Philistines strike down Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua, the sons of Saul.
The battle presses hard against Saul, and the archers find him, and he is wounded by the archers.

Then Saul says to his armour-bearer, "Draw your sword and thrust me through with it, lest these uncircumcised men come and mistreat me." But his armour-bearer is unwilling, for he is very afraid. So Saul takes his own sword and falls upon it.
And when his armour-bearer sees that Saul is dead, he also falls upon his sword and dies.
Thus Saul dies — he and his three sons and all his house dies together.
And when all the men of Israel who are in the valley see that the army has fled and that Saul and his sons are dead, they abandon their cities and flee; and the Philistines come and settle in them.
The Philistines and the Body of Saul · 10:8–12
The next day, when the Philistines come to strip the slain, they find Saul and his sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.
They strip him and take his head and his armour, and they send messengers throughout the land of the Philistines to carry the good news to their idols and to the people.
And they put his armour in the house of their gods and fastened his head in the temple of Dagon.
But when all Jabesh-gilead hears all that the Philistines have done to Saul,
all the valiant men arise and take away the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons, and bring them to Jabesh. And they bury their bones under the oak in Jabesh and fast seven days.
The Reason for Saul's Death · 10:13–14
So Saul dies for his unfaithfulness. He is unfaithful to the LORD in that he does not keep the command of the LORD, and also consults a medium, seeking guidance.
He does not seek guidance from the LORD. Therefore the LORD puts him to death and turns the kingdom over to David son of Jesse.
David Becomes King Over All Israel · 11:1–3
Then all Israel gathers to David at Hebron and says, "Behold, we are your bone and flesh.

In times past, even when Saul was king, it was you who led out and brought in Israel. And the LORD your God said to you, 'You shall be shepherd of my people Israel, and you shall be prince over my people Israel.'"

So all the elders of Israel come to the king at Hebron, and David makes a covenant with them at Hebron before the LORD. And they anoint David king over Israel, according to the word of the LORD by Samuel.
David Captures Jerusalem · 11:4–9
And David and all Israel go to Jerusalem — that is, Jebus — where the Jebusites are, the inhabitants of the land.
The inhabitants of Jebus say to David, "You will not come in here." Nevertheless David takes the stronghold of Zion — that is, the city of David.
David says, "Whoever strikes the Jebusites first shall be chief and commander." And Joab son of Zeruiah goes up first, so he becomes chief.
And David lives in the stronghold; therefore they call it the city of David.
And he builds the city all around from the Millo in complete circuit; and Joab restores the rest of the city.
And David grows greater and greater, for the LORD of hosts is with him.
The Three Warriors · 11:10–19
Now these are the chiefs of David's warriors, who give him strong support in his kingdom, together with all Israel, to make him king, according to the word of the LORD concerning Israel.
This is the list of David's warriors: Jashobeam, a Hachmonite, is chief of the thirty; he wields his spear against three hundred whom he kills at one time.
And next to him among the three mighty warriors is Eleazar son of Dodo, the Ahohite.
He is with David at Pas-dammim when the Philistines are gathered there for battle. There is a plot of ground full of barley, and the men flee from the Philistines.
But he takes his stand in the middle of the plot and defends it and kills the Philistines. And the LORD saves them by a great victory.
Three of the thirty chiefs go down to the rock to David at the cave of Adullam, when the army of Philistines is encamped in the Valley of Rephaim.
David is in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Philistines is at Bethlehem.
And David says longingly, "Oh that someone would give me water to drink from the well of Bethlehem that is by the gate!"

Then the three break through the camp of the Philistines and draw water out of the well of Bethlehem that was by the gate and carry it to David. But David will not drink it; he pours it out to the LORD

and says, "Far be it from me before my God that I should do this. Shall I drink the blood of these men who risked their lives? For at the risk of their lives they bring it." Therefore he will not drink it. These things the three mighty warriors do.
Abishai and Benaiah · 11:20–25
Now Abishai, the brother of Joab, is chief of the thirty. And he wields his spear against three hundred and kills them, and wins a name beside the three.
He is the most renowned of the thirty and becomes their commander, but he does not attain to the three.
And Benaiah son of Jehoiada is a valiant man of Kabzeel, a doer of great deeds. He strikes down two heroes of Moab. He also goes down and strikes down a lion in a pit on a day when snow has fallen.

And he strikes down an Egyptian man, a man of great stature, five cubits tall. The Egyptian has in his hand a spear like a weaver's beam, but Benaiah goes down to him with a staff and snatches the spear out of the Egyptian's hand and kills him with his own spear.
These things Benaiah son of Jehoiada does, and wins a name beside the three mighty warriors.
He is renowned among the thirty, but he does not attain to the three. And David sets him over his bodyguard.
The List of David's Warriors · 11:26–47
The warriors of the armies: Asahel brother of Joab, Elhanan son of Dodo of Bethlehem,
Shammoth of Harod, Helez the Pelonite,
Ira son of Ikkesh of Tekoa, Abiezer of Anathoth,
Sibbecai the Hushathite, Ilai the Ahohite,
Maharai of Netophah, Heled son of Baanah of Netophah,
Ithai son of Ribai of Gibeah of the sons of Benjamin, Benaiah of Pirathon,
Hurai of the brooks of Gaash, Abiel the Arbathite,

Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,
Uriah the Hittite, Zabad son of Ahlai,
Adina son of Shiza the Reubenite, a chief of the Reubenites, and thirty with him,
Hanan son of Maacah, and Joshaphat the Mithnite,
Uzzia the Ashterathite, Shama and Jeiel the sons of Hotham the Aroerite,
Jediael son of Shimri, and Joha his brother, the Tizite,
Eliel the Mahavite, and Jeribai and Joshaviah the sons of Elnaam, and Ithmah the Moabite,
Eliel, Obed, and Jaasiel the Mezobaite.
Warriors Who Join David at Ziklag · 12:1–7
Now these are the men who come to David at Ziklag, while he is still kept away from Saul son of Kish. They are among the mighty warriors who help him in war.
They are armed with bows and can use both the right hand and the left hand to hurl stones and shoot arrows with the bow. They are Benjaminites, kinsmen of Saul.
The chief is Ahiezer, then Joash, the sons of Shemaah the Gibeathite; also Jeziel and Pelet, the sons of Azmaveth; Beracah, Jehu of Anathoth,
Ishmaiah of Gibeon, a warrior among the thirty, a leader over the thirty; Jeremiah, Jahaziel, Johanan, Jozabad the Gederathite,
Eluzai, Jerimoth, Bealiah, Shemariah, Shephatiah the Haruphite;
Elkanah, Isshiah, Azarel, Joezer, and Jashobeam, the Korahites;
Joelah and Zebadiah, the sons of Jeroham of Gedor.
Gadites Who Join David in the Wilderness · 12:8–15

From the Gadites there come over to David at the stronghold in the wilderness mighty and experienced warriors, expert with shield and spear, whose faces are like the faces of lions, and who are swift as gazelles upon the mountains:
Ezer the chief, Obadiah second, Eliab third,
Mishmannah fourth, Jeremiah fifth,
Attai sixth, Eliel seventh,
Johanan eighth, Elzabad ninth,
Jeremiah tenth, Machbannai eleventh.
These Gadites are officers of the army; the least of them is a match for a hundred men, and the greatest for a thousand.
These are the men who cross the Jordan in the first month, when it is overflowing all its banks, and put to flight all those in the valleys, to the east and to the west.
Benjaminites and Judahites Who Come to David · 12:16–18
Some of the men of Benjamin and Judah come to the stronghold to David.

David goes out to meet them and says to them, "If you have come to me in peace to help me, my heart will be joined to you; but if to betray me to my adversaries, although there is no wrong in my hands, may the God of our ancestors see and rebuke you."
Then the Spirit comes upon Amasai, chief of the thirty, and he says:
"We are yours, O David,
and with you, O son of Jesse!
Peace, peace to you,
and peace to those who help you,
for your God helps you."
Then David receives them and makes them officers of his troops.
Manassites Who Defect to David · 12:19–22

Some of the men of Manasseh defect to David when he comes with the Philistines for the battle against Saul. Yet he does not help them, for the lords of the Philistines, after consultation, send him away, saying, "At the peril of our heads he will desert to his master Saul."
As he goes to Ziklag, these men of Manasseh defect to him: Adnah, Jozabad, Jediael, Michael, Jozabad, Elihu, and Zillethai, chiefs of thousands in Manasseh.
They help David against the band of raiders, for they are all mighty warriors and are commanders in the army.
For from day to day men come to David to help him, until there is a great army, like an army of God.
The Army That Comes to David at Hebron · 12:23–40
These are the numbers of the armed troops who come to David at Hebron to transfer the kingdom of Saul to him, according to the word of the LORD.
The men of Judah bearing shield and spear are six thousand eight hundred armed troops.
Of the sons of Simeon, mighty warriors fit for war: seven thousand one hundred.
Of the sons of Levi: four thousand six hundred.
The prince Jehoiada, of the house of Aaron, and with him are three thousand seven hundred.
Zadok, a young man mighty in valour, and twenty-two officers from his ancestral house.
Of the sons of Benjamin, kinsmen of Saul: three thousand — for until then the majority of them kept their allegiance to the house of Saul.
Of the sons of Ephraim: twenty thousand eight hundred, mighty warriors, men of renown in their ancestral houses.
Of the half-tribe of Manasseh: eighteen thousand, who are listed by name to come and make David king.
Of the sons of Issachar, men who have understanding of the times to know what Israel ought to do: two hundred chiefs, with all their kinsmen under their command.
Of Zebulun: fifty thousand seasoned troops, equipped for battle with all the weapons of war, with singleness of purpose.
Of Naphtali: a thousand commanders, and with them with shield and spear thirty-seven thousand.
Of the Danites: twenty-eight thousand six hundred equipped for battle.
Of Asher: forty thousand seasoned troops ready for battle.
Of the Reubenites and Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh from beyond the Jordan: a hundred and twenty thousand, equipped with all the weapons of war.
All these, warriors arrayed in battle order, come to Hebron with full intent to make David king over all Israel. Likewise all the rest of Israel are of a single mind to make David king.
And they are there with David for three days, eating and drinking, for their kinsmen have prepared for them.

And also their neighbors, from as far as Issachar and Zebulun and Naphtali, come bringing food on donkeys and on camels and on mules and on oxen — provisions of flour, figs, raisins, wine, oil, oxen, and sheep in abundance, for there is joy in Israel.
David Proposes to Bring the Ark · 13:1–4
David consults with the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and with every leader.

And David says to all the assembly of Israel, "If it seems good to you and if it is from the LORD our God, let us send abroad to our brothers who remain in all the lands of Israel, as well as to the priests and Levites in the cities that have pasturelands, that they may be gathered to us.
Then let us bring back the ark of our God to us, for we did not seek it in the days of Saul."

Then on that day David first appoints that thanksgiving be sung to the LORD by Asaph and his brothers.
Oh give thanks to the LORD; call upon his name;
make known his deeds among the peoples!
Sing to him, sing praises to him;
tell of all his wondrous works!
Glory in his holy name;
let the hearts of those who seek the LORD rejoice!
Seek the LORD and his strength;
seek his presence continually!
Remember the wondrous works that he has done,
his miracles and the judgments he uttered,
O offspring of Israel his servant,
children of Jacob, his chosen ones!
He is the LORD our God;
his judgments are in all the earth.
Remember his covenant forever,
the word that he commanded, for a thousand generations,
the covenant that he made with Abraham,
his sworn promise to Isaac,
which he confirmed to Jacob as a statute,
to Israel as an everlasting covenant,
saying, "To you I will give the land of Canaan,
as your portion for an inheritance."
When you were few in number,
of little account, and sojourners in it,
wandering from nation to nation,
from one kingdom to another people,
he allowed no one to oppress them;
he rebuked kings on their account,
saying, "Touch not my anointed ones,
do my prophets no harm!"
Sing to the LORD, all the earth!
Tell of his salvation from day to day.
Declare his glory among the nations,
his marvellous works among all the peoples!
For great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised,
and he is to be feared above all gods.
For all the gods of the peoples are worthless idols,
but the LORD made the heavens.
Splendour and majesty are before him;
strength and joy are in his place.
Ascribe to the LORD, O clans of the peoples,
ascribe to the LORD glory and strength!
Ascribe to the LORD the glory due his name;
bring an offering and come before him!
Worship the LORD in the splendour of holiness;
tremble before him, all the earth;
yes, the world is established; it shall never be moved.
Let the heavens be glad, and let the earth rejoice,
and let them say among the nations, "The LORD reigns!"
Let the sea roar, and all that fills it;
let the field exult, and everything in it!
Then shall the trees of the forest sing for joy
before the LORD, for he comes to judge the earth.
Oh give thanks to the LORD, for he is good;
for his steadfast love endures forever!
Say also: "Save us, O God of our salvation,
and gather and deliver us from among the nations,
that we may give thanks to your holy name
and glory in your praise."
Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel,
from everlasting to everlasting!"
And all the people say, "Amen!" and praise the LORD.

But that same night the word of God comes to Nathan, saying,
"Go and tell my servant David, 'Thus says the LORD: It is not you who will build me a house to dwell in.

In all places where I have moved with all Israel, did I speak a word with any of the judges of Israel, whom I commanded to shepherd my people, saying, Why have you not built me a house of cedar?'
Now, therefore, thus shall you say to my servant David: Thus says the LORD of hosts, I took you from the pasture, from following the sheep, to be the prince over my people Israel.

O LORD, for your servant's sake, and according to your own heart, you have done all this greatness, in making known all these great things.

But the princes of the Ammonites say to Hanun, "Do you think, because David has sent comforters to you, that he is honoring your father? Have not his servants come to you to search and to overthrow and to spy out the land?"

These are the sons of Levi by their fathers' houses, the heads of fathers' houses as they are listed according to the number of the names of the individuals from twenty years old and upward who were to do the work for the service of the house of the LORD.

And so the Levites no longer need to carry the tabernacle or any of the things for its service."

For their duty is to assist the sons of Aaron for the service of the house of the LORD, having the care of the courts and the chambers, the cleansing of all that is holy, and any work for the service of the house of God.

Their duty is also to assist with the showbread, the fine flour for the grain offering, the wafers of unleavened bread, the baked offering, the offering mixed with oil, and all measures of quantity or size.

David's Final Assembly · 28:1–8

David assembles at Jerusalem all the officials of Israel — the officials of the tribes, the officers of the divisions that serve the king, the commanders of thousands, the commanders of hundreds, the stewards of all the property and livestock of the king and his sons, together with the palace officials, the mighty men, and all the seasoned warriors.

Then King David rises to his feet and says: "Hear me, my brothers and my people. I had it in my heart to build a house of rest for the ark of the covenant of the LORD and for the footstool of our God, and I made preparations for building.
But God says to me, 'You may not build a house for my name, for you are a man of war and have shed blood.'

Yet the LORD God of Israel chose me from all my father's house to be king over Israel forever. For he chose Judah as leader, and in the house of Judah my father's house, and among my father's sons he takes pleasure in me to make me king over all Israel.
And of all my sons — for the LORD has given me many sons — he has chosen Solomon my son to sit on the throne of the kingdom of the LORD over Israel.
He says to me, 'It is Solomon your son who shall build my house and my courts, for I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father.
I will establish his kingdom forever if he continues strong in keeping my commandments and my rules, as he is today.'

Now therefore, in the sight of all Israel, the assembly of the LORD, and in the hearing of our God, observe and seek out all the commandments of the LORD your God, that you may possess this good land and leave it for an inheritance to your children after you forever.

"And you, Solomon my son, know the God of your father and serve him with a whole heart and with a willing mind, for the LORD searches all hearts and understands every plan and thought. If you seek him, he will be found by you, but if you forsake him, he will cast you off forever.
Know now that the LORD has chosen you to build a house for the sanctuary. Be strong and do it."
Then David gives Solomon his son the plan of the vestibule of the temple, and of its houses, its treasuries, its upper rooms, and its inner chambers, and of the room for the mercy seat;
and the plan of all that he has in mind: for the courts of the house of the LORD, all the surrounding chambers, the treasuries of the house of God, and the treasuries for dedicated gifts;
for the divisions of the priests and of the Levites, and all the work of the service in the house of the LORD; for all the vessels for the service in the house of the LORD,
the weight of gold for all golden vessels for each service, the weight of silver vessels for each service,

the weight of the golden lampstands and their lamps, the weight of gold for each lampstand and its lamps, and the weight of silver for a lampstand and its lamps, according to the use of each lampstand in the service,
the weight of gold for each table for the showbread, the silver for the silver tables,
and pure gold for the forks, the basins, and the cups; for the golden bowls and the weight of each; for the silver bowls and the weight of each;

"All this he makes clear to me in writing from the hand of the LORD — all the work to be done according to the plan."

Then David says to Solomon his son, "Be strong and courageous and do it. Do not be afraid and do not be dismayed, for the LORD God, even my God, is with you. He will not leave you or forsake you, until all the work for the service of the house of the LORD is finished.

And behold the divisions of the priests and the Levites for all the service of the house of God; and with you in all the work will be every willing man who has skill for any kind of service; also the officers and all the people will be wholly at your command."
The Freewill Offerings of the Assembly · 29:1–9
And David the king says to all the assembly: "Solomon my son, whom alone God has chosen, is young and inexperienced, and the work is great, for the palace will not be for man but for the LORD God.

So I have provided for the house of my God, so far as I was able, the gold for the things of gold, the silver for the things of silver, and the bronze for the things of bronze, the iron for the things of iron, and wood for the things of wood, besides great quantities of onyx and stones for setting, antimony, colored stones, all sorts of precious stones and marble.

Moreover, in addition to all that I have provided for the holy house, I have a treasure of my own of gold and silver, and because of my devotion to the house of my God I give it to the house of my God:

and for all the work to be done by craftsmen, gold for the things of gold and silver for the things of silver. Who then will offer willingly, consecrating himself today to the LORD?"
Then the leaders of fathers' houses made their freewill offerings, as did also the leaders of the tribes, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and the officers over the king's work.
They give for the service of the house of God 5,000 talents and 10,000 darics of gold, 10,000 talents of silver, 18,000 talents of bronze, and 100,000 talents of iron.
And whoever has precious stones gives them to the treasury of the house of the LORD, in the care of Jehiel the Gershonite.
Then the people rejoice because they have given willingly, for with a whole heart they offer freely to the LORD. David the king also rejoices greatly.
David's Great Prayer of Thanksgiving · 29:10–20
Therefore David blesses the LORD in the presence of all the assembly. And David says: "Blessed are you, O LORD, the God of Israel our father, forever and ever.

Yours, O LORD, is the greatness and the power and the glory and the victory and the majesty, for all that is in the heavens and in the earth is yours. Yours is the kingdom, O LORD, and you are exalted as head above all.
Both riches and honor come from you, and you rule over all. In your hand are power and might, and in your hand it is to make great and to give strength to all.
And now we thank you, our God, and praise your glorious name.
But who am I, and what is my people, that we should be able thus to offer willingly? For all things come from you, and of your own have we given you.
For we are strangers before you and sojourners, as all our fathers were. Our days on the earth are like a shadow, and there is no abiding.
O LORD our God, all this abundance that we have provided for building you a house for your holy name comes from your hand and is all your own.

I know, my God, that you test the heart and have pleasure in uprightness. In the uprightness of my heart I have freely offered all these things, and now I have seen your people, who are present here, offering freely and joyously to you.
O LORD, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, our fathers, keep forever such purposes and thoughts in the hearts of your people, and direct their hearts toward you.
Grant to Solomon my son a whole heart that he may keep your commandments, your testimonies, and your statutes, performing all, and that he may build the palace for which I have made provision."
Then David says to all the assembly, "Bless the LORD your God." And all the assembly blesses the LORD, the God of their fathers, and bows their heads and pays homage to the LORD and to the king.

And they offer sacrifices to the LORD, and on the next day burnt offerings to the LORD — a thousand bulls, a thousand rams, and a thousand lambs, with their drink offerings, and sacrifices in abundance for all Israel.
And they eat and drink before the LORD on that day with great gladness. And they make Solomon the son of David king the second time, and they anoint him as prince for the LORD, and Zadok as priest.
Then Solomon sits on the throne of the LORD as king in place of David his father. And he prospers, and all Israel obeys him.
All the leaders and the mighty men, and also all the sons of King David, pledge their allegiance to King Solomon.
And the LORD makes Solomon very great in the sight of all Israel and bestows on him such royal majesty as had not been on any king before him in Israel.
Thus David the son of Jesse reigns over all Israel.
The time that he reigns over Israel is forty years. He reigns seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
Then he dies in a good old age, full of days, riches, and honor. And Solomon his son reigns in his place.
Now the acts of King David, from first to last, are written in the Chronicles of Samuel the seer, and in the Chronicles of Nathan the prophet, and in the Chronicles of Gad the seer,
with accounts of all his rule and his might and of the circumstances that came upon him and upon Israel and upon all the kingdoms of the countries.

Solomon the son of David establishes himself in his kingdom, and the LORD his God is with him and makes him exceedingly great.

The Dream at Gibeon: Solomon's Request · 1:7–13
In that night God appears to Solomon, and says to him, “Ask what I shall give you.“
And Solomon says to God, “You have shown great and steadfast love to David my father, and have made me king in his place.
O LORD God, let your word to David my father be now fulfilled, for you have made me king over a people as numerous as the dust of the earth.
Give me now wisdom and knowledge to go out and come in before this people, for who can govern this people of yours, which is so great?“

God answers Solomon, “Because this was in your heart, and you have not asked for possessions, wealth, honor, or the life of those who hate you, and have not even asked for long life, but have asked for wisdom and knowledge for yourself that you may govern my people over whom I have made you king,
wisdom and knowledge are granted to you. I will also give you riches, possessions, and honor, such as none of the kings had who were before you, and none after you shall have the like.“
So Solomon comes from the high place at Gibeon, from before the tent of meeting, to Jerusalem. And he reigns over Israel.
