Gath, Mareshah, Ziph,
Adoraim, Lachish, Azekah,
Zorah, Aijalon, and Hebron, fortified cities that are in Judah and in Benjamin.
He makes the fortresses strong, and puts commanders in them, and stores of food, oil, and wine.
And he puts shields and spears in all the cities and makes them very strong. So he holds Judah and Benjamin.
Priests and Levites Come to Jerusalem · 11:13–17
And the priests and the Levites who are in all Israel present themselves to him from all places where they live.
For the Levites leave their common lands and their holdings and come to Judah and Jerusalem, because Jeroboam and his sons cast them out from serving as priests to the LORD,
and he appoints his own priests for the high places and for the goat idols and for the calves that he has made.
And those who have set their hearts to seek the LORD God of Israel come after them from all the tribes of Israel to Jerusalem to sacrifice to the LORD, the God of their fathers.
They strengthen the kingdom of Judah, and for three years they make Rehoboam the son of Solomon secure, for they walk for three years in the way of David and Solomon.
Rehoboam's Family · 11:18–23
Rehoboam takes as wife Mahalath the daughter of Jerimoth the son of David, and of Abihail the daughter of Eliab the son of Jesse,
and she bears him sons: Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham.
After her he takes Maacah the daughter of Absalom, who bears him Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith.
Rehoboam loves Maacah the daughter of Absalom above all his wives and concubines — he takes eighteen wives and sixty concubines and fathers twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.
And Rehoboam appoints Abijah the son of Maacah as chief prince among his brothers, for he intends to make him king.
And he deals wisely and distributes some of his sons through all the districts of Judah and Benjamin, in all the fortified cities, and he gives them abundant provisions and procures wives for them.
Rehoboam Abandons the Law; Shishak Invades · 12:1–12
When the rule of Rehoboam is established and he is strong, he abandons the law of the LORD, and all Israel with him.

In the fifth year of King Rehoboam, because they have been unfaithful to the LORD, Shishak king of Egypt comes up against Jerusalem with twelve hundred chariots and sixty thousand horsemen. And the people are without number who come with him from Egypt — Libyans, Sukkiim, and Cushites.
And he takes the fortified cities of Judah and comes as far as Jerusalem.

Then Shemaiah the prophet comes to Rehoboam and to the princes of Judah, who have gathered at Jerusalem because of Shishak, and says to them, “Thus says the LORD, 'You abandoned me, so I have abandoned you to the hand of Shishak.'“
Then the princes of Israel and the king humble themselves and say, “The LORD is righteous.“

When the LORD sees that they have humbled themselves, the word of the LORD comes to Shemaiah: “They have humbled themselves. I will not destroy them, but I will grant them some deliverance, and my wrath shall not be poured out on Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak.
Nevertheless, they shall be servants to him, so that they may know my service and the service of the kingdoms of the countries.“

So Shishak king of Egypt comes up against Jerusalem. He takes away the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the king's house. He takes everything. He also takes away the shields of gold that Solomon had made.
And King Rehoboam makes in their place shields of bronze and commits them to the hands of the officers of the guard, who keep the door of the king's house.
And as often as the king enters the house of the LORD, the guard comes and carries them and brings them back to the guardroom.
And when he humbles himself, the wrath of the LORD turns from him, so as not to make a complete destruction. Moreover, conditions are good in Judah.

So King Rehoboam strengthens himself in Jerusalem and reigns. Rehoboam is forty-one years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city that the LORD had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel to put his name there. His mother's name is Naamah the Ammonite.
Rehoboam's Death · 12:13–16
And he does evil, for he does not set his heart to seek the LORD.

Now the acts of Rehoboam, from first to last, are they not written in the records of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the seer? There were genealogical records. And there were continual wars between Rehoboam and Jeroboam.
And Rehoboam sleeps with his fathers and is buried in the city of David, and Abijah his son reigns in his place.
And he does evil, for he does not set his heart to seek the LORD.
Abijah's War with Jeroboam · 13:1–3
In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam, Abijah begins to reign over Judah.
He reigns for three years in Jerusalem. His mother's name is Micaiah the daughter of Uriel of Gibeah. Now there is war between Abijah and Jeroboam.
Abijah goes into battle with an army of valiant warriors, four hundred thousand chosen men. And Jeroboam draws up his line of battle against him with eight hundred thousand chosen mighty warriors.
Abijah's Speech on Mount Zemaraim · 13:4–12
Then Abijah stands up on Mount Zemaraim, which is in the hill country of Ephraim, and says, “Hear me, O Jeroboam and all Israel!
Ought you not to know that the LORD God of Israel gave the kingship over Israel forever to David and his sons by a covenant of salt?
Yet Jeroboam the son of Nebat, a servant of Solomon the son of David, rose up and rebelled against his lord,
and certain worthless scoundrels gathered about him and defied Rehoboam the son of Solomon, when Rehoboam was young and irresolute and could not withstand them.
“And now you think to withstand the kingdom of the LORD in the hand of the sons of David, because you are a great multitude and have with you the golden calves that Jeroboam made you for gods.

Have you not driven out the priests of the LORD, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and made priests for yourselves like the peoples of other lands? Whoever comes for ordination with a young bull or seven rams becomes a priest of what are not gods.
But as for us, the LORD is our God, and we have not forsaken him. We have priests ministering to the LORD who are sons of Aaron, and Levites for their service.

They offer to the LORD every morning and every evening burnt offerings and incense of sweet spices, set out the showbread on the table of pure gold, and care for the golden lampstand that its lamps may burn every evening. For we keep the charge of the LORD our God, but you have forsaken him.

Behold, God is with us at our head, and his priests with their battle trumpets to sound the call to battle against you. O sons of Israel, do not fight against the LORD, the God of your fathers, for you cannot succeed.“
Judah's Victory · 13:13–20
Jeroboam has sent an ambush around to come upon them from behind. Thus his troops are in front of Judah, and the ambush is behind them.
And when Judah looks, behold, the battle is in front of and behind them. And they cry to the LORD, and the priests blow the trumpets.
Then the men of Judah raise the battle shout. And when the men of Judah shouted, God defeats Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah.
The men of Israel flee before Judah, and God gives them into their hand.
Abijah and his people strike them with great force, and 500,000 chosen men of Israel fall slain.
Thus the people of Israel are subdued at that time, and the people of Judah prevail, because they rely on the LORD, the God of their fathers.
And Abijah pursues Jeroboam and takes cities from him: Bethel with its villages, Jeshanah with its villages, and Ephron with its villages.
Jeroboam does not recover his power in the days of Abijah. And the LORD strikes him down, and he dies.
Abijah's Death · 13:21–22
But Abijah grows mighty. And he takes fourteen wives and fathers twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.
The rest of the acts of Abijah, his ways and his sayings, are written in the story of the prophet Iddo.
Asa's Reforms and Peace · 14:1–8
Abijah sleeps with his fathers, and they bury him in the city of David. And Asa his son reigns in his place. In his days the land has rest for ten years.
And Asa does what is good and right in the eyes of the LORD his God.
He takes away the foreign altars and the high places and breaks down the pillars and cuts down the Asherim
and commands Judah to seek the LORD, the God of their fathers, and to keep the law and the commandment.
He also takes out of all the cities of Judah the high places and the incense altars. And the kingdom has rest under him.
He builds fortified cities in Judah, for the land has rest. He has no war in those years, for the LORD gives him peace.

And he says to Judah, “Let us build these cities and surround them with walls and towers, gates and bars. The land is still ours, because we have sought the LORD our God. We have sought him, and he has given us peace on every side.“ So they build and prosper.
And Asa has an army of 300,000 from Judah, armed with large shields and spears, and 280,000 men from Benjamin who carried shields and drew bows. All these are mighty men of valour.
Victory over the Cushites · 14:9–15
Zerah the Cushite comes out against them with an army of a million men and three hundred chariots, and comes as far as Mareshah.
And Asa goes out to meet him, and they draw up their lines of battle in the Valley of Zephathah at Mareshah.

And Asa cries to the LORD his God, “O LORD, there is none like you to help, between the mighty and the weak. Help us, O LORD our God, for we rely on you, and in your name we have come against this multitude. O LORD, you are our God; let not man prevail against you.“
So the LORD defeats the Cushites before Asa and before Judah, and the Cushites flee.

Asa and the people who are with him pursue them as far as Gerar, and the Cushites fall until none remain alive, for they are broken before the LORD and his army. The men of Judah carry away very much plunder.
And they attack all the cities around Gerar, for the fear of the LORD is upon them. They plunder all the cities, for there is much plunder in them.
And they also attack the tents of those who had livestock and carry away sheep in abundance and camels. Then they return to Jerusalem.
The Prophecy of Azariah · 15:1–7
The Spirit of God comes upon Azariah the son of Oded,

and he goes out to meet Asa and says to him, “Hear me, Asa, and all Judah and Benjamin: The LORD is with you while you are with him. If you seek him, he will be found by you, but if you forsake him, he will forsake you.
For a long time Israel was without the true God, and without a teaching priest, and without law.
But when in their distress they turned to the LORD, the God of Israel, and sought him, he was found by them.
In those times there was no peace to him who went out or to him who came in, for great disturbances afflicted all the inhabitants of the lands.
They were broken in pieces. Nation was crushed by nation and city by city, for God troubled them with every sort of distress.
But you, take courage! Do not let your hands be weak, for your work shall be rewarded.“
Asa's Great Reformation · 15:8–15

As soon as Asa hears these words, the prophecy of Azariah the son of Oded, he takes courage and puts away the detestable idols from all the land of Judah and Benjamin and from the cities that he has taken in the hill country of Ephraim, and he repairs the altar of the LORD that was in front of the vestibule of the house of the LORD.

And he gathers all Judah and Benjamin, and those from Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon who are residing with them, for great numbers had deserted to him from Israel when they saw that the LORD his God was with him.
They are gathered at Jerusalem in the third month of the fifteenth year of the reign of Asa.
They sacrifice to the LORD on that day from the spoil that they have brought, seven hundred oxen and seven thousand sheep.
And they enter into a covenant to seek the LORD, the God of their fathers, with all their heart and with all their soul,
and that whoever would not seek the LORD, the God of Israel, should be put to death, whether young or old, man or woman.
They swear to the LORD with a loud voice and with shouting and with trumpets and with horns.
And all Judah rejoices over the oath, for they swear with all their heart and seek him with their whole desire, and he is found by them, and the LORD gives them rest all around.
Asa Deposes His Mother · 15:16–19
Even Maacah, his mother, King Asa removes from being queen mother because she had made a detestable image for Asherah. Asa cuts down her image, crushes it, and burns it at the brook Kidron.
But the high places were not taken out of Israel. Nevertheless, the heart of Asa is wholly true all his days.
And he brings into the house of God the sacred gifts of his father and his own sacred gifts, silver, and gold, and vessels.
And there is no more war until the thirty-fifth year of the reign of Asa.
Asa's Treaty with Aram and the Prophet Hanani · 16:1–10
In the thirty-sixth year of the reign of Asa, Baasha king of Israel goes up against Judah and builds Ramah, that he might permit no one to go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.
Then Asa takes silver and gold from the treasuries of the house of the LORD and the king's house and sends them to Ben-hadad king of Syria, who lived in Damascus, saying,

“There is a covenant between me and you, as there was between my father and your father. Behold, I am sending you silver and gold. Go, break your covenant with Baasha king of Israel, that he may withdraw from me.“
And Ben-hadad listens to King Asa and sends the commanders of his armies against the cities of Israel, and they conquer Ijon, Dan, Abel-maim, and all the store cities of Naphtali.
And when Baasha hears of it, he stops building Ramah and lets his work cease.
Then King Asa takes all Judah, and they carry away the stones of Ramah and its timber, with which Baasha had been building, and with them he builds Geba and Mizpah.

At that time Hanani the seer comes to Asa king of Judah and says to him, “Because you relied on the king of Syria, and did not rely on the LORD your God, the army of the king of Syria has escaped you.
Were not the Cushites and the Libyans a huge army with very many chariots and horsemen? Yet because you relied on the LORD, he gave them into your hand.
For the eyes of the LORD run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to give strong support to those whose heart is wholly his. You have done foolishly in this, for from now on you will have wars.“
Then Asa is angry with the seer and puts him in the stocks in prison, for he is in a rage with him because of this. And Asa inflicts cruelties upon some of the people at the same time.
Asa's Disease and Death · 16:11–14
The acts of Asa, from first to last, are written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
In the thirty-ninth year of his reign Asa is diseased in his feet, and his disease becomes severe. Yet even in his disease he does not seek the LORD, but seeks help from physicians.
And Asa sleeps with his fathers, dying in the forty-first year of his reign.

They bury him in the tomb that he cuts for himself in the city of David. They lay him on a bier that is filled with various kinds of spices prepared by the perfumer's art, and they make a very great fire in his honor.
Jehoshaphat's Faithful Reign · 17:1–6
Jehoshaphat his son reigns in his place and strengthens himself against Israel.
He places forces in all the fortified cities of Judah and sets garrisons in the land of Judah, and in the cities of Ephraim that Asa his father had captured.
The LORD is with Jehoshaphat, because he walks in the earlier ways of his father David. He does not seek the Baals,
but seeks the God of his father and walks in his commandments, and not according to the practices of Israel.
Therefore the LORD establishes the kingdom in his hand. And all Judah brings tribute to Jehoshaphat, and he has great riches and honor.
His heart is courageous in the ways of the LORD. And furthermore, he takes the high places and the Asherim out of Judah.
The Teaching Mission · 17:7–9
In the third year of his reign he sends his officials, Ben-hail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel, and Micaiah, to teach in the cities of Judah;
and with them the Levites, Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tobadonijah; and with these Levites the priests Elishama and Jehoram.
And they teach in Judah, having the Book of the Law of the LORD with them. They go throughout all the cities of Judah and teach among the people.
Jehoshaphat's Greatness · 17:10–19
And the fear of the LORD falls upon all the kingdoms of the lands that are around Judah, and they make no war against Jehoshaphat.
Some of the Philistines bring Jehoshaphat presents and silver for tribute, and the Arabians also bring him flocks: seven thousand seven hundred rams and seven thousand seven hundred goats.
And Jehoshaphat grows ever greater. He builds in Judah fortresses and store cities,
and he has large supplies in the cities of Judah. He has soldiers, mighty men of valour, in Jerusalem.
This is the muster of them by their fathers' houses: Of Judah, the commanders of thousands: Adnah the commander, with three hundred thousand mighty men of valour;
and next to him Jehohanan the commander, with two hundred and eighty thousand;
and next to him Amasiah the son of Zichri, a volunteer for the service of the LORD, with two hundred thousand mighty men of valour;
and of Benjamin: Eliada, a mighty man of valour, with two hundred thousand armed with bow and shield;
and next to him Jehozabad, with a hundred and eighty thousand armed for war.
These are in the service of the king, besides those whom the king had placed in the fortified cities throughout all Judah.
Jehoshaphat Allies with Ahab · 18:1–3
Now Jehoshaphat has great riches and honor, and he makes a marriage alliance with Ahab.
After some years he goes down to Ahab in Samaria. And Ahab kills an abundance of sheep and oxen for him and for the people who are with him, and induces him to go up against Ramoth-gilead.
Ahab king of Israel says to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, “Will you go with me to Ramoth-gilead?“ And he answers him, “I am as you are, my people as your people. We will be with you in the war.“
The Prophets of Ahab and Micaiah · 18:4–27
And Jehoshaphat says to the king of Israel, “Inquire first for the word of the LORD.“

Then the king of Israel gathers the prophets together, four hundred men, and says to them, “Shall we go to battle against Ramoth-gilead, or shall I refrain?“ And they say, “Go up, for God will give it into the hand of the king.“
But Jehoshaphat says, “Is there not here another prophet of the LORD of whom we may inquire?“

And the king of Israel says to Jehoshaphat, “There is yet one man by whom we may inquire of the LORD, Micaiah the son of Imlah; but I hate him, for he never prophesies good concerning me, but always evil.“ And Jehoshaphat says, “Let not the king say so.“
Then the king of Israel summons an officer and says, “Bring quickly Micaiah the son of Imlah.“

Now the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat the king of Judah are sitting on their thrones, arrayed in their robes. And they are sitting at the threshing floor at the entrance of the gate of Samaria, and all the prophets are prophesying before them.
And Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah makes for himself horns of iron and says, “Thus says the LORD, 'With these you shall push the Syrians until they are destroyed.'“
And all the prophets prophesy so and say, “Go up to Ramoth-gilead and triumph. The LORD will give it into the hand of the king.“

And the messenger who goes to summon Micaiah says to him, “Behold, the words of the prophets with one accord are favourable to the king. Let your word be like the word of one of them, and speak favourably.“
But Micaiah says, “As the LORD lives, what my God says, that I will speak.“
And when he has come to the king, the king says to him, “Micaiah, shall we go to Ramoth-gilead to battle, or shall I refrain?“ And he answers, “Go up and triumph; they will be given into your hand.“
But the king says to him, “How many times shall I make you swear that you speak to me nothing but the truth in the name of the LORD?“
And he says, “I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains, as sheep that have no shepherd. And the LORD said, 'These have no master; let each return to his home in peace.'“
And the king of Israel says to Jehoshaphat, “Did I not tell you that he would not prophesy good concerning me, but evil?“
And Micaiah says, “Therefore hear the word of the LORD: I saw the LORD sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven standing on his right hand and on his left.
And the LORD says, 'Who will entice Ahab the king of Israel, that he may go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead?' And one says one thing, and another says another.
Then a spirit comes forward and stands before the LORD, saying, 'I will entice him.' And the LORD says to him, 'By what means?'
And he says, 'I will go out, and will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.' And he says, 'You are to entice him, and you shall succeed; go out and do so.'
Now therefore behold, the LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouth of these your prophets. The LORD has declared disaster for you.“
Then Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah comes near and strikes Micaiah on the cheek and says, “Which way did the Spirit of the LORD go from me to speak to you?“
And Micaiah says, “Behold, you shall see on that day when you go into an inner chamber to hide yourself.“
And the king of Israel says, “Seize Micaiah and take him back to Amon the governor of the city and to Joash the king's son,
and say, 'Thus says the king, Put this fellow in prison and feed him with meagre rations of bread and water until I return in peace.'“
And Micaiah says, “If you return in peace, the LORD has not spoken by me.“ And he says, “Hear, all you peoples!“
The Battle of Ramoth-gilead · 18:28–34
So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat the king of Judah go up to Ramoth-gilead.
And the king of Israel says to Jehoshaphat, “I will disguise myself and go into battle, but you wear your robes.“ And the king of Israel disguises himself, and they go into battle.
Now the king of Syria has commanded the captains of his chariots, “Fight with no one small or great, but only with the king of Israel.“

As soon as the captains of the chariots see Jehoshaphat, they say, “It is the king of Israel.“ So they turn to fight against him. And Jehoshaphat cries out, and the LORD helps him; God draws them away from him.
For as soon as the captains of the chariots see that it is not the king of Israel, they turn back from pursuing him.

But a certain man draws his bow at random and strikes the king of Israel between the scale armour and the breastplate. Therefore he says to the driver of his chariot, “Turn around and carry me out of the battle, for I am wounded.“
And the battle continues that day, and the king of Israel props himself up in his chariot facing the Syrians until evening. Then at sunset he dies.
The Prophet Jehu Rebukes Jehoshaphat · 19:1–3
Jehoshaphat the king of Judah returns safely to his house in Jerusalem.

But Jehu the son of Hanani the seer goes out to meet him and says to King Jehoshaphat, “Should you help the wicked and love those who hate the LORD? Because of this, wrath has gone out against you from the LORD.
Nevertheless, some good is found in you, for you destroyed the Asherahs out of the land, and have set your heart to seek God.“
Jehoshaphat Appoints Judges · 19:4–11
Jehoshaphat lives at Jerusalem. And he goes out again among the people, from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim, and brings them back to the LORD, the God of their fathers.
He appoints judges in the land in all the fortified cities of Judah, city by city,
and says to the judges, “Consider what you do, for you judge not for man but for the LORD. He is with you in giving judgment.
Now then, let the fear of the LORD be upon you. Be careful what you do, for there is no injustice with the LORD our God, or partiality or taking bribes.“
Moreover, in Jerusalem Jehoshaphat appoints certain Levites and priests and heads of families of Israel, to give judgment for the LORD and to decide disputed cases. They have their seat at Jerusalem.
And he charges them: “Thus you shall do in the fear of the LORD, in faithfulness, and with your whole heart:

whenever a case comes to you from your brothers who live in their cities, concerning bloodshed, law or commandment, statutes or rules, you shall warn them, that they may not incur guilt before the LORD and wrath may not come upon you and your brothers. Thus you shall do, and you will not incur guilt.

And behold, Amariah the chief priest is over you in all matters of the LORD; and Zebadiah the son of Ishmael, the governor of the house of Judah, in all the king's matters, and the Levites will serve you as officers. Deal courageously, and may the LORD be with the upright!“
The Vast Army Approaches · 20:1–4
After this the Moabites and Ammonites, and with them some of the Meunites, come against Jehoshaphat for battle.
Some men come and tell Jehoshaphat, “A great multitude is coming against you from Edom, from beyond the sea; and behold, they are in Hazazon-tamar“ — that is, En-gedi.
Then Jehoshaphat is afraid and sets his face to seek the LORD, and proclaims a fast throughout all Judah.
And Judah assembles to seek help from the LORD; from all the cities of Judah they come to seek the LORD.
Jehoshaphat's Prayer · 20:5–13
And Jehoshaphat stands in the assembly of Judah and Jerusalem, in the house of the LORD, before the new court,
and says, “O LORD, God of our fathers, are you not God in heaven? You rule over all the kingdoms of the nations. In your hand are power and might, so that none is able to withstand you.
Did you not, our God, drive out the inhabitants of this land before your people Israel, and give it forever to the descendants of Abraham your friend?
And they have lived in it and have built for you in it a sanctuary for your name, saying,

'If disaster comes upon us, the sword, judgment, or pestilence, or famine, we will stand before this house and before you — for your name is in this house — and cry out to you in our affliction, and you will hear and save.'
And now behold, the men of Ammon and Moab and Mount Seir, whom you would not let Israel invade when they came from the land of Egypt, and whom they avoided and did not destroy —
behold, they reward us by coming to drive us out of your possession, which you have given us to inherit.
O our God, will you not execute judgment on them? For we are powerless against this great horde that is coming against us. We do not know what to do, but our eyes are on you.“
Meanwhile all Judah stands before the LORD, with their little ones, their wives, and their children.
The Spirit Speaks Through Jahaziel · 20:14–19
And the Spirit of the LORD comes upon Jahaziel the son of Zechariah, son of Benaiah, son of Jeiel, son of Mattaniah, a Levite of the sons of Asaph, in the midst of the assembly.

And he says, “Listen, all Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem and King Jehoshaphat: Thus says the LORD to you, 'Do not be afraid and do not be dismayed at this great horde, for the battle is not yours but God's.'
Tomorrow go down against them. Behold, they will come up by the ascent of Ziz. You will find them at the end of the valley, east of the wilderness of Jeruel.

You will not need to fight in this battle. Stand firm, hold your position, and see the salvation of the LORD on your behalf, O Judah and Jerusalem. Do not be afraid and do not be dismayed. Tomorrow go out against them, and the LORD will be with you.'“
Then Jehoshaphat bows his head with his face to the ground, and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem fall down before the LORD, worshipping the LORD.
And the Levites, of the Kohathites and the Korahites, stand up to praise the LORD, the God of Israel, with a very loud voice.
The Battle Won by Praise · 20:20–30

And they rise early in the morning and go out into the wilderness of Tekoa. And as they go out, Jehoshaphat stands and says, “Hear me, Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem! Believe in the LORD your God, and you will be established; believe his prophets, and you will succeed.“
And when he has taken counsel with the people, he appoints those who are to sing to the LORD and praise him in holy attire, as they go before the army, and say,
“Give thanks to the LORD,
And when they begin to sing and praise, the LORD sets an ambush against the men of Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir, who had come against Judah, so that they are routed.

For the men of Ammon and Moab rise against the inhabitants of Mount Seir, devoting them to destruction, and when they have made an end of the inhabitants of Seir, they all help to destroy one another.
When Judah comes to the watchtower of the wilderness, they look toward the horde, and behold, there are dead bodies lying on the ground; none have escaped.

When Jehoshaphat and his people come to take their spoil, they find among them, in great quantities, goods, clothing, and precious things, which they take for themselves until they can carry no more. They spend three days taking the plunder, it is so much.
On the fourth day they assemble in the Valley of Beracah, for there they bless the LORD. Therefore the name of that place has been called the Valley of Beracah to this day.
Then they return, every man of Judah and Jerusalem, and Jehoshaphat at their head, returning to Jerusalem with joy, for the LORD had made them rejoice over their enemies.
They come to Jerusalem with harps and lyres and trumpets to the house of the LORD.
And the fear of God comes upon all the kingdoms of the countries when they hear that the LORD had fought against the enemies of Israel.
So the realm of Jehoshaphat is quiet, for his God gives him rest on every side.
Jehoshaphat's Later Failures and Death · 20:31–37
Thus Jehoshaphat reigns over Judah. He is thirty-five years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns twenty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother's name is Azubah the daughter of Shilhi.
He walks in the way of his father Asa and does not turn aside from it, doing what is right in the sight of the LORD.
The high places, however, are not taken away; the people have not yet set their hearts upon the God of their fathers.
Now the rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, from first to last, are written in the chronicles of Jehu the son of Hanani, which are recorded in the Book of the Kings of Israel.
After this Jehoshaphat king of Judah joins with Ahaziah king of Israel, who acted wickedly.
He joins him in building ships to go to Tarshish, and they build the ships in Ezion-geber.

Then Eliezer the son of Dodavahu of Mareshah prophesies against Jehoshaphat, saying, “Because you have joined with Ahaziah, the LORD will destroy what you have made.“ And the ships are wrecked and are not able to go to Tarshish.
Jehoram's Wicked Reign · 21:1–11
Jehoshaphat sleeps with his fathers and is buried with his fathers in the city of David, and Jehoram his son reigns in his place.
He has brothers, the sons of Jehoshaphat: Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariah, Michael, and Shephatiah; all these are the sons of Jehoshaphat king of Israel.
Their father gives them great gifts of silver, gold, and valuable possessions, together with fortified cities in Judah, but he gives the kingdom to Jehoram, because he is the firstborn.
When Jehoram has ascended the throne of his father and is established, he kills all his brothers with the sword, and also some of the princes of Israel.
Jehoram is thirty-two years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns eight years in Jerusalem.
And he walks in the way of the kings of Israel, as the house of Ahab had done, for the daughter of Ahab is his wife. And he does what is evil in the sight of the LORD.
Yet the LORD is not willing to destroy the house of David, because of the covenant that he had made with David, and since he had promised to give a lamp to him and to his sons forever.
In his days Edom revolts from the rule of Judah and sets up a king of their own.
Then Jehoram crosses over with his commanders and all his chariots. And he rises by night and strikes the Edomites who had surrounded him and his chariot commanders.
So Edom revolts from the rule of Judah to this day. At that time Libnah also revolts from his rule, because he had forsaken the LORD, the God of his fathers.
Moreover, he makes high places in the hill country of Judah and leads the inhabitants of Jerusalem into whoredom and makes Judah go astray.
Elijah's Letter and the Plagues · 21:12–20

And a letter comes to him from Elijah the prophet, saying, “Thus says the LORD, the God of David your father, 'Because you have not walked in the ways of Jehoshaphat your father, or in the ways of Asa king of Judah,

but have walked in the way of the kings of Israel and have enticed Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem into whoredom, as the house of Ahab led Israel into whoredom, and also you have killed your brothers, of your father's house, who were better than you,
behold, the LORD will bring a great plague on your people, your children, your wives, and all your possessions,
and you yourself will have a severe sickness with a disease of your bowels, until your bowels come out because of the disease, day by day.'“
And the LORD stirs up against Jehoram the anger of the Philistines and of the Arabians who are near the Cushites.

And they come up against Judah and invade it and carry away all the possessions they find that belonged to the king's house, and also his sons and his wives, so that no son is left to him except Jehoahaz, his youngest son.
And after all this the LORD strikes him also in his bowels with an incurable disease.
In the course of time, at the end of two years, his bowels come out because of the disease, and he dies in great agony. His people make no fire in his honor, like the fires made for his fathers.
He is thirty-two years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns eight years in Jerusalem. And he departs with no one's regret. They bury him in the city of David, but not in the tombs of the kings.
Ahaziah's Brief Reign · 22:1–9

And the inhabitants of Jerusalem make Ahaziah, his youngest son, king in his place, for the band of men that came with the Arabians to the camp had killed all the older sons. So Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah reigns.
Ahaziah is forty-two years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns one year in Jerusalem. His mother's name is Athaliah, the granddaughter of Omri.
He also walks in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother is his counselor in doing wickedly.
He does what is evil in the sight of the LORD, as the house of Ahab had done. For after the death of his father they are his counselors, to his undoing.
He even follows their counsel and goes with Jehoram the son of Ahab king of Israel to make war against Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth-gilead. And the Syrians wound Joram.

And he returns to be healed in Jezreel of the wounds that he had received at Ramah, when he fought against Hazael king of Syria. And Azariah the son of Jehoram king of Judah goes down to see Joram the son of Ahab in Jezreel, because he is sick.

But it is ordained by God that the downfall of Ahaziah should come about through his going to visit Joram. For when he comes there, he goes out with Jehoram to meet Jehu the son of Nimshi, whom the LORD had anointed to strike down the house of Ahab.
And when Jehu is executing judgment on the house of Ahab, he meets the princes of Judah and the sons of Ahaziah's brothers, who were attending Ahaziah, and he kills them.

He searches for Ahaziah, and he is captured while hiding in Samaria, and he is brought to Jehu and put to death. They bury him, for they say, “He is the grandson of Jehoshaphat, who sought the LORD with all his heart.“ And the house of Ahaziah has no one able to rule the kingdom.
Athaliah Seizes Power; Joash Hidden · 22:10–12
Now when Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah sees that her son is dead, she rises and destroys all the royal family of the house of Judah.

But Jehoshabeath, the daughter of the king, takes Joash the son of Ahaziah and steals him away from among the king's sons who are about to be killed, and she puts him and his nurse in a bedroom. Thus Jehoshabeath, the daughter of King Jehoram and wife of Jehoiada the priest, because she was a sister of Ahaziah, hides him from Athaliah, so that she does not kill him.
And he remains hidden with them in the house of God six years, while Athaliah reigns over the land.
The Coup Against Athaliah · 23:1–11

But in the seventh year Jehoiada takes courage and enters into a covenant with the commanders of hundreds, Azariah the son of Jeroham, Ishmael the son of Jehohanan, Azariah the son of Obed, Maaseiah the son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat the son of Zichri.
And they go about through Judah and gather the Levites from all the cities of Judah, and the heads of fathers' houses of Israel, and they come to Jerusalem.
And all the assembly makes a covenant with the king in the house of God. And Jehoiada says to them, “Behold, the king's son! Let him reign, as the LORD spoke concerning the sons of David.
This is the thing that you shall do: of you priests and Levites who come off duty on the Sabbath, one third shall be gatekeepers,
one third shall be at the king's house, and one third shall be at the Gate of the Foundation. And all the people shall be in the courts of the house of the LORD.
Let no one enter the house of the LORD except the priests and ministering Levites. They may enter, for they are holy, but all the people shall keep the charge of the LORD.
The Levites shall surround the king, each with his weapons in his hand. And whoever enters the house shall be put to death. Be with the king when he comes in and when he goes out.“

The Levites and all Judah do according to all that Jehoiada the priest commands. And each brings his men, those who are to come on duty on the Sabbath and those who are to go off duty on the Sabbath, for Jehoiada the priest does not dismiss the divisions.
And Jehoiada the priest gives to the commanders the spears and the large and small shields that had been King David's, which were in the house of God.
And he sets all the people as a guard for the king, every man with his weapon in his hand, from the south side of the house to the north side of the house, around the altar and the house.
Then they bring out the king's son and put the crown on him and give him the testimony. And they proclaim him king, and Jehoiada and his sons anoint him, and they say, “Long live the king!“
Athaliah Executed; The Covenant Renewed · 23:12–21
When Athaliah hears the noise of the people running and praising the king, she goes into the house of the LORD to the people.

And when she looks, there is the king standing by his pillar at the entrance, and the captains and the trumpeters beside the king, and all the people of the land rejoicing and blowing trumpets, and the singers with their musical instruments leading in the celebration. And Athaliah tears her clothes and cries, “Treason! Treason!“

Then Jehoiada the priest brings out the captains who were set over the army, saying to them, “Bring her out between the ranks, and anyone who follows her is to be put to death with the sword.“ For the priest says, “Do not put her to death in the house of the LORD.“
So they seize her; and she goes into the entrance of the horse gate of the king's house, and they put her to death there.
And Jehoiada makes a covenant between himself and all the people and the king that they should be the LORD's people.
Then all the people go to the house of Baal and tear it down; his altars and his images they break in pieces, and they kill Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars.

And Jehoiada appoints the oversight of the house of the LORD to the Levitical priests whom David had organized to be in charge of the house of the LORD, to offer burnt offerings to the LORD, as it is written in the Law of Moses, with rejoicing and with singing, according to the order of David.
He stations the gatekeepers at the gates of the house of the LORD so that no one should enter who was in any way unclean.

And he takes the captains, the nobles, the governors of the people, and all the people of the land, and they bring the king down from the house of the LORD, marching through the upper gate to the king's house. And they set the king on the royal throne.
So all the people of the land rejoice, and the city is quiet after Athaliah has been put to death with the sword.
Joash Repairs the Temple · 24:1–14
Joash is seven years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns forty years in Jerusalem. His mother's name is Zibiah of Beersheba.
And Joash does what is right in the eyes of the LORD all the days of Jehoiada the priest.
Jehoiada gets him two wives, and he fathers sons and daughters.
After this Joash decides to restore the house of the LORD.

And he gathers the priests and the Levites and says to them, “Go out to the cities of Judah and gather from all Israel money to repair the house of your God from year to year, and see that you act quickly.“ But the Levites do not act quickly.

So the king summons Jehoiada the chief and says to him, “Why have you not required the Levites to bring in from Judah and Jerusalem the tax levied by Moses, the servant of the LORD, on the congregation of Israel for the tent of testimony?“
For the sons of Athaliah, that wicked woman, had broken into the house of God, and had also used all the dedicated things of the house of the LORD for the Baals.
So the king commands, and they make a chest and set it outside the gate of the house of the LORD.
And proclamation is made throughout Judah and Jerusalem to bring in for the LORD the tax that Moses the servant of God laid on Israel in the wilderness.
And all the princes and all the people rejoice and bring their tax and drop it into the chest until it is full.

And whenever the chest is brought to the king's officers by the Levites, when they see that there is much money in it, the king's secretary and the officer of the chief priest come and empty the chest and take it and return it to its place. Thus they do day after day, and collect money in abundance.

And the king and Jehoiada give it to those who have charge of the work of the house of the LORD, and they hire masons and carpenters to restore the house of the LORD, and also workers in iron and bronze to repair the house of the LORD.
So those who are engaged in the work labour on, and the repairing goes forward in their hands, and they restore the house of God to its proper condition and strengthen it.

And when they have finished, they bring the rest of the money before the king and Jehoiada, and with it are made utensils for the house of the LORD, both for the service and for the burnt offerings, and dishes for incense and vessels of gold and silver. And they offer burnt offerings in the house of the LORD regularly all the days of Jehoiada.
Joash Turns After Jehoiada's Death · 24:15–22
But Jehoiada grows old and full of days, and dies. He is a hundred and thirty years old at his death.
And they bury him in the city of David among the kings, because he had done good in Israel, and toward God and his house.
Now after the death of Jehoiada the princes of Judah come and pay homage to the king. Then the king listens to them.
And they abandon the house of the LORD, the God of their fathers, and serve the Asherahs and the idols. And wrath comes upon Judah and Jerusalem for this guilt of theirs.
Yet he sends prophets among them to bring them back to the LORD. These testify against them, but they will not pay attention.

Then the Spirit of God clothes Zechariah the son of Jehoiada the priest, and he stands above the people and says to them, “Thus says God, 'Why do you break the commandments of the LORD, so that you cannot prosper? Because you have forsaken the LORD, he has forsaken you.'“
But they conspire against him, and by command of the king they stone him with stones in the court of the house of the LORD.
Thus Joash the king does not remember the kindness that Jehoiada, Zechariah's father, had shown him, but kills his son. And when he is dying, he says, “May the LORD see and avenge!“
Joash Punished; His Death · 24:23–27

At the end of the year the army of Syria comes up against Joash. They come to Judah and Jerusalem and destroy all the princes of the people from among the people and send all their spoil to the king of Damascus.

Though the army of Syria has come with few men, the LORD delivers into their hand a very great army, because Judah had forsaken the LORD, the God of their fathers. Thus they execute judgment on Joash.

When they have departed from him, leaving him severely wounded, his servants conspire against him because of the blood of the son of Jehoiada the priest, and kill him on his bed. So he dies, and they bury him in the city of David, but they do not bury him in the tombs of the kings.
Those who conspire against him are Zabad the son of Shimeath the Ammonite, and Jehozabad the son of Shimrith the Moabite.
Accounts of his sons, and of the many oracles against him, and of the rebuilding of the house of God are written in the Commentary on the Book of the Kings. And Amaziah his son reigns in his place.
Amaziah's Reign Begins Well · 25:1–4
Amaziah was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigns twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name is Jehoaddan of Jerusalem.
And he does what is right in the eyes of the LORD, yet not with a whole heart.
And as soon as the royal power is firmly in his hand he kills his servants who had struck down the king his father.

But he does not put their children to death, according to what is written in the Law, in the Book of Moses, where the LORD commanded, “Fathers shall not die because of their children, nor children die because of their fathers, but each one shall die for his own sin.“
The War with Edom · 25:5–13

Then Amaziah assembles the men of Judah and sets them by fathers' houses under commanders of thousands and of hundreds for all Judah and Benjamin. He musters those twenty years old and upward and finds that they are three hundred thousand choice men, fit for war, able to handle spear and shield.
He also hires one hundred thousand mighty men of valour from Israel for one hundred talents of silver.
But a man of God comes to him and says, “O king, do not let the army of Israel go with you, for the LORD is not with Israel, with all these Ephraimites.
But go, act, be strong for the battle. Why should you suppose that God will cast you down before the enemy? For God has power to help or to cast down.“

And Amaziah says to the man of God, “But what shall we do about the hundred talents that I have given to the army of Israel?“ The man of God answers, “The LORD is able to give you much more than this.“
Then Amaziah discharges the army that had come to him from Ephraim to go home again. And they become very angry with Judah and return home in fierce anger.
But Amaziah takes courage and leads his people and goes to the Valley of Salt and strikes down ten thousand men of Seir.
The men of Judah capture another ten thousand alive and bring them to the top of a rock and throw them down from the top of the rock, and they all are dashed to pieces.

But the men of the army whom Amaziah sends back, not letting them go with him to battle, raid the cities of Judah, from Samaria to Beth-horon, and strike down three thousand people in them and take much spoil.
Amaziah Follows Edomite Gods; His Downfall · 25:14–28
After Amaziah comes from striking down the Edomites, he brings the gods of the men of Seir and sets them up as his gods and worships them, making offerings to them.
Therefore the LORD is angry with Amaziah and sends to him a prophet, who says to him, “Why have you sought the gods of a people who did not deliver their own people from your hand?“

But as he is speaking the king says to him, “Have we made you a royal counselor? Stop! Why should you be struck down?“ So the prophet stops, but says, “I know that God has decided to destroy you, because you have done this and have not listened to my counsel.“
Then Amaziah king of Judah takes counsel and sends to Joash the son of Jehoahaz, son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, “Come, let us look one another in the face.“

And Joash the king of Israel sends word to Amaziah king of Judah, “A thistle on Lebanon sent to a cedar on Lebanon, saying, 'Give your daughter to my son for a wife,' and a wild beast of Lebanon passed by and trampled down the thistle.
You say, 'See, I have struck down Edom,' and your heart has lifted you up in boasting. But now stay at home. Why should you provoke trouble so that you fall, you and Judah with you?“
But Amaziah would not listen, for it was of God, in order that he might give them into the hand of their enemies, because they had sought the gods of Edom.
So Joash king of Israel goes up, and he and Amaziah king of Judah face one another in battle at Beth-shemesh, which belongs to Judah.
And Judah is defeated by Israel, and every man flees to his home.

And Joash king of Israel captures Amaziah king of Judah, the son of Joash, son of Ahaziah, at Beth-shemesh, and brings him to Jerusalem and breaks down the wall of Jerusalem for four hundred cubits, from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate.

And he seizes all the gold and silver, and all the vessels that are found in the house of God, and Obed-edom with them, and also the treasuries of the king's house, and hostages, and he returns to Samaria.
Amaziah the son of Joash, king of Judah, lives fifteen years after the death of Joash the son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel.
Now the rest of the acts of Amaziah, from first to last, are they not written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel?
From the time when Amaziah turns away from the LORD they make a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem, and he flees to Lachish. But they send after him to Lachish and put him to death there.
And they bring him upon horses and bury him with his fathers in the city of Judah.
Uzziah's Prosperous Reign · 26:1–15
And all the people of Judah take Uzziah, who is sixteen years old, and make him king instead of his father Amaziah.
He builds Eloth and restores it to Judah, after the king sleeps with his fathers.
Uzziah is sixteen years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name is Jecoliah of Jerusalem.
And he does what is right in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that his father Amaziah had done.
He sets himself to seek God in the days of Zechariah, who instructed him in the fear of God, and as long as he seeks the LORD, God makes him prosper.

He goes out and makes war against the Philistines and breaks down the wall of Gath and the wall of Jabneh and the wall of Ashdod, and he builds cities in the territory of Ashdod and elsewhere among the Philistines.
God helps him against the Philistines and against the Arabians who live in Gur-baal and against the Meunites.
The Ammonites pay tribute to Uzziah, and his fame spreads even to the border of Egypt, for he grows exceedingly strong.
Moreover, Uzziah builds towers in Jerusalem at the Corner Gate and at the Valley Gate and at the Angle, and fortifies them.

And he builds towers in the wilderness and cuts out many cisterns, for he has large herds, both in the Shephelah and in the plain, and he has farmers and vinedressers in the hills and in the fertile lands, for he loves the soil.

Moreover, Uzziah has an army of soldiers, fit for war, in divisions according to the numbers in the muster made by Jeiel the secretary and Maaseiah the officer, under the direction of Hananiah, one of the king's commanders.
The whole number of the heads of fathers' houses of mighty men of valour is two thousand six hundred.
Under their command is an army of three hundred and seven thousand five hundred, who make war with mighty power, to help the king against the enemy.
And Uzziah prepares for all the army shields, spears, helmets, coats of mail, bows, and stones for slinging.

In Jerusalem he makes machines, invented by skilful men, to be on the towers and the corners, to shoot arrows and great stones. And his fame spread far, for he is marvellously helped, till he is strong.
Uzziah's Pride and Leprosy · 26:16–23
But when he is strong, he grows proud, to his destruction. For he is unfaithful to the LORD his God and enters the temple of the LORD to burn incense on the altar of incense.
But Azariah the priest goes in after him, with eighty priests of the LORD who are men of valour,

and they withstand King Uzziah and say to him, “It is not for you, Uzziah, to burn incense to the LORD, but for the priests the sons of Aaron, who are consecrated to burn incense. Go out of the sanctuary, for you have done wrong, and it will bring you no honor from the LORD God.“

Then Uzziah is angry. Now he has a censer in his hand to burn incense, and when he becomes angry with the priests, leprosy breaks out on his forehead in the presence of the priests in the house of the LORD, by the altar of incense.

And Azariah the chief priest and all the priests look at him, and behold, he is leprous in his forehead! And they rush him out quickly, and he himself hurries to go out, because the LORD has struck him.

And King Uzziah is a leper to the day of his death, and being a leper lives in a separate house, for he is excluded from the house of the LORD. And Jotham his son is over the king's household, governing the people of the land.
Now the rest of the acts of Uzziah, from first to last, Isaiah the prophet the son of Amoz writes.
And Uzziah sleeps with his fathers, and they bury him with his fathers in the burial field that belonged to the kings, for they say, “He is a leper.“ And Jotham his son reigns in his place.
Jotham's Faithful Reign · 27:1–9
Jotham is twenty-five years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother's name is Jerushah the daughter of Zadok.
And he does what is right in the eyes of the LORD according to all that his father Uzziah had done — except he does not enter the temple of the LORD. But the people still act corruptly.
He builds the upper gate of the house of the LORD and does much building on the wall of Ophel.
Moreover, he builds cities in the hill country of Judah, and in the forests he builds fortresses and towers.

He fights with the king of the Ammonites and prevails over them. And the Ammonites give him that year one hundred talents of silver, and ten thousand cors of wheat and ten thousand of barley. The Ammonites pay him the same amount in the second and the third years.
So Jotham becomes mighty, because he orders his ways before the LORD his God.
Now the rest of the acts of Jotham, and all his wars and his ways, behold, they are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah.
He is twenty-five years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns sixteen years in Jerusalem.
And Jotham sleeps with his fathers, and they bury him in the city of David, and Ahaz his son reigns in his place.
Ahaz's Wicked Reign · 28:1–8
Ahaz is twenty years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns sixteen years in Jerusalem. And he does not do what is right in the eyes of the LORD, as his father David had done,
but he walks in the ways of the kings of Israel. He even makes metal images for the Baals,
and he makes offerings in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom and burns his sons as an offering, according to the abominations of the nations whom the LORD drove out before the people of Israel.
And he sacrifices and makes offerings on the high places and on the hills and under every green tree.

Therefore the LORD his God gives him into the hand of the king of Syria, who defeats him and takes captive a great number of his people and brings them to Damascus. He is also given into the hand of the king of Israel, who strikes him with great force.
For Pekah the son of Remaliah killed 120,000 from Judah in one day, all of them men of valour, because they had forsaken the LORD, the God of their fathers.
And Zichri, a mighty man of Ephraim, kills Maaseiah the king's son and Azrikam the commander of the palace and Elkanah the next in authority to the king.
The men of Israel take captive 200,000 of their relatives, women, sons, and daughters. They also take much spoil from them and bring the spoil to Samaria.
The Prophet Oded and the Northern Captives · 28:9–15

But a prophet of the LORD is there, whose name is Oded, and he goes out to meet the army that came to Samaria and says to them, “Behold, because the LORD, the God of your fathers, was angry with Judah, he gave them into your hand, but you have killed them in a rage that has reached up to heaven.
And now you intend to subjugate the people of Judah and Jerusalem, male and female, as your slaves. Have you not sins of your own against the LORD your God?
Now hear me, and send back the captives from your relatives whom you have taken, for the fierce wrath of the LORD is upon you.“

Certain chiefs also of the men of Ephraim, Azariah the son of Johanan, Berechiah the son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah the son of Shallum, and Amasa the son of Hadlai, stand up against those who are coming from the war

and say to them, “You shall not bring the captives in here, for you propose to bring upon us guilt against the LORD in addition to our present sins and guilt. For our guilt is already great, and there is fierce wrath against Israel.“
So the armed men leave the captives and the spoil before the princes and all the assembly.

And the men who have been mentioned by name rise and take the captives, and with the spoil they clothe all who are naked among them. They clothe them, give them sandals, provide them with food and drink, and anoint them, and carrying all the feeble among them on donkeys, they bring them to their relatives at Jericho, the city of palms. Then they return to Samaria.
Ahaz Appeals to Assyria · 28:16–27
At that time King Ahaz sends to the king of Assyria for help.
For the Edomites had again invaded and defeated Judah and carried away captives.

And the Philistines had made raids on the cities in the Shephelah and the Negeb of Judah and had taken Beth-shemesh, Aijalon, Gederoth, Soco with its villages, Timnah with its villages, and Gimzo with its villages, and they settle there.
For the LORD humbles Judah because of Ahaz king of Israel, for he has made Judah act sinfully and has been very unfaithful to the LORD.
So Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria comes against him and afflicts him instead of strengthening him.
For Ahaz takes a portion from the house of the LORD and the house of the king and of the princes, and gives tribute to the king of Assyria, but it does not help him.
In the time of his distress he becomes yet more faithless to the LORD — this same King Ahaz.

For he sacrifices to the gods of Damascus that had defeated him and says, “Because the gods of the kings of Syria helped them, I will sacrifice to them that they may help me.“ But they are the ruin of him and of all Israel.

And Ahaz gathers together the vessels of the house of God and cuts in pieces the vessels of the house of God, and he shuts up the doors of the house of the LORD, and he makes himself altars in every corner of Jerusalem.
In every city of Judah he makes high places to make offerings to other gods, provoking to anger the LORD, the God of his fathers.
Now the rest of his acts and all his ways, from first to last, behold, they are written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
And Ahaz sleeps with his fathers, and they bury him in the city of Jerusalem, for they do not bring him into the tombs of the kings of Israel. And Hezekiah his son reigns in his place.
Hezekiah Opens the Temple · 29:1–11
Hezekiah begins to reign when he is twenty-five years old, and he reigns twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name is Abijah the daughter of Zechariah.
And he does what is right in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that David his father had done.
In the first year of his reign, in the first month, he opens the doors of the house of the LORD and repairs them.
He brings in the priests and the Levites and assembles them in the square on the east
and says to them, “Hear me, Levites! Now consecrate yourselves, and consecrate the house of the LORD, the God of your fathers, and carry out the filth from the holy place.

For our fathers have been unfaithful and have done what was evil in the sight of the LORD our God. They have forsaken him and have turned away their faces from the habitation of the LORD and turned their backs.
They also shut the doors of the vestibule and put out the lamps and have not burned incense or offered burnt offerings in the holy place to the God of Israel.
Therefore the wrath of the LORD came on Judah and Jerusalem, and he has made them an object of horror, of astonishment, and of hissing, as you see with your own eyes.
For behold, our fathers have fallen by the sword, and our sons and our daughters and our wives are in captivity for this.
Now it is in my heart to make a covenant with the LORD, the God of Israel, in order that his fierce anger may turn away from us.
My sons, do not now be negligent, for the LORD has chosen you to stand before him, to minister to him and to be his ministers and make offerings to him.“
The Temple Cleansed · 29:12–19

Then the Levites arise: Mahath the son of Amasai, and Joel the son of Azariah, of the sons of the Kohathites; and of the sons of Merari, Kish the son of Abdi, and Azariah the son of Jehallelel; and of the Gershonites, Joah the son of Zimmah, and Eden the son of Joah;
and of the sons of Elizaphan, Shimri and Jeuel; and of the sons of Asaph, Zechariah and Mattaniah;
and of the sons of Heman, Jehuel and Shimei; and of the sons of Jeduthun, Shemaiah and Uzziel.

And for the sons of Aaron, the priests, who are in the fields of common land belonging to their cities, there are men in every city who are designated by name to distribute portions to every male among the priests and to everyone among the Levites who is enrolled.
Thus Hezekiah does throughout all Judah, and he does what is good and right and faithful before the LORD his God.

“Thus says Sennacherib king of Assyria, 'On what are you trusting, that you endure the siege in Jerusalem?
Is not Hezekiah misleading you, that he may give you over to die by famine and by thirst, when he tells you, “The LORD our God will deliver us from the hand of the king of Assyria“?
Has not this same Hezekiah taken away his high places and his altars and commanded Judah and Jerusalem, “Before one altar you shall worship, and on it you shall make your offerings“?
Do you not know what I and my fathers have done to all the peoples of other lands? Were the gods of the nations of those lands at all able to deliver their lands out of my hand?
Who among all the gods of those nations that my fathers devoted to destruction was able to deliver his people from my hand, that your God should be able to deliver you from my hand?

Now, therefore, do not let Hezekiah deceive you or mislead you in this fashion, and do not believe him, for no god of any nation or kingdom has been able to deliver his people from my hand or from the hand of my fathers. How much less will your God deliver you out of my hand!'“

Then Hezekiah the king and Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, pray because of this and cry to heaven.

So the LORD saves Hezekiah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem from the hand of Sennacherib king of Assyria and from the hand of all his enemies, and he provides for them on every side.
And many bring offerings to Jerusalem and precious gifts to Hezekiah king of Judah, so that he is exalted in the sight of all nations from that time onward.

In those days Hezekiah becomes sick and is at the point of death, and he prays to the LORD, and he answers him and gives him a sign.
But Hezekiah does not make return according to the benefit done to him, for his heart is proud. Therefore wrath comes upon him and Judah and Jerusalem.
But Hezekiah humbles himself for the pride of his heart, both he and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so that the wrath of the LORD does not come upon them in the days of Hezekiah.
And Hezekiah has very great riches and honor, and he makes for himself treasuries for silver, gold, precious stones, spices, shields, and all kinds of desirable objects;
storehouses also for the yield of grain, wine, and oil; and stalls for all kinds of cattle, and sheepfolds.
He likewise provides cities for himself, and flocks and herds in abundance, for God gives him very great possessions.
This same Hezekiah closes the upper outlet of the waters of Gihon and directs them down to the west side of the city of David. And Hezekiah prospers in all his works.

And so in the matter of the envoys of the princes of Babylon, who are sent to him to enquire about the sign that was done in the land, God leaves him to himself, in order to test him and to know all that was in his heart.
Now the rest of the acts of Hezekiah and his good deeds, behold, they are written in the vision of Isaiah the prophet the son of Amoz, in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.

And Hezekiah sleeps with his fathers, and they bury him in the upper part of the tombs of the sons of David, and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem do him honor at his death. And Manasseh his son reigns in his place.
Manasseh's Wickedness · 33:1–9
Manasseh is twelve years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns fifty-five years in Jerusalem.
And he does what is evil in the sight of the LORD, according to the abominations of the nations whom the LORD drove out before the people of Israel.
For he rebuilds the high places that his father Hezekiah had broken down, and he erects altars to the Baals, and makes Asherahs, and worships all the host of heaven and serves them.
And he builds altars in the house of the LORD, of which the LORD had said, “In Jerusalem shall my name be forever.“
And he builds altars for all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of the LORD.

And he burns his sons as an offering in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, and uses fortune-telling and omens and sorcery, and deals with mediums and with necromancers. He does much evil in the sight of the LORD, provoking him to anger.

And the carved image of the idol that he had made he sets in the house of God, of which God had said to David and to Solomon his son, “In this house, and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I will put my name forever.

And I will not again remove the foot of Israel from the land that I appointed for your fathers, if only they are careful to do all that I have commanded them, all the law, the statutes, and the rules given through Moses.“
Manasseh leads Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem astray, to do more evil than the nations whom the LORD destroyed before the people of Israel.

The LORD speaks to Manasseh and to his people, but they pay no attention.
Therefore the LORD brings upon them the commanders of the army of the king of Assyria, who capture Manasseh with hooks and bind him with chains of bronze and bring him to Babylon.
And when he is in distress, he entreats the favour of the LORD his God and humbles himself greatly before the God of his fathers.
He prays to him, and God is moved by his entreaty and hears his plea and brings him again to Jerusalem into his kingdom. Then Manasseh knows that the LORD is God.

Afterwards he builds an outer wall for the city of David west of Gihon, in the valley, and for the entrance into the Fish Gate, and carries it around Ophel, and raises it to a very great height. He also puts commanders of the army in all the fortified cities in Judah.

And he takes away the foreign gods and the idol from the house of the LORD, and all the altars that he had built on the mountain of the house of the LORD and in Jerusalem, and he throws them outside the city.
He also restores the altar of the LORD and offers on it sacrifices of peace offerings and of thanksgiving, and he commands Judah to serve the LORD, the God of Israel.
Nevertheless, the people still sacrifice at the high places, but only to the LORD their God.

Now the rest of the acts of Manasseh, and his prayer to his God, and the words of the seers who spoke to him in the name of the LORD, the God of Israel, behold, they are in the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.

And his prayer, and how God was moved by his entreaty, and all his sin and his faithlessness, and the sites on which he built high places and set up the Asherahs and the images, before he humbled himself, behold, they are written in the Chronicles of the Seers.
So Manasseh sleeps with his fathers, and they bury him in his house. And Amon his son reigns in his place.

And he does what is evil in the sight of the LORD, as Manasseh his father had done. Amon sacrifices to all the images that Manasseh his father had made, and serves them.
And he does not humble himself before the LORD, as Manasseh his father had humbled himself, but this same Amon incurs guilt more and more.
And his servants conspire against him and put him to death in his house.

For in the eighth year of his reign, while he is yet a boy, he begins to seek the God of David his father, and in the twelfth year he begins to purge Judah and Jerusalem of the high places, the Asherahs, the carved idols, and the metal images.

And they tear down in his presence the altars of the Baals, and he cuts down the incense altars that stood above them. And he breaks in pieces the Asherahs and the carved and the metal images, and he makes dust of them and scatters it over the graves of those who had sacrificed to them.
He also burns the bones of the priests on their altars and cleanses Judah and Jerusalem.

Now in the eighteenth year of his reign, when he has cleansed the land and the house, he sends Shaphan the son of Azaliah, and Maaseiah the governor of the city, and Joah the son of Joahaz, the recorder, to repair the house of the LORD his God.

They come to Hilkiah the high priest and deliver the money that had been brought into the house of God, which the Levites, the keepers of the threshold, had collected from Manasseh and Ephraim and from all the remnant of Israel and from all Judah and Benjamin and from the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
And they give it to the workmen who are working in the house of the LORD. And the workmen who are working in the house of the LORD give it for repairing and restoring the house.
They give it to the craftsmen and the builders to buy quarried stone, and timber for binders and beams for the buildings that the kings of Judah have let go to ruin.

And the men do the work faithfully. Over them are set Jahath and Obadiah the Levites, of the sons of Merari, and Zechariah and Meshullam, of the sons of the Kohathites, to oversee. And the Levites, all who are skilful with instruments of music,
are over the burden-bearers and superintend all who do work in every kind of service. And some of the Levites are scribes and officials and gatekeepers.

Shaphan brings the book to the king, and further reports to the king, “All that was committed to your servants they are doing.
They have emptied out the money that was found in the house of the LORD and have given it into the hand of the overseers and the workmen.“
Then Shaphan the secretary tells the king, “Hilkiah the priest has given me a book.“ And Shaphan reads from it before the king.
And when the king hears the words of the Law, he tears his clothes.
And the king commands Hilkiah, Ahikam the son of Shaphan, Abdon the son of Micah, Shaphan the secretary, and Asaiah the king's servant, saying,

“Go, inquire of the LORD for me and for those who are left in Israel and in Judah, concerning the words of the book that has been found. So Hilkiah and those whom the king had sent go to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum the son of Tokhath, son of Hasrah, keeper of the wardrobe — now she lives in Jerusalem in the Second Quarter — and they speak to her to that effect.
And she says to them, “Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: 'Tell the man who sent you to me,
Thus says the LORD, Behold, I will bring disaster upon this place and upon its inhabitants, all the curses that are written in the book that was read before the king of Judah.

Because they have forsaken me and have made offerings to other gods, that they might provoke me to anger with all the works of their hands, therefore my wrath will be poured out on this place and will not be quenched.'
But to the king of Judah, who sent you to inquire of the LORD, thus shall you say to him, Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Regarding the words that you have heard,

because your heart was tender and you humbled yourself before God when you heard his words against this place and its inhabitants, and you have humbled yourself before me and have torn your clothes and wept before me, I also have heard you, declares the LORD.

Behold, I will gather you to your fathers, and you shall be gathered to your grave in peace, and your eyes shall not see all the disaster that I will bring upon this place and its inhabitants.'“ And they bring back word to the king.

Then the king sends and gathers together all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

And the king goes up to the house of the LORD, with all the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem and the priests and the Levites, all the people both great and small. And he reads in their hearing all the words of the Book of the Covenant that had been found in the house of the LORD.

And Josiah takes away all the abominations from all the territory that belonged to the people of Israel and makes all who are present in Israel serve the LORD their God. All his days they do not turn away from following the LORD, the God of their fathers.

And they slaughter the Passover lamb, and the priests throw the blood that they receive from them while the Levites skin the animals.

And they roast the Passover lamb with fire according to the rule; and they boil the holy offerings in pots, in cauldrons, and in pans, and carry them quickly to all the lay people.

And afterward they prepare for themselves and for the priests, because the priests the sons of Aaron were busy until night offering the burnt offerings and the fat parts. So the Levites prepare for themselves and for the priests, the sons of Aaron.

The singers, the sons of Asaph, are in their place according to the command of David, and Asaph, and Heman, and Jeduthun the king's seer; and the gatekeepers are at each gate. They need not depart from their service, for their brothers the Levites prepare for them.
So all the service of the LORD is prepared that day, to keep the Passover and to offer burnt offerings on the altar of the LORD, according to the command of King Josiah.
And the people of Israel who are present keep the Passover at that time, and the Feast of Unleavened Bread seven days.

No Passover like it had been kept in Israel since the days of Samuel the prophet. None of the kings of Israel had kept such a Passover as was kept by Josiah, and the priests, and the Levites, and all Judah and Israel who are present, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
In the eighteenth year of the reign of Josiah this Passover is kept.
The Death of Josiah · 35:20–27
After all this, when Josiah has prepared the temple, Neco king of Egypt goes up to fight at Carchemish on the Euphrates, and Josiah goes out to meet him.

But he sends envoys to him, saying, “What have we to do with each other, king of Judah? I am not coming against you this day, but against the house with which I am at war. And God has commanded me to hurry. Stop opposing God, who is with me, lest he destroy you.“

Nevertheless Josiah does not turn away from him, but disguises himself in order to fight with him. He does not listen to the words of Neco from the mouth of God, and comes to fight in the Valley of Megiddo.
And the archers shoot King Josiah. And the king says to his servants, “Take me away, for I am badly wounded.“

So his servants take him out of the chariot and carry him in his second chariot and bring him to Jerusalem. And he dies and is buried in the tombs of his fathers. All Judah and Jerusalem mourn for Josiah.

Jeremiah also utters a lament for Josiah; and all the singing men and singing women have spoken of Josiah in their laments to this day. They make these a rule in Israel; behold, they are written in the Laments.
Now the rest of the acts of Josiah, and his good deeds according to what is written in the Law of the LORD,
and his acts, first and last, behold, they are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah.

Nebuchadnezzar also carries part of the vessels of the house of the LORD to Babylon and puts them in his palace in Babylon.

Now the rest of the acts of Jehoiakim, and the abominations that he commits, and what is found against him, behold, they are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah. And Jehoiachin his son reigns in his place.
