Moved in his very gut, he reaches out his hand and touches him. “I am willing,” he says. “Be clean.”
And immediately the leprosy leaves him, and he is made clean.
And warning him sternly, he sends him away at once,
saying: “See that you say nothing to anyone. But go — show yourself to the priest and offer what Moses commanded for your cleansing, as a testimony to them.”

But he goes out and begins to proclaim it freely and to spread the word — so that Jesus can no longer openly enter a town. He stays out in deserted places. And people keep coming to him from everywhere.
THE PARALYZED MAN
After some days he comes back into Capernaum. Word gets out that he is home.
And so many gather that there is no room left — not even at the door. And he speaks the word to them.
They come bringing a paralyzed man to him, carried by four.
And not being able to bring him in because of the crowd, they unroof the roof above him. Having dug through it, they lower the mat on which the paralyzed man is lying.
Seeing their faith, Jesus says to the paralyzed man: “Child — your sins are released.”
But some of the scribes are sitting there, reasoning in their hearts:
“Why does this man speak like this? He is blaspheming. Who can release sins except God — God alone?”
And immediately Jesus, knowing in his spirit that they are reasoning this way within themselves, says to them: “Why are you reasoning these things in your hearts?
Which is easier — to say to the paralyzed man, “Your sins are released,” or to say, “Get up, take your mat, and walk”?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to release sins —”
he says to the paralyzed man — “I say to you: get up, take your mat, and go home.”
And he gets up. Immediately. He takes the mat and goes out in front of everyone. They are all amazed and glorify God, saying: “We have never seen anything like this.”
THE CALL OF LEVI
He goes out again beside the sea. The whole crowd comes to him, and he teaches them.
And passing by, he sees Levi the son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax booth. “Follow me,” he says to him. And he gets up and follows him.
And it happens — he is reclining at table in Levi’s house, and many tax collectors and sinners are reclining with Jesus and his disciples. For there are many of them, and they are following him.
The scribes of the Pharisees, seeing that he is eating with sinners and tax collectors, say to his disciples: “Why does he eat with tax collectors and sinners?”
Hearing this, Jesus says to them: “The healthy have no need of a doctor — but those who are sick. I did not come to call the righteous — but sinners.”
THE QUESTION ABOUT FASTING
John’s disciples and the Pharisees are fasting. And they come and say to him: “Why do John’s disciples and the disciples of the Pharisees fast — but your disciples do not fast?”
Jesus says to them: “Can the wedding guests fast while the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.
But days are coming when the bridegroom is taken away from them — and then they will fast in that day.
No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth onto an old garment. If they do, the new patch tears away from the old — and a worse tear is made.
And no one puts new wine into old wineskins. If they do, the wine bursts the skins — and the wine is destroyed, and the skins as well. New wine goes into fresh skins.”
LORD OF THE SABBATH
And it happens — on the Sabbath he is going through the grain fields. And his disciples begin to make their way, plucking heads of grain.
The Pharisees say to him: “Look — why are they doing what is not lawful on the Sabbath?”
And he says to them: “Have you never read what David did when he had need and was hungry — he and those with him?

How he entered the house of God in the time of Abiathar the high priest, and ate the bread of the Presence — which is not lawful for anyone to eat except the priests — and also gave it to those with him?”
And he says to them: “The Sabbath came into being for the sake of the human. Not the human for the sake of the Sabbath.
So the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath.”
THE MAN WITH THE WITHERED HAND
He enters a synagogue again. There is a man there with a withered hand.
And they watch him closely — will he heal on the Sabbath? — so that they might accuse him.
He says to the man with the withered hand: “Stand up in the middle.”
And he says to them: “Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do harm? To save a life — or to kill?” They are silent.
And looking around at them with anger — grieved at the hardness of their hearts — he says to the man: “Stretch out your hand.” He stretches it out. And his hand is restored.
And the Pharisees go out immediately and begin plotting with the Herodians against him — how they might destroy him.
THE CROWD BY THE SEA
Jesus withdraws with his disciples to the sea. A large crowd follows from Galilee —
and from Judea, and from Jerusalem, and from Idumea, and from beyond the Jordan, and from around Tyre and Sidon. A great multitude, hearing all that he is doing, comes to him.
And he tells his disciples to have a small boat ready for him because of the crowd — so they will not crush him.
For he heals many, so that all who have afflictions press in on him to touch him.
And whenever the unclean spirits see him, they throw themselves down before him and cry out: “You are the Son of God!”
And he warns them strongly not to make him known.
THE TWELVE APPOINTED
And he goes up on the mountain and calls to him those he himself wants. And they come to him.
And he appoints twelve — so that they might be with him, and so that he might send them out to proclaim,
and to have authority to drive out demons.
He appoints the twelve: Simon — to whom he gives the name Peter;
James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James — to whom he gives the name Boanerges, which means Sons of Thunder;
Andrew; Philip; Bartholomew; Matthew; Thomas; James the son of Alphaeus; Thaddaeus; Simon the Zealot;
and Judas Iscariot — who also hands him over.
A HOUSE DIVIDED
And he comes into a house. The crowd gathers again — so that they cannot even eat bread.
And when his own people hear about it, they go out to seize him. For they are saying: “He is out of his mind.”
And the scribes who have come down from Jerusalem are saying: “He has Beelzebul — and by the ruler of the demons he drives out demons.”
And calling them to him, he speaks to them in parables: “How can Satan drive out Satan?
If a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.
And if a house is divided against itself, that house will not be able to stand.
And if Satan has risen against himself and is divided — he cannot stand, but has come to an end.
But no one can enter the house of the strong man and plunder his goods unless he first binds the strong man. Then he will plunder his house.
Truly I tell you — all sins will be released to the children of men, and whatever blasphemies they may speak.
But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit does not have release into the age — but is held in an eternal sin.”
This because they are saying: “He has an unclean spirit.”
THE TRUE FAMILY
And his mother and his brothers arrive. Standing outside, they send to him and call him.
A crowd is sitting around him, and they say to him: “Look — your mother and your brothers are outside, looking for you.”
And answering them, he says: “Who is my mother? And my brothers?”
And looking around at those sitting in a circle around him, he says: “Look — my mother and my brothers.
Whoever does the will of God — this is my brother and sister and mother.”
THE PARABLE OF THE SOWER
He begins to teach again beside the sea. An enormous crowd gathers around him — so he gets into a boat and sits there, out on the water. And the whole crowd is along the shore, facing the sea.
And he teaches them many things in parables. And in his teaching he says to them:
“Listen. Look — the sower goes out to sow.
And as he sows, some falls along the path — and the birds come and devour it.
Some falls on rocky ground where there is not much soil. And immediately it springs up — because it has no depth of soil.
But when the sun rises, it is scorched. And because it has no root, it withers.
Some falls among thorns. The thorns grow up and choke it — and it produces no fruit.
And some falls into good soil and produces fruit — coming up and growing, yielding thirty, and sixty, and a hundredfold.”
And he says: “Whoever has ears to hear — let them hear.”
WHY PARABLES
And when he is alone, those around him — with the Twelve — begin asking him about the parables.
And he says to them: “To you the mystery of the kingdom of God has been given. But for those outside — everything comes in parables,
so that looking they may look and not see, and hearing they may hear and not understand, lest they turn — and be released.”
THE PARABLE EXPLAINED
And he says to them: “Do you not understand this parable? Then how will you understand any of the parables?
The sower sows the word.
And these are the ones along the path where the word is sown: when they hear, Satan comes immediately and takes away the word that was sown in them.
And these are the ones sown on rocky ground: when they hear the word, they receive it immediately with joy.
But they have no root in themselves — they are temporary. When affliction or persecution comes because of the word, they immediately fall away.
And others are the ones sown among thorns: they are those who hear the word,
but the cares of the age and the seduction of wealth and desires for other things come in and choke the word — and it produces no fruit.
And these are the ones sown on good soil: they hear the word and receive it and bear fruit — thirty, and sixty, and a hundredfold.”
THE LAMP
And he says to them: “Does the lamp come in order to be put under a basket or under a bed? Does it not come to be placed on the stand?
For there is nothing hidden except to be revealed — and nothing concealed except to come into the open.
If anyone has ears to hear — let them hear.”
And he says to them: “Pay attention to what you hear. The measure you use will be the measure used for you — and more will be added.
For to the one who has, more will be given. And from the one who has nothing — even what they have will be taken.”
THE SEED GROWING
And he says: “The kingdom of God is like this — as when a man scatters seed on the ground.
He sleeps and rises, night and day. And the seed sprouts and grows — he does not know how.
The earth produces by itself: first the blade, then the head, then the full grain in the head.
And when the grain delivers itself up, he immediately puts in the sickle — because the harvest has come.”
THE MUSTARD SEED
And he says: “How shall we liken the kingdom of God? Or with what parable shall we present it?
It is like a mustard seed — which, when sown in the ground, is the smallest of all seeds on earth.
Yet when it is sown, it comes up and becomes greater than all the garden plants and puts out large branches — so that the birds of the sky can nest in its shade.”
PARABLES AND THE CROWD
And with many parables like these he speaks the word to them — as much as they are able to hear.
He says nothing to them without a parable. But privately, to his own disciples, he explains everything.
THE STORM
And on that day, when evening comes, he says to them: “Let us cross to the other side.”
And leaving the crowd, they take him with them in the boat — just as he is. And other boats are with him.
And a great squall of wind arises. The waves beat into the boat so that it is already filling.
And he is in the stern, asleep on the cushion. And they wake him and say to him: “Teacher — don’t you care that we are perishing?”
And waking up, he rebukes the wind and says to the sea: “Silence. Be muzzled.” And the wind dies down. And there is a great calm.
And he says to them: “Why are you afraid? Do you still have no faith?”
And they fear a great fear and say to one another: “Who then is this — that even the wind and the sea obey him?”
THE GERASENE DEMONIAC
They come to the other side of the sea — to the region of the Gerasenes.
And immediately, as he steps out of the boat, a man with an unclean spirit comes out of the tombs and meets him.
He lives among the tombs. And no one can bind him anymore — not even with a chain.
For he has often been bound with shackles and chains — and the chains have been wrenched apart by him, and the shackles smashed. No one has the strength to subdue him.
And continually — night and day — among the tombs and on the mountains, he is crying out and cutting himself with stones.
And seeing Jesus from a distance, he runs and prostrates himself before him.
And crying out with a loud voice he says: “What do you want with me, Jesus — Son of the Most High God? I adjure you by God: do not torment me!”
For Jesus has been saying to him: “Come out of the man, you unclean spirit.”
And he asks him: “What is your name?” “My name is Legion,” he says — “for we are many.”
And he begs him urgently not to send them out of the region.
Now there is a large herd of pigs on the hillside, feeding.
And they beg him: “Send us into the pigs — let us enter them.”
And he gives them permission. And the unclean spirits come out and enter the pigs. And the herd rushes down the steep bank into the sea — about two thousand of them. And they are choked in the sea.
The herdsmen flee and report it in the town and in the countryside. And people come out to see what has happened.
And they come to Jesus and see the man who had been possessed by the legion — sitting, clothed, in his right mind. And they are afraid.
And those who had seen it tell them what happened to the demon-possessed man — and about the pigs.
And they begin to beg Jesus to leave their region.
And as he is getting into the boat, the man who had been possessed begs him — that he might be with him.
And Jesus does not allow him, but says to him: “Go home to your own people. And tell them how much the Lord has done for you — and how he had mercy on you.”
And he goes away and begins to proclaim in the Decapolis how much Jesus has done for him. And everyone is astonished.
JAIRUS, AND THE WOMAN WITH THE HEMORRHAGE
When Jesus has crossed again in the boat to the other side, a large crowd gathers around him. And he is beside the sea.
And one of the synagogue rulers comes — Jairus by name. And seeing him, he falls at his feet
and begs him urgently: “My little daughter is at the point of death. Come and lay your hands on her — so that she may be saved and live.”
And he goes with him. And a large crowd follows and presses in on him.
And a woman who has had a discharge of blood for twelve years —
and who has suffered much under many doctors, and has spent everything she had, and is not better but rather has grown worse —
hears about Jesus. She comes through the crowd from behind and touches his garment.
For she has been saying to herself: “If I touch even his garments, I will be saved.”
And immediately the source of her blood dries up. And she knows in her body that she is healed of her affliction.
And immediately Jesus, knowing in himself that power has gone out from him, turns around in the crowd and says: “Who touched my garments?”
And his disciples say to him: “You see the crowd pressing in on you — and you say, ‘Who touched me?’”
And he looks around to see who has done this.
And the woman — knowing what has happened to her — comes in fear and trembling. She falls before him and tells him the whole truth.
And he says to her: “Daughter — your faith has saved you. Go in peace. Be well from your affliction.”
While he is still speaking, people come from the house of the synagogue ruler: “Your daughter has died. Why trouble the teacher any further?”
But overhearing what is said, Jesus says to the synagogue ruler: “Don’t be afraid. Only believe.”
And he allows no one to follow with him except Peter and James and John the brother of James.
They come to the house of the synagogue ruler. And he sees the commotion — people weeping and wailing loudly.
And going in he says to them: “Why this commotion and weeping? The child has not died — she is sleeping.”
And they laugh at him. But putting them all outside, he takes the father and the mother of the child and those with him — and goes in where the child is.
And taking the child by the hand, he says to her: “Talitha koum” — which means: “Little girl, I say to you — get up.”
And immediately the little girl gets up and walks about. She is twelve years old. And immediately they are overcome with great astonishment.
And he gives them strict orders that no one should know about this. And he tells them to give her something to eat.
THE REJECTION AT NAZARETH
He leaves there and comes to his hometown. And his disciples follow him.

When the Sabbath comes, he begins to teach in the synagogue. And many who hear him are astonished: “Where does this man get these things? What is this wisdom given to him? What mighty works are done by his hands?
Is this not the craftsman — the son of Mary and brother of James and Joses and Judas and Simon? And are not his sisters here with us?” And they are tripped up by him.
And Jesus says to them: “A prophet is not without honor except in his hometown and among his relatives and in his own house.”
And he is not able to do any mighty work there — except that he lays his hands on a few sick people and heals them.
And he marvels at their unbelief. And he goes around among the villages teaching.
THE SENDING OF THE TWELVE
And he calls the Twelve and begins to send them out two by two. And he gives them authority over unclean spirits.
And he charges them to take nothing for the road except a staff — no bread, no bag, no money in their belt.
But to wear sandals. And not to put on two tunics.
And he says to them: “Wherever you enter a house, stay there until you leave the place.
And wherever they do not receive you and they do not listen to you — when you leave, shake off the dust from under your feet as a testimony against them.”
And going out, they proclaim that people should repent.
And they drive out many demons. And they anoint many sick people with oil and heal them.
HEROD AND THE DEATH OF JOHN
King Herod hears of it — for Jesus’ name has become known. And people are saying: “John the Baptist has been raised from the dead. That is why these powers are at work in him.”
But others say: “He is Elijah.” And others: “He is a prophet — like one of the prophets of old.”
But when Herod hears, he says: “John — whom I beheaded — he has been raised.”
For Herod himself had sent and seized John and bound him in prison — on account of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife, whom he had married.
For John had been saying to Herod: “It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife.”
And Herodias had it in for him and wanted to kill him. But she could not —
for Herod feared John, knowing him to be a righteous and holy man, and kept him safe. And when he heard him he was deeply perplexed — and yet he heard him gladly.
But an opportune day comes — when Herod on his birthday gives a banquet for his nobles and his military commanders and the leading men of Galilee.
And the daughter of Herodias comes in and dances. She pleases Herod and his guests. And the king says to the girl: “Ask me for whatever you want and I will give it to you.”
And he swears to her: “Whatever you ask I will give you — up to half my kingdom.”
And she goes out and says to her mother: “What should I ask for?” “The head of John the Baptist,” she says.
And coming back immediately — with urgency — she asks the king: “I want you to give me right now the head of John the Baptist on a platter.”
And the king is deeply grieved. But because of his oaths and because of his guests, he does not want to refuse her.
And immediately the king sends an executioner with orders to bring his head. And he goes and beheads him in the prison
and brings his head on a platter and gives it to the girl. And the girl gives it to her mother.
When his disciples hear of it, they come and take his body and lay it in a tomb.
THE RETURN AND THE FEEDING
The apostles gather around Jesus and report to him everything they have done and everything they have taught.
And he says to them: “Come away by yourselves to a deserted place and rest a little.” For many are coming and going, and they have no opportunity even to eat.
And they go away in the boat to a deserted place by themselves.
And many see them going and recognize them. And from all the towns they run there on foot and arrive ahead of them.
And stepping out of the boat, he sees a large crowd. And his heart breaks for them — because they are like sheep without a shepherd. And he begins to teach them many things.
And when the hour is already late, his disciples come to him and say: “This is a deserted place and the hour is already late.
Send them away — so they can go into the surrounding countryside and villages and buy themselves something to eat.”
But he answers them: “You give them something to eat.” “Are we to go and spend two hundred denarii on bread,” they say, “and give it to them to eat?”
“How many loaves do you have?” he says. “Go and see.” And when they find out, they say: “Five. And two fish.”
And he orders them to have everyone recline in groups on the green grass.
And they recline — group by group — in hundreds and in fifties.

And taking the five loaves and the two fish, he looks up to heaven and blesses and breaks the loaves and gives them to the disciples to set before the people. And he divides the two fish among them all.
And they all eat and are satisfied.
And they gather up twelve baskets full of broken pieces — and pieces of the fish.
And those who ate the loaves are five thousand men.
WALKING ON THE WATER
And immediately he makes his disciples get into the boat and go ahead to the other side — to Bethsaida — while he dismisses the crowd.
And after taking leave of them, he goes up on the mountain to pray.
When evening comes, the boat is in the middle of the sea, and he is alone on the land.
And seeing them straining at the oars — for the wind is against them — sometime between three and six in the morning he comes toward them, walking on the sea. And he intends to pass by them.
But when they see him walking on the sea, they think it is a ghost and cry out.
For they all see him and are terrified. But immediately he speaks with them: “Take courage — it is I. Do not be afraid.”
And he gets into the boat with them, and the wind dies down. And they are utterly astounded within themselves —
for they had not understood about the loaves. Their hearts were hardened.
HEALINGS AT GENNESARET
And when they have crossed over, they come to land at Gennesaret and moor the boat.
And when they get out of the boat, immediately the people recognize him.
They run through that whole region and begin to carry around on mats those who are sick — to wherever they hear he is.

And wherever he enters — into villages or cities or countryside — they lay the sick in the marketplaces and beg him that they might touch even the hem of his garment. And as many as touch it are saved.
THE TRADITION OF THE ELDERS
The Pharisees gather around him — along with some of the scribes who have come from Jerusalem.
And they see that some of his disciples are eating bread with unclean hands — that is, unwashed.
For the Pharisees — and all the Jews — do not eat unless they wash their hands with the fist, holding to the tradition of the elders.
And when they come from the marketplace, they do not eat unless they wash. And there are many other things they hold to — the washing of cups and pitchers and copper vessels and dining couches.
And the Pharisees and scribes ask him: “Why do your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders? Why do they eat bread with unclean hands?”
And he says to them: “Isaiah prophesied rightly about you hypocrites — as it is written:
‘This people honors me with their lips,
but their heart is far from me.
They worship me in vain,
teaching as doctrines the commandments of men.’
Leaving aside the commandment of God, you hold to the tradition of men.”
And he says to them: “How well you set aside the commandment of God — in order to keep your tradition.
For Moses said: ‘Honor your father and your mother’ — and: ‘Whoever speaks evil of father or mother must surely die.’
But you say: if a man says to his father or his mother, ‘Whatever I might have given you is Korban’ — that is, a gift dedicated to God —
you no longer allow him to do anything for his father or mother.
You are nullifying the word of God by your tradition that you have handed down. And many such things you do.”
WHAT DEFILES
And calling the crowd to him again, he says to them: “Hear me — all of you — and understand.
There is nothing outside a person that by going into them can defile them. But the things that come out of a person — those are what defile.”
And when he has gone into a house away from the crowd, his disciples ask him about the parable.
And he says to them: “Are you also so without understanding? Do you not see that whatever goes into a person from outside cannot defile them —
since it does not enter the heart but the stomach, and passes out into the sewer?” — declaring all foods clean.
And he says: “What comes out of a person — that is what defiles a person.
For from within — out of the human heart — come evil intentions: sexual immorality, theft, murder,
adultery, greed, wickedness, deceit, lewdness, envy, slander, pride, foolishness.
All these evil things come from within — and they defile a person.”
THE SYROPHOENICIAN WOMAN
Rising from there, he goes into the region of Tyre. And going into a house, he wants no one to know — but he cannot escape notice.
For immediately a woman whose little daughter has an unclean spirit hears about him and comes and falls at his feet.
The woman is a Greek — Syrophoenician by race. And she begs him to drive the demon out of her daughter.
And he says to her: “Let the children first be satisfied — for it is not good to take the children’s bread and throw it to the little dogs.”
But she answers him: “Lord — even the little dogs under the table eat the children’s crumbs.”
And he says to her: “Because of this word — go. The demon has gone out of your daughter.”
And going home, she finds the child lying on the bed — and the demon gone.
THE DEAF MAN
And going out again from the region of Tyre, he comes through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee — through the region of the Decapolis.
And they bring to him a man who is deaf and speaks with difficulty. And they beg him to lay his hand on him.
And taking him aside privately from the crowd, he puts his fingers into his ears — and having spat, he touches his tongue.
And looking up to heaven, he sighs deeply and says to him: “Ephphatha” — which means: “Be opened.”
And immediately his ears are opened. And the bond of his tongue is released. And he speaks correctly.
And Jesus charges them to tell no one. But the more he charges them, the more they proclaim it.
And they are astonished beyond all measure: “He has done all things well,” they say. “He even makes the deaf hear and the mute speak.”
THE FEEDING OF THE FOUR THOUSAND
In those days, when again a great crowd has gathered and they have nothing to eat, he calls his disciples and says to them:
“My heart breaks for this crowd — they have been with me now for three days and have nothing to eat.
And if I send them away hungry to their homes, they will faint on the road — and some of them have come from far away.”
And his disciples answer him: “How can anyone satisfy these people with bread here in this deserted place?”
And he asks them: “How many loaves do you have?” “Seven,” they say.

And he directs the crowd to sit down on the ground. And taking the seven loaves, he gives thanks and breaks them and gives them to his disciples to set before the people. And they set them before the crowd.
And they have a few small fish. And having blessed them, he says to distribute these also.
And they eat and are satisfied. And they gather up seven baskets of broken pieces left over.
There are about four thousand people. And he sends them away.
And immediately getting into the boat with his disciples, he comes to the region of Dalmanutha.
THE DEMAND FOR A SIGN
And the Pharisees come out and begin to debate with him, seeking from him a sign from heaven — testing him.
And sighing deeply in his spirit, he says: “Why does this generation seek a sign? Truly I tell you — no sign will be given to this generation.”
And leaving them, he gets into the boat again and goes to the other side.
THE LEAVEN OF THE PHARISEES
And they have forgotten to bring bread — and they have only one loaf with them in the boat.
And he charges them: “Watch out — be on guard against the leaven of the Pharisees and the leaven of Herod.”
And they begin talking with one another about the fact that they have no bread.
And knowing this, he says to them: “Why are you talking about having no bread? Do you not yet see or understand? Do you have hardened hearts?
Having eyes — do you not see? And having ears — do you not hear? And do you not remember?
When I broke the five loaves for the five thousand — how many baskets full of broken pieces did you gather?” “Twelve,” they say.
“And the seven for the four thousand — how many baskets full of broken pieces did you gather?” “Seven,” they say.
And he says to them: “Do you not yet understand?”
THE BLIND MAN OF BETHSAIDA
And they come to Bethsaida. And they bring to him a blind man and beg him to touch him.
And taking the blind man by the hand, he leads him outside the village. And spitting into his eyes and laying his hands on him, he asks him: “Do you see anything?”
And looking up he says: “I see people — but I see them as trees, walking.”
Then he lays his hands on his eyes again. And he looks intently — and is restored and sees everything clearly.
And Jesus sends him home, saying: “Do not even enter the village.”
PETER’S CONFESSION
And Jesus goes out with his disciples to the villages of Caesarea Philippi. And on the road he asks his disciples: “Who do people say that I am?”
And they tell him: “John the Baptist. And others: Elijah. And others: one of the prophets.”
And he asks them: “But you — who do you say that I am?” Peter answers him: “You are the Messiah.”
And he sternly charges them to say nothing about him to anyone.
THE FIRST PASSION PREDICTION
And he begins to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things and be rejected by the elders and the chief priests and the scribes — and be killed — and after three days rise.
And he speaks this word openly. And Peter takes him aside and begins to rebuke him.
But turning and seeing his disciples, he rebukes Peter and says: “Get behind me, Satan. For you are not thinking the things of God — but the things of men.”
THE COST OF FOLLOWING
And calling the crowd to him with his disciples, he says to them: “If anyone wants to come after me — let them deny themselves and take up their cross and follow me.
For whoever wants to save their life will lose it. But whoever loses their life for my sake and the gospel’s will save it.
For what does it profit a person to gain the whole world and forfeit their life?
For what can a person give in exchange for their life?
For whoever is ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation — the Son of Man will also be ashamed of them when he comes in the glory of his Father with the holy angels.”
THE TRANSFIGURATION
And he says to them: “Truly I tell you — there are some standing here who will not taste death before they see the kingdom of God having come in power.”
And after six days Jesus takes Peter and James and John and brings them up a high mountain privately — just themselves. And he is transfigured before them.
And his garments become dazzling — intensely white, as no launderer on earth can whiten them.
And Elijah appears to them with Moses. And they are talking with Jesus.
And Peter answers and says to Jesus: “Rabbi — it is good for us to be here. Let us make three shelters: one for you and one for Moses and one for Elijah.”
For he does not know what to say — for they are terrified.
And a cloud comes, overshadowing them. And a voice comes out of the cloud: “This is my Son — the Beloved. Listen to him.”
And suddenly, looking around, they no longer see anyone — only Jesus with them.
THE QUESTION ABOUT ELIJAH
And as they are coming down from the mountain, he charges them to say nothing about what they have seen to anyone — until the Son of Man rises from the dead.
And they keep the word to themselves, debating with one another what “rising from the dead” means.
And they ask him: “Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”
And he says to them: “Elijah does come first and restores all things. And how is it written of the Son of Man — that he should suffer many things and be treated with contempt?
But I tell you that Elijah has come — and they did to him whatever they wanted, just as it is written of him.”
THE BOY WITH THE CONVULSING SPIRIT
And coming to the disciples, they see a large crowd around them and scribes arguing with them.
And immediately all the crowd, when they see him, are greatly amazed and run to greet him.
And he asks them: “What are you arguing about with them?”
And one from the crowd answers him: “Teacher — I brought my son to you. He has a spirit that makes him mute.
And wherever it seizes him, it throws him down. And he foams and grinds his teeth and becomes rigid. And I asked your disciples to drive it out — and they were not able.”
And he answers them: “O faithless generation — how long am I to be with you? How long am I to bear with you? Bring him to me.”
And they bring the boy to him. And when the spirit sees him, immediately it convulses the boy. And falling on the ground, he rolls about, foaming.
And Jesus asks his father: “How long has this been happening to him?” “From childhood,” he says.
“And it has often thrown him into fire and into water to destroy him. But if you are able to do anything — have compassion on us and help us.”
And Jesus says to him: “‘If you are able’ — all things are possible for the one who believes.”
Immediately the father of the boy cries out: “I believe — help my unbelief!”
And seeing that a crowd is running together, Jesus rebukes the unclean spirit: “You mute and deaf spirit — I command you: come out of him and never enter him again.”
And crying out and convulsing him terribly, it comes out. And the boy becomes like a corpse — so that most say: “He has died.”
But Jesus takes him by the hand and raises him up. And he stands.
And when he has gone into a house, his disciples ask him privately: “Why could we not drive it out?”
And he says to them: “This kind cannot be driven out by anything except prayer.”
THE SECOND PASSION PREDICTION
Going out from there, they pass through Galilee. And he does not want anyone to know —
for he is teaching his disciples and saying to them: “The Son of Man is being handed over into the hands of men. And they will kill him. And when he is killed, after three days he will rise.”
But they do not understand the saying. And they are afraid to ask him.
WHO IS THE GREATEST
And they come to Capernaum. And when he is in the house he asks them: “What were you discussing on the road?”
But they are silent — for on the road they had discussed with one another who was the greatest.
And sitting down, he calls the Twelve and says to them: “If anyone wants to be first — they shall be last of all and servant of all.”
And taking a child, he sets it in the middle of them. And taking it in his arms, he says to them:
“Whoever receives one such child in my name receives me. And whoever receives me — receives not me but the one who sent me.”
THE ONE WHO IS NOT AGAINST US
John says to him: “Teacher — we saw someone driving out demons in your name. And we tried to stop him, because he was not following us.”
But Jesus says: “Do not stop him — for there is no one who will do a mighty work in my name and be able soon after to speak evil of me.
For whoever is not against us is for us.
For truly I tell you — whoever gives you a cup of water to drink because you bear the name of Christ will by no means lose their reward.”
WARNINGS ABOUT STUMBLING
“And whoever causes one of these little ones who believe to stumble — it would be better for them if a great millstone were hung around their neck and they were thrown into the sea.
And if your hand causes you to stumble — cut it off. It is better for you to enter life crippled than to go with two hands into Gehenna — into the unquenchable fire.
And if your foot causes you to stumble — cut it off. It is better for you to enter life lame than to be thrown with two feet into Gehenna.
And if your eye causes you to stumble — tear it out. It is better for you to enter the kingdom of God with one eye than to be thrown with two eyes into Gehenna —
where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched.
For everyone will be salted with fire.
Salt is good — but if the salt has lost its saltiness, how will you make it salty again? Have salt in yourselves — and be at peace with one another.”
ON DIVORCE
And rising from there, he comes into the region of Judea and beyond the Jordan. And crowds gather to him again. And again, as was his custom, he teaches them.
And Pharisees come to him and ask: “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife?” — testing him.
He answers them: “What did Moses command you?”
They say: “Moses permitted a man to write a certificate of divorce and to send her away.”
And Jesus says to them: “Because of the hardness of your hearts he wrote you this commandment.
But from the beginning of creation —
‘Male and female he made them.
‘For this reason a man will leave his father and mother
and the two will become one flesh.’
What therefore God has joined together — let no human being separate.”
And in the house the disciples ask him again about this.
And he says to them: “Whoever divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery against her.
And if she divorces her husband and marries another — she commits adultery.”
LET THE CHILDREN COME
And they are bringing children to him so that he might touch them. But the disciples rebuke them.
And seeing this, Jesus is indignant. And he says to them: “Let the children come to me — do not stop them. For the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
Truly I tell you — whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a child will never enter it.”
And taking them in his arms, he blesses them, laying his hands on them.
THE RICH MAN
And as he is setting out on the road, a man runs up and kneels before him and asks him: “Good Teacher — what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
And Jesus says to him: “Why do you call me good? No one is good except God alone.
You know the commandments: ‘Do not murder. Do not commit adultery. Do not steal. Do not bear false witness. Do not defraud. Honor your father and mother.’”
And he says to him: “Teacher — all these I have kept from my youth.”
And looking at him, Jesus loves him. And he says to him: “You lack one thing. Go — sell everything you have and give to the poor. And you will have treasure in heaven. Then come — follow me.”
But his face falls at this word. And he goes away grieving — for he has great possessions.
THE DANGER OF WEALTH
And looking around, Jesus says to his disciples: “How hard it will be for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God!”
And the disciples are astonished at his words. But Jesus answers again: “Children — how hard it is to enter the kingdom of God!
It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God.”
And they are utterly astonished, saying to one another: “Then who can be saved?”
Looking at them, Jesus says: “With human beings it is impossible — but not with God. For all things are possible with God.”
Peter begins to say to him: “Look — we have left everything and followed you.”
Jesus says: “Truly I tell you — there is no one who has left house or brothers or sisters or mother or father or children or fields for my sake and for the gospel’s sake
who will not receive a hundredfold now in this age — houses and brothers and sisters and mothers and children and fields, with persecutions — and in the age to come eternal life.
But many who are first will be last — and the last first.”
THE THIRD PASSION PREDICTION

And they are on the road going up to Jerusalem. And Jesus is going ahead of them. And they are astonished. And those following are afraid. And taking the Twelve aside again, he begins to tell them what is going to happen to him:
“Look — we are going up to Jerusalem. And the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes. And they will condemn him to death and hand him over to the Gentiles.
And they will mock him and spit on him and flog him and kill him. And after three days he will rise.”
THE REQUEST OF JAMES AND JOHN
And James and John, the sons of Zebedee, come forward to him and say: “Teacher — we want you to do for us whatever we ask of you.”
And he says to them: “What do you want me to do for you?”
They say to him: “Grant us to sit — one at your right hand and one at your left — in your glory.”
But Jesus says to them: “You do not know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I drink — or to be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized?”
And they say to him: “We are able.” And Jesus says to them: “The cup that I drink you will drink — and with the baptism with which I am baptized, you will be baptized.
But to sit at my right hand or at my left — this is not mine to grant. It is for those for whom it has been prepared.”
And when the ten hear it, they begin to be indignant at James and John.
And calling them to him, Jesus says to them: “You know that those who are considered rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them — and their great ones exercise authority over them.
But it shall not be so among you. But whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant.
And whoever wants to be first among you must be slave of all.
For even the Son of Man did not come to be served — but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.”
BLIND BARTIMAEUS
And they come to Jericho. And as he is leaving Jericho with his disciples and a large crowd, the son of Timaeus — Bartimaeus, a blind beggar — is sitting by the road.
And hearing that it is Jesus of Nazareth, he begins to cry out: “Son of David — Jesus — have mercy on me!”
And many rebuke him, telling him to be quiet. But he cries out all the more: “Son of David — have mercy on me!”
And Jesus stops and says: “Call him.” And they call the blind man, saying to him: “Take courage — get up. He is calling you.”
And throwing off his cloak, he springs up and comes to Jesus.
And Jesus answers him: “What do you want me to do for you?” The blind man says to him: “Rabbouni — let me see again.”
And Jesus says to him: “Go — your faith has saved you.” And immediately he receives his sight. And he follows him on the road.
THE TRIUMPHAL ENTRY
And when they draw near to Jerusalem — to Bethphage and Bethany, at the Mount of Olives — he sends two of his disciples
and says to them: “Go into the village ahead of you. And immediately as you enter it you will find a colt tied — one on which no one has ever sat. Untie it and bring it.
And if anyone says to you, ‘Why are you doing this?’ — say: ‘The Lord has need of it.’”
And they go and find a colt tied at a door outside in the street. And they untie it.
And some of those standing there say to them: “What are you doing, untying the colt?”
And they say to them just as Jesus had told them. And they let them go.
And they bring the colt to Jesus and throw their cloaks on it. And he sits on it.
And many spread their cloaks on the road. And others spread leafy branches they have cut from the fields.
And those going ahead and those following are crying out:
“Hosanna!
Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!
Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David!
Hosanna in the highest!”
And he enters Jerusalem — into the temple. And looking around at everything, since the hour is already late, he goes out to Bethany with the Twelve.
THE FIG TREE
And on the following day, when they go out from Bethany, he is hungry.
And seeing a fig tree in the distance with leaves on it, he goes to see if he can find anything on it. And coming to it, he finds nothing but leaves — for it is not the season for figs.
And he answers and says to it: “May no one ever eat fruit from you again.” And his disciples hear it.
THE CLEANSING OF THE TEMPLE

And they come into Jerusalem. And going into the temple, he begins to drive out those who sold and those who bought in the temple. And he overturns the tables of the money-changers and the seats of those who sold pigeons.
And he does not allow anyone to carry anything through the temple.
And he teaches and says to them: “Is it not written: ‘My house shall be called a house of prayer for all the nations’? But you have made it a den of robbers.”
And the chief priests and the scribes hear it and seek a way to destroy him — for they fear him, because all the crowd is astonished at his teaching.
And when evening comes, they go out of the city.
THE WITHERED FIG TREE
And passing by in the morning, they see the fig tree withered from its roots.
And Peter remembers and says to him: “Rabbi — look, the fig tree that you cursed has withered.”
And Jesus answers them: “Have faith in God.
Truly I tell you — whoever says to this mountain, ‘Be taken up and thrown into the sea,’ and does not doubt in his heart but believes that what he says will happen — it will be done for him.
Therefore I tell you — whatever you ask in prayer, believe that you have received it, and it will be yours.
And whenever you stand praying — if you have anything against anyone — release it, so that your Father in heaven may also release your trespasses to you.”
THE QUESTION OF AUTHORITY
And they come again into Jerusalem. And as he is walking in the temple, the chief priests and the scribes and the elders come to him
and say to him: “By what authority are you doing these things? Or who gave you this authority to do them?”
And Jesus says to them: “I will ask you one question. Answer me — and I will tell you by what authority I do these things.
The baptism of John — was it from heaven or from human beings? Answer me.”
And they discuss it among themselves: “If we say ‘from heaven,’ he will say, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’
But if we say ‘from human beings’—” They are afraid of the crowd — for everyone holds that John really was a prophet.
And they answer Jesus: “We do not know.” And Jesus says to them: “Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.”
THE PARABLE OF THE WICKED TENANTS
And he begins to speak to them in parables. “A man plants a vineyard and puts a fence around it and digs a pit for the winepress and builds a tower. And he leases it to tenants and goes abroad.
When the time comes, he sends a servant to the tenants to receive from them some of the fruit of the vineyard.
But they seize him and beat him and send him away empty-handed.
And again he sends another servant to them. They strike him on the head and treat him with contempt.
And he sends another — and him they kill. And many others: some they beat, and some they kill.
He still has one — a beloved son. He sends him last to them, saying: ‘They will respect my son.’
But those tenants say to one another: ‘This is the heir. Come — let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’
And they seize him and kill him and throw him out of the vineyard.
What will the owner of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy the tenants and give the vineyard to others.
Have you not read this scripture:
‘The stone the builders rejected —
this has become the cornerstone.
This is from the Lord
and it is marvelous in our eyes’?”
And they seek to seize him — but they fear the crowd. For they know he has told this parable against them. And leaving him, they go away.
THE QUESTION ABOUT TAXES
And they send to him some of the Pharisees and some of the Herodians — to trap him in his word.

And coming, they say to him: “Teacher — we know that you are true and care for no one’s opinion. For you do not look at people’s faces but teach the way of God in truth. Is it lawful to pay the census tax to Caesar — or not? Should we pay — or should we not pay?”
But knowing their hypocrisy, he says to them: “Why are you testing me? Bring me a denarius and let me see it.”
And they bring one. And he says to them: “Whose image is this — and whose inscription?” “Caesar’s,” they say.
And Jesus says to them: “Give back to Caesar what belongs to Caesar — and to God what belongs to God.” And they are utterly astonished at him.
THE QUESTION ABOUT THE RESURRECTION
And Sadducees come to him — those who say there is no resurrection. And they ask him:
“Teacher — Moses wrote for us that if a man’s brother dies and leaves a wife but no child, the man must take the wife and raise up offspring for his brother.
There were seven brothers. The first took a wife — and dying, left no offspring.
And the second took her and died, leaving no offspring. And the third likewise.
And the seven left no offspring. Last of all, the woman also died.
In the resurrection — when they rise — whose wife will she be? For the seven had her as wife.”
Jesus says to them: “Is this not the reason you are mistaken — because you know neither the scriptures nor the power of God?
For when they rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage — but are like angels in heaven.

And as for the dead being raised — have you not read in the book of Moses, in the passage about the burning bush, how God says to him: ‘I am the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob’?
He is not the God of the dead — but of the living. You are greatly mistaken.”
THE GREATEST COMMANDMENT
And one of the scribes comes forward — having heard them debating and seeing that he has answered them well. He asks him: “Which commandment is first of all?”
Jesus answers: “The first is: ‘Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one.
And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind and with all your strength.’
The second is this: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ There is no other commandment greater than these.”
And the scribe says to him: “Well said, Teacher — you have spoken the truth. He is one, and there is no other besides him.
And to love him with all the heart and with all the understanding and with all the strength — and to love one’s neighbor as oneself — is much more than all burnt offerings and sacrifices.”
And Jesus, seeing that he has answered wisely, says to him: “You are not far from the kingdom of God.” And after that no one dares to ask him any more questions.
WHOSE SON IS THE MESSIAH
And Jesus answers and says, while teaching in the temple: “How do the scribes say that the Messiah is the son of David?
David himself says by the Holy Spirit:
‘The Lord said to my Lord:
“Sit at my right hand
until I place your enemies under your feet.”’
David himself calls him ‘Lord’ — so how is he his son?” And the large crowd hears him gladly.
WARNING ABOUT THE SCRIBES
And in his teaching he says: “Beware of the scribes — those who like to walk around in long robes and want greetings in the marketplaces
and the best seats in the synagogues and the places of honor at feasts —
who devour widows’ houses and for a pretense make long prayers. These will receive a heavier judgment.”
THE WIDOW’S OFFERING
And sitting opposite the treasury, he watches how the crowd puts money into the offering box. Many rich people put in large amounts.
And a poor widow comes and puts in two lepta — which is a quadrans.
And calling his disciples to him, he says: “Truly I tell you — this poor widow has put in more than all those putting into the treasury.
For they all gave out of their abundance. But she — out of her poverty — has put in everything she had — her whole livelihood.”
THE STONES WILL FALL
And as he is going out of the temple, one of his disciples says to him: “Teacher — look, what stones and what buildings!”
And Jesus says to him: “Do you see these great buildings? Not one stone will be left on another that will not be thrown down.”
And as he is sitting on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter and James and John and Andrew ask him privately:
“Tell us — when will these things be? And what will be the sign when all these things are about to be accomplished?”
THE BEGINNING OF BIRTH PAINS
And Jesus begins to say to them: “See to it that no one leads you astray.
Many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am he’ — and they will lead many astray.
And when you hear of wars and reports of wars — do not be alarmed. These things must happen. But the end is not yet.
For nation will rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom. There will be earthquakes in various places. There will be famines. These are the beginning of birth pains.
But watch yourselves. They will hand you over to councils — and you will be beaten in synagogues — and you will stand before governors and kings for my sake, as a testimony to them.
And the gospel must first be proclaimed to all the nations.

And when they lead you away and hand you over — do not be anxious beforehand about what you will say. But say whatever is given to you in that hour. For it is not you who are speaking — but the Holy Spirit.
And brother will hand over brother to death — and a father his child. And children will rise against parents and put them to death.
And you will be hated by all because of my name. But the one who endures to the end — will be saved.”
THE DESOLATING SACRILEGE
“But when you see the desolating sacrilege standing where it should not be — let the reader understand — then let those in Judea flee to the mountains.
Let the one on the rooftop not go down and not enter to take anything from his house.
And let the one in the field not turn back to take his cloak.
And how terrible it will be in those days for women who are pregnant and for those who are nursing infants.
Pray that it does not happen in winter.
For those days will be a time of affliction such as has not been from the beginning of creation which God created until now — and never will be.
And if the Lord had not cut short the days — no flesh would be saved. But for the sake of the elect whom he has chosen — he has cut short the days.
And then if anyone says to you: “Look — here is the Messiah!” or “Look — there!” — do not believe it.
For false messiahs and false prophets will arise and will perform signs and wonders to lead astray — if possible — the elect.
But watch — I have told you everything beforehand.”
THE COMING OF THE SON OF MAN
“But in those days, after that affliction, the sun will be darkened and the moon will not give its light
and the stars will be falling from heaven and the powers in the heavens will be shaken.
And then they will see the Son of Man coming in clouds with great power and glory.
And then he will send out the angels and gather his elect from the four winds — from the end of the earth to the end of heaven.”
THE PARABLE OF THE FIG TREE
“From the fig tree learn this parable: when its branch becomes tender and puts out its leaves — you know that summer is near.
So also you — when you see these things happening — know that he is near, at the very gates.
Truly I tell you — this generation will not pass away until all these things have happened.
Heaven and earth will pass away — but my words will not pass away.”
NO ONE KNOWS THE HOUR
“But concerning that day or that hour — no one knows: not the angels in heaven, not even the Son — but only the Father.
Watch — stay awake. For you do not know when the time is.
It is like a man going abroad — leaving his house and giving authority to his servants, each with his own work, and commanding the doorkeeper to stay awake.
Therefore watch — for you do not know when the master of the house is coming: whether in the evening or at midnight or at the crowing of the rooster or in the morning —
so that coming suddenly he does not find you sleeping.
And what I say to you I say to all: Watch.”
THE PLOT TO KILL JESUS
It is two days before the Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread. And the chief priests and the scribes are seeking how to seize him by stealth and kill him.
For they say: “Not during the feast — or there may be an uproar among the people.”
THE ANOINTING AT BETHANY

And while he is in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper, reclining at table — a woman comes with an alabaster jar of ointment of pure nard, very costly. And breaking the jar, she pours it over his head.
And some are indignant among themselves: “Why has this ointment been wasted like this?
For this ointment could have been sold for more than three hundred denarii and given to the poor.” And they scold her.
But Jesus says: “Leave her alone. Why do you trouble her? She has done a beautiful thing to me.
For you always have the poor with you and you can do good for them whenever you want — but you do not always have me.
She has done what she could. She has anointed my body beforehand for burial.
And truly I tell you — wherever the gospel is proclaimed in the whole world, what she has done will also be spoken of, in memory of her.”
JUDAS ARRANGES THE BETRAYAL
And Judas Iscariot — one of the Twelve — goes to the chief priests in order to hand him over to them.
And hearing it they are glad and promise to give him money. And he seeks an opportune moment to hand him over.
PREPARATION FOR THE PASSOVER
And on the first day of Unleavened Bread — when they sacrifice the Passover lamb — his disciples say to him: “Where do you want us to go and prepare for you to eat the Passover?”
And he sends two of his disciples and says to them: “Go into the city — and a man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him.
And wherever he enters, say to the owner of the house: ‘The Teacher says — where is my guest room, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?’
And he will show you a large upper room furnished and ready. Prepare it for us there.”
And the disciples go out and come into the city and find it just as he told them. And they prepare the Passover.
THE LAST SUPPER
And when evening comes, he comes with the Twelve.
And as they are reclining at table and eating, Jesus says: “Truly I tell you — one of you will hand me over — one who is eating with me.”
They begin to be grieved and to say to him one by one: “Is it I?”
He says to them: “It is one of the Twelve — one who is dipping with me in the bowl.
For the Son of Man goes just as it is written of him. But woe to that man by whom the Son of Man is handed over. It would be better for that man if he had never been born.”
And as they are eating, he takes bread. And blessing it he breaks it and gives it to them and says: “Take — this is my body.”
And taking a cup and giving thanks, he gives it to them and they all drink from it.
And he says to them: “This is my blood of the covenant — poured out for many.
Truly I tell you — I will no longer drink of the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new in the kingdom of God.”
ON THE WAY TO THE MOUNT OF OLIVES
And singing a hymn, they go out to the Mount of Olives.
And Jesus says to them: “You will all fall away — for it is written:
‘I will strike the shepherd and the sheep will be scattered.’
But after I am raised up, I will go before you into Galilee.”
But Peter says to him: “Even if they all fall away — I will not.”
And Jesus says to him: “Truly I tell you — today, this very night, before the rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times.”
But he says with great vehemence: “Even if I must die with you — I will not deny you.” And they all say the same.
GETHSEMANE
And they come to a place called Gethsemane. And he says to his disciples: “Sit here while I pray.”
And he takes with him Peter and James and John. And he begins to be deeply distressed and troubled.
And he says to them: “My soul is overwhelmed with grief — even to death. Stay here and watch.”
And going a little further, he falls on the ground and prays that, if it were possible, the hour might pass from him.
And he says: “Abba — Father — all things are possible for you. Take this cup from me. Yet not what I want — but what you want.”
And he comes and finds them sleeping. And he says to Peter: “Simon — are you sleeping? Could you not watch one hour?
Watch and pray that you may not enter into testing. The spirit is willing — but the flesh is weak.”
And going away again he prays — saying the same words.
And coming again he finds them sleeping — for their eyes are very heavy. And they do not know what to answer him.
And he comes a third time and says to them: “Are you still sleeping and taking your rest? It is enough. The hour has come. Look — the Son of Man is handed over into the hands of sinners.
Rise — let us go. Look — the one who hands me over has drawn near.”
THE ARREST
And immediately — while he is still speaking — Judas arrives, one of the Twelve, and with him a crowd with swords and clubs, from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders.
Now the one who handed him over has given them a signal, saying: “The one I kiss — he is the one. Seize him and lead him away securely.”
And coming — immediately approaching him — he says: “Rabbi!” And he kisses him.
And they lay hands on him and seize him.
But one of those standing nearby draws a sword and strikes the servant of the high priest and cuts off his ear.
And Jesus answers and says to them: “Have you come out with swords and clubs to arrest me as if against a robber?
Day after day I was with you in the temple teaching — and you did not seize me. But let the scriptures be fulfilled.”
And they all leave him and flee.
And a young man follows him — wearing nothing but a linen cloth over his naked body. And they seize him.
But leaving the linen cloth, he flees naked.
THE TRIAL BEFORE THE SANHEDRIN
And they lead Jesus to the high priest. And all the chief priests and the elders and the scribes come together.
And Peter follows him from a distance — right into the courtyard of the high priest. And he is sitting with the guards and warming himself at the fire.
Now the chief priests and the whole council are seeking testimony against Jesus to put him to death — and they find none.
For many bear false witness against him — and their testimonies do not agree.
And some stand up and bear false witness against him:
“We heard him say, ‘I will destroy this temple made with hands and in three days build another not made with hands.’”
But even on this point their testimony does not agree.
And the high priest stands up in the middle and asks Jesus: “Do you have no answer? What is it that these men testify against you?”
But he is silent and answers nothing. Again the high priest asks him: “Are you the Messiah — the Son of the Blessed?”
And Jesus says: “I am. And you will see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of Power and coming with the clouds of heaven.”
And the high priest tears his robes and says: “What further need do we have of witnesses?
You have heard the blasphemy. What is your verdict?” And they all condemn him as deserving death.
And some begin to spit on him and to cover his face and strike him and say to him: “Prophesy!” And the guards receive him with blows.
PETER’S DENIAL
And while Peter is below in the courtyard, one of the servant girls of the high priest comes.
And seeing Peter warming himself, she looks at him and says: “You too were with the Nazarene — with Jesus.”
But he denies it: “I neither know nor understand what you are saying.” And he goes out into the forecourt. And a rooster crows.
And the servant girl sees him and begins again to say to those standing nearby: “This man is one of them.”
But again he denies it. And after a little while those standing nearby say to Peter again: “You certainly are one of them — for you are a Galilean.”
But he begins to invoke a curse on himself and to swear: “I do not know this man you are talking about.”
And immediately a rooster crows a second time. And Peter remembers the word — how Jesus had said to him: “Before the rooster crows twice you will deny me three times.” And he breaks down and weeps.
BEFORE PILATE
And immediately — in the early morning — the chief priests hold a consultation with the elders and scribes and the whole council. And binding Jesus they lead him away and hand him over to Pilate.
And Pilate asks him: “Are you the King of the Jews?” And he answers him: “You say so.”
And the chief priests accuse him of many things.
And Pilate asks him again: “Do you have no answer? See how many things they accuse you of.”
But Jesus makes no further answer — so that Pilate is amazed.
BARABBAS
Now at the feast he used to release for them one prisoner — whichever one they requested.
And there is a man called Barabbas — imprisoned with the rebels who had committed murder in the uprising.
And the crowd comes up and begins to ask him to do as he usually did for them.
And Pilate answers them: “Do you want me to release for you the King of the Jews?”
For he knows that the chief priests have handed him over out of envy.
But the chief priests stir up the crowd to have him release Barabbas for them instead.
And Pilate again answers and says to them: “Then what shall I do with the man you call the King of the Jews?”
And they cry out again: “Crucify him!”
And Pilate says to them: “Why — what evil has he done?” But they cry out all the more: “Crucify him!”
And Pilate — wishing to satisfy the crowd — releases Barabbas for them. And having flogged Jesus he hands him over to be crucified.
THE SOLDIERS MOCK JESUS
And the soldiers lead him away inside the palace — that is, the praetorium — and they call together the whole cohort.
And they dress him in purple and weave a crown of thorns and put it on him.
And they begin to salute him: “Hail, King of the Jews!”
And they strike his head with a reed and spit on him and kneel down in homage to him.
And when they have mocked him, they strip him of the purple and put his own clothes on him. And they lead him out to crucify him.
THE CRUCIFIXION
And they compel a passerby — Simon of Cyrene, coming in from the country, the father of Alexander and Rufus — to carry his cross.
And they bring him to the place called Golgotha — which means the Place of the Skull.
And they offer him wine mixed with myrrh — but he does not take it.
And they crucify him and divide his garments among them, casting lots for them to decide what each should take.
And it is the third hour when they crucify him.
And the inscription of the charge against him reads: THE KING OF THE JEWS.
And with him they crucify two robbers — one on his right and one on his left.
And those who pass by hurl abuse at him — shaking their heads and saying: “Aha! You who would destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days —
save yourself and come down from the cross!”
So also the chief priests mock him among themselves with the scribes: “He saved others — he cannot save himself.
Let the Messiah — the King of Israel — come down from the cross now so that we may see and believe.” And those who are crucified with him also heap abuse on him.
THE DEATH OF JESUS
And when the sixth hour comes, darkness falls over the whole land until the ninth hour.
And at the ninth hour Jesus cries out with a loud voice: “Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani” — which means: “My God, my God — why have you forsaken me?”
And some of those standing nearby, hearing it, say: “Look — he is calling Elijah.”
And someone runs and fills a sponge with sour wine and puts it on a reed and offers it to him to drink, saying: “Wait — let us see whether Elijah comes to take him down.”
And Jesus utters a loud cry and breathes his last.
And the curtain of the temple is torn in two — from top to bottom.
And when the centurion who stands opposite him sees that he thus breathes his last, he says: “Truly this man was the Son of God.”
And there are also women watching from a distance — Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses, and Salome.
When he was in Galilee they followed him and served him. And there are many other women who came up with him to Jerusalem.
THE BURIAL
And when evening has come — since it is the day of Preparation, that is, the day before the Sabbath —
Joseph of Arimathea, a respected member of the council, who is himself waiting for the kingdom of God, takes courage and goes to Pilate and asks for the body of Jesus.
And Pilate is amazed that he is already dead. And summoning the centurion, he asks him whether he has already died.
And when he finds out from the centurion, he grants the corpse to Joseph.
And buying a linen cloth and taking him down, Joseph wraps him in the linen cloth and lays him in a tomb that had been cut out of rock. And he rolls a stone against the door of the tomb.
And Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses see where he is laid.
THE EMPTY TOMB
And when the Sabbath is over, Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of James and Salome buy spices — so that they might go and anoint him.
And very early on the first day of the week they come to the tomb — when the sun has risen.
And they say to one another: “Who will roll away the stone for us from the door of the tomb?”
And looking up they see that the stone has been rolled back — for it is very large.
And going into the tomb, they see a young man sitting on the right side — clothed in a white robe. And they are utterly astounded.
And he says to them: “Do not be alarmed. You are looking for Jesus of Nazareth — the crucified. He has risen. He is not here. See — the place where they laid him.
But go — tell his disciples and Peter: “He is going ahead of you into Galilee. You will see him there — just as he told you.”’
And going out, they flee from the tomb — for trembling and astonishment seize them. And they say nothing to anyone — for they are afraid.
Here the earliest and most reliable manuscripts of Mark end.
THE LONGER ENDING

The following verses are absent from the earliest manuscripts. They represent an early addition to Mark’s gospel, compiled from traditions preserved in Matthew, Luke, and John, and appended by a later hand.
Now after he rose early on the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene — from whom he had driven out seven demons.
She went and told those who had been with him — those who were grieving and weeping.
And hearing that he was alive and had been seen by her — they did not believe it.
And after these things he appeared in a different form to two of them as they were walking — going into the country.
And they went and told the rest. But they did not believe them either.

And later he appeared to the Eleven themselves as they were reclining at table. And he rebuked their unbelief and hardness of heart — because they had not believed those who saw him after he had risen.
And he said to them: “Go into all the world and proclaim the gospel to all creation.
The one who believes and is baptized will be saved. But the one who does not believe will be condemned.
And these signs will accompany those who believe: in my name they will drive out demons; they will speak in new tongues;
they will pick up serpents with their hands; and if they drink anything deadly it will not harm them; they will lay hands on the sick and they will recover.”
So then the Lord Jesus — after speaking to them — was taken up into heaven and sat down at the right hand of God.
And they went out and proclaimed everywhere — the Lord working with them and confirming the word through the accompanying signs.

Since many have taken in hand to draw up a narrative of the events that have been brought to completion among us — 2 just as they were handed down to us by those who from the beginning were eyewitnesses and attendants of the word — 3 it seemed good to me as well, having followed everything carefully from the very beginning, to write an orderly account for you, most excellent Theophilus, 4 so that you may know the certainty of the things in which you have been instructed.
In the days of Herod, king of Judea, there is a priest named Zechariah, from the priestly division of Abijah. His wife Elizabeth is a descendant of Aaron.
Both of them are righteous before God — walking blamelessly in all the commandments and requirements of the Lord.
But they have no child. Elizabeth is barren, and both of them are well along in years.
One day Zechariah’s division is on duty and he is serving as priest before God.
The sacred lot falls to him — as it sometimes did in a priest’s lifetime, and sometimes never did — to enter the sanctuary of the Lord and burn incense.
And the whole crowd of people is outside, praying during the hour of incense.
Then an angel of the Lord appears to him, standing on the right side of the altar of incense.
Zechariah sees him and is shaken to his core. Fear falls on him.
“Don’t be afraid, Zechariah,” the angel says. “Your petition has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you are to name him John.
He will be your joy and delight — and many will rejoice at his birth.
He will be great before the Lord. He must drink no wine or strong drink. And he will be filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother’s womb.
He will turn many of the children of Israel back to the Lord their God.

He will go before him in the spirit and power of Elijah — turning the hearts of fathers toward their children, and the disobedient toward the wisdom of the righteous — to make ready a people prepared for the Lord.”
“How am I supposed to know this is true?” Zechariah says to the angel. “I’m an old man. My wife is well along in years.”
“I am Gabriel,” the angel answers. “I stand in the presence of God. He sent me to speak to you — to bring you this good news.
And now, because you didn’t believe my words — which will be fulfilled at their appointed time — you will be silent and unable to speak until the day these things happen.”
The people are waiting for Zechariah outside. They are puzzled — he’s taking so long in the sanctuary.
When he finally comes out, he can’t speak to them. They realize he’s seen a vision inside. He keeps motioning to them, but he stays mute.
When his days of service are done, he goes home.
And after those days his wife Elizabeth conceives. She keeps herself in seclusion for five months
and says, “This is what the Lord has done for me — in the days when he looked on me and took away my disgrace among people.”
In the sixth month, God sends the angel Gabriel to a town in Galilee called Nazareth,
to a virgin pledged to be married to a man named Joseph, of the house of David. The virgin’s name is Mary.
And coming to her, he says, “Rejoice, you who have been graced! The Lord is with you.”
She is deeply troubled by his word. She turns it over in her mind — what kind of greeting is this?
“Don’t be afraid, Mary,” the angel says. “You have found favor with God.
Listen — you will conceive in your womb and give birth to a son, and you are to call his name Jesus.
He will be great. He will be called Son of the Most High. And the Lord God will give him the throne of his ancestor David.
He will reign over the house of Jacob forever, and his kingdom will have no end.”
“But how?” Mary asks the angel. “I haven’t known a man.”
“The Holy Spirit will come upon you,” the angel answers her. “And the power of the Most High will overshadow you. And for this reason the holy one being born will be called Son of God.
And listen — your relative Elizabeth has also conceived a son in her old age. This is the sixth month for her who was called barren.
No word from God will be impossible.”
“Here I am,” Mary says. “The Lord’s servant. Let it happen to me according to your word.”
And the angel departs from her.
In those days Mary sets out and travels quickly into the hill country, to a town in Judah.
She enters the house of Zechariah and greets Elizabeth.
And when Elizabeth hears Mary’s greeting, the baby leaps in her womb. Elizabeth is filled with the Holy Spirit
and cries out with a great cry: “Blessed are you among women — and blessed is the fruit of your womb!
Why has this been granted to me — that the mother of my Lord should come to me?
For look — when the sound of your greeting reached my ears, the baby in my womb leaped for joy!
Blessed is she who believed — that what was spoken to her from the Lord would be fulfilled.”
And Mary says:
“My soul makes the Lord great;
my spirit exults in God my Savior,
for he has looked upon the lowliness of his servant.
From now on, every generation will call me blessed —
because the Mighty One has done great things for me.
Holy is his name.
And his mercy reaches from generation to generation
to those who fear him.
He has acted with the strength of his arm.
He has scattered the arrogant in the schemes of their hearts.
He has brought down the powerful from their thrones
and lifted up the lowly.
He has filled the hungry with good things
and sent the rich away empty.
He has come to the aid of his servant Israel,
remembering mercy —
just as he spoke to our ancestors,
to Abraham and his descendants forever.”
Mary stays with her about three months, and then returns home.
When the time is fulfilled, Elizabeth gives birth to a son.
And her neighbors and relatives hear that the Lord has shown her great mercy. They rejoice with her.
On the eighth day they come to circumcise the child, and they are going to name him Zechariah — after his father.
But his mother speaks up. “No,” she says. “He is to be called John.”
“There’s no one in your family with that name,” they tell her.
So they make signs to his father to find out what he wants the child called.
He asks for a writing tablet and writes: “His name is John.” And everyone is amazed.
At once his mouth opens and his tongue is freed. And he speaks — blessing God.
Fear comes on all their neighbors. And all through the hill country of Judea, people are talking about these things.
Everyone who hears lays it up in their heart. “What then will this child become?” they ask. And the hand of the Lord is with him.
And his father Zechariah is filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesies:
“Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel —
for he has visited and accomplished redemption for his people.
He has raised up a horn of salvation for us
in the house of his servant David —
as he spoke through the mouth of his holy prophets from of old —
salvation from our enemies,
and from the hand of all who hate us;
to show mercy to our ancestors
and to remember his holy covenant,
the oath he swore to Abraham our ancestor,
to grant us that we, rescued from the hand of our enemies,
might serve him without fear,
in holiness and righteousness before him
all our days.
And you, child — you will be called prophet of the Most High,
for you will go before the Lord to prepare his ways,
to give his people the knowledge of salvation
in the forgiveness of their sins —
through the tender mercy of our God,
by which the rising sun will visit us from on high,
to shine on those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death,
to guide our feet into the way of peace.”
And the child grows and becomes strong in spirit. And he is in the wilderness until the day of his appearing to Israel.
In those days a decree goes out from Caesar Augustus — all the inhabited world is to be registered.
This first registration takes place while Quirinius is governing Syria.
And everyone makes their way to their own town to be registered.
Joseph too goes up from Galilee, from the town of Nazareth, into Judea — to the city of David called Bethlehem — because he belongs to the house and lineage of David.
